> **v34.0 governing ontology correction (11 October 2026).** **Matter and its stress-energy content live fundamentally in the five-dimensional middle space** $\mathcal M=E/U(1)_H$, not solely on the representational bisection. The four-dimensional gravity base $B_{\rm grav}=\mathcal M/U_{\rm mer}$ is the quotient where the effective Einstein equation is expressed. The source $T^{(g)}$ must be obtained from the **entire** one-dimensional meridian fiber, including both arcs and possible pole/core contributions, by a covariant, action-compatible fiber reduction with a geometrically justified measure and tensor projection. A sum of contributions at the two points of $B_{\rm rep}$ is **not Law I**: it is only a distributionally leaf-supported special case. Einstein equations on the base impose constraints on the admissible middle-space configurations; equivalently their pullback imposes a horizontal constraint on $\mathcal M$, **not** independent five-dimensional Einstein equations. The full measure, singular-fiber rule, conservation identity and parent variational principle are **open**. Previously frozen text about source localization and two-point sourcing is superseded by this paragraph, the corrected Law I in Part III, and §XXIX.8; historical derivations remain conditional benchmarks where their premises apply. The observation that $\ell/G$ has a numerically suggestive relation to a galactic mass was an exploratory coincidence, **not** a premise that the closure mass is the Galaxy's baryonic mass. The author also prefers a *macroscopic middle-space* origin of $G$ (with the closure ratio as a target) and a separate Boltzmannian-compatibility origin of the effective quantum/Planck-area scale; the induced-gravity calculation remains a benchmark, not the preferred ontological explanation of $G$.

> **What this document is.** A complete, self-contained statement of the theory in Parts 0–XI, which assume no earlier document: every term is defined in Part 0, every law is stated with its equation, and every identity imported from an earlier version is restated in full rather than cited. Part XII is a detached exploratory appendix; it imports the few definitions it needs rather than citing the notes where they began. Part XIII is the version-17 branch, structural and open throughout.
>
> **The architectural change (v34.0 ontology corrected).** Versions 6 through 14 posited a space and then decorated it with a fiber. Version 15 inverts the order: the **canonical space** $E$ is the axiom; the **middle space** is derived by quotienting the Hopf circle and **is the physical habitat of matter/stress**. Its two four-dimensional constructions are different: the representational bisection is a selected **matter/light readout**, while the gravity base is the quotient supporting an **Einstein constraint sourced by the entire middle-space meridian**. The latter cannot be built by summing only the two bisection crossings.
>
> **What the fiber now is.** A shell of fixed nonzero radius about a *complex* source worldline is not a real 2-sphere: in the complexified normal space it is the affine quadric $Q^2_{\rm aff}$, a complex surface. And that surface is a homogeneous space of the complex spin group,
> $$\mathbb{C}^\times\ \longrightarrow\ SL(2,\mathbb{C})\ \longrightarrow\ Q^2_{\rm aff}\cong SL(2,\mathbb{C})/\mathbb{C}^\times$$
> whose compact real form is the ordinary Hopf fibration $U(1)\to SU(2)\simeq S^3\to S^2$. **So the Hopf character is no longer decoration. It is the compact real form of the complex spin geometry belonging to an isotropic shell**, and it was the right guess for the wrong reason in every version that assumed it.
>
> **The centrepiece.**
> $$\boxed{\ \text{spin geometry fixes the fiber's topology;}\qquad\text{gravity fixes only its metric length.}\ }$$
> These are different kinds of information. The spin structure says what the fiber **is** — $U(1)\hookrightarrow SU(2)\simeq S^3\to S^2$, the **unit Hopf class** — and Law I says how large that already-existing circle is at each base point, $L_H = \mathcal{F}[g_G]$. Changing $L_H$ does not change the Chern class or make it a different bundle. One fixed spin-derived Hopf bundle, whose fibers stretch and contract with the gravitational geometry.
>
> **What this version retires.** Because the fiber is now *derived*, its Chern class is **fixed at the unit Hopf class** — not a free integer. That contradicts the inherited second-order sector, in which $c_1 = M_-/m_{\rm unit}$ was mass-dependent with a free parameter. **The whole flux branch therefore goes** (§XI.1): the quantum $m_{\rm unit}$, the quantization fork, mass-proportional winding counts, the Reissner–Nordström-like charge $P$ and its Mercury bound, and the candidate source law $dF_H = 2\pi\star J_-$. This is not a loss of content but the removal of an inconsistency — and it takes two free parameters with it.
>
> **The seed, in one line.**
> > Light resolves a representative in $B_{\rm rep}$; gravity resolves only its meridian class in $B_{\rm grav}$.
>

# PART 0 — VOCABULARY AND THE HIERARCHY

## 0.0 The leading intuitions [D/S/O]

*The theory grew from a handful of intuitions. The formal parts sometimes carry an intuition further than its first statement, sometimes find a different form for it, and sometimes retire it. This section states each one plainly, then says what the mathematics made of it and where.*

**1. Matter in the middle; gravity resolves entire meridian classes.** The seed is a non-injective relation between physical middle-space matter and its base-space gravitational source. A chosen representational bisection exhibits two crossings $x$ and $\tau x$ of the same full meridian; their electromagnetic and detector readouts can differ even when the gravity base records one class. *v34.0 correction:* the former law summing stress only at $x$ and $\tau x$ was an unintended restriction. Law I now requires full-fiber reduction $q_*$ of physical middle-space content; the two-point source sum survives only if the physical source distribution has support on that bisection. The two-lift theorem on $S^3\to\mathbb{RP}^3$ is a mathematical property of a quotient solution, not proof of the physical source law. *Status:* ontology adopted; reduction dynamics open.

**2. A barren representational twin can share a gravitational class with a luminous one.** The two crossings may have different matter and electromagnetic **readouts** while receiving the same class geometry. *v34.0 correction:* a dark readout does not prove the absence of matter elsewhere along the physical middle-space meridian; the old twin-energy lunar-ranging bound excludes a particular duplicated-energy source ansatz, not generic full-fiber sourcing (§§V.2–3, X.13). *Status:* conditional representative-selection model; full middle-space matter distribution and source reduction open.

**3. Change the shells, not the tangent spaces.** Rather than add structure to spacetime's tangent spaces, let the shells around each source carry an extra circle — the first gesture toward the Hopf fiber — and let a rotating hole be a source tilted against that grain. *Made into:* the complex spin lift of Part I, where the shell's circle acts on normalized spinor representatives exactly as their overall phase (§I.6), and the complex displacement of Part VI, which captures Kerr's complex structure though not, alone, all of Kerr. *Status:* verified for the phase; partial for Kerr; in bundle form the fiber's holonomy acquires a size, $\Delta s_H = (L_H/2\pi)\Delta\chi$ (§IX.1).

**4. Time as what is not quotiented.** Time might be the one direction of the deeper structure that is never quotiented away. *Made into:* three attempted routes, none successful. *Status:* open; time is still an input (§XI.2).

**5. A galaxy fills one hemisphere of a small closed universe.** A galaxy occupies one hemisphere of a closed three-sphere and its dark twin the other, and an exponential falloff of mass from one point makes the rotation curve flatten — flat curves as a closure effect rather than a halo. *Made into:* the galactic arena, one galaxy with no cosmological slot (the note on scale), and the plateau $v^2 = 2.994\,GM_{\rm grav}/\ell$ (§IV.8). *Status:* the plateau is verified within the specified Einstein-static/rigid-closure **base-source benchmark**, not rederived from full-meridian middle-space matter; the closure background and optical distance cap remain open (§XI.2).

**6. Charge as a signed imbalance.** Reissner–Nordström might be the small-charge face of a projective effect: two chiral pieces whose balance is Schwarzschild and whose full imbalance is an extremal hole. *Made into:* the factor-weight picture of §X.0 — mass the sum of two weights, charge their signed difference, gravity blind to the sign. *Status:* exact as the algebra of Reissner–Nordström; the readout hypothesis is open. The factorization is a target, not a mechanism, and its rapidity holds $\delta$ fixed rather than the horizon area (§XIII.5).

**7. Other galaxies through apparent scale.** A galaxy's apparent size may differ from its actual size, and the mismatch may be what produces Tully–Fisher's square root. *Made into:* a detached wing, scoped but deliberately not attached (Part XII). *Status:* exploratory.

**8. The observed event is rigid downstairs; its canonical realizations are flexible upstairs.** Two canonical alternatives remain one observed event when their positions project to exactly the same point and their directions agree to within the resolution of whatever physical channel could record a difference — a camera being only an example of such a channel. *Made into:* Part XIII's canonical optics — two agreement rules, a readout map, and a connection whose holonomy separates the canonical endpoints of one observed event. *Status:* definitions and constraints; coherence is governed by what the detector and environment can distinguish, with phase holonomy the cleanest carrier (§XIII.3).

**9. One thing can appear twice.** One underlying point may show up at two places in an output space, each appearance keeping a different part of a common structure — like a logo with different parts quotiented away, read as two logos. Nobody would have noticed, because each appearance keeps something the other lacks. *Made into:* rendering as a correspondence, and agreeing structure as what both appearances retain (§XIII.4); the seed is its first instance. *Status:* definitions.

**10. Fields are what failed to unpack.** A *centrade* can be packed and unpacked: fully unpacked in the Kerr direction it has no angular momentum, in the Reissner–Nordström direction no charge. Unpackings conflict, "whack-a-mole", so there is a budget. *Made into:* admissible unpackings as a non-product set, and fields as residual obstructions, with standard precedents (§XIII.5). *Status:* conjecture, with a verified miniature in the Hopf-sign budget of §V.4.

**11. Our spacetime is one rendering among many.** Each global unpacking scheme outputs its own visual spacetime; ours is privileged by the sheer number of microstates and the relational complexity it supports, not by the laws. A hexagonal sheet of richly linked nodes, each carrying an infinite single-file tower, would hide the towers from its inhabitants. *Made into:* a renderer, multiplicity, and relational complexity as the criterion of visibility (§XIII.6). *Status:* conjecture; what stays invariant across renderings is open. The motivation is Machian — the galaxy's frame dominates because the galaxy holds far more centrades — but the statement concerns renderings, not a preferred frame inside one spacetime (§XIII.0).

**12. The galactic plane is a fixed set, and spirals are rendered.** The stress-energy upstairs may be roughly isotropic, with the galactic plane the fixed set of an involution; and a star at a turning point of its orbit might be rendered on the opposite side, making rosettes look like spirals. *Made into:* the involution fixing a great two-sphere, and the two readings of the orbital flip, computed (§XIII.7). *Status:* the fixed set is standard; neither simple flip makes spirals from a symmetric disk, though a handedness flip freezes each rosette into a stationary spiral segment, and the author's own cut-and-flip gives two point-symmetric spirals, trailing when the outgoing halves are flipped (§XIII.7).

**13. Our motion may be simpler upstairs than it looks.** Stars may share a simpler canonical motion, with its normal part hidden and what we see a readout of the rest — and the in-plane part of our velocity relative to the cosmic background lies almost exactly opposite our orbital motion. *Made into:* the readout package and the dipole clue (§XIII.8). *Status:* a clean formalism and a numerical clue; the test for one unifying structure fails in its strong form, with two shared pieces surviving.

**14. Centres gravitate as centres; relations between them do not.** Between the centrade that emits a photon and the centrade that absorbs it, the propagation may carry no gravitational identity of its own, and a charged hole's metric and Coulomb field may be two readouts of one centre. *Made into:* the gravitational firewall and the two-readout picture (§XIII.9). *Status:* conjecture. Imposing zero Weyl curvature fails, and the weaker rule needs a local split of Weyl curvature that general relativity does not supply.

**15. Far out along the normal, a lift stops closing.** Gravity above the disk is real, so what changes far along the normal is not gravity but how visual representatives of a gravitational class glue together. *Made into:* prospect holonomy (§XIII.9). *Status:* no flat bundle can do it, but curvature odd under the plane reflection makes the plane's connection flat and opens loops along the normal — the shape of a mechanism, not yet derived; exact closure of every planar loop also needs trivial holonomy on the projective plane.

**16. A photon's two legs may separate where the geometry allows.** The isolated ray is only the generic limit; where the geometry makes the endpoints conjugate, a photon's stationary history may be a whole class with the same observed ends — the author's picture of a pair that opens. *Made into:* the Jacobi-kernel gate, with the round arena's release points at $L = n\pi\ell$ and the first at the twin (§XIII.10). *Status:* standard theory already sums stationary rays, so the new content can only lie in the readout; within the solar system the gate stays shut; no observable difference is yet derived.

**17. Other galaxies may be recurrent canonical history classes of the one arena.** What an observer calls an external galaxy might be a returning two-path photon history of the single arena, rendered at an apparent distance with a redshift, rather than a second arena far away. *Made into:* Part XIV — the antipodal family broken by secondaries, a return map, a unitary spectral-dilation readout. *Status:* provisional throughout; the self-return requirement fixes the price, the first-order member count is not a galaxy count, and the branch's sharpest test is an invariant placing the observer's own return in the readout kernel.

**18. The Galaxy's own well may set the Hubble scale.** The dimensionless depth of the Galaxy's well on the arena scale, $GM/c^2\ell$, may be the dimensionless redshift of one arena radius, $H_0\ell/c$. *Made into:* the well-Hubble calibration of §XIV.6, with its coefficient to be derived. *Status:* the literal hemisphere flux vanishes by symmetry and the depth is packing-dominated; the surface through which the well would act is not yet defined.

**19. Light and gravitational waves must not be able to tell which of them is objective.** If a galaxy's image is a two-history object for light, uniqueness of that galaxy under both messengers demands the same structure for gravitational waves, with no mechanism privileging either — a no-privileging principle in the spirit of general covariance. *Made into:* the Universal Null-History Principle (§XV.0), exact at leading eikonal order, with $\eta_{\rm EM} = \eta_{\rm GW}$ as its test. *Status:* adopted; anchored by GW170817; standard footholds real.

**20. Bake it into spacetime: the middle space as a combination of two deeper structures.** Rather than append readouts, let the middle geometry emerge as the symmetric resolution of two deeper transports, designed so that the dual gravitational-wave picture lives there and is wired to the electromagnetic one — a substrate-deepening move that might make the Hubble behaviour emergent. *Made into:* the bi-connection of §XV.1, adopted by decision, whose scale character is a homothety complementary to the Jacobi squeeze (§XV.2), the real-loop form superseded in 20.2 by the conjugate lifts; the fiber-product form of $\mathcal M$ deferred (§XV.5). *Status:* the structure is verified; its sign rule, dynamics and universality are open.

**21. The two Born paths and the two connections are one thing.** The two paths a photon always requires and the two connections of the substrate would be manifestations of one representation-independent structure — the gravitational analogue of the quantum pair — with a gauge-like freedom to offload a system's defining constraints from the quantum pair onto the Weyl decomposition and back. *Made into:* the closed-time-path dictionary, one complex relative holonomy with phase and scale as its parts, and the offloading theorem (§XV.6). *Status:* the dictionary and the theorem are standard mathematics assembled; that the theory's three $\mathbb C^\times$'s are one is the deepest open conjecture, and the exchange of the bi-connection turns out to be the compact real structure acting on $\mathbb C^\times$, which derives the firewall; the Hopf connection then analytically determines its own noncompact partner, and a class's scale character is a Hopf flux (§XV.7, §XV.3).

**22. One sky point, many galaxies.** Index versions of visual space by the dual-path degrees of freedom beyond the arrival direction and the source point; then constraining a rendering by "this exact point is included" can paint several different galaxies through it, the object swept out as the direction tilts depending on the relational data. *Made into:* the Visual-Sheet Principle (§XVI.0) and the fiber experiment (§XVI.3). *Status:* adopted; the phenomenon needs several fiber states lying on distinct continuable branches with distinct images — several states alone are only necessary — and whether that occurs is a computation on the broken family.

**23. The privileged normal as an equilibrium, killed off the plane.** A galaxy's normal may be less a $\cos(\text{angle})$ than a stationary condition met in the plane and lost off it by a phase incompatibility — with real off-plane density falling off exponentially as wavefunctions do in forbidden regions. *Made into:* off-sheet suppression by complex saddles (§XVI.5), the only version of rendering-made disks left after shear fails (§XVI.2). *Status:* a mechanism class, not a derivation; the isotropic-ball reading is excluded by local dynamics (§XVI.7).

**24. The galaxy as a fixed point of a duality.** The off-plane structure may be a duality in its own right, interlocking with the complexified geometry, with the galaxy — or its plane — as its fixed point. *Made into:* the lift of the plane reflection to the Hopf bundle — an anti-equivariant, fiber-inverting lift forced by the Chern class, antilinear in its real-slice expression — commuting with the real structure and agreeing with it on the normal history mode; the plane as the intersection of two real forms; the normal as the odd Hessian mode (§XVI.8). *Status:* derived on the local model; it gives Part XIII's assumed odd parity a canonical enforcer, conditional on the connection's equivariance under the lift, and imposes two parity kill tests on Part XV's redshift sector, of which the meridian mode fails the first and the normal mode may survive.

**25. Two equally intrinsic types of reality.** The complexified canonical geometry may be primary because it supports more than one real form: one compact real structure, where matter lives, and an equally intrinsic split real-form *type*, occurring as an isotropic family whose member is solution-selected, with the scale transport on the selected split form and the two agreeing on the selected plane. *Made into:* Part XVII, with the diamond, the two restrictions of one connection, the dual Lorentzian shell, and the reflection theorem selecting the surviving sector. *Status:* an experiment in architecture; derives more than it assumes locally; does not yet earn modification of the core.

**26. Alignment exposes a projective opening direction.** The author's original form — that nearly aligned paths can reorient the direction between them far more sharply than distant ones, so that the same common-real intersection that fixes the Galactic plane at full scale might select each Kerr black hole's equatorial plane in the path-aligned regime — motivated the branch, and the calculation narrowed it: small separation makes the direction ill-conditioned, actual flexibility needs a small Jacobi gap, and the Kerr near zone, computed, has a large one — the theory correcting its author. *Made into:* the projective opening direction $[Y]$, a family $\sigma_{[N]}$ of second real structures with solution-selected members, and the Kerr bridge — the Newman–Janis displacement is a displacement into the split real form (§XVII.9). *Status:* the family is a conjugacy orbit derived from the shell symmetry and the Kerr reality is verified on the local model; the freedom of the direction is the Jacobi nullity, not smallness; the selection of $[N]$ by the history geometry is derived at the level of symmetry and confirmed numerically for the Galaxy, with the strong-field Kerr near zone now computed: the spin twists kernels by at most about $20°$, and the Kerr axis is reconstructed from the spin-selected axial symmetry, not recovered from the local spin-induced twisting of an otherwise isotropic history family (§XVII.10).

**27. Repacking within a budget, by one conformal transformation.** Switching among selections and redistributing a body's charge, spin and nonextremality could both be operations of one conformal transformation on the pre-quotient space, tuning the agreeing structure in the quotient while preserving the gravity-base metric that controls the fiber lengths. *Made into:* the repacking transformation and its invariance condition (§XVIII.6), the budget corrected to a simplex (§XVIII.1). *Status:* the fork is real — Law I makes a hole's parameters gravitationally visible — and the guaranteed budget is between a source and its twin; between two bodies the static sector's constraint is same-sign joint extremality with no continuous compensation, and degree $-1$ throat and twin identifications invert the Hopf fiber while the Couch–Torrence pairing forces no inversion (§XVIII.3, §XVIII.5).

**28. Extremality as the idealized case; nonextremality as a gained irreducibility.** The extremal black hole, with its traceless optical Ricci tensor, may be profoundly idealized, and tilting out of extremality — losing the neat Laplacian condition — may be the beefing-up of a connection. *Made into:* $R_{\rm opt} = -6\delta^2/r^4$, and the Poisson equation for the optical conformal factor whose source is the nonextremality, harmonic at extremality (§XVIII.2). *Status:* exact; its reading as a connection's curvature open.

**29. Boltzmannian space.** If each repacking is a microstate, the Galactic frame is privileged by conditioning on the vastly larger macrostate of the Galaxy's bulk, and a black hole's fixed parameters are a remnant of that conditioning. *Made into:* the microstate space without gauge copies, the coarse-graining and the entropy (§XVIII.8). *Status:* a construction awaiting a derived measure; the collective normal of §XVII.10 its first shape.

**30. Three complex amplitudes before three physical roles.** A black hole's spin, charge and nonextremality may be three abstract channels of a deeper centrade, with the rendering choosing which appears as which — perhaps three because space has three dimensions. *Made into:* the triality conjecture with its firewall, the abstract budget operator, representation type as what the rendering assigns, and the $\mathbb Z_2$ step (Part XIX). *Status:* all three readouts share a fall-off and differ in representation type, so any symmetry is pre-rendering; the spectral numerology fails for spherical symmetry; an unlabelled object with a real $S_3$ action is the whole question.

**31. Reuse the flavor structure.** Nature reuses its structures, so unification should follow them: as the two connections came from the two Born paths, the channel space should come from lepton flavor — complex, not real — with flavor's interplay with phase imported as this structure's interplay with the theory's phase, and the complex data either kept in the complexified-spacetime slot or quotiented away in the output. *Made into:* the channel space $\mathbb C^3\supset S^5\to\mathbb{CP}^2$, the Kerr–Newman weights as phase-blind intensities, $S_3$ as the Weyl group, the mixing-matrix rendering by which relative phase repacks the budget, the Hopf phase as the common phase, and the two-imaginary-units firewall (§XIX.2). *Status:* the structure is standard and verified, and the theory canonically contains the carrier — the shell's ${\rm Sym}^2\mathbb C^2$, weight two under the Hopf phase, twin-even, the complexified 3-space; promoting states in that carrier to channel states, and identifying renderings with real frames, remain the hypotheses. Under them the polarization classifies exactly which budgets a centrade can wear, and single-spinor states, being null, are excluded by observation.

**32. Use Kerr's own construction as the instance.** No internal direction may be attached to the canonical space by hand; the sanity check is that the way Kerr is built must itself instantiate the general principle. And the microstate picture was always this: a new gravity base for each render, constrained so that the base keeps controlling the middle space's curvature and fiber lengths. *Made into:* §XIX.2b — the Kerr–Newman source as the complex axial datum $\zeta = \delta+ia$, rod half-length real and Newman–Janis displacement imaginary, with spacetime's own imaginary unit and $p = 1$; and the locking law as the invariant of repacking (§XIX.1). *Status:* the instance is exact, and Law I's own Kinnersley symmetry explains the budget — charging is a boost of the split pair $(M,Q)$ that leaves the compact pair $\zeta$ untouched, so $M^2-Q^2 = |\zeta|^2$ (§XIX.2c); the soldering that makes the instance canonical is the theorem target.

**33. A vanishing separation may leave a spin-state slot.** The magnitude separating two equipped histories can vanish while a projective direction survives; perhaps for massive matter the resolved degree of freedom is not another spacetime direction but the slot in which a spin state lives. The cosmos does not choose the electron's spin: the canonical geometry supplies the slot, local preparation and dynamics choose the state. If the slot is real it must lift through the theory's Hopf $U(1)$ to $\mathbb{CP}^1$, reproduce the half-solid-angle Berry phase and the $2\pi$ spinor sign, and extend by existing Lorentz and spin indices to the Dirac kinematics without adding coordinates. *Made into:* Part XX. *Status:* the theory already contains exactly the right local Hopf and spin geometry — the spin-group identification and its Hopf–Bloch bundle are Part I's own — and the complete free Dirac plane-wave spinor data, both mode families, with the internal discrete-symmetry intertwiners, follow from the lift and the theory's two spinor structures; and the connection constructed on the spin bundle over the mass shell reproduces Bargmann–Michel–Telegdi for every $g$ with nothing added, while a counterfactual meridian-Kaluza–Klein transport is excluded as spin dynamics, its $g = 1$ half of Dirac's; the candidate slot exists along every massive history; the canonical connection is Berry's, constraining its deformations; the conjugate structure gives the orthogonal partner; the local antipodal sign is the $2\pi$ rotation while its identification with the global twin is open — and proving that this geometry is the state bundle of physical matter is what remains.

**34. From kinematics to matter.** The reconstructed spinor kinematics is not yet an electron; the electron needs a local field on representational spacetime, an action, statistics and a vacuum, and none may be appended by fiat. *Made into:* Part XXI — the two bundles kept apart, the spacetime spinor bundle topologically unambiguous on the cover with its global gluing open, the twin sign as a choice of descent to the gravity base, the action and statistics as the open half. *Status:* topology settled, dynamics open.

**35. What spin becomes when the legs separate.** In the aligned-legs regime a pair's separation has only a direction; when the legs genuinely separate it acquires a magnitude. Perhaps what the coincident regime reads as quantum spin is repurposed in the resolved regime while remaining rooted in the same object — the projective residue of a relational degree of freedom whose radial part becomes physical only when the histories resolve. *Made into:* §XX.12, a question with a theorem target — one state space over $[0,\infty)$ with $\mathbb{CP}^1$ as its $r = 0$ boundary and a connection interpolating Berry transport and the comparative dual-history transport — and its kill tests. *Status:* speculative; the conservative alternative, spin as a local state at all separations, is equally open.

**36. A transformation that cycles the lepton family.** Perhaps a transformation of the whole rendered universe cycles through the charged-lepton family, and the Koide structure of their masses is geometry rather than a numerical relation. *Made into:* §XXI.4 — the mass eigenvalue as a product of two dual factors a quarter turn apart, $m_n = m_*(\cos\theta_n+1/\sqrt2)^2$, so that Koide's $2/3$ follows from the $\mathbb Z_3$ identities; the operator form on the theory's own spin-one carrier with the weight states of the selected axis as sectors; each factor twice a Born overlap; the cycle as rendering covariance, $CM(\theta)C^{-1} = M(\theta+2\pi/3)$. *Status:* exact mathematics, available pieces, nothing forced: the quarter turn's use is a postulate, the cycle is not a shell operation, and only one relation is explained — but the three has a structural candidate: the carrier is the regular representation of a cyclic group only for order three, the three being the dimension of the rest space, with the occupancy premise the open theorem (§XXI.4a); and the native conjugation exchanges the two transverse sectors covariantly with the axial sector, the $\tau$'s candidate, fixed. The descent exists conditional on the reduction (§XXI.4b), and the reduction has a candidate origin in the split real-form selection every rendering makes (§XXI.4d): the generation space is the multiplicity space of the selected axis's stabilizer on the native carrier — three weights, Lorentz-scalar, sector-preserving under the canonical transport with a diagonal holonomy when the axis moves (§XXI.4c) — so the three is $\dim H_u$ without any $\mathbb Z_3$, the third turn entering only as the equal spacing of the Koide phases, which is channel-before-role applied to the sector phases.

**37. The three modes as equilibrium spots, and commuting reductions.** Perhaps the three lepton states are stationary spots of a deeper substrate, with oscillation on tilting away, and reducing that substrate first commutes with varying the ordinary action afterwards; perhaps neutrino flavor merely names the charged-lepton states it interacts with, so that neutrino mass is a clue to a more flexible lepton action. *Made into:* §XXI.5 — the sectors as the critical rays of a Rayleigh functional on $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with Morse indices $0,2,4$, fixed points of the projective flow with off-mode oscillation and no collapse; the nested-variation identity as the exact commutativity; neutrino flavor as charged-current indexing with $U_{\rm PMNS}$ the mismatch of two stationary structures. *Status:* exact where it is representation theory; the deeper functional is open; the computed constraint is that mixing requires the neutrino operator to break the charged-lepton axis's residual symmetry, and a single tilted axis is excluded.

The backtransform.** Neutrinos may be the inaccessible images of charged leptons under a curvature-reflective, history-rooted transformation of the representational three-sphere, visible spacetime being the overlay of both, a weak vertex the forced meeting of one worldline's two images, quarks a third imposed spacetime, and weak isospin the elephant. *Made into:* Part XXII — two renderings of one history state related by a correspondence, the fiber-product vertex, the channel map $e\mapsto\nu_e$, accessibility as the charge projector, the ranked candidates with the compact/split product tested and rejected, weak isospin as the benchmark, the hypercharge route for quarks. *Status:* typed and open; the history-rooted backtransform is the first construction.

Apparent proximity as conditioning.** A neutrino leg and its charged-lepton counterpart are far apart in the underlying space; if standard spacetime's vertex is conditioned on their worldlines meeting anywhere in their future, an inversion-like transformation unfolds that distance into the pinpoint that is the vertex — apparent proximity is a conditioning constraint on something seemingly unrelated in the underlying space, and the inversion is a probe of how an exotic ontology looks usual downstairs. *Made into:* §XXII.6 — the vertex as an incidence class of a history-pair correspondence rendered to one event, underlying distance and apparent locality as different observables, the future condition as a stationary coupled history with no backward signal. *Status:* typed and open; its causality firewall is the branch's first constraint.

Accessibility as metric matching.** Inaccessible means the neutrino's natural metric differs from representational spacetime, a history-rooted transformation rendering it from the charged-lepton version; charge one is the remnant of the charged lepton's metric matching apparent spacetime, which conditions on it, the neutrino's being orthogonal — neutrality as orthogonal-function shenanigans. *Made into:* §XXII.8 — accessibility as a projector, neutrality as a kernel of the rendering algebra, two sheet geometries with apparent spacetime adapted to one, the firewall that matching is not yet charge, and chirality as a theorem target. *Status:* typed and open.

**41. Bi-electromagnetism.** A deeper interaction on a deeper space whose history-based quotient has exactly two disjoint exhaustive modes landing on the middle space — one yielding our middle space with its electromagnetism, the other an ortho-middle space in which electromagnetism is killed and neutrinos are natural, carrying charge one under an ortho-electromagnetism: the same monopoles with expanded qualifying slots, each killed by the other mode — and one invariant bi-electromagnetism in the common space, with the electroweak interaction a stunted limiting case. *Made into:* §XXII.9 — two complementary charge readouts $Q_\ell = -P_\ell$, $Q_\nu = -P_\nu$ exchanged by the backtransform, whose algebra with the exchange is exactly $\mathfrak u(2)$, the two modes the eigensectors of an involution, the parent connection classified with $F_\ell = dA_\ell+W^-\wedge W^+$ and rendering selection the only symmetry breaking. *Status:* algebra exact, the rest open.

Offloading into the canonical space.** Check how much of the canonical space can take the load of the deeper space: both middle spaces a three-sphere with a meridian direction, literally orthogonal, from a total space of fewer than $2n$ dimensions with great redundancy, the outputs unrecognizable to each other — next door in one almost maximally far in the other, monotonicity rearranged, the Hopf fibers' closing reoriented — with history and bi-connection as arguments. *Made into:* §XXII.10 — the Hopf circle direction and the complementary meridian line structure of $E$ as the two modes, exactly orthogonal in the canonical metric for the horizontal representative, two five-dimensional reductions exchanging roles locally, the six-in-ten correspondence with multivalued near/far, the common four-dimensional reduction that is the gravity base $B_{\rm grav}$, the bare structure abelian so that the non-abelian sector must live in the history-dependent label transport, and the parent as a package with two reduction functors. *Status:* the frozen part configured and verified; the history-dependent part open.

Branch symmetry, solution asymmetry.** Make the laws symmetric to both renderings — the ortho-middle space's fiber lengths relying on its own quotient to the gravity base — while letting the matter distribution privilege the canonical meridian as "the meridian," so that electrons are the accessible ones. *Made into:* §XXII.11 — the two directions unnamed until a solution chooses, the gravity base their common quotient, a symmetric length-locking with an exchange rule, a derived rendering selector with two symmetry-related stationary branches, Law IV following the selector, "meridian" branch-relative, and the kill tests. *Status:* typed and open; the exchange a symmetry of the package if of anything.

**44. The interlocking core.** The meeting point of the meridians is not a point but an interior region — Hopf fibers over two-sphere shells, or whatever admits a stress-energy-oriented generation per the ortho-middle space — where the meridians interlock in a tight space and the topological cost is bagged, with our representation three-sphere in the exterior beyond a smooth threshold; meridians being the same stuff as Hopf fibers, since in the ortho-middle space its Hopf fibers are the meridians, a Hopfian linking should extend to the general structure; the seed needs only orthogonal, radially ingoing, antipodally continuing meridians in the exterior; and the interior matter distribution, switching from exterior-type to interior-type stress-energy, is the contingent constraint. *Made into:* §XXII.12 — the oriented blow-up of the pole with its $S^3$ of directions, unoriented to $\mathbb{RP}^3$, Hopf-fibered by the great two-spheres if the complex structure extends; the core polarization's charge a Hopf invariant with linked preimage circles and no monopole flux, the twin sign as core holonomy; the switch as the change of focusing branch of the Jacobi expansion, the caustic dissolved by a finite core; the pole model the zero-core limit. *Status:* toy verified, construction open.

The central mass as selector.** The huge mass at the apparent middle-space center privileges the meridians as the meridians, and the same configuration might fix the gravitational readout. *Made into:* §XXII.13 — primary matter selecting the electron-accessible branch $P_\ell$, after which the projector algebra $P_\ell P_\nu = 0$ enforces exact neutrino neutrality with no continuous dependence on mass; the core as the parent symmetric phase and the exterior orientation as the selected rendering; $G$ not derived — the coupling question housed in §VIII.3 — one configuration controlling both the realized gravitational geometry and the realized rendering; the selection operator with its spectral gap as the construction. *Status:* typed and open.

Right-handed weak isospin as the neutrino rendering's own.** Attach the missing right-handed weak isospin to the neutrino's own rendered space, so that it fails empirically exactly with the neutrino's change of rendering; keep anomaly cancellation's reasoning for the hypercharges fully valid, strictly within our rendering where the ortho contributions are already lost. *Made into:* Part XXIII — the selector-gated chirality, Lorentz-covariant and parity-breaking only, with the backtransform untouched by spin; $Y_R = -2$ and the sterility of $\nu_R$ forced rather than inserted; the closure warning met by gating the whole traceless part; right-handed charged currents exactly absent by charge superselection; anomaly cancellation rendering by rendering making the quark sector mandatory. *Status:* the gate's consistency proved, its derivation open.

The hybrid space for quarks.** A hybrid between the middle and ortho-middle spaces — rotating the flavors themselves between them rather than two space axes from one and one from the other — as the counterpart of up and down quarks. *Made into:* §XXIII.7 — the pencil of complementary reductions in the canonical two-plane, all sharing $B_{\rm grav}$, the hybrid pair's weak isospin a conjugate of the lepton pair's, up/down as complementarity; flavors rotated as projector data on $G_{\rm gen}\otimes W$, CKM as a mismatch of stationary operators; the obstruction exactly hypercharge, no angle giving $Y_Q = \tfrac13$; the theorem target of a geometrically distinguished hybrid position; quarks as the hybrid polarization of one geometry rather than a third spacetime. *Status:* typed and open.

The full effective symmetry behind hypercharge.** For the hypercharge obstruction, account for the charge of neutrinos and the right-handed $W$ sector — the full effective symmetry. *Made into:* §XXIII.8 — hypercharge as the rendering-symmetric charge $Y_L = Q_\ell+Q_\nu$, the parent su(2) carrying $\gamma^0$ on its ladders and commuting with the gate, the descent $Y/2 = X+T_{3R}$ with $T^\pm_R$ not descending and $T_{3R}$ not separately, the whole lepton table from one $X = -\tfrac12$ with $\nu_R$'s sterility and $e_R$'s $-2$ as complementary cancellations, the quark offset $X_q = \tfrac16$ from anomaly and color, and the hybrid pencil left only the placement. *Status:* bookkeeping verified; the descent as a property of the rendering functor open.

Hypercharge as the fossil of the lost rendering.** *Made into:* §XXIII.9 — the gate producing the left–right endomorphism algebra, the primary gauge parent the minimal one with only the singlet Cartan gauged, the stabilizer of the $\nu_R$-character selector being exactly $\{\mathfrak{su}(2)_\Pi,\,X+R\}$ with a one-dimensional omitted complement, the descent of §XXIII.8 following from one vector, and the omitted direction having no local support here. *Status:* the stabilizer verified; the rendering reduction built on objects in §XXIII.10; the parent gauging open.

The functor, pushed; the microstate hint.** Push now for the fundamental functor, and ask whether the electron/neutrino distinction is a special case of the Boltzmannian space-microstate concept. *Made into:* §XXIII.10 — the reduction on objects along the internal sterile vector with the complement omitted, image algebra electroweak by construction; two reductions of one kind with different categorical fates of the complement; the exchange sharing the weak force between renderings and splitting the neutral center; the minimal parent; both ledgers clean; the microstate counting placed as the hint for why the section and the branch are what they are. *Status:* the construction derived on objects; morphisms and three clauses open.

The Higgs four-sphere.** The square of the Higgs-to-$Z$ mass ratio is about $1+\cos\theta_W$; the sombrero replaced by a dual-factor potential on a four-sphere valued in latitude, the Higgs mass at $a = w/2$, with the normalization a fundamental constant causing the $Z$ mass rather than set by it; the factors resembling the leptons' $A^\pm$; and the four-sphere's likeness to the middle space's. *Made into:* Part XXIV — the perfect square and its curvature, the completion of Part XXIII's algebra to $SO(5)/SO(4)$ up to a sign, $Y = +1$ derived, the Higgs as the selector's dynamics with an exact VEV and spectrum, the latitude reading killed by $\kappa_V$ and the colatitude reading surviving with predictions, the factors a great-circle artifact, $\mu = M_Z$ a hypothesis, the spheres not identified. *Status:* one input replaced, one coincidence left as a clue.

Branch rendering spaces.** Branch rendering spaces atop the centrade nodes, large-spatially invisible and quantum-visible as Feynman-diagram complexity, with the Higgs sphere related to the branch space and the middle space reached by abstraction, as the spinorial precedent did. *Made into:* §XXIV.6 — deferred and formulated as a fibered configuration space with a multiplicity selecting the rendering, diagrams replaced by a defined multiplicity before they enter. *Status:* open.

**53. The squared-defect motif.** The structure $(\sin a-\sin b)^2$ recurs — found first in the Reissner–Nordström metric, concurrently in the lepton masses, then sought and found in the Higgs sector — with the Kerr–Newman $\Delta$ at extremality and zero spin reducing to it, an angle $m$ that vanishes at an alignment, the Ricci tensor invariant under $m$ so that $m$ is not charge but the interpolation to general Kerr–Newman, hyperbolic trigonometry possibly belonging, leptons linear and the Higgs quadratic in mass as Dirac against boson, and $m$ as a rendering-separation irreducibility that is, for the Higgs, the source of the Weinberg angle. *Made into:* §XXIV.8 — the full $\Delta/\ell^2 = (\sin x-\sin m)^2-d^2$ exactly, $m$ the centre of the horizon roots and $d$ their splitting; the Ricci tensor of Reissner–Nordström free of $M$, verified; Harrison charging as the hyperbolic partner; the lepton law as the same squared difference; the dimensionless defect with representation-dependent readouts; irreducibility as a principal angle between projectors; and the Weinberg angle shown to be exactly such an angle, fixing the theorem a derivation must prove. *Status:* the gravitational instance exact, the principle a hypothesis, the second test decisive.

**54. The defect under the theory's own equations.** Find how the Reissner–Nordström $\Delta$ behaves under the actual field-equation solution and the deviation from general relativity; let the antipodal symmetry make $d$ a function of cosines of $x$ and $m$; seek "no distinction between $r$ and $m$," with $m$ the areal radius of the ortho-middle space rather than the complex meridian direction; and read the Weinberg angle from it. *Made into:* §XXIV.9 — $m_{\rm ext}$ and the hidden $\mu$ kept separate; the root construction with the cosine in the nonextremality and the pure split norm too restrictive; the closed arena's zero-charge $\Delta$ exactly a sine-defect times a cosine-defect; the closure forcing extremal cylindrical ends with throat radius equal to charge and a charge bound; no exterior in the twin-symmetric electrovac ansatz, the mass closure required; the paired-resolution space with $Z^2$ descending; the Weinberg angle as the same operation, not the same number. *Status:* kinematics and the zero-charge deviation exact; the exterior solution open.

**55. The original defect and its three faces.** The factorized $\Delta$ as an alignment measure in which each antipode gets a say; the original expression $-Q^2\cos^2m\cos^2x+(Q-\sin m\sin x)^2$ with $q^2 = (Q^2+a^2)/M^2$; setting any one of $q,\sin m,\sin x$ to one giving the square of the difference of the other two; the standard rendering privileging $\sin x$ as radius and one amplitude as charge-maker, the other an external marker the Ricci tensor disregards or absorbs into a permittivity, with the Ricci flip as the experiment; and the Higgs dictionary. *Made into:* §XXIV.10 — the exact $S_3$ polynomial, three square faces, the two double-root faces as a role fork, the rapidity and Gram forms, the Fricke cubic with horizons as reducibility, Dictionary A killed and Dictionary B's finite-$\ell$ candidate derived with its roots, the $\rho$ fork, the zero-source split of the two $\Delta$'s with the candidate matching the lapse, the static Ricci flip, the covariant $\mathcal K_H$ rehabilitating the factors upstairs, and the two-level dictionary. *Status:* algebra verified; the closed charged solution and the trace realization were decisive — both later done, with negative verdicts on the scalar lapse and on Fricke as a mechanism (§§XXIV.22–24).

**56. The original normalization restored.** The original $-g_{tt} = 1/g_{rr} = \Delta/(\sin x\sin m)^2$ forces $q$ to bear the charge and blinds the Ricci tensor to $m$; whichever amplitude the normalization is against, the other arbitrates charge; the lost one is the ortho datum, so extremality is $\sin^2m = (Q^2+a^2)/M^2$, explaining $m\propto1/M$; $m$ the neutrino leg's areal ratio with its own scale, $q$ the communicator; check against Law I with the small-radius limit correct; and read the hiding of $m$ for how the ortho space and neutrino charge are hidden. *Made into:* §XXIV.11 — the restored dictionary $u = A/\ell$, $v = A/M$, $w = R/\ell$ giving the same candidate, the normalization theorem, $m = \pi/2$ as conventional extremality; the candidate's exact Einstein tensor (Maxwell plus a solid-angle excess) against Law I's dust closure, the closure living in $g_{RR}$ with $N = 1$, so the candidate is a lapse only and its constant a reparameterization until the lapse equation fixes time; the small-radius limit verified; $m_\nu$ typed as the ortho leg's ratio with three angles kept apart; and the general hiding principle. *Status:* checked where checkable; the lapse equation decisive.

**57. Equal footing for the ortho-middle space.** If the ortho space is on equal footing, the Hopf fibers' clean response to the gravity-base stress tensor may be an idealization exact at small $\sin^2m$; generalize the laws to recover the Hopf form there, be invariant in the ortho arena, and close the gap from pretty algebra to a deeper application. *Made into:* §XXIV.12 — Law I unchanged on one base, the scalar locking as the $\chi\to0$ projection of an exchange-covariant two-plane lift, the toy lift exactly covariant, the participation $\chi$ kept distinct from the discrete selector, the determinant denominator $\det(w^2P_\ell+v^2P_\nu) = v^2w^2$, and the lapse as a ratio of determinants as the theorem target. *Status:* architecture typed; the lift law from an action open.

**58. The Law I derivation pushed.** *Made into:* §XXIV.12 — the barren-twin compact Gauss configuration with local Reissner–Nordström and no duplicated energy; the Bianchi theorem for the closure; the integrated constraint and the nonexistence of a regular charged exterior with uniform closure; the first finite-$\ell$ lapse correction in two closure models; "hidden" split three ways, twin and ortho kept apart, descent as factorization. *Status:* the candidate reduced to one unknown function, the closure's response.

Flux invariants in place of polar sines.** Replace the areal-radius sines by coordinate-invariant electromagnetic flux scalars along each meridian direction for the two angles and along the remaining tangent directions for $q$. *Made into:* §XXIV.13 — flux alone measures charge, flux with field strength reconstructs the radius exactly in Reissner–Nordström and the complex principal radius $r-ia\cos\theta$ in Kerr–Newman, computed; the firewall against electric flux along the meridian; rendering-relative invariants with the canonical directions as frame; the paired radial operator from a response operator; and the neutral limit resolved by the field calibrating a fundamental radial response rather than defining it. *Status:* reconstruction verified; the response operators open.

**60. The isotropic idealization.** The $(q,\sin m_\nu,\sin x)$ construction as the isotropic idealization of the actual field-equation solutions, something rigid to riff off for the total ontology. *Made into:* §XXIV.13 — the standing of the whole branch: operators $\mathbb U,\mathbb V,\mathbb W$ which, in the neutral spherical sector, are jointly diagonalized by charge superselection, $\mathfrak D$ the maximally symmetric shadow, $N^2 = \det(\mathbb H^{-1}_{\rm rad}\mathbb K)$ in general and the sine formula only in the spherical sector, the Higgs analogy protected as a shared kind of reduction. *Status:* adopted as the branch's standing; the operators are the derivation's object.

**61. **A method, not an intuition: stay conservative.** Where a choice is not forced, keep the smaller assumption — an ordinary one-form photon, a twin empty of matter, an isotropic galaxy profile — until the evidence decides.

## 0.1 The four layers

Earlier versions had three layers and conflated two of them. Version 15 has four.

| layer | symbol | what it is | $\dim_\mathbb{R}$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--:|
| **canonical space** | $E$ | the axiom. A semi-free circle space — a principal circle bundle on its regular stratum $E^\circ$, the circle collapsing on restored meridians (§II.2) — whose restriction to every source shell is the compact real form of the complex spin lift | 6 |
| **middle space** | $\mathcal{M} = E/U(1)_H$ | **derived** by forgetting spin phase; **physical matter/stress-energy inhabit this five-dimensional space** | 5 |
| **representational base** | $B_{\rm rep}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{M}$ | embedded Lorentzian bisection: a **selected localization/readout** of matter, light and detectors, not the exhaustive matter support | 4 |
| **gravity base** | $B_{\rm grav} = \mathcal{M}/U_{\rm mer}$ | four-dimensional meridian quotient: **effective Einstein constraint and reduced source**, not the fundamental matter arena | 4 |

**Static spatial slices.** In the static regime used throughout Part IV, $B_{\rm grav}^{\rm static}\simeq\mathbb{R}_t\times\Sigma_{\rm grav}$ and $B_{\rm rep}^{\rm static}\simeq\mathbb{R}_t\times\Sigma_{\rm rep}$, with

$$\Sigma_{\rm grav}\equiv\mathbb{RP}^3(\ell),\qquad\Sigma_{\rm rep}\equiv S^3(\ell),\qquad\pi:\Sigma_{\rm rep}\to\Sigma_{\rm grav}$$

the antipodal double cover. $B_{\rm grav}$ and $B_{\rm rep}$ always mean the four-dimensional bases; statements about the static operator, its Green's functions and integrated masses refer to the slices.

The two bases have the same dimension and arise by opposite operations:

$$B_{\rm rep} = \text{a resolved representative},\qquad B_{\rm grav} = \text{an equivalence class}$$

Conflating the two bases, and then treating the two bisection crossings as the entire physical meridian, obscured the intended ontology. The bisection concerns a **rendering**, while the gravitational fiber reduction concerns **all of $\mathcal M$**.

## 0.2 Terms

| term | meaning |
|:--|:--|
| **shell** | the set of points at fixed nonzero distance from a source worldline, within its normal space |
| **complex shell** $\Sigma^\mathbb{C}_{\gamma,R}$ | the same at fixed *complex* radius about a *complex* worldline: an affine quadric, a complex surface |
| **spin phase** $U(1)_H$ | the compact fiber of the shell lift; the physical real form of the complex stabilizer $\mathbb{C}^\times$ |
| **meridian** | a leaf of the one-dimensional **meridian structure** $U_{\rm mer}$. *Standard usage in this document:* $U_{\rm mer}$ is a **meridian structure**; its **regular part** is a foliation; its **static singular case** is a **pencil**, since distinct meridians meet at the poles. In the static limit a leaf is a great circle of $S^4$ through both poles |
| **twin** | for $x\in B_{\rm rep}$, the other bisection crossing $\tau x$ on the same complete meridian; this pair does **not** exhaust the meridian fiber |
| **barren twin** | a representational crossing with no localized resolved matter/readout but with gravitational geometry induced by the **full meridian class**; it does not imply that the rest of the middle-space fiber is empty |
| **$T_\pm$** | $T(x)\pm T(\tau x)$ only for **resolved bisection data**; these combinations alone do not determine the full middle-space gravitational source |
| **jellium** | the uniform closure source required by the static solution; its microscopic or geometric origin is open (§XI.2, item 0′) |
| **primary** | the dominant mass at a degeneracy of the meridian structure |
| **conformal factor** | $\phi$, with $g_3 = \phi^4g_{\rm ref}$ and $\Omega\equiv\phi^2$ |
| **fiber length** $L_H$ | the circumference the canonical metric assigns the $U(1)_H$ orbit |

## 0.3 The tower

$$E^{(6)}\ \xrightarrow{\ /\,U(1)_H\ }\ \mathcal{M}^{(5)}\ \xrightarrow{\ /\,U_{\rm mer}\ }\ B_{\rm grav}^{(4)},\qquad B_{\rm rep}^{(4)}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{M}^{(5)}$$

Verified consistent: a circle quotient drops one dimension, a one-dimensional meridian quotient drops one more, and an embedded hypersurface of a five-manifold is four-dimensional **[V]**. Two distinct losses of information occur, and they must not be confused:

| quotient | what is forgotten |
|:--|:--|
| $E\to\mathcal{M}$ | the **spin phase** |
| $\mathcal{M}\to B_{\rm grav}$ | **where along the meridian** the matter sits |

**Source versus quotient [v34.0].** The second quotient erases **where anywhere along the full meridian fiber** physical matter and relational structure occur, not merely which antipodal bisection representative is populated. Distinct bulk configurations can give the same base source. Conversely, restricting to $B_{\rm rep}$ and then summing at two crossings is a separate, strong *support assumption* and is not entailed by the topology. See corrected Law I (§III) and §XXIX.8.

## 0.4 What is axiomatic

The primitive data are $\big(E,\ \hat g,\ U(1)_H,\ \mathcal{A}_H,\ \rho_E,\ \widehat{\mathcal{U} }_{\rm mer}\big)$ — **all living on $E$**: the canonical space, its metric, the fiber action, its connection, the real-analytic structure needed to complexify shells, and an upstairs meridian datum.

That last is a rank-one structure $\widehat{\mathcal{U} }_{\rm mer}\subset TE$, regular away from the preimage of a controlled singular set, which is (i) **$U(1)_H$-invariant**, $(R_\theta)_*\widehat{\mathcal{U} }_{\rm mer} = \widehat{\mathcal{U} }_{\rm mer}$, and (ii) **transverse to the fibers**, $\widehat{\mathcal{U} }_{\rm mer}\cap\ker d\pi_H = 0$. Invariance makes its image independent of the point chosen on each fiber; transversality keeps that image rank one. So it is projectable, and the middle space's meridian structure is *defined* as the image:

$$\mathcal{U}_{\rm mer} = d\pi_H\big(\widehat{\mathcal{U} }_{\rm mer}\big)$$

Everything else — the middle space, its meridian structure, both bases, the seed — then genuinely **descends**:

$$E\ \Longrightarrow\ (\mathcal{M},\ \mathcal{U}_{\rm mer})\ \Longrightarrow\ B_{\rm grav}$$

**The theory is top-down**, functorially and not just rhetorically. *(A previous revision listed $\mathcal{U}_{\rm mer}$ itself among the primitives while calling it "the meridian structure of the quotient" — one layer too low, since the quotient is not primitive.)*

**The real structure $\rho_E$, defined [S/T].** $E$ is real-analytic, so it sits inside a complexification $E_\mathbb{C}$, carrying an **antiholomorphic involution**

$$\rho_E:E_\mathbb{C}\to E_\mathbb{C},\qquad\rho_E^2 = 1,\qquad E = \operatorname{Fix}(\rho_E)$$

For reality to descend through the tower, $\rho_E$ must satisfy two compatibilities. **With the fiber:** writing $\mathbb{C}^\times$ for the complexified fiber group, $\rho_E(\lambda\cdot x) = \bar\lambda^{-1}\cdot\rho_E(x)$. The map $\lambda\mapsto\bar\lambda^{-1}$ fixes exactly $|\lambda| = 1$ **[V]**, so the compact $U(1)_H$ — and nothing larger — preserves $E$: the physical real form of §I.4, stated as a condition rather than observed. **With the meridian datum:** $d\rho_E$ preserves the complexification of $\widehat{\mathcal{U} }_{\rm mer}$, so its real part is what descends. *This version adopts the real-first reading: $E$ with its real-analytic structure is primitive, and $(E_\mathbb{C},\rho_E)$ is a complexification of it, with $E = \operatorname{Fix}\rho_E$. That complexification is canonical — unique up to isomorphism — only as a germ along $E$; a global complexification can exist, but requires further global choices. The complex-first reading, with $(E_\mathbb{C},\rho_E)$ primitive, remains available, and the global-$E$ problem (§XI.2, item 1) includes whether a global $E_\mathbb{C}$ can be chosen compatibly with the fiber and the meridian datum.* **[O]**.

*What the upstairs datum carries [T].* Lifts of a given line field downstairs are not unique: two lifts differ by a $U(1)_H$-invariant vertical component, which projects to zero. The lift horizontal with respect to $\mathcal{A}_H$ is canonical, and choosing it adds nothing beyond the connection already present.

# PART I — THE COMPLEX SHELL AND ITS SPIN LIFT

*This part supplies the fiber. It is the version's substantive addition, and it is the reason the Hopf structure is no longer an assumption.*

## I.1 The complex worldline and its normal space [T/S]

Let $\Gamma_\mathbb{C} = \{\gamma(\tau)\}$ be the analytic complex worldline of a source, with non-null tangent, $g_\mathbb{C}(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)\neq0$. At each $\gamma(\tau)$ the **complex normal space** is

$$N_\gamma = \{\xi : g_\mathbb{C}(\xi,\dot\gamma) = 0\}$$

complex three-dimensional — the complexification of the ordinary spatial rest space about a real timelike worldline.

*v34.1 (R73).* This is the normal space of a worldline in a **four**-dimensional (complexified) spacetime, whose small spatial link is $S^2$ and whose Hopf lift is the content of §§I.2–I.6. Under the v34.0 ontology, a timelike worldline in a nondegenerate **five**-dimensional matter geometry has a four-dimensional real normal space with link $S^3$; a linking $S^2$ fits instead a codimension-three object — a timelike worldsheet generated by a spatial meridian, or a three-dimensional horizontal rest space after a specified reduction. The document must say which object the shell is attached to: a shell in the gravitational or representational four-geometry, a transverse link to a source worldsheet in $\mathcal M$, or a selected three-dimensional normal structure supplied by the parent data. The local construction stands; its universal applicability to a full middle-space source is an additional theorem target (§XXIX.15).

## I.2 A complex shell is an affine quadric [T]

A shell of nonzero complex squared radius $R^2$ is

$$\Sigma^\mathbb{C}_{\gamma,R} = \{\xi\in N_\gamma : g_\mathbb{C}(\xi,\xi) = R^2\}$$

Choosing an orthonormal complex frame and rescaling,

$$\Sigma^\mathbb{C}_{\gamma,R}\ \cong\ Q^2_{\rm aff} = \{(z_1,z_2,z_3)\in\mathbb{C}^3 : z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2 = 1\}$$

**a complex surface, not a real 2-sphere.** Its symmetry group is the complex rotation group $SO(3,\mathbb{C})$, whose spin double cover is $Spin(3,\mathbb{C})\cong SL(2,\mathbb{C})$.

## I.3 The complex Hopf lift [T/V]

$SO(3,\mathbb{C})$ acts **transitively** on the affine quadric — any non-null vector of given norm rotates to any other — with stabilizer the complex torus $SO(2,\mathbb{C}) = \mathbb{C}^\times$. Lifting to the double cover:

$$\boxed{\ \mathbb{C}^\times\ \hookrightarrow\ SL(2,\mathbb{C})\ \twoheadrightarrow\ Q^2_{\rm aff}\cong SL(2,\mathbb{C})/\mathbb{C}^\times\ }$$

Checked by dimension: $\dim_\mathbb{R}SL(2,\mathbb{C}) - \dim_\mathbb{R}\mathbb{C}^\times = 6-2 = 4 = \dim_\mathbb{R}Q^2_{\rm aff}$ **[V]**.

**This is the complex Hopf shell.** The old Hopfian character survives complexification not by pretending the complex shell is still a 2-sphere, but by complexifying the *homogeneous-space relation itself*.

## I.4 The physical real form is exactly the Hopf fibration [T/V]

For a timelike source on the Lorentzian real slice, the normal rest space is ordinary Euclidean three-space, and each piece passes to its compact real form:

| complex | real | check |
|:--|:--|:--|
| $Q^2_{\rm aff}$ | $S^2$ | $z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2 = 1$ with $z$ real *is* the unit 2-sphere |
| $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ | $SU(2)\simeq S^3$ | maximal compact subgroup |
| $\mathbb{C}^\times$ | $U(1)$ | maximal compact subgroup |

$$\boxed{\ U(1)\ \hookrightarrow\ SU(2)\simeq S^3\ \twoheadrightarrow\ S^2\ }$$

with $3-1 = 2 = \dim S^2$ **[V]**. So the earlier versions' assertion — *every spherical shell lifts to a Hopf 3-sphere* — is **recovered as the physical real form** of the complex statement, rather than imposed before complexification.

## I.5 Why this is isotropic [T/D]

The shell is defined by the invariant condition $g_\mathbb{C}(\xi,\xi) = R^2$ alone. The rotation group acts transitively on it, so no angular direction is preferred; and the lift $SL(2,\mathbb{C})\to SL(2,\mathbb{C})/\mathbb{C}^\times$ is likewise homogeneous. **The fiber is not attached by choosing a longitude. It is the stabilizer of the spin-group action.** On the real form, $SU(2)\to SU(2)/U(1)\simeq S^2$ is equally isotropic under ordinary rotations — which is the precise sense in which the magnetic/isotropic motivation of the original picture is preserved.

## I.6 The shell fiber acts as the spinor phase [T/V]

*Noting that the same group appears twice would be a coincidence-of-names argument. The identification can be made explicit, and it is an equality of **actions**, not of group labels.*

$SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ is already the spin group of four-dimensional Lorentzian two-spinor geometry — the group under which Newman–Penrose spinors transform. The question is whether the $U(1)$ that the shell quotients is the *same* circle as the spinor's phase. It is.

**The construction.** Identify a normalized spinor $\psi = (z_1,z_2)^{\mathsf T}\in S^3\subset\mathbb{C}^2$ with the group element

$$U(\psi) = \begin{pmatrix} z_1 & -\bar z_2\\ z_2 & \bar z_1\end{pmatrix}\ \in\ SU(2)$$

which is unitary with unit determinant precisely because $|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2 = 1$ **[V]**. Now act on the right by the diagonal stabilizer

$$h_\theta = \begin{pmatrix} e^{i\theta} & 0\\ 0 & e^{-i\theta}\end{pmatrix}$$

The first column of $U(\psi)h_\theta$ is $e^{i\theta}\psi$ **[V]**.

> **Given the timelike direction $u$ that defines the physical rest-space shell and its $SU(2)$ stabilizer, the shell's $U(1)$ stabilizer acts on a normalized spinor as ordinary spinor phase.** Not the same group twice — *the same action*.

> **Which action this is [T].** The phase arises through the Hopf bundle's principal *right* action. Under the identification $SU(2)\simeq S^3$ of group elements with normalized spinor representatives, right multiplication by $h_\theta$ coincides exactly with overall phase multiplication of the spinor. It is not the spin group's *left* action, through which spinors transform under rotations and boosts — and the scalar $e^{i\theta}I$ lies in $SU(2)$ only for $e^{i\theta} = \pm1$. What is identified is the principal fiber action with the spinor's overall phase, not the fiber with a subgroup of the spin representation.

**Relative to what [T/V].** The qualifier is not decorative. $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ does not preserve $|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2$: the boost $\operatorname{diag}(e^{\eta/2},e^{-\eta/2})$ takes the unit spinor $\psi = (0,1)$ to norm $e^{-\eta/2}$ — $0.670$ at $\eta = 0.8$ — while $SU(2)$ keeps every unit spinor at $1$ **[V]**. (For unit $\psi$ the boosted norm ranges over $[e^{-\eta/2},e^{\eta/2}]$.) The positive-definite spinor norm is $u_{AA'}\psi^A\bar\psi^{A'}$ and needs a timelike $u$; $SU(2)$ is exactly its stabilizer. So "normalized," "$S^3\subset\mathbb{C}^2$" and "phase" are all defined relative to $u$ — **the same $u$ whose stabilizer is the diagonal $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ of §XI.3.** Stated this way §I.6 and §XI.3 are one fact seen twice, rather than an observer-independent claim sitting beside an observer-dependent one.

**And the Hopf map is the quotient by exactly that action [V].** With $n(\psi) = \big(2\,\mathrm{Re}(z_1\bar z_2),\,2\,\mathrm{Im}(z_1\bar z_2),\,|z_1|^2-|z_2|^2\big)$, one has $n(e^{i\theta}\psi) = n(\psi)$ identically — verified. So the shell $S^2$ is the space of spinors modulo phase, and the fiber is the phase.

**The complex version is the same statement [V].** $h_\lambda = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda,\lambda^{-1})\in SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ scales the first column by $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ — verified. So the complex stabilizer is complex phase-and-scale on the spinor, and the compact real form recovers pure phase.

**This is the "not bolted on" claim, discharged.** Every earlier version had to *posit* a circle. Here the circle is the spinor phase of a group the theory already contains, acting in the way it already acts.

## I.7 What the complex shell is **not** [T]

At a point of complexified four-dimensional spacetime, the projectivized complex null cone is a different object — a projective quadric built from two independent chiral spinors, natural for **null directions**. The shell used here represents **fixed nonzero radius in the complexified rest space of a non-null worldline**. These must not be conflated:

$$\text{null-direction quadric}\ \neq\ \text{fixed-radius worldline shell}$$

The affine quadric is preferred because its three pieces complexify *together* and its real limits are exactly the three wanted (§I.4). The projective version does not have the $S^2$ limit for a source shell.

# PART II — THE CANONICAL SPACE AND THE TWO BASES

## II.1 Law 0 [S/O]

> ### ◆ LAW 0 — THE CANONICAL SPACE
> There exists a canonical space $E$ such that: (i) its quotient by the compact fiber action is the middle space, $\mathcal{M} = E/U(1)_H$, the action being semi-free and principal on the regular stratum $E^\circ$ (§II.2); (ii) near a source worldline, its analytic continuation restricted to every nonzero-radius complex shell is the homogeneous bundle $\mathbb{C}^\times\to SL(2,\mathbb{C})\to Q^2_{\rm aff}$; (iii) on the physical rest-space shell this reduces to $U(1)\to SU(2)\to S^2$; (iv) the fiber carries a connection $\mathcal{A}_H$; (v) the metric $\hat g$ gives the compact fiber a length $L_H$.

**Two obstructions, and the second is the real problem.**

**(a) The cohomological one [V].** Condition (iii) cannot hold over an *unpunctured* static middle space: $H^2(S^4) = 0$, so every circle bundle over $\mathbb{R}_t\times S^4$ is trivial, and a trivial bundle restricts to $S^2\times S^1$ on each shell — **not** $S^3$. The Hopf lift needs a nontrivial class on the shell, which needs the secondary meridians removed. What the argument requires is precisely the **cohomological** statement, and no more: by Alexander duality,

$$H^2\big(S^4\setminus S^1;\mathbb{Z}\big)\ \cong\ \tilde H_1(S^1;\mathbb{Z})\ \cong\ \mathbb{Z}$$

which permits a nontrivial circle bundle **[T]**. More is true, though not needed: smooth circles in $S^4$ are **unknotted** — homotopic embeddings of an $n$-manifold in an $m$-manifold are isotopic once $m\geq2n+2$, here $4\geq4$, and $\pi_1(S^4) = 0$ makes every circle homotopic to every other. Since $S^4 = (S^1\times D^3)\cup_{S^1\times S^2}(D^2\times S^2)$, the complement of a tubular neighbourhood is $D^2\times S^2\simeq S^2$ **[T]**. *A previous revision of this section claimed smooth 1-knots in $S^4$ exist and treated the homotopy statement as an embedding debt. That was wrong and is retired (§XI.1); knotting in $S^4$ begins with embedded 2-spheres.* Alexander duality nonetheless remains all the argument uses.

**With $N$ secondaries the removed set is a graph [T].** In the static pencil every meridian passes through both poles, so $\Gamma$ has two vertices and $2N$ arcs, and

$$H^2\big(S^4\setminus\Gamma;\mathbb{Z}\big)\cong\tilde H_1(\Gamma;\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}^{2N-1}$$

— one integer per arc, less one relation. That relation forces the Hopf classes at all crossings to sum to zero — a pairing for a single meridian, one global constraint for several (§V.4). **Law 0 must therefore be stated over $\mathcal{M}$ minus the secondary meridians**; the architecture inherits that surgery rather than escaping it.

**(b) The global one, which is now the main construction problem [O].** Part I builds its shell on the **normal space** $N_\gamma$ — a space of *vectors*, not of spacetime points. Passing from normal vectors to nearby points of the middle space uses the exponential map, and that identification is **local**: curvature, cut loci and caustics obstruct it globally. So even granting (a), it does not follow that **one** global six-dimensional $E$ restricts to the unit Hopf bundle around **every** source worldline simultaneously.

> **That is the version's central open construction**, and it is a sharper problem than the ones it replaces. The local spin geometry of Part I is settled mathematics; whether it glues is not.

## II.2 The middle space is derived [D]

$$\mathcal{M} = E/U(1)_H$$

*Stated precisely: the circle action is free only on the regular locus, $U(1)_H\hookrightarrow E^\circ\to\mathcal M^\circ = \mathcal M\setminus\Gamma$, because the nontrivial circle bundle cannot extend over the removed meridians (§II.1). $E$ is a stratified completion of $E^\circ$ over $\Gamma$, and the quotient above holds in that stratified sense; without the completion, $E/U(1)_H$ is $\mathcal M^\circ$ and not all of $\mathcal M$.*

> **A local model of the completion [V/T], new in 17.3.** Near one meridian, take $E_{\rm loc} = \mathbb R_t\times S^1_{\rm mer}\times\mathbb C^2$, with the diagonal circle action $e^{i\theta}\cdot(z_1,z_2) = (e^{i\theta}z_1,e^{i\theta}z_2)$. The action is *semi-free*: free away from $z = 0$, while the whole circle fixes $z = 0$. The map $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto\big(2z_1\bar z_2,\,|z_1|^2-|z_2|^2\big)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R\cong\mathbb R^3$ is invariant, satisfies $|\pi(z)| = |z|^2$, and identifies $\mathbb C^2/U(1)$ with the cone on $S^3/U(1) = S^2$ — that is, with $\mathbb R^3$, the fixed point going to the origin. So $E_{\rm loc}$ is a smooth six-manifold whose quotient is topologically $\mathbb R_t\times S^1_{\rm mer}\times\mathbb R^3$: five-dimensional, with the meridian **restored rather than removed**. On every small sphere linking the meridian the circle bundle is the Hopf bundle, with Chern number exactly $1$, so Structure III's unit class is *produced* by the local model rather than postulated. Topologically and smoothly, nothing is singular in $E$; *metrically*, see the next box. What remains open is gluing these local models into a global $E$, including at the poles, where several meridians meet **[O]**. *(v34.1, R74.)* A constraint on that gluing: the fixed-point set of a smooth compact-group action is a disjoint union of smooth submanifolds. If a global circle action on $E$ is semi-free, the locus where its orbits collapse is its fixed-point set, so distinct branches of that locus cannot meet as the vertex of a graph, and distinct fixed points remain distinct orbits in the quotient. Several meridians meeting at a common pole are therefore incompatible with an **unchanged smooth global semi-free action** having exactly that fixed locus; a stratified canonical space, a resolved source locus or different singularity data is required there (§XXII.12, §XXIX.10). The local model shows the local completion is smooth; it is not evidence that the global one is.

> **What the completion does to the fiber's length [V/D], new in 17.6.** The circle's generator, $X_H(z) = (iz_1,iz_2)$, vanishes on the restored meridian, so for any smooth nondegenerate metric on $E$ the orbit collapses there: $L_H = O(|z|) = O(\sqrt\rho)$, exactly $2\pi\sqrt\rho$ for the flat metric. The fiber-length locking of §III.2 instead *grows* toward a source, $L_H = \Omega L_H^{\rm ref}$ with $\Omega = (1+GM_{\rm grav}/2r)^2$. The same orbit cannot do both. The smooth example is known: at the nut of self-dual Taub–NUT the circle shrinks as $\sqrt r$ while the base factor grows, and the space is flat $\mathbb R^4$ there — the *reciprocal* warping already recorded as Obstruction 1 of §XI.3, now forced into the core by smoothness. So three things the architecture had run together must be kept apart: **the topological existence of the circle orbit, the metric size assigned to a regular orbit, and the behaviour of an orbit that collapses on an exceptional stratum.** The locking $L_H = \mathcal F[g_G]$ is therefore a law on the regular stratum $E^\circ$, and its behaviour approaching a restored meridian must be derived from whatever metric completes $E^\circ$ — a collapse core, as in Taub–NUT, or a metric on $E$ singular there. Likewise a principal connection satisfies $\mathcal A_H(X_H) = 1$, which cannot hold where $X_H = 0$: $\mathcal A_H$ lives on $E^\circ$, and Structure III's Chern class belongs on linking spheres in the regular complement.

Nothing in this version may treat $\mathcal{M}$ as more fundamental than $E$. The quotient discards the spin phase while retaining the meridian-completed localization geometry. **This is the first loss of information in the tower.**

## II.3 The representational base is a bisection, not a section [S/O]

$B_{\rm rep}$ is an embedded Lorentzian bisection $\iota:B_{\rm rep}\hookrightarrow\mathcal M$ on which a **selected representation** localizes matter interactions and electromagnetic/detector readouts. Physical matter and stress-energy, prior to rendering, inhabit $\mathcal M$; the bisection is **not** a completeness statement about their support. The detailed bulk-to-readout map, including Maxwell localization and Newman–Janis realization, remains open.

In the old static picture, the equatorial $S^3$ met each meridian at **two** points, $\hat n$ and $-\hat n$. The general statement is

$$L_b\cap B_{\rm rep} = \{x,\ \tau x\},\qquad \tau^2 = 1,\qquad q(x) = q(\tau x) = b$$

Thus $B_{\rm rep}$ is a **bisection**: two *readout crossings* of a full gravity fiber. The second crossing may be representationally barren while the full meridian still carries bulk matter. The two-crossing property establishes the topology of the selected readout, not a fundamental two-point physical source law.

## II.4 The gravity base is a quotient [S]

$$B_{\rm grav} = \mathcal{M}/U_{\rm mer}$$

Gravity forgets the position of source content **anywhere along** $q^{-1}(b)$; it reads the covariantly reduced source of the entire meridian class. That class contains more than the two bisection crossings. A quotient alone supplies no physical measure or conservation law; these must come from the parent matter and reduction dynamics.

*v34.1 (R56).* The displayed equation is a **target**, not a construction. Where $U_{\rm mer}$ is the static great-circle pencil the circles share the poles and are not disjoint, so they are not the fibers of a map on $S^4$; on the regular stratum $S^4\setminus\{\pm p\}\simeq(0,\pi)\times S^3$ the connected leaves are indexed by $S^3$, the map to $\mathbb{RP}^3$ has two open arcs per fiber and adds the pairing $n\sim-n$, and a space with genuine complete fibers exists only after a resolution of the poles (§XXIX.10). Three names are used from here on: the *connected meridian foliation* of the regular stratum, the *regular $\mathbb{RP}^3$ reduction* (foliation plus pairing), and a *resolved space* with disjoint complete fibers. "$B_{\rm grav}=\mathcal M/U_{\rm mer}$" means the third once it is built.
