# PART XIV — MODULAR RETURN OPTICS AND THE GALACTIC WELL: THE VERSION-19 BRANCH [T/V/D/S/O]

*This part is deliberately ambitious and deliberately provisional. It asks whether the full-sky antipodal family of the galactic arena, broken by secondary structure into a countable set of stable recurrent photon-history classes, could be rendered as finite galaxy images with a unitary multiplicative redshift $1+z = e^\eta$ — the same $\eta$ giving the observed time dilation and an apparent Hubble law — and whether the Milky Way's own well could set the scale of that dilation. Nothing here is established. Parts 0–XIII are unchanged by it; standard quantum mechanics is retained; the Jacobi gate of §XIII.10 is the opening condition; the full secondary-inclusive optical metric is used throughout; and every mechanism begins as [S/O] unless it is actually derived. The branch's job is to find out whether the idea can be made coherent while keeping the empirical meaning of astronomical redshift — and to fail cleanly if it cannot.*

## XIV.0 The ambition and its firewall [D]

**The hypothesis.** What an observer calls an external galaxy may be a rendered, recurrent photon-history object of the single galactic arena — a two-path history returning through the twin structure — rather than a second gravitational arena at a literal cosmological distance.

**The non-negotiable target.** The branch must reproduce an apparent Hubble law in *actually observed* redshift: one multiplicative shift of every spectral line, $(1+z)$ time dilation of transients, the measured behaviour of angular-diameter and luminosity distances, Tolman-like surface-brightness dimming, and ordinary foreground lensing. A relation that merely correlates image size or interference phase with an invented distance is not enough.

**The firewall inherited from §XIII.10.** Canonical position cannot be visual position for returning light: the Sun's own light would return at the solar constant. So a rendered return must be registered at whatever flux the observable map assigns — smaller than naive return by a factor of order $(D_{\rm app}/\ell)^2$, $10^7$ to $10^{11}$, *conditionally*, since that presupposes $D_{\rm app}$ acting as a luminosity distance, which the branch has not yet derived — and the observer's own return must lie in the readout kernel by an invariant, not by fiat. The brightness budget of §XIV.8 needs no such assumption. That is the price of admission, paid before any return map is built.

> **Three layers, never merged [D].** *Canonical refocusing* — where a returning family converges on the arena — is not *visual image location* — where the readout places it — and neither is *source identity*. The branch's claim is not that the Sun's photons circle the arena and one return is called Andromeda. It is that global conjugate geometry creates recurrent history freedom; collective secondary structure breaks and selects it; stable recurrent classes result; and the readout assigns sky position, morphology, flux and $z$. The self-return test is then a tool rather than a verdict: **what invariant distinguishes a recurrent class that renders as an external galaxy from the self-return class that must lie in the readout kernel?** Found without "do not render the Sun" put in by hand, it would be real progress; not found, the objection returns with full force.

## XIV.1 The round antipodal family, and what breaks it [T/V]

On the round $S^3(\ell)$ the first conjugate traversal, $L_1 = \pi\ell$, is reached by a whole two-parameter family of great circles, the critical manifold $\mathcal C_1\simeq S^2$, on which the optical action is constant — the self-image problem in its sharpest form (§XIII.10). The branch's first mechanism is standard perturbation theory of a Morse–Bott critical manifold: turn on the actual arena perturbation, $g_{\rm opt} = g_{\rm round}+\epsilon\,\delta g$, and restrict the action to the family,

$$S_{\rm eff}(\Omega) = S_0+\epsilon V(\Omega)+O(\epsilon^2)$$

whose stationary members, $\nabla_\Omega V(\Omega_\ast) = 0$, are the candidates for isolated recurrent histories. The secondaries do not open the family — the round geometry does that — they carve it.

**Computed [V].** With $V(\Omega) = 2GM\int ds/r(s)$ along each great circle, the first-order optical length of a weak secondary: one secondary leaves a *degenerate ring* of minima, by the axial symmetry of a single point mass about the source–antipode axis; several break the family into isolated members, **about two per secondary** — a sharp maximum for the circle passing through the mass, and a saddle between. That is a property of the sum's singular structure: each star's $1/r$ diverges on the ray through it whatever the other stars do, and the saddles follow by the Euler characteristic — with one hygiene condition: the $1/r$ perturbation is singular on the ray through each point mass, so the count was made with every secondary softened to a smooth potential of finite core, $1/\sqrt{r^2+\epsilon^2}$, on which compact Morse theory applies; strict point masses would need the singular directions excised and the boundary accounted for, and the conclusion that the degeneracy breaks does not depend on it. It is **not a galaxy count** — galaxy counts themselves run from $10^{11}$ to $10^{12}$ depending on which faint systems are included — and the maxima are rays through the stars, absorbed rather than imaged. The right object is the return map's periodic orbits, below; the first-order count shows only that the degeneracy does break.

## XIV.2 The return map and modular classes [S/O]

Homotopy cannot supply a catalogue: $\pi_1(S^3) = 0$ and $\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^3) = \mathbb Z_2$. The candidate object is a return map on the canonical photon-history state $\xi = (\Omega, J, D_\lambda J, \text{phase data}, \mu_{\rm opt},\ldots)$,

$$\mathscr P:\mathcal X_{\rm ph}\to\mathcal X_{\rm ph},\qquad \mathscr P^n(\xi)\sim\xi$$

where "one traversal" — source to twin, twin to source class, one projective half-circumference, one pass through the correspondence — is itself open, and $\sim$ means equality after exactly the identifications the readout legitimately forgets. For fixed period the recurrent set ${\rm Fix}_n(\mathscr P)$ is at most countable *if* the perturbed map is nondegenerate — hyperbolicity, twist, transversality, broken continuous symmetry — which must be shown, not assumed. An optional second integer, the phase closure $\Delta\Phi = 2\pi m$ of two legs, would give labels $(n,m)$. The stability matrix $M_n = D\mathscr P^n|_{\xi_\ast}$ classifies members as elliptic or hyperbolic and locates image *islands*: a finite apparent image would be the sky projection of a stable island or caustic patch, an extent achromatic to leading geometric-optics order — finite-source and wave effects can add wavelength dependence — rather than a stationary-phase width, which would carry a wavelength dependence real galaxies do not show. A meridian coordinate $\mu_{\rm opt}$ could enter as a morphology variable only through $\mu_{\rm opt}\mapsto M_n\mapsto$ caustic and shear class $\mapsto$ rendered morphology, never by declaration; it is not the charge rapidity $\mu$ of §X.0 unless derived to be.

## XIV.3 Apparent distance [S/O]

Gravitational separation is bounded, $0\le d_{\rm grav}\lesssim\pi\ell$; recurrent data are not: $n$, $m$, cumulative phase, holonomy and action. An apparent distance $D_{\rm app} = \mathcal D(n,m,\mu_{\rm opt},\Phi_{\rm hol},\Delta T,M_n,\ldots)$ built from them need not equal geodesic distance — the intended route to a compact gravitational arena with effectively noncompact optical distance. It must be universal, never tuned object by object.

## XIV.4 Two no-gos that shape the redshift [T/V]

**The static wall.** Identical source and twin wells have identical lapse, so ordinary gravitational redshift between them is zero (Part IV); path delay changes phase, enclosed area changes holonomy, and two-path interference makes frequency *fringes*, $\Delta\phi(\omega) = \omega\Delta T$ — none is a universal multiplicative shift of every line.

**The coboundary.** If a per-return increment were a difference of one scalar potential, $\rho(\xi) = f(\mathscr P\xi)-f(\xi)$, then on a period-$n$ orbit $\eta_n = f(\mathscr P^n\xi)-f(\xi) = 0$. In particular a dilation connection $\mathcal A_z = d\ln N$ gives $\oint d\ln N = 0$ on every closed orbit. So a nonzero closed-orbit redshift needs a non-exact structure: a genuine holonomy, a readout dilation not reducible to endpoint differences, or a larger clock structure. The galactic well may *source* a dilation law; it cannot enter as an endpoint potential difference.

## XIV.5 The spectral-dilation readout [T/S]

The least invasive candidate leaves quantum composition unchanged and puts redshift in the canonical-to-observed readout. With $\eta = \ln(1+z)$ the dilation

$$(U_\eta\psi)(\omega) = e^{\eta/2}\,\psi(e^\eta\omega)$$

is unitary on $L^2(\mathbb R_+,d\omega)$ **[T]** and sends a packet at $\omega_{\rm em}$ to $\omega_{\rm obs} = e^{-\eta}\omega_{\rm em}$, every feature shifted by the same factor, while its time-domain conjugate stretches transients by $e^\eta = 1+z$ — the requirement that tired-light mechanisms fail, and that a survey of 1,504 Type Ia supernovae meets with a time-dilation exponent of $1.003\pm0.005\pm0.010$. That is a design success, not yet a physical one: $\eta$ has still to be derived from the well and return geometry, and flux, $D_L$, $D_A$, surface brightness and lensing must come from the same map. Three readings of $\eta$ are kept apart and tried in order: a clock normalization between canonical and detector frequencies, in which no photon loses energy in transit; a larger unitary sector with which energy is exchanged; a modified optical Hamiltonian. Redshift is composed by $\eta_n(\xi) = \sum_{j<n}\rho(\mathscr P^j\xi)$, additive in $\eta$ and multiplicative in $1+z$; the dilation is noncompact, $\mathbb R_+$, and must not be identified with the compact $U(1)$ phase without derivation. A dilation connection with $\eta = \oint\mathcal A_z$ was the last resort, after existing canonical structures had been tried; version 20 adopts a specific one by decision — the relative connection of a Weyl pair whose mean is the metric geometry — and derives its scale character (Part XV).

## XIV.6 The galactic well as the dilation scale [V/D/S/O]

**The coincidence.** Dividing $M_{\rm gal}\sim cH_0\ell^2/G$ by $c^2\ell/G$ gives its conceptual form,

$$\frac{GM_{\rm gal} }{c^2\ell}\;\sim\;\frac{H_0\ell}{c}$$

the dimensionless depth of a galactic well on the arena scale against the dimensionless Hubble redshift of one arena radius. The speculative bridge: the number that measures the Galaxy's arena-scale gravitational strength may set the dilation accumulated by one recurrent traversal, with the Milky Way's well the universal dial and the individual recurrent state the position on the relation. In a first-traversal calibration, $D_{ {\rm app},1} = q_D\ell$, a well functional $\mathcal W = C_W\,GM_{\rm grav}/c^2\ell$ and $\eta_1 = \alpha\mathcal W$ give $M_{\rm gal} = \beta\,cH_{\rm app}\ell^2/G$ with $\beta = q_D/\alpha C_W$; the heuristic $q_D = \pi$, $\alpha = 1$, $C_W = 4\pi$ gives $\beta = 1/4$ — to be derived or rejected, never inserted. The arithmetic, with $M_{\rm gal} = 6\times10^{10}M_\odot$ and $H_0 = 70$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ **[V]**:

| arena radius $\ell$ | $cH_0\ell^2/G$ | $\beta_{\rm MW} = GM_{\rm gal}/cH_0\ell^2$ | where this radius comes from |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 7.0 kpc | $2.4\times10^{11}M_\odot$ | $1/4$ | the heuristic coefficient |
| 8 kpc | $3.1\times10^{11}M_\odot$ | $1/5$ | the Sun's Galactocentric distance, the addendum's proposal |
| 13 kpc | $8.3\times10^{11}M_\odot$ | $1/14$ | the isotropic profile's 220 km/s (§IV.8) |
| 16 kpc | $1.3\times10^{12}M_\odot$ | $1/21$ | the compact-source 220 km/s |
| 25 kpc | $3.1\times10^{12}M_\odot$ | $1/51$ | the detached wing's arena law, $\beta_{\rm BTFR}\approx1/49$ |

Since $\beta\propto\ell^{-2}$, "the coefficient" encodes the arena radius: a derived $\beta$ would be a radius-selection rule, $\ell = \sqrt{\Gamma GM_{\rm gal}/cH_{\rm app} }$ with $\Gamma = 1/\beta$. That is why the addendum's $\ell\approx8$ kpc is a **version-19 selection hypothesis**, not a result of Part IV, which puts the plateau at 13–16 kpc.

**The literal well, computed [V].** The addendum's functional is the hemisphere flux $\mathcal W_{\mathcal H} = \ell^{-1}\int_{\partial\mathcal H}*_h\,d\ln N$ through the equator separating the source's hemisphere from its twin's, evaluated on the arena's actual static solution — source, same-sign twin and compensating closure background, with $\ln N\simeq-2\,\delta\phi$ in the weak field. It **vanishes identically**: the lifted source is even under the antipodal map, so its potential is even about the equator and its normal derivative there is zero, for the compact source and for the Milky Way's profile alike. Gauss on the closed slice says the same — the source's hemisphere holds the source and exactly minus one half of the background, and the curvature term $3\int\delta\phi$ that remains is killed by the same symmetry. The addendum's first null test, "the hemisphere flux vanishes by symmetry", is met, and its most literal option — a source-centred hemisphere on the cover — fails. The natural alternative, the arena-scale well *depth* $2[\delta\phi({\rm centre})-\delta\phi({\rm equator})]$, is finite but **dominated by the galaxy's own central self-potential** $M/4h$: in units of $GM_{\rm grav}/c^2\ell$ it is $1.4$, $2.6$ and $3.3$ for the Milky Way's profile at $\ell = 8$, $13$ and $16$ kpc, and $26$ for a compact lump, with the twin and the background adding only $\pm0.3$. A universal Hubble calibration cannot be hypersensitive to baryonic packing, so this is not the dial either. What survives is a surface the branch has not yet defined: a history-dependent surface spanned by the two recurrent legs, or a meridian-selected region [O].

**The history-dependent functional, computed [T/V/D].** Three candidates were proposed for the surviving object — a Jacobi-weighted tidal integral along the pair, the curvature flux through the pair's ribbon, and the boost component of the Lorentz holonomy around the two-leg loop — and the arena decides among them.

*The boost holonomy.* In any static spacetime the curvature has no boost component on spatial surfaces: every $R^0{}_{ijk}$ vanishes, checked on isotropic Schwarzschild, so around a purely spatial loop the Lorentz holonomy is a pure rotation **[T/V]**. The two photon legs are null, and for their loop the boost part reduces at first order to the tidal integral along the ray contracted with the separation, $\eta^i\sim\int E^i{}_jJ^j\,ds$: the elegant candidate collapses onto the cheap one, and the static arena supplies no $SO(1,1)$ of its own. A derived rapidity would have to come from non-static structure — the fiber, the meridian, or time — all open.

*The Jacobi-weighted tidal integral,* $\mathcal W_J = \ell^2\int E_{JJ}|J|^2ds\big/\!\int|J|^2ds$, on the isotropic Milky Way profile: with the source at the Galaxy's centre it is sign-definite and isotropic, but only $0.04$–$0.07$ of the needed $H_0\ell/c$ — the log-enhanced $f$; from the Sun's position its magnitude swings twenty-fold with direction and its sign flips with the pair's orientation, because the tidal tensor is trace-free. It cannot give a redshift that is all one sign **[V]**.

*The null focusing column.* What the sign analysis leaves is the trace: the Ricci focusing a photon accumulates along its history, made affine-invariant with the conserved Killing energy of the static arena — $\mathcal E = -\xi\cdot k$, $\bar k = k/\mathcal E$, $d\bar\lambda = \mathcal E\,d\lambda$, which stays affine, unlike a normalization by local static observers, whose energy varies with the lapse — and taken relative to the exact round arena of the same $\ell$, $\delta R_{ab} = R_{ab}-R^{(0)}_{ab}$:

$$\mathcal F[\gamma] = \ell\int_\gamma\delta R_{ab}\,\bar k^a\bar k^b\,d\bar\lambda,\qquad \mathcal F[\Xi] = \tfrac12\big(\mathcal F[\gamma_+]+\mathcal F[\gamma_-]\big)$$

For comoving dust $\delta R_{ab}\bar k^a\bar k^b\,d\bar\lambda = (8\pi G\,\delta\rho/c^2)\,ds/N$, from which $\Lambda$ drops out; the lapse correction is of order $10^{-6}$, and the numbers below are unchanged. The subtraction is essential to the definition: the round background alone focuses by $\ell\int_0^{\pi\ell}2/\ell^2\,ds = 2\pi$ per traversal, a million times the Hubble number, and that common focusing is what makes the conjugate gate; the Galaxy's *departure* from it is the small, class-dependent quantity. This **renormalized, history-averaged Ricci focusing functional** is exactly the kind of quantity the coboundary no-go allows — a path integral of a density, not an endpoint difference — additive traversal by traversal, symmetric under leg exchange, zero wherever the geometry equals the round reference — which is not the same as physical vacuum — and attached to Jacobi-open classes by construction. For a source at the Galaxy's centre it gives $1.05$, $1.53$ and $1.63$ times $H_0\ell/c$ at $\ell = 8$, $13$ and $16$ kpc, and analytically $GM\ell/c^2h^2$, so that

$$\frac{\text{focusing column per arena radius} }{H_0\ell/c} = \frac{GM_{\rm gal} }{cH_0h^2} = 1.8$$

**independent of $\ell$** **[V]**. The coincidence becomes $M_{\rm gal}/h^2\approx2\,cH_0/G$ — $18.5$ against $10.2$ kg m$^{-2}$ — the Freeman-limit surface-density coincidence the detached wing already carries (§XII.1), no longer tied to the arena radius. The two jobs previously forced onto $\ell$ separate: **$\ell$ sets the recurrence geometry — topology, conjugacy, return periods — while the Galaxy's baryonic column, $GM/h^2$, sets the candidate dilation per traversal**; no choice among 7, 8, 13 or 16 kpc is needed for the coincidence to hold. That is the best-behaved candidate found. **Its limitation is the off-centre observer, and it is not a small one:** from a source at the Sun's radius the column runs from $-0.7$ to $+3.4$ times the target with direction, negative whenever a ray misses the dense centre and sees only the compensating underdensity, and its direction-average falls from $1.1$–$1.6$ at the centre to about zero at $8$–$12$ kpc **[V]**. So it can serve only if the rendered class is a *collective* object whose column is the Galaxy's own, centred — the brief's picture of a class, but an assumption about what a class is, not a result. Three things stay postulated here: that class, the identification $\eta = C\mathcal F$ with $C$ of order one-half to one, and $D_{\rm app}$ itself **[S/O]** — and §XIV.9 derives the first two further from the optical transfer matrix.

**Local suppression [D].** The Sun and the Earth generate no Hubble-like readout: $\eta$ attaches only to Jacobi-open recurrent classes, and within the solar system the gate stays shut (§XIII.10). Local secondaries bend and focus rays; they do not open the global sector, and they do not set $H_{\rm app}$.

**The Tully–Fisher fork [D].** The detached wing's arena law $GM = A_{\rm dyn}\ell^2$ gives $v^4 = 4C_{\rm plat}^2A_{\rm dyn}GM$, slope four for any constant coefficient; a well-Hubble law would give $A_{\rm dyn} = \beta cH_{\rm app}$ *if* one $M$–$\ell$ relation governed both dynamics and optics. The wing's normalization wants $\beta\approx1/49$; the heuristic well argument wants $1/4$; the document's own plateau radii sit at $1/14$ to $1/21$. Branch A, one universal coefficient, must explain a factor of order ten or fail; Branch B, linked but distinct coefficients $A_{\rm dyn}$ and $A_z$ with a derived ratio, is safer, and is the one carried.

**Emergent $G$ [O].** The rearrangement $G = \beta\,cH_{\rm app}\ell^2/M_{\rm inertial}$ is dimensional only: if $G$ entered the well that set $H_{\rm app}$, solving backward is circular. A genuine route needs an operational inertial mass, an $H_{\rm app}$ from readout geometry, an independently selected $\ell$ and a derived $\beta$, and then $G_{\rm pred}$ must reproduce the weak-field law, the equivalence of masses, the plateau, the local Schwarzschild comparison and Law I's coupling.

## XIV.7 The apparent Hubble law and the cosmological slot [S/O]

At low redshift $z\simeq\eta\simeq(H_{\rm app}/c)D_{\rm app}$, so the branch needs $\eta/D_{\rm app}$ constant across the rendered population — a strong, falsifiable requirement — and the full curve $z(D_{\rm app})$ must match the observed distance-redshift relation, not merely its slope. The status of $H_{\rm app}$ must be stated: derived from return-map statistics, from $\ell$ and a large dimensionless recurrence number, or from a canonical coupling — or simply inserted, in which case the claim that the model has no cosmological slot is weakened, and this document says so rather than hiding it.

## XIV.8 Celestial-sphere acceptance tests [D]

So large $z$ cannot come mainly from traversal number, or the recurrent object is not a literal chronological history, or the simple cumulative branch fails |

Determine the finite-$\epsilon$ scale character, and whether the allowed class family spans $\eta = \ln(1+z)$ from $O(10^{-6})$ to $O(1)$ without violating the complex-lift construction — failure is fatal to a universal high-$z$ reading |

> **The brightness budget, sourced [V].** The extragalactic side is the New Horizons direct measurement of the optical background, $11.16\pm1.65$ nW m$^{-2}$ sr$^{-1}$ near $0.6\,\mu$m, most of it accounted for by integrated galaxy light. The Milky Way side is the *integrated starlight* of standard night-sky tabulations, quoted in $S_{10}$ units — one tenth-magnitude star per square degree, or $27.78$ mag arcsec$^{-2}$ — at roughly $30$–$100\,S_{10}$ at high Galactic latitude and several hundred toward the plane, in the $V$ band near $0.55\,\mu$m. The conversion uses the Vega zero point, $f_\lambda\simeq3.63\times10^{-11}$ W m$^{-2}$ nm$^{-1}$ at $V = 0$, and $\nu I_\nu = \lambda I_\lambda$ at $550$ nm: one $S_{10}$ is then $6.6$ nW m$^{-2}$ sr$^{-1}$, so a $22$ mag arcsec$^{-2}$ dark sky is $1{,}350$, and the integrated starlight is $200$–$2{,}000$ nW m$^{-2}$ sr$^{-1}$ — $20$ to $180$ times the optical background. Two caveats cut the other way: the bandpasses differ slightly ($0.55$ against $0.61\,\mu$m), and the starlight we receive directly is dust-extinguished through the disk, whereas a return travelling through the barren hemisphere would not be, so the returned flux would if anything be larger. The conclusion does not depend on any distance interpretation: whatever the readout assigns, all but a few per cent of returned starlight must go into its kernel.

Foreground lensing is both a constraint and a laboratory: the branch may use the same conjugate threshold ordinary lensing uses, but must say what survives once ordinary lensing is subtracted.

## XIV.9 Relative optical monodromy and the collective focusing class [T/V/D/S/O]

*Rather than postulate $\eta = C\mathcal F$, derive as much of it as possible from the Jacobi system that already defines the gate and the return map.*

**The transfer matrix [T].** On the two-dimensional screen the optical tidal matrix splits into trace and traceless parts, $\mathcal T = \tfrac12R_{ab}k^ak^b\,I+\mathcal T_{\rm shear}$ — the Sachs decomposition into isotropic focusing and Weyl shear. The full screen system is four-dimensional, $Y = (J^1,J^2,\ell DJ^1,\ell DJ^2)$, and its transfer map is symplectic, $\mathsf M\in Sp(4,\mathbb R)$. What follows first is its **isotropic $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ sector** — the identical scalar block obtained when the trace part of $\mathcal T$ is isolated — and the full symplectic object comes after. In the variables $(J,\ell J')$ that sector is a first-order system $y' = \mathsf A(s)y$; one traversal gives a transfer matrix $\mathsf M_\Xi$, and the round arena gives the reference $\mathsf M_0$, a rotation by $s/\ell$, equal to $-I$ after one traversal. The **relative monodromy** $\mathsf R_\Xi = \mathsf M_0^{-1}\mathsf M_\Xi$ removes the round background geometrically rather than by subtracting a number, and equals $I$ for the control arena. To first order in the isotropic perturbation $\delta\mathcal R = \tfrac12\delta R_{ab}k^ak^b$, with $\sigma = s/\ell$,

$$\log\mathsf R_\Xi = \ell\int_0^{\pi\ell}\delta\mathcal R(s)\begin{pmatrix}\sin\sigma\cos\sigma & \sin^2\sigma\\ -\cos^2\sigma & -\sin\sigma\cos\sigma\end{pmatrix}ds$$

an element of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R)$, which decomposes into a rotation and a squeeze,

$$\theta_\Xi = \tfrac12\,\ell\!\int\!\delta\mathcal R\,ds = \tfrac14\mathcal F[\Xi],\qquad \eta_\Xi = \tfrac12\,\ell\,\Big|\int\delta\mathcal R\,e^{2is/\ell}\,ds\Big|$$

with the squeeze axis at the phase of the second Fourier harmonic — the centroid angle $2s_0/\ell$ only for a localized or symmetric perturbation.

**What this gives [V].** Checked against direct integration of the transfer system, to three digits:

| | rotation $\theta_\Xi$, compact | squeeze $\eta_\Xi$, noncompact |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the uniform closure background, or any uniform perturbation | nonzero: the conjugate-point shift | **zero**: its second harmonic over a traversal vanishes |
| a compact lump anywhere along the traversal | $\mathcal F_{\rm lump}/4$ | $\mathcal F_{\rm lump}/4$, wherever it sits |
| the Milky Way profile, class centred on the Galaxy | $\mathcal F/4$ | $0.38$–$0.43$ times $H_0\ell/c$ at $\ell = 8$–$16$ kpc |
| from the Sun's radius, toward the centre / sideways / away | can be negative | $0.65$–$0.82$ / $0.04$–$0.05$ / $0.02$ times $H_0\ell/c$: positive throughout |

So the trace sector of the relative monodromy *already contains a noncompact parameter*, derived from the optical transfer matrix rather than added as a connection, and three things come with it. The normalization is derived, not fitted: for a sharply localized lump $\eta = \mathcal F/4$, the $\tfrac14$ from the Sachs $\tfrac12$ and the half-period of a traversal; for an extended profile the value is the second-harmonic-weighted one in the table, not $\mathcal F/4$. This $\tfrac14$ has nothing to do with the old heuristic $\beta = 1/4$ of the $M\sim\beta cH_0\ell^2/G$ relation. The background subtraction is automatic: uniform density rotates the beam's phase and never squeezes it, so the compensating underdensity that made the raw column negative for rays missing the Galaxy drops out. And the squeeze is one-signed as a *magnitude* — but a positive squeeze is not yet a positive redshift: an $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ squeeze has reciprocal branches $e^{\pm\eta}$, and the geometry has supplied a magnitude and an axis, not which branch the detector reads as the spectral dilation. That choice must come from time orientation, endpoint orientation, or the canonical readout — and it, rather than another well functional, is now the real redshift bridge. *(Version 20 dissolves it structurally: the candidate dilation is carried by a scale character, which has one scale factor, and the squeeze keeps the job of shape, §XV.2.)* And the two Jacobi sectors divide the labour the phenomenology wants: **trace, with its rotation and squeeze, for the gate and a scalar dilation; traceless shear for shape, morphology and splitting.**

**What it does not yet give [D/O].** A Sachs squeeze dilates the beam's phase space, not the photon's frequency; the step from isotropic optical dilation to the spectral and temporal readout of §XIV.5 is still the postulate. Squeezes about different axes do not add as scalars, since $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ is non-abelian — though a periodic class repeats the same generator, so that $\eta_n = n\eta_1+O(\delta\mathcal R^2)$ within one class — the first-order generator adds, while the finite squeeze of a product that also contains rotation need not — which is what "modular" can now mean. And **the off-centre observer remains decisive**: individual rays from the Sun's radius still span a factor of forty between the directions toward and away from the centre. The scalar must be an invariant of a *class*, not of a ray.

**The full symplectic monodromy [T/V].** The round arena supplies a natural scale between $J$ and $\ell DJ$, hence a positive metric on Jacobi phase space; with its adjoint $\dagger_0$ the object $\mathsf C_\Xi = \mathsf R_\Xi^{\dagger_0}\mathsf R_\Xi$ has, by symplecticity, stretch eigenvalues in reciprocal pairs $e^{\pm2\chi_1}$, $e^{\pm2\chi_2}$, and

$$\eta_{\rm iso} = \tfrac12(\chi_1+\chi_2),\qquad \gamma_{\rm aniso} = \tfrac12(\chi_1-\chi_2)$$

are invariant under rotations of the Sachs screen and divide the labour exactly as the phenomenology wants: $\eta_{\rm iso}$ for a scalar dilation, $\gamma_{\rm aniso}$ for shear and morphology. Computed on the isotropic Milky Way with its Weyl screen shear $\tfrac32GM(<r)\,r_\perp^2/c^2r^5$ **[V]**: the transfer map is symplectic to seven digits; for the centred class $\gamma_{\rm aniso}$ vanishes and $\eta_{\rm iso}$ equals the isotropic-sector squeeze exactly; for rays from the Sun toward or away from the centre the shear vanishes by symmetry and the same holds; for oblique rays the two blocks' second harmonics combine with a relative phase, so that $\eta_{\rm iso}$ and $\gamma_{\rm aniso}$ are the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of the block squeezes — of the same size as the isotropic and shear harmonics, but not equal to them separately.

**The collective class, defined [D].** An arbitrary island contains rays the observer never reads. Since the Photon History Postulate fixes observed endpoints, take an *observer-conditioned* return section $\mathcal S_O$, an island $\mathcal I_O\subset\mathcal S_O$, and the Liouville measure $\mu_L$ that the Poincaré map preserves, and set

$$\bar\eta_{\mathcal I_O} = \frac{1}{\mu_L(\mathcal I_O)}\int_{\mathcal I_O}\eta_{\rm iso}(\xi)\,d\mu_L$$

An apparent galaxy is already meant to be the sky projection of an island, so its redshift being an island invariant is far less arbitrary than assigning it to one ray. The crucial prediction is then testable before anything else: **$\bar\eta_{\mathcal I_O} > 0$ and narrowly distributed across islands, for an observer at $R_0\neq0$** — averaging over rays the observer actually reads, not over rays it never sees. If island averaging recentres the directional swing, this candidate lives; if the swing survives, it fails on the record.

**The prize, and a caution [S/O].** If one transfer object carries everything, Part XIV collapses from five readout assignments to one: trace → $\eta$, $z$ and perhaps $D_L/D_A$; traceless part → shear and morphology; return period → $D_{\rm app}$; island size → angular extent; the trivial-monodromy class → the self-return kernel. And the caution goes straight into the acceptance tests: with $\eta_n = n\eta_1$ and $D_{\rm app}\propto n$ too rigidly, galaxies would sit on a discrete redshift comb, which they do not; the island invariant, a further modular index, or the map to $D_{\rm app}$ must supply enough continuous variation to wash it out.

**The program.** Build one return map for the smoothed Milky Way profile with a controlled ensemble of lumps; find its recurrent classes, islands and stability matrices; compute $\bar\eta_{\mathcal I}$; test its sign and spread for $R_0 = 8$ kpc; only then ask whether the relative monodromy fixes the readout coefficient, and whether repeated traversals give $\eta_n = n\eta_1$ with $D_{\rm app}\sim nD_\ast$, from which the low-$z$ Hubble law would follow with no further input.

## XIV.10 Status and falsification ledger [D]

| grade | contents |
|:--|:--|
| **standard mathematics and physics** | Morse–Bott perturbation theory; Poincaré return maps, periodic points and stability matrices; the static-wall and coboundary no-gos; the unitary dilation on $L^2(\mathbb R_+)$; cosmological distance measures; the supernova time-dilation measurement; Etherington reciprocity; Tolman dimming; the CMB temperature–redshift relation |
| **verified here** | one secondary leaves a degenerate ring; several carve about two first-order stationary members each, which is not a galaxy count; the source-centred hemisphere flux vanishes by symmetry; the arena-scale depth is packing-dominated; the coincidence's arithmetic and the radii it encodes; returned starlight would exceed the optical background twenty- to two-hundredfold; the boost part of the two-leg holonomy vanishes for spatial loops in any static spacetime and reduces to the tidal integral for the null loop; the tidal functional is sign-indefinite off centre; the null focusing column gives $1.0$–$1.6$ times $H_0\ell/c$ from the centre, independently of $\ell$, and about zero on average from the Sun's radius; the relative monodromy of the screen Jacobi system decomposes into a rotation $\mathcal F/4$ and a squeeze $\tfrac12\ell\lvert\int\delta\mathcal R\,e^{2is/\ell}ds\rvert$, to which uniform density contributes nothing and a compact lump contributes $\mathcal F/4$ wherever it sits; from the Sun's radius the squeeze is positive throughout, $0.02$–$0.8$ of the Hubble number; the full $Sp(4,\mathbb R)$ relative monodromy separates $\eta_{\rm iso}$ from $\gamma_{\rm aniso}$, the shear vanishing for the centred class; the recurrence-age bound, $\ell$ cancelling |

| **proposals** | the Modular Galaxy Readout — an apparent galaxy as a stable recurrent class with $\mathscr P^n\xi\sim\xi$; the Apparent Hubble Readout — $1+z = e^{\eta}$ with the same $\eta$ dilating time; the galactic well as the dilation scale, through a surface not yet defined; the null focusing column as the dilation cocycle, $\eta = C\rho(\Xi)$, for collective classes centred on the Galaxy; the island-averaged squeeze $\bar\eta_{\mathcal I}$ of the relative monodromy as the class redshift, with its coefficient $1/4$ derived |
| **failed so far** | the source-centred hemisphere flux as the dial; the arena-scale depth as a universal dial; $\ell\approx8$ kpc as anything but a selection hypothesis; the boost holonomy as an $SO(1,1)$ source in the static arena; the tidal functional as a one-signed redshift; the simple cumulative reading of large $z$ as traversal number, which the Galaxy's age caps at $z\lesssim0.1$ |
| **open** | the definition of one traversal; nondegeneracy of the return map; stable islands and achromatic image extents; the flux-redistribution formalism; a non-exact dilation cocycle and where its scale comes from; the surface through which the well would act; source diversity; whether $H_{\rm app}$ is derived or inserted; and above all an invariant that places the self-return class in the readout kernel; whether a collective class's column is universal — whether the return map's islands centre on the Galaxy rather than on individual sources — and where the constant $C$ comes from; whether island averaging recentres the directional swing; the step from beam dilation to spectral readout; the redshift comb; which squeeze branch the detector reads, the redshift bridge; $\eta_n = n\eta_1$ beyond first order; where large $z$ comes from if not from $n$ |

> **The single question [D].** Can one static galactic projective arena produce a discrete celestial population of finite apparent galaxies whose spectra, time scales, angular sizes, fluxes and lensing reproduce the empirical redshift–distance sky, including an apparent Hubble law, through the dynamics and readout of recurrent Jacobi-open photon-history classes — without modifying the Born rule, and without hiding a Friedmann cosmology inside a free observable map? If yes, the branch has found a real extension. If no, it should fail cleanly, on this ledger. **The next calculation is fixed by the ledger.** A very good additive history scalar has been found — the renormalized Ricci focusing functional, non-exact, additive and one-signed for centred classes, with the Hubble magnitude to within a factor of $1$–$1.6$ independently of the arena radius — though not yet shown to be a cocycle of the return map in the dynamical sense; and §XIV.9 derives its noncompact partner, the squeeze of the relative monodromy, from the optical transfer matrix itself, with coefficient $1/4$ and no background to subtract. What remains is one construction — the return map's islands, and whether their average squeeze is positive and narrowly distributed for an observer at $8$ kpc — with two tests to pass first: the recurrence-age bound, which already caps the cumulative reading at $z\lesssim0.1$, and the choice of squeeze branch that would make a dilation a redshift.

# PART XV — THE BI-CONNECTION SUBSTRATE AND THE UNIVERSAL NULL-HISTORY PRINCIPLE: THE VERSION-20 BRANCH [T/V/D/S/O]

*Two of the author's intuitions open this part, and one of them is adopted by decision rather than derived: that the middle geometry should be the symmetric resolution of two deeper transports — a pair of Weyl-type connections sharing one null geometry — with candidate dilation carried by the scale character of their relative transport. What follows states the principle, verifies what the pair does, answers the one question that decides its relation to Part XIV, and records what remains. Parts 0–XIV are unchanged.*

## XV.0 The decision and the principle

**The intuitions, in the author's terms.** Since a galaxy's image is already a two-history object for light, uniqueness of that galaxy under *both* light and gravitational waves demands an exactly analogous two-history structure for gravitational radiation — with no mechanism that could privilege one, "as if being able to determine which one is more objective." And rather than add readouts after the fact, "bake this straight into spacetime": let the middle space itself emerge as a combination of two deeper structures, designed so that the dual gravitational-wave picture lives on it and is wired to the electromagnetic one by the same no-privileging principle — a substrate-deepening move that might make the Hubble behaviour emergent rather than imposed.

> **The foundation, independent of any model [T].** What the branch rests on is a theorem, not the Jacobi machinery built on it. A round three-sphere of radius $\ell$ is flat to order $(d/\ell)^2$: rays from a point fan out as in flat space, so between two nearby points the ray is unique and isolated. Positive curvature bends the fanning rays back, and at distance $\pi\ell$ every ray from a point reconverges at its antipode — the twin — so the two endpoints are joined by a continuum of paths, sharing both ends and spreading apart by up to order $\ell$ between them. The transition is a threshold, the conjugate point, not a drift. It is robust: by Bonnet–Myers, any closed space whose Ricci curvature is at least the round sphere's forces a conjugate point on every geodesic longer than $\pi\ell$ — given that lower bound — and for this particular arena the explicit weak-lump calculation, which shifts and splits the focus by parts per million without removing it (§XIII.10), is the stronger evidence. Lumps can add paths locally, through ordinary gravitational lensing — standard physics, not the arena's mechanism, which is why the solar focus lies at $548$ AU while nothing in the solar system joins two points by more than one path. **Aligned when zoomed in; separable at the arena scale.** The Jacobi equation is only the calculator; the Photon History Postulate and the monodromy squeeze are optional, and this part uses the fact alone: in §XV.3 the imaginary displacement of a class is a Jacobi field vanishing at the real endpoints, so the local half is $Y = 0$ with no scale character, and the global half is the sine profile at the twin.

**The Universal Null-History Principle [S].** The existence and canonical equivalence of histories is decided *before* the propagating field's spin is specified:

$$\mathcal N_{\rm can}\subset\mathbb P(T\mathcal M)\ \text{transverse to}\ \ker dq,\qquad d\iota(\mathcal N_{\rm EM}) = \mathcal N_{\rm can}\big|_{B_{\rm rep} },\qquad dq(\mathcal N_{\rm can}) = \mathcal N_{\rm GW}$$

— one canonical null structure on the middle space, of which the electromagnetic cone on $B_{\rm rep}$ is the restriction and the gravitational-wave cone on $B_{\rm grav}$ the image, a commuting diagram rather than an equality between objects on different manifolds; the Jacobi gate $\mathcal J_{\rm can}$ and the history class $\Xi_{\rm can}$ live on $\mathcal M$ likewise, read on $B_{\rm rep}$ for light and on $B_{\rm grav}$ for gravitational waves — while spin one and spin two are representation data, $\rho_1(\Xi_{\rm can})\neq\rho_2(\Xi_{\rm can})$, with different polarizations, amplitudes and couplings. The standard foothold is real **[T]**: at leading geometric-optics order both Maxwell waves and high-frequency gravitational waves propagate on the null geodesics of the background, with amplitude and polarization transported along them, and both lens, interfere and show wave-optical behaviour at caustics. The principle is therefore exact at leading eikonal order only; beyond it, gravitational waves acquire known polarization-dependent corrections, and the theory must not claim more.

## XV.1 The bi-connection [T/V]

On the middle-space geometry, with its conformal null structure $[h]$, take two exchange-related connections

$$\nabla^\pm_a h_{bc} = \mp2A_ah_{bc},\qquad \Gamma^{\pm a}{}_{bc} = \Gamma^a{}_{bc}\pm\big(\delta^a_bA_c+\delta^a_cA_b-h_{bc}A^a\big)$$

with the exchange $+\leftrightarrow-$ sending $A\to-A$. Their mean is the Levi-Civita connection, $\tfrac12(\nabla^++\nabla^-) = \nabla^{\rm LC}$, and their difference $K = \tfrac12(\nabla^+-\nabla^-)$ carries the relative structure **[V]**. Three facts, each checked symbolically: the difference tensor contracted on a null vector is along that vector, $C^a{}_{bc}k^bk^c = 2(A\cdot k)k^a$, so all three connections have the same unparametrized null geodesics **[V]**; along a $\nabla^\pm$-parallel field the squared norm $h(v,v)$ changes as $e^{\mp2\int A}$, lengths as $e^{\mp\int A}$ **[V]**; and everything that couples to $\bar\nabla = \nabla^{\rm LC}$ sees the metric geometry of Parts 0–IX unchanged.

**Where it lives — the correction of version 20.2.** As a pair of connections *on the real middle space* this structure cannot carry the redshift, because §XV.7 shows that the scale part of the canonical complex connection vanishes on every real direction: on the real locus all three connections coincide. What survives is better. The pair is the shadow of *one* $\mathbb C^\times$-connection on the complexification, seen from a complex history and its $\rho_E$-conjugate: by equivariance, transporting along the conjugate history with the one connection equals transporting along the original with the conjugate connection — the offloading identity of §XV.6 realized by $\rho_E$ itself. Real single histories see only $U(1)_H$ and the metric, which is the firewall, now derived rather than stipulated; pairs of conjugate lifts see the difference.

## XV.2 The relative transport and its scale character [V/D]

**Definitions.** Reserve *relative transport* for the full element: for two connections carried around the same loop, $H_{\rm rel}(\Xi) := {\rm Hol}_{\nabla^-}(C_\Xi)^{-1}{\rm Hol}_{\nabla^+}(C_\Xi)$, or, in the complex form of §XV.7, one connection carried around the loop $\widetilde\gamma_+\cup\overline{\widetilde\gamma_-}$ of conjugate lifts. On the full screen system of §XIV.9 this element lies in the conformal symplectic group,

$$CSp(4,\mathbb R)\simeq\mathbb R_+\cdot Sp(4,\mathbb R):\qquad \text{the scale part supplies the overall homothety; the Jacobi system supplies focusing, shear, squeeze and rotation}$$

— on one scalar block $GL^+(2,\mathbb R)\simeq\mathbb R_+\times SL(2,\mathbb R)$. What is unambiguously abelian is its *scale character*, $\chi_{\rm sc}(H_{\rm rel}) = e^{-\eta_\Xi}$: for the Weyl pair around one real loop, $\eta_\Xi = 2\oint_{C_\Xi}A = 2\int_{\Sigma_\Xi}F_A$ (the factor two from comparing the two connections rather than either with the mean); for one connection around the conjugate-lift loop, $\eta_\Xi = \int_{\Sigma_{\mathbb C} }F_A$ over the complex ribbon. Both are Stokes-expressible, non-exact, history-dependent and additive; the branchwise composition — each connection on its own leg — is a sum rather than a loop integral, exchange-odd, and not a cocycle, which is why the closed-time-path dictionary of §XV.6 must double transports around one loop, not histories with separate connections.

**What it is not [V].** The scale character does not reproduce the Jacobi squeeze of §XIV.9 and cannot: the Weyl transport has determinant $e^{4\int A}\neq1$ on a screen block, while the Jacobi monodromy is symplectic with determinant one. The two are complementary — scale and shape — and the reciprocal-branch problem of §XIV.9 dissolves, since a homothety has one scale factor.

**The real loop carries nothing [D].** With $A|_{TE} = 0$ (§XV.7), the pull-back of $A$ to the real locus vanishes and so does $i^*F_A = d(i^*A)$: every ribbon tangent to the real geometry has zero scale flux, and the redshift candidate of versions 20 and 20.1 — evaluated on the real Jacobi ribbon — is zero. The scale character of a class is evaluated instead on the complex ribbon between the conjugate canonical lifts of its legs, $\widetilde\gamma_\pm = \gamma_\pm\pm iY$, which is where §XV.3 goes. The Jacobi geometry decides when a real class exists; the complex geometry decides its scale.

## XV.3 Where the flux lives [V/D/O]

**The complex ribbon and the Hopf flux, at first order [V/D].** Type the objects downstairs: the Hopf curvature is basic, $F_H = \pi_H^*\bar F_H$ with $\bar F_H$ a 2-form on $\mathcal M$, and $k,Y\in T\mathcal M$ are evaluated on their horizontal lifts. Let a real leg $\gamma$ have a one-parameter family of complex lifts $\widetilde\gamma_\epsilon = \gamma+i\epsilon Y+O(\epsilon^2)$ with $\rho_E\widetilde\gamma_\epsilon = \widetilde\gamma_{-\epsilon}$, and let $\Sigma_{\mathbb C}$ be the complex ribbon between $\widetilde\gamma_{\pm\epsilon}$. By the bridge of §XV.7, $F_A(k,JY) = -F_H(k,Y)$ on the real locus and $F_H(k,JY)$ vanishes there, so the conjugate lifts' phases cancel and their scale character is

$$\eta_\Xi(\epsilon) = 2\epsilon\int_\gamma\bar F_H(Y,k)\,ds+O(\epsilon^3)$$

— odd in $\epsilon$, because exchanging the lifts reverses the relative scale. The formula is exact only on the real locus: a finite ribbon samples the continued curvature away from it. On the Hopf model the residual scales as $\epsilon^3$, with coefficient $0.119$ in the test geometry, and the phase cancels to $10^{-17}$ **[V]**. **At first order the scale character of a class is a Hopf flux** — the flux of a curvature the theory already has, through the real ribbon that the imaginary displacement sweeps along the ray. No new independent field enters; what enters is the full Hopf connection.

**The imaginary displacement is a Jacobi field, and the gate returns [V/D].** A complex geodesic variation of a real null geodesic has, as its first-order term, a complex Jacobi field, since the Jacobi equation is linear over $\mathbb C$; so $Y = \tfrac1i\,\partial_\epsilon\widetilde\gamma_\epsilon|_0$ is a real Jacobi field along the ray. A real source and a real observer force $Y(0) = Y(S) = 0$, and a Jacobi field vanishing at both ends exists only when they are conjugate: **conjugacy is the necessary infinitesimal gate for a nontrivial complex family.** So the gate of §XIII.10 returns as the existence condition of a complex lift: zoomed in, $Y = 0$ and no scale character; at the twin, $Y = y_0\sin(s/\ell)\,\hat e$. In the round arena the finite family exists explicitly: on the complexified sphere, $\cos(s)\,p+\sin(s)(d_R+id_I)$ with $|d_R|^2-|d_I|^2 = 1$ and $d_R\cdot d_I = 0$ is a complex geodesic from $p$ to $-p$ for every such $d$, with imaginary displacement $\sin(s)\,d_I$ — the sine profile, exactly **[V]**; once lumps split the degeneracy, finite existence is a nonlinear theorem not yet proved. This is the foundation of §XV.0 doing its work twice: the local half as $Y = 0$, the global half as the sine profile.

**The decisive component, the parity law and the sign [V/D/O].** The formula is linear in $\hat e$: a free imaginary direction would give classes in opposite-sign pairs. Part XV's original candidate for the canonical direction is the imaginary *meridian* displacement of Part X, along the fourth spatial direction of $\mathcal M$ off the representational base — on the round $S^4$ the unit normal $N$ of the base, parallel along its geodesics, so that $Y = y_0\sin(s/\ell)\,N$ is a legitimate Jacobi field. That candidate is excluded by §XVI.8 if the actual Hopf data are plane-reflection equivariant, and the admissible displacement is reopened as the representation problem of §XVI.9; what follows is stated for it as originally proposed. What the class then needs is the mixed curvature, which is gauge-invariant where the meridian component of the connection is not, so it is the fundamental observable:

$$f_\Xi(s) := \bar F_H(N,k),\qquad \eta_\Xi = 2\epsilon y_0\int_0^{\pi\ell}\sin(s/\ell)\,f_\Xi(s)\,ds$$

Since $\sin(s/\ell)>0$ between source and twin, **the minimal acceptance criterion is the weighted moment, $\int_0^{\pi\ell}\sin(s/\ell)f_\Xi\,ds>0$, for every admissible class**; pointwise positivity, $f_\Xi\ge0$, is the *sufficient local positivity theorem* — a stronger target, since a function may change sign and keep a positive weighted moment. §XV.7 computes the component on the local model: in a meridian-invariant gauge, $f = -k\cdot\nabla a_{\rm mer}$, with $a_{\rm mer}$ the meridian component of the Hopf connection — zero for the product connection, not forced by topology or smoothness, an unsourced deformation of Structure III (item 3 of §XI.2). In that gauge, integrating by parts with $Y$ vanishing at the ends, $\eta_\Xi = (2\epsilon y_0/\ell)\int a_{\rm mer}\cos(s/\ell)\,ds$, and since $\cos((\pi\ell-s)/\ell) = -\cos(s/\ell)$ the parity statement is exact and no more: *a component even between source and twin gives zero; an odd one gives a moment that is symmetry-allowed* — allowed, not guaranteed nonzero, and not guaranteed one-signed, since an odd profile can wiggle and cancel **[T]**.

**The twin-equivariant parity law [D, conditional].** Structure III's opposite Chern signs at the two crossings are a statement about the orientation of $\bar F_H$ on linking spheres, and do not by themselves say how a longitudinal component transforms. What does is the geometry of one meridian crossing the base twice: with the meridian circle oriented, its tangent is $+N$ at the source crossing and $-N$ at the twin crossing, because the circle continues over the pole and comes back through the base the other way. Take the connection to be *twin-equivariant* — invariant under the involution whose invariance of the bundle produces Structure III's signs. Then, since the twin map carries the class through $d$ onto the class through $-d$ reversed, $\tau\gamma_d(s) = \gamma_{-d}(\pi\ell-s)$, the law relates *paired* histories: $f_d(s) = f_{-d}(\pi\ell-s)$ — checked on explicit twin-invariant connections on the round arena to $10^{-10}$, including one with no further symmetry, for which the per-history evenness $f_d(s) = f_d(\pi\ell-s)$ fails by seventy percent **[V]**. Per-history evenness needs, in addition, invariance under $d\to-d$ — a profile axisymmetric about the meridian has it — or a class average invariant under that exchange; and because $\sin(s/\ell)$ is itself symmetric about the midpoint, the weighted moment is already the same for the two paired members, $\eta_d = \eta_{-d}$ **[V]**. The topological parity and the optical parity law thus hang on one assumption. Positivity is separate: if the meridian component decays monotonically away from each crossing, $f = -\partial_ra\ge0$ and $\eta_\Xi>0$; a wiggling profile keeps the parity law and loses the sign **[V]**. Twin equivariance fixes the transformation law, not the sign; the sign is the profile's, and the profile is item 3's. Version 21.4 adds two parity tests from the plane duality (§XVI.8): with reflection-equivariant Hopf data, the meridian displacement gives planar classes no scale character and mirror classes opposite signs — a systematic hemispheric reversal the sky forbids — while the normal displacement survives that test; so the choice of displacement and the parity assignments of item 10 stand ahead of positivity.

**The self-return kernel, and the convention the age bound selects [D, conditional].** With the imaginary direction along the global normal $N$, the round smooth self-return $p\to-p\to p$ — the continuation of the same great circle, whose second half is the twin image of the first, point for point — sees $-f$ on the return leg: it has zero net scale character, and repeated returns alternate $0,\eta,0,\eta$ with no cumulative growth **[V]**. The statement covers the round smooth self-return and any exactly twin-paired continuation; a perturbed recurrent loop through the observer need not be twin-paired point for point, so persistence of the kernel under the perturbed return map is a theorem to prove or a test to run, not a result in hand. Within its scope this is the kernel behaviour the self-return test of §XIV.2 requires of the observer's own class, and it removes the cumulative reading outright. What it establishes is *scale-kernel* membership, not readout-kernel membership: a class with $\eta = 0$ can still carry phase, amplitude, angular structure and flux, and the returned-starlight problem of §XIV.2 needs the self-return's visual observable to vanish, $\mathcal O_{\rm vis}(\Xi_{\rm self}) = 0$, or a unitary routing into a non-visual sector. **Scale kernel is not visual kernel.** The other convention, the imaginary direction along the meridian's own orientation at each class's source, gives $+\eta$ on every leg — cumulative growth, which the recurrence-age bound of §XIV.8 already excludes beyond $z\approx0.1$. So the global-normal convention passes the recurrence-age test where the cumulative meridian-oriented one fails it — the bound rules out that reading, not every alternative — and with the global-normal convention the twin image becomes the *candidate* one-traversal carrier of dilation — whether that half-return is what renders as an external galaxy remains Part XIV's observable-map proposal, given its structure in Part XVI — where §XVI.2 shows the round twin image to be one inverted sky, so that separate galaxies need the broken family's sheets. Two consequences follow. The continuum of observed redshifts cannot come from traversal number and must come from $y_0$ and the profile varying across classes; and the comb of §XIV.8 *may* be washed out by that variation — a possibility, since neither the distribution of $y_0$ nor that of the islands is derived. For a component of height $a_0$ within a width $w$ of each meridian the estimate is $\eta_\Xi\approx2\sqrt\pi\,\epsilon y_0a_0w/\ell$, and the Hubble number $H_0\ell/c\approx4\times10^{-6}$ at $\ell = 16$ kpc asks $\epsilon y_0a_0w/\ell\approx10^{-6}$. The relation of $\eta_\Xi$ to $D_{\rm app}$ is untouched, and the recurrence-age bound itself carries over from Part XIV unchanged. The repair also creates a pressure point of its own, entered in §XIV.8 as the finite-width test: with exactly twin-paired returns not accumulating, large observed redshift must arise within a single class, four to five orders of magnitude above the local calibration and outside the small-$\epsilon$ regime in which the formula is proved.

## XV.4 The action and the empirical firewall [S/O]

The target is no longer Einstein–Hilbert plus a readout but

$$S_{\rm deep} = S_{\rm geom}[\bar\nabla,K,h]+S_{\rm matter}+S_{\rm EM}+\cdots,\qquad K\to-K\ \text{a symmetry}$$

in which matter and single-history propagation see only the even combination $\bar\nabla$, while recurrent two-history objects probe the odd structure through ${\rm Hol}_{\rm rel}(\Xi)$ — and, if the descent of §XV.7 holds, $K$ is not an independent field at all but the analytic continuation of the Hopf connection, with the exchange symmetry being $\rho_E$. The empirical requirement is then brutal and clean: one event producing both electromagnetic and gravitational radiation must show

$$\eta_{\rm EM} = \eta_{\rm GW}$$

for the same canonical class, modulo emission delays, with matched path multiplicities — amplitudes and polarizations free to differ, the class not. The real sky anchors the first half of this **[T]**: the binary neutron-star merger GW170817 and its gamma-ray burst arrived within seconds after some forty megaparsecs, bounding any difference in propagation speed at the $10^{-15}$ level — exactly the shared-cone, no-privileging constraint. It does not yet test the second half: a gravitational waveform carries the mass–redshift degeneracy, so GW170817 measured no gravitational-wave spectral redshift to set against its host's, and its "standard siren" distance agreeing with the host's redshift, $z\approx0.01$, is *consistent with* the shared-redshift proposal rather than evidence for it. The stronger claim awaits measurements that break that degeneracy.

## XV.5 The deeper construction, deferred [S/O]

If neither $B_{\rm rep}$ nor $B_{\rm grav}$ may be the fundamental home of a history — the first houses light, the second gravity, and the principle forbids privileging either — the common home lies before they separate: in $\mathcal M$, or beneath it. The candidate is an incidence construction, two four-dimensional prospect spaces over a common three-dimensional incidence space,

$$\mathcal M = X_+\times_CX_- = \{(x_+,x_-):\pi_+(x_+) = \pi_-(x_-)\},\qquad 4+4-3 = 5$$

which produces the five-dimensional middle space by dimension count: a point of $\mathcal M$ would be an agreement between one $+$ prospect and one $-$ prospect over common relational data — the author's intersecting-leaves intuition as a fiber product rather than two foliations. Twistor theory's double fibrations are the precedent for spacetime as incidence data between deeper null structures, and the chiral $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ sectors of Part I are the obvious candidates for $X_\pm$. This is deliberately not adopted: it would be a *second theorem about* $\mathcal M$, to be proved compatible with $\mathcal M = E/U(1)_H$, not a replacement axiom, and it comes only after the bi-connection has earned its place.

## XV.6 One thing, two representations: the doubled transport [T/D/S/O]

*The author's larger ambition: that the two Born paths a photon always requires and the two connections of §XV.1 are manifestations of one representation-independent structure — one the gravitational analogue of what the other is for quantum particles — with a gauge-like freedom to offload the constraints that define a system's degrees of freedom from the quantum pair onto the Weyl decomposition and back. There is a standard doubled formalism with precisely the algebraic pattern needed for this identification.*

**The closed-time-path dictionary [T].** Quantum probabilities are double path integrals over a closed-time-path contour: a forward branch $\gamma_+$ weighted by $e^{iS[\gamma_+]/\hbar}$ and a backward branch $\gamma_-$ weighted by $e^{-iS[\gamma_-]/\hbar}$, required to close at the final time. Exchanging the branches is complex conjugation. In the Keldysh basis every doubled quantity splits into a *classical* mean and a *quantum* difference, $\varphi_{\rm cl} = \tfrac12(\varphi_++\varphi_-)$ and $\varphi_q = \tfrac12(\varphi_+-\varphi_-)$; the exchange fixes the mean and flips the difference; single-time observables see only the classical component; and the interference between branches is carried by the difference of their actions, $e^{i(S_+-S_-)/\hbar}$ — in the eikonal limit the circulation $\oint k$ of the phase form around the two-leg loop. Set beside §XV.1, line by line:

| closed-time-path | bi-connection |
|:--|:--|
| the doubled object: forward and backward branches — two *histories*, one connection | the doubled object: two *transports* around one loop, $\nabla^\pm$ |
| the classical component, the mean | $\bar\nabla = \nabla^{\rm LC}$, what matter and clocks see |
| the quantum component, the difference | $K = \tfrac12(\nabla^+-\nabla^-)$, what only pairs see |
| branch exchange, complex conjugation | $K\to-K$ |
| the contour closing at the final time | the loop $C_\Xi$ closing at the observer |
| the interference factor $e^{i(S_+-S_-)/\hbar} = e^{i\oint k}$: one form, two paths | the relative holonomy $e^{-2\oint A}$: two connections, one loop — both loop integrals, both exchange-even |
| diagonal histories see no interference | single histories see no relative holonomy |

The same mean-and-difference algebra, with the same exchange, appears in both; but the objects doubled differ — histories in one, transports in the other — and the closed-time-path branches are the doubling that computes probabilities, not by that fact the two separated stationary geodesics at a conjugate point. What is earned is that *the same mathematics of doubling appears in both*; that the two Born paths and the two connections *are one thing* remains a conjecture **[S]**, whose sharpest form §XV.7 states. What the doubling does carry is the representation independence the author asked for: the doubled structure belongs to transports, not to spin, and spin one, spin two and the metric itself are its representations. The doubling makes the adopted principle representation-independent; it does not derive it — that light and gravitational waves share one canonical cone remains the structural postulate of §XV.0.

**One complex holonomy [D].** The two legs carry a single complex relative exponent,

$$H_{\rm rel}(\Xi) = \exp\Big(\tfrac{i}{\hbar}\oint_{C_\Xi}k\;-\;2\oint_{C_\Xi}A\Big)\;\in\;\mathbb C^\times = U(1)\times\mathbb R_+$$

whose compact part is the interference phase — chromatic, read by quantum detectors as fringes, the object the static-wall no-go of §XIV.4 showed cannot be the Hubble redshift — and whose noncompact part is the dilation — achromatic, read as scale. This is a *combined* $\mathbb C^\times$-valued relative factor, and the claim that quantum phase and gravitational scale are the two parts of *one* holonomy is what §XV.7 sets out to prove — it does so for the Hopf phase and the scale, leaving the identification of the eikonal phase $\oint k$ with the Hopf phase as the spin–phase locking of Part IV seen from the optics. This is the third appearance of the same $\mathbb C^\times$: as $w = e^{-\mu+i\chi}$ in the charge branch, where the phase is the meridian angle and the modulus the chiral weight rapidity (§X.0); as Berry's phase with a size in §IX.1, where $F_H$ says how far around the fiber a loop goes and $L_H$ how far that is; and now as phase and scale of the two-leg loop. Whether these are one $\mathbb C^\times$ or three is the branch's deepest open question, and it is stated as such **[S/O]**.

**The offloading theorem [T/D].** The author's gauge flexibility is exact. If a map $\phi$ carries one leg onto the other, fixing the endpoints to first order, transporting along $\gamma_-$ with $\nabla$ equals transporting along $\gamma_+$ with the pulled-back connection $\phi^*\nabla$; so the loop holonomy of one connection around two paths *is* the relative holonomy of two connections along one path: **two paths with one connection equals one path with two connections.** When $\phi$ is a conformal deformation, $\phi^*h = e^{2\sigma}h$, the pulled-back Levi-Civita connection is exactly a Weyl-type connection with $A = d\sigma$ — checked symbolically — so deforming the legs generates precisely the bi-connection's form. But $d\sigma$ is exact, and its holonomy around every loop is trivial: **what can be offloaded into a deformation of the legs carries no redshift.** The part of a relative connection that cannot be so offloaded is, locally, its curvature $F_A$; globally a flat but non-exact connection could still carry holonomy on a non-simply-connected domain. In this architecture that loophole is closed for the scale part: $B_{\rm rep} = S^3$ is simply connected, $H^1(\mathbb{RP}^3;\mathbb R) = 0$ because $\pi_1 = \mathbb Z_2$ is torsion, and $H^1(S^4\setminus\Gamma;\mathbb R)\cong\widetilde H_2(\Gamma;\mathbb R) = 0$ for the meridian graph by Alexander duality, so every flat $\mathbb R_+$-connection is exact and the obstruction to offloading is the curvature alone **[T]**. The phase part is different, and rightly so: $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z_2,U(1)) = \mathbb Z_2$ is the sign monodromy of §XIII.9, and $H^2(S^4\setminus\Gamma)\cong\widetilde H_1(\Gamma)$ is where the Hopf classes live. And that curvature is the obstruction that sources the candidate dilation. This is the coboundary no-go of §XIV.4 in connection language, and it fixes the abstraction level the author proposed: the freedom is real, and the physics is exactly its obstruction.

**The exchange as the twin [S/O].** The pair's exchange involution may be one the theory already has. On the arena the twin map carries each half of a great circle through $p$ and $-p$ onto the other half, so the two arcs of one great circle are a twin-exchanged pair, and on the gravity slice one closed geodesic through the source is already "two legs" **[V]**. If the exchange is $\tau$, then $A$ is twin-odd, $\tau^*A = -A$, the flux through any twin-symmetric surface vanishes, and classes come in opposite-sign pairs under $\tau$ — either the sign rule §XV.3 asked for or its obstacle. That is a calculation, not yet done.

**Status [D].** Standard: the closed-time-path doubling and the Keldysh basis; the naturality of parallel transport under pull-back; the conformal transformation of the Levi-Civita connection. Derived: the dictionary; the complex relative holonomy and its split into phase and scale; that offloading is exact and its obstruction is the curvature, the global loophole being closed for the scale part. Conjectured: that the three $\mathbb C^\times$'s are one — two of them now are, the Hopf phase and the scale (§XV.7); that the exchange is the real structure, established for conjugate lifts, with the twin's role on the legs still open. Open: the dynamics that make the doubling of the *connection* physical rather than a rewriting — the same open item as §XV.4.

## XV.7 The complex connection, constructed [T/V/D/C]

*The question was why $A$ exists and what fixes $F_A$ from geometry the theory already has. The answer is analytic continuation, and it leaves no independent redshift field.*

**Construction [T/V].** On a complexification of the real locus $E$, with holomorphic coordinates $z = x+iy$ and $J\partial_x = \partial_y$, let $\mathcal A_H$ be real-analytic in compatible analytic trivializations — a smooth connection on an analytic manifold need not extend, and in the round arena everything is analytic — and let $\mathcal A_{\mathbb C}$ be a holomorphic $\mathbb C^\times$-connection, a $(1,0)$-form $a_j(z)\,dz^j$ with holomorphic coefficients. The compact real structure on $\mathbb C^\times$ — the one whose fixed set is $U(1)$ — is $w\mapsto1/\bar w$, acting on the Lie algebra as $-\mu+i\chi\mapsto+\mu+i\chi$: it flips the modulus and fixes the phase **[V]**. So the exchange $K\to-K$ of §XV.1 is $\rho_E$ acting on the $\mathbb C^\times$ part. Equivariance, $\rho_E^*\mathcal A_{\mathbb C} = -\overline{\mathcal A_{\mathbb C} }$, forces $a_j = i\,b_j$ with $b_j$ real on the real locus, and holomorphy then makes $b_j(z)$ the unique analytic continuation of $b_j(x)$:

$$\mathcal A_{\mathbb C} = i\,b_j(z)\,dz^j,\qquad \text{on }E:\quad \mathcal A_H = b_j\,dx^j\ \text{(the Hopf connection)},\qquad A = -b_j\,dy^j$$

Three consequences, checked symbolically **[V]**: $A|_{TE} = 0$ — the firewall, single real histories see only $U(1)_H$ and the metric; $A(Jw) = -\mathcal A_H(w)$ for real $w$ — along an imaginary displacement the scale connection *is* the Hopf connection along the corresponding real direction; and, by Cauchy–Riemann, the curvatures obey

$$F_A(v,Jw) = -F_H(v,w),\qquad F_A\big|_{TE\wedge TE} = 0,\qquad F_H(v,Jw) = 0\qquad(v,w\in TE)$$

Tested on the local Hopf model of §II.2, $b_\phi = \tfrac12(1-\cos\theta)$: $F_H(\partial_\theta,\partial_\phi) = \tfrac12\sin\theta$ and $F_A(\partial_\theta,J\partial_\phi) = -\tfrac12\sin\theta$, exactly **[V]**. **The Hopf connection analytically determines its own noncompact partner, uniquely.** So $A$ introduces no new independent field — but $F_A$ is determined by the *full* $\mathcal A_H$, not by its Chern class alone: Structure III deliberately leaves the connection's local, unsourced deformations unassigned, and it is exactly one of those, the mixed meridian component, that the redshift needs.

**The decisive component on the local model [V].** On $E_{\rm loc} = \mathbb R_t\times S^1_\theta\times\mathbb C^2$ with the Hopf action on $\mathbb C^2$, the quotient $\mathcal M_{\rm loc} = \mathbb R_t\times S^1_\theta\times\mathbb R^3$ has the meridian at $x = 0$ and $\partial_{\rm mer} = \partial_\theta$. A connection on the regular stratum with the right Chern class is the monopole on $\mathbb R^3$ — curvature $x\cdot dS/2r^3$, flux $2\pi$ on every linking sphere — plus a meridian component $a_\theta\,d\theta$, a time component $a_t\,dt$, and horizontal deformations $\delta A_i\,dx^i$ that the class does not fix; its mixed curvature is $F_{\theta i} = \partial_\theta A_i-\partial_ia_\theta$ in general, which in a *meridian-invariant gauge*, $\partial_\theta A_i = 0$ — an ansatz the static local model admits and which is stated here rather than assumed silently — reduces to $\bar F_H(\partial_\theta,k) = -k\cdot\nabla a_\theta$ **[V]**. The component $a_\theta$ is gauge-dependent; the mixed curvature is not, and it is the observable. The product connection gives zero; a constant $a_\theta$ is a flat Hopf-phase monodromy around the meridian and gives zero too; nothing in topology or smoothness forces $a_\theta$, which may be finite at the meridian. The component is an unsourced deformation — though not a symmetry-forbidden one, because the meridian carries an orientation from the sign of $c_1$ — and what it does to a class is worked out in §XV.3: a moment that vanishes for like parities and is symmetry-allowed, not guaranteed, for opposite ones, with the parity law itself following from twin equivariance.

**The scale character of conjugate lifts [V/D].** For a history $\widetilde\gamma_+ = \gamma+iY$ and its conjugate $\widetilde\gamma_- = \rho_E\widetilde\gamma_+$, equivariance gives ${\rm Hol}(\widetilde\gamma_-) = 1/\overline{ {\rm Hol}(\widetilde\gamma_+)}$, so the phases cancel in ${\rm Hol}(\widetilde\gamma_-)^{-1}{\rm Hol}(\widetilde\gamma_+)$ and the scales double: the mean of the two transports is the Berry phase a single history sees, their difference the scale only a pair sees — the mean-and-difference algebra of §XV.6 realized by one connection and one involution. Stokes over the complex ribbon then gives §XV.3's variation formula, $\eta_\Xi = 2\epsilon\int\bar F_H(Y,k)\,ds+O(\epsilon^3)$.

**What is conditional [C].** The construction is local and standard — a real-analytic $U(1)$-connection extends uniquely to a holomorphic $\mathbb C^\times$-connection on a neighbourhood of the real locus — and in the round arena everything is analytic. What remains conditional is the *descent*: that the scale part of this continuation on the complex shell lift is the $A$ of the middle-space bi-connection, and that the conjugate lifts of §XV.3 are its holomorphic null curves. Until that is proved, every statement above is **[D, conditional on the descent]**, and the firewall with it.

**What remains [O].** The **twin-equivariant mixed-curvature theorem**: determine from the bundle-form metric or the action whether $f_\Xi = \bar F_H(N,k)$ obeys a forced sign law, the acceptance criterion being $\int\sin(s/\ell)f_\Xi\,ds>0$ for every admissible externally rendered class with the self-return kernel of §XV.3 preserved — the parity law is derived, the sign is not (item 3 of §XI.2); the canonical imaginary width $y_0$ (item (f) of Part X); finite existence of the complex family once lumps split the degeneracy; the descent; whether the eikonal phase $\oint k$ of §XV.6 is the Hopf phase, which is the spin–phase locking of Part IV seen from the optics; and the frequency readout of a length homothety. The chain to the sky is still $\mathcal A_H\to\bar F_H(\partial_{\rm mer},k)\to y_0\to\eta_\Xi\to\omega_{\rm obs}/\omega_{\rm em}\to D(z)$, and nothing here has deduced Hubble phenomenology; what has changed is the question, from which field to invent to whether the existing Hopf connection has the mixed geometry required.
