**Thesis.** A deeper history-enriched canonical structure carries two complementary rendering modes, generated as the eigensectors of an involution and exchanged by the backtransform. A single parent $\mathfrak u(2)$-valued bi-electromagnetic connection acts on this two-mode space; each rendering projects one diagonal $U(1)$ channel as its electromagnetism and places the complementary channel in its kernel, while the off-diagonal components mix the modes. Our apparent rendering therefore sees the charged lepton as electromagnetically active and the neutrino as neutral, and the complementary rendering reverses the roles. The electroweak question is whether this parent connection, with chirality and rendering selection imposed by existing history geometry, reduces to $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y\to U(1)_{\rm em}$ rather than requiring a postulated weak fiber **[S]**. **Next construction:** the minimal parent two-mode $*$-algebra with every unitary connection compatible with the backtransform, the grading, Lorentz commutation and history rendering — the classification above is its algebraic first step — and whether its apparent projection necessarily has the electroweak algebra with Law IV exactly on the charged-lepton rendering.

## XXII.10 Offloading the deeper space into $E$: the audit [T/V/D/S/O]

*v34.0 supersession note.* In the inventory below, $B_{\rm rep}$ as "two points per gravity fiber" is the bisection readout; physical matter inhabits all of $\mathcal M$ and the gravitational source is the full-fiber reduction $\mathscr R_q$, not the two-crossing sum (Part III; §XXIX.8).

*The author's brief, in his terms: check how much of the canonical space can already take the load of the deeper space, offloading degrees of freedom into it — a toy example being to change which of the two real-structure involutions is privileged, repurposing the existing space with its redundancy. Both the middle space and the ortho-middle space should each be, qualitatively, a representation three-sphere and a meridian direction, so that neither is privileged; then the naive choice is to interpret them as literally orthogonal, not merely abstractly as functions or an algebra decomposable two ways. The theme throughout: given an $n$-dimensional output, do not build a $2n$-dimensional total space and chunk it; take less than $2n$ and constrain the mapping so that there is great redundancy while the two outputs are unrecognizable to each other — right-next-door points of one almost maximally far in the other, describing one with the other's metric or connection giving a vastly different near and far, an almost inside-out phenomenology in which an electron–neutrino interaction constrains the entire future history rather than transporting a common closeness. So not a naive quotient per branch: even monotonicity in moving out from a point can be rearranged, as if a vast reorientation of how the Hopf fibers close — the inside of a fiber in one spot being outside in another, an entire outside inside in the other mode — with history and bi-connection kept as arguments to preserve the richness and the non-arbitrariness, and the net sum of structures in the canonical total space reviewed to see whether it can already configure this.*

**The parent as a package, not a space — read this first [S].** A middle rendering is more than a quotient: it is quotient plus history class plus bi-connection transport plus Jacobi and conjugacy data plus incidence structure. So the parent is a package $\mathfrak P_\Xi = (E,\mathcal A_H,\nabla^\pm,\Xi,\mathcal J_\Xi,\mathcal R_\Xi,\ldots)$ and the two middle spaces are the outputs of two reduction functors, $\mathfrak R_\ell(\mathfrak P_\Xi) = \mathbf M_\ell$ and $\mathfrak R_\nu(\mathfrak P_\Xi) = \mathbf M_\nu$, each an enriched object of which the five-dimensional carrier is only the underlying set. The two carriers may even coincide as manifolds while the history geometries on them are inequivalent — the difference between electron-natural and neutrino-natural worlds coming from two inequivalent readings of transport on one substrate, with no extra dimension — and the backtransform is an intertwiner of packages, $\mathfrak B_\Xi:\mathfrak P_\Xi\to\mathfrak P_{\mathfrak B\Xi}$ with $\mathfrak R_\nu\circ\mathfrak B_\Xi\simeq\mathfrak R_\ell$, acting on $\nabla^\pm$, $\mathcal A_H$ and the Jacobi and return data, not merely exchanging two line fields. **The quotient supplies the carrier; history-dependent transport supplies the experienced geometry.** Everything below is to be read in that order: the canonical two-plane says why exactly two modes; the history package says why the two worlds look inside-out to each other. This is Part XV's own ambition — the middle geometry as the symmetric resolution of two deeper transports — taken more seriously, not a new arena.

**The inventory, stated no more globally than $E$ is [D].** The frozen canonical total space is six-dimensional with local model $\mathbb R_t\times S^1_{\rm mer}\times\mathbb C^2$, the Hopf circle acting on $\mathbb C^2$ and space arising as its Hopf quotient; the middle space is $\mathcal M = E/U(1)_H$; $B_{\rm rep}$ is an *embedded bisection* of $\mathcal M$, two points per gravity fiber; and $B_{\rm grav} = \mathcal M/U_{\rm mer}$ is the *quotient* by the meridian structure. On the regular stratum $E^\circ$ carries one principal Hopf-circle direction $V_H$ and one invariant transverse meridian *line structure* $\widetilde V_{\rm mer}$ — Law II's regular part is a foliation and its static singular case a pencil with common poles, not a free circle action, so the meridian may be represented circlewise only in regular closed-leaf regions — spanning a rank-two plane $\mathcal D = V_H\oplus\widetilde V_{\rm mer}$. The two-mode structure the author wants is the pair of reductions by one line each: $E/V_H = \mathcal M$, time $\times$ the spatial three-sphere with the meridian as residual direction; and $E/\widetilde V_{\rm mer}$, a local or regular leaf space rather than an assured global five-manifold, time $\times$ the shell $\mathbb C^2\supset S^3$ with the Hopf phase as residual circle, space unresolved there, a point of space being a whole Hopf circle of shell states. **The local canonical model thus exhibits a dimensionally symmetric exchange of the two reduction directions** — $6\to5+5$ as two overlapping readouts of one space, not ten degrees of freedom, each rendering retaining the direction the other removed. Whether this globalizes to two equivalent middle-type renderings is open, and the firewall of Parts XIX–XXI applies: $S^3_{\rm rep}$, the static spatial representative slice, and $S^3_{\rm shell}\subset\mathbb C^2$, the fixed-radius Hopf total space, occupy the same geometric slot without being the same physical representation. And since one global $E$ gluing the local shell constructions is itself open, none of this is more global than $E$.

**Orthogonality, exactly and with its typing [D].** The primitive upstairs meridian datum is only $U(1)_H$-invariant and transverse to the Hopf fiber; lifts of the descended meridian line differ by vertical components, and the canonical connection supplies the horizontal representative. The exact statement is that the Hopf vertical is orthogonal to the $\mathcal A_H$-*horizontal* representative of the meridian direction: $A_H(K^{\rm hor}_{\rm mer}) = 0$, so in $\hat g = \pi^*g_{\mathcal M}+R_H^2\vartheta^2$, $\hat g(K_H,K^{\rm hor}_{\rm mer}) = 0$ **[D]** — the author's literal orthogonality, as directions upstairs, which is the only place it means anything; the output metrics are not called orthogonal. The primitive lift is not silently identified with its horizontalization: quotienting by two different lifts of one downstairs line can give different leaf geometry, and the vertical discrepancy between the primitive meridian lift and its canonical horizontalization is a candidate carrier of history information **[O]**.

**The common reduction is $B_{\rm grav}$, and the corrected diamond [V/D].** The Hopf vertical commutes with the horizontal meridian direction and with the horizontal lift of any spatial field, $[K_H,K^{\rm hor}_{\rm mer}] = 0$, $[K_H,\widetilde X] = 0$ **[V]**, so on the regular stratum $\mathcal D$ is Frobenius integrable and the common two-direction reduction exists, of dimension $6-2 = 4$ — *and it is $B_{\rm grav} = E/(V_H\oplus\widetilde V_{\rm mer})$*, the gravity base, not $B_{\rm rep}$, which is a resolved bisection above $\mathcal M$ and not a quotient of it. The diamond is
$$E\ \longrightarrow\ \mathcal M_\ell = E/V_H,\quad \mathcal M_\nu = E/\widetilde V_{\rm mer}\ \longrightarrow\ B_{\rm grav} = E/\mathcal D,$$
each middle rendering reaching the gravity base by quotienting the direction the other rendering removed, and it reads better than the version it corrects: **gravity is the common, rendering-independent reduction of both modes; electromagnetic and matter accessibility belong to a chosen resolution above it.** Our representational spacetime remains $B^{(\ell)}_{\rm rep}\hookrightarrow\mathcal M_\ell$, and the neutrino-natural construction should seek its own $B^{(\nu)}_{\rm rep}\hookrightarrow\mathcal M_\nu$, the two resolved slices not required to coincide — *same gravitational class downstairs, two radically different matter resolutions upstairs*, with the weak vertex relating the two slices through the history-enriched correspondence: gravity sees what both renderings agree on, electromagnetism sees one resolved rendering, the weak interaction transports between the resolutions.

**The correspondence and the multivalued near/far [V/D].** The two projections define $\mathcal C_E = \{(\pi_\ell(e),\pi_\nu(e))\}\subset\mathcal M_\ell\times\mathcal M_\nu$, six-dimensional on the regular transverse locus inside a ten-dimensional product: not the graph of a map, which is the redundancy asked for. Each point of one rendering has a whole circle of correspondents in the other, so the invariant fact is *multivaluedness*: with $\Delta_{\ell\to\nu}(x) = {\rm diam}_{d_\nu}\{y:(x,y)\in\mathcal C_E\}$, the bare Hopf correspondence already has $\Delta_{\ell\to\nu}(x) = \pi$ — one spatial point represented by shell states at every phase, at shell distance up to $\pi$ — while the Hopf map is Lipschitz, spatial distance at most twice the shell distance for nearby states, so close on the shell implies close in space **[V]**. That is the germ of the author's near/far, and the target is stronger: $\Delta_{\ell\to\nu}$ and $\Delta_{\nu\to\ell}$ as nontrivial history-dependent quantities with folds, caustics and branching. The kill test in precise form: **if the backtransform descends to a global bi-Lipschitz identification of $(\mathcal M_\ell,d_\ell)$ with $(\mathcal M_\nu,d_\nu)$, the intended mechanism has failed**; the Jacobi and bi-connection data are arguments, not decoration.

**Where the weak sector may live, and where it must not [D/V].** Since the integrable plane is precisely what gives the common gravitational quotient, the non-abelian sector must *not* be sought in a history-dependent failure of Frobenius integrability, $[K_{\ell,\Xi},K_{\nu,\Xi}]\notin\mathcal D_\Xi$ — that would destroy the shared quotient the frozen gravitational architecture needs. The safer route keeps the reduction plane integrable and lets the *connection on the two mode labels* carry the curvature: the Frobenius curvature of the canonical plane and the gauge holonomy of the history-dependent two-mode bundle are different things, and the second is to carry the weak interaction while the first stays zero. This has been computed. With the canonical orthogonal frame $(K_H,K_{\rm mer})$ the induced connection on the plane bundle is diagonal, $\mathfrak u(1)\oplus\mathfrak u(1)$, and all curvature components commute — no mode mixing from the canonical structure **[V/D]**. A history-dependent polarization that rotates the mode frame by a field $\alpha(x)$ produces exactly the $\mathfrak u(2)$ *form* of §XXII.9 — off-diagonal components $W\propto d\alpha$ and $(a_H-a_{\rm mer})\sin2\alpha$ **[V]** — but its curvature is a gauge transform of the diagonal one, its holonomy still abelian: **a single frame rotation gives the form and not the substance** **[V/D]**. Genuine non-abelian holonomy requires off-diagonal transport that is not the rotation of one diagonal transport — with an independent off-diagonal field the curvature components no longer commute **[V]** — which in the theory's terms means *the two Weyl-type transports $\nabla^+$, $\nabla^-$ carrying the mode frame differently, so that no single frame diagonalizes both* **[D]**. The reduction plane stays integrable throughout; the non-abelian content is entirely in the label transport; and the criterion is the v26 lesson again — one transport is abelian and tame, two independent ones are not. That is the theorem target: derive the history-dependent connection on the two reduction labels from $\nabla^\pm$, keeping the plane integrable, and determine whether its holonomy is genuinely $U(2)$.

**Two typings kept honest [S].** The existing pair $(\rho,\sigma_{[N]})$ is not the charged/ortho pair: their fixed geometries are of compact and split type respectively, while both renderings here must be of one compact type; the better use of the author's real-structure intuition is a second compact real structure generated by the backtransform, $\rho_\nu = \mathfrak B_\Xi\rho_\ell\mathfrak B_\Xi^{-1}$, two compact slices of one complex parent, with the split structure helping to select or orient $\mathfrak B_\Xi$. A Hopf fiber, being a circle, has no inside or outside; the intuition survives typed as *a direction removed as vertical in one rendering survives as horizontal, relational structure in the other*, made global and non-arbitrary by the history dependence of the polarization. And the two-state carrier is not the literal complexified plane $\mathbb C\otimes(V_\ell\oplus V_\nu)$, which would still transform as geometry: as generation was a multiplicity space and not a vector, $W_{\rm bi}$ is the *multiplicity or mode-label bundle associated with the two canonical reductions*, the plane explaining why there are two slots and the descent making them internal, with $[{\rm Spin}(1,3),W_{\rm bi}] = 0$ to be proved. **Result of the audit:** the two modes, their orthogonality, their common four-dimensional reduction — $B_{\rm grav}$ — and the multivalued near/far are already configured by the frozen canonical space on its regular stratum; everything that makes the two worlds inside-out and the label connection non-abelian is exactly the history-dependent part, still to be constructed. Wherever the earlier sections say "a deeper space," read *a deeper history and polarization structure on the existing canonical space*.

## XXII.11 Branch symmetry, solution asymmetry [S/O]

*The author's question: how to make the laws symmetric to both cases — in the ortho-middle space its own fiber lengths relying on how its quotient to the gravity base behaves — while allowing the matter distribution to be such that the canonical middle-space meridian is the one visibly privileged as "the meridian," so that electrons rather than neutrinos are the accessible ones.*

**The principle:** the laws should not know which mode is electron and which is neutrino. They are to be written on the parent history geometry invariant under $\ell\leftrightarrow\nu$, $V_\ell\leftrightarrow V_\nu$, $\mathcal M_\ell\leftrightarrow\mathcal M_\nu$; that our world uses one mode as its resolved rendering is a property of the solution, not of the laws. Write the two canonical directions as $V_0$, $V_1$ before naming either, with $\mathcal M_a = E/V_a$ and $B_{\rm grav} = E/(V_0\oplus V_1)$, each rendering reaching the gravity base by quotienting the direction the other removed; only after a solution chooses does one write $V_0 = V_H$, $V_1 = V_{\rm mer}$ and call $\mathcal M_0$ our middle space, the ortho solution reversing the reading. Law I already lives on $B_{\rm grav}$ and does two jobs, the gravitational geometry there and the canonical fiber length; its symmetric lift assigns a length matrix to the whole plane, $G_{AB}[g_G,\Xi]$, $A,B\in\{0,1\}$, with the exchange rule $G[g_G,\mathfrak B\Xi] = \sigma_xG[g_G,\Xi]\sigma_x$ — in the simplest phase $G = L^2\delta_{AB}$, more generally $G = L_0^2P_0+L_1^2P_1$ with $L_0[\mathfrak B\Xi] = L_1[\Xi]$ — so that each rendering gets the same law, *gravity-base geometry $\mapsto$ the length of the direction hidden in that rendering*, ours $g_G\mapsto L_H$ and the ortho rendering's $g_G\mapsto L_{\rm ortho}$, related by the backtransform rather than by a second law. **The selection is not in gravity:** the common quotient stays blind to the distinction. It is a derived rendering selector $P$ on the mode bundle, $P^2 = P$, ${\rm rank}\,P = 1$, the parent laws invariant under $P\mapsto I-P$, our solution occupying $P = P_\ell$ — the author's matter-distribution intuition as a variational selection rule, a parent functional $\mathcal S_{\rm render}[P;\Xi,\Psi,g_G]$ with $\mathcal S_{\rm render}[P;\Xi,\Psi] = \mathcal S_{\rm render}[I-P;\mathfrak B\Xi,\mathfrak B\Psi]$ whose two symmetry-related stationary branches are $P_\ell$ and $P_\nu$. Charged leptons being accessible then means *our history solution lies on the $P_\ell$ branch*; spontaneous breaking in form, not called Higgs-like before an action exists. Law IV follows the selector: one parent connection $\mathbb A$, the apparent electromagnetic connection $A^{(P)}_{\rm em} = P\mathbb AP$, ours $P_\ell\mathbb AP_\ell$ and the ortho branch's $P_\nu\mathbb AP_\nu$, with $\mathfrak BA^{(\ell)}_{\rm em}\mathfrak B^{-1} = A^{(\nu)}_{\rm em}$ — each mode with its own electromagnetism, neither a second photon beside ours. And "meridian" becomes branch-relative: the parent contains two complementary canonical directions, and a rendering $P$ defines $V_{\rm hidden}(P)$, the direction quotiented first, and $V_{\rm mer}(P)$, the surviving localization direction in the five-dimensional rendering — exchanged under the backtransform. That is the author's topological swapping of meridians and Hopf fibers, as a definition.

**The serious constraint, and the kill tests [O].** Frozen structure gives the two directions different intrinsic jobs: the Hopf direction has unit Chern class and comes from spin geometry; the meridian is Law II's localization and gravity-reduction structure, a singular great-circle pencil in the static limit rather than a principal circle. So the exchange is not declared a symmetry of the bare manifold; if it is a symmetry at all, it is one of the whole package $(E,\mathcal A_H,\nabla^\pm,\Xi,\mathcal J,\ldots)$, with history and bi-connection data converting one apparent role into the other — which is the author's insistence, again, as a requirement. **The difficult theorem:** can the history-enriched package make these apparently different structures two branchwise presentations of one deeper object? **Kill tests:** the exchange must preserve the parent action; both branches must reproduce the same $B_{\rm grav}$ and Law I; each branch must have an analogous Law IV; the selector $P$ must be derivable from matter and history data rather than stipulated; our branch must be stable — ordinary environments must not flip $P_\ell\leftrightarrow P_\nu$; and branch selection must leave the off-diagonal weak connection alive while making only one diagonal $U(1)$ electromagnetically visible. If these pass: *electrons are not fundamentally more real or accessible than neutrinos; our realized middle-space branch is the one in which the electron channel defines the resolved electromagnetic geometry, and from the ortho branch the converse holds* — **branch symmetry, solution asymmetry.**



*v34.1 (R77).* The exchange test is restated for the full-middle-space ontology in §XXIX.14: both presentations must reduce the **same** parent configuration to the same base source and the same quotient constraint, with transformed fiber-length laws, and the test is for symmetry-related states, not arbitrary pairs. Nothing here identifies the singular meridian pencil with a principal Hopf circle as bare manifolds; the exchange, if it exists, acts on enriched reductions with core data. The Law II restatement of Part III now carries the branch-symmetry requirement as condition (iii).

## XXII.12 The pole resolved: the interlocking core, Hopfian linking, and the exterior conditions [T/V/D/S/O]

*The author's proposal, in his terms: the point where the meridians meet need not be a point — it may topologically be something like Hopf fibers over two-sphere shells, or more generally something admitting a stress-energy-oriented generation per the ortho-middle space, molded so that it approximates a three-sphere with in-facing meridians while toward the true center the meridians go haywire as the topological cost is finally bagged there; this interplaying with the idea that where the meridians meet, as a contingency of the net matter distribution, the stress-energy switches from exterior-type to interior-type, with as much matter away from the center of mass as toward it. Made specific: if there is truly no privileging of electrons over neutrinos, the meridians are of the same stuff as the Hopf fibers — in the ortho-middle space its own upstairs Hopf fibers* are *the meridians — so, without demanding the matter isotropy that gives the apparent middle space Hopf fibers on shells, there should be a phenomenology of "Hopfian linking" extending to the general structure through the gravity-base constraint on the meridians via the ortho-middle space. The fixed point in theory space: an effective interior region deep inside the enclosed space of the apparent three-sphere, our own representation three-sphere lying beyond it in the exterior, with the contingent constraint on matter that the meridians' interlocking happens in the interior in a relatively tight region rather than at a single point of intersection — the topological storing spent directly there — and a smooth interpolating threshold between. What the central dark-matter seed actually needs is only that on a three-sphere of the effective exterior (1) the meridians are locally roughly orthogonal to it, (2) they are arranged roughly as radially ingoing, and (3) a meridian on one side roughly follows through to the antipodal side when it returns; the interior matter distribution is what makes this so.*

**Why this attacks an open place rather than a new one.** The frozen static model's antipodal great-circle pencil — all meridians through two poles — is a structural assumption, not something forced by Law 0 or topology; the global completion of $E$ is unresolved precisely at the poles where meridians meet, while the local canonical completion already produces Hopf bundles on small linking spheres; and the topology already records a cost there: with $N$ secondary meridians the removed set is a graph with the poles as vertices and $H^2(S^4\setminus\Gamma;\mathbb Z)\simeq\mathbb Z^{2N-1}$, one fewer independent Hopf class than arcs — *when many meridian branches meet at a pole, their linking topology cannot be assigned independently.* The author's proposal replaces "all meridians intersect at $p$" by "there is an interior interlocking region $\mathcal I$ in which the meridian family undergoes its nontrivial linking," with the pencil the exterior approximation, and the four requirements are: (1) replace the exact pole by a finite interlocking core $\mathcal I$, the apparent rendering divided into interior $\mathcal I_\ell$, transition $\mathcal T_\ell$ and exterior $\mathcal E_\ell\ni S^3_{\rm rep}$; (2) a branch-symmetric parent linking law for both reduction modes; (3) the three exterior conditions recovered; (4) the core's size, transition and polarization derived from matter and history data. **Regression requirement:** the old pole model is the zero-core-size limit, ${\rm diam}\,\mathcal I\to0$ returning the great circles through $\pm p$, so everything computed from the static pencil remains the zeroth-order approximation.

**Two constructions, kept apart.** A *blow-up* replaces a point by its directions and creates no metric region: it is the kinematic resolution of the zero-core singular limit. A *finite Hopfion core* is a dynamical regularization selected by matter and history, with $r_c\to0$ recovering the blow-up and pencil limit in the appropriate sense. §XXII.12 treats them in that order and does not slide between them.

**The pole is a point only after quotienting: the blow-up [D/C].** Replace $p\in S^4$ by its oriented real blow-up, $\beta^{-1}(p)\simeq S(T_pS^4)\simeq S^3_p$, the sphere of directions through it. Every meridian that "hit the same point" now reaches $S^3_p$ at its incoming tangent direction, so the apparently coincident endpoints are resolved into distinct points — the center topologically squeezed to a point by the rendering, as the author put it. The static meridians are unoriented, $C_n = C_{-n}$, while the incoming direction distinguishes $n$ from $-n$: the oriented history resolution sees $S^3_p$ and forgetting orientation gives $S^3_p/\{\pm1\}\simeq\mathbb{RP}^3$, which has the topology of the static gravity slice $\Sigma_{\rm grav}$. Same diffeomorphism type is not same geometrical object, and the identification is *proved* for the ideal pencil rather than noticed: the meridian through $p$ with tangent line $[n]$ is the great circle $\cos s\,p+\sin s\,n$, which meets the equatorial $S^3_{\rm rep}$ exactly at $\pm n$ **[V]**, so the map $\Phi_p:S(T_pS^4)/\{\pm1\}\to\Sigma_{\rm grav}$, unoriented pole direction $\mapsto$ global meridian class, is a diffeomorphism, and the bisection $S^3_{\rm rep}\to\Sigma_{\rm grav}$ is the double cover $x\mapsto[x]$ **[D, exact for the pencil]**. Beyond the pencil, "the gravity base is what remains when the oriented resolution of the pole is forgotten" is a proposal **[S/O]**. And if the canonical complex structure identifies $T_pS^4\simeq\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb C^2$ — the missing theorem being that the $\mathbb C^2$ structure defined around individual meridians extends canonically to the blow-up — then $S^3_p$ carries the Hopf fibration and its Hopf circles are the families of meridians whose directions span one complex line, the great two-spheres through the poles: the author's "Hopf fibers over two-sphere shells," conditional **[D/C]**. The two renderings would treat the stratum oppositely — collapsed to $p$ in the charged rendering, an extended shell in the ortho rendering, one point in one rendering a whole shell in the other **[S]** — with two centers, the rendered $p_{\rm app}$ and the canonical stratum $\mathcal E_p\simeq S^3$, $p_{\rm app} = \mathcal E_p/\!\sim$.

**The interlocking core: a Hopfion texture, and three separate invariants [V/T].** Take a localized Hopfion polarization *texture* $\mathbf n(\mathbf x)$ on the two-mode label space — genuinely spatial, with a spherically symmetric envelope of scale $r_c$, constant $\hat z$ outside the core; a purely radial $\mathbf n(r)$ factors through an interval and carries no invariant at all, which the toy's first attempt confirmed by giving zero. With the core a ball whose boundary polarization is constant, $B^3/\partial B^3\simeq S^3$, so $\mathbf n$ defines a class in $\pi_3(S^2)\simeq\mathbb Z$, the Hopf invariant $H[\mathbf n] = \tfrac{1}{4\pi^2}\int A\wedge F$ of the Berry connection of $P = \tfrac12(I+\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\tau)$. **This is not the shell's Hopf class**: the shell carries $c_1\in H^2(S^2;\mathbb Z)$, the core carries $H\in\pi_3(S^2)$ — both use the Hopf map and they are different topological statements. Three objects are then computed separately, because they are separate. The exterior first-Chern charge $c_1(S^2_R) = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^2_R}F$ is zero on every enclosing sphere, below $10^{-2}$ at radii $0.5$, $1$, $3$ **[V]**: *the mode texture carries no exterior monopole charge*, so the exterior congruence is trivializable — a statement about the mode bundle, with nothing gravitational inferred from it, since gravity sees $T^{(g)}$ on $B_{\rm grav}$ and not a Chern number unless an action relates them. The core Hopf invariant is $\pm1$: the preimages of two mode states are two closed curves forming a Hopf link, Gauss linking number $0.993$ in magnitude at $r_c = 0.7$ **[V]**, conserved under smooth admissible deformations within a fixed sector by homotopy invariance **[T]** — not "immutable by matter": it can change if the order parameter becomes undefined, the boundary condition changes, a defect crosses the boundary, or a singular topology-changing event occurs, which an action and a defect theory would have to govern. Within a sector, matter determines the core's metric realization — tight or broad, spherical or distorted, centered or displaced, its transition sharp or gradual — while $H$ is fixed. This gives the author's "topological storing spent in the core" a candidate invariant: $c_1^{\rm exterior} = 0$ and $H_{\rm core}\neq0$, topologically nontrivial without advertising a flux outside. What it does *not* yet give is "the meridians interlock": the linked curves are level sets of the mode polarization, not the integral curves of the physical meridian field, and *whether the history-derived meridian congruence coincides with, or canonically threads, the linked fibers of the core map* is the theorem target that would make the interlocking literal **[O]**; until then, **Hopfion linking is a candidate topology for the meridian core.** The third object is the core holonomy $U_\gamma = \mathcal P\exp(-\int_\gamma\mathbb A_{\rm mode})$ along a physical path. Along a loop of the mode sphere that is a great circle the Berry phase is $e^{-i\Omega/2}$ with $\Omega = 2\pi$, i.e. $-1$ **[V]**, which *supplies a candidate geometric representative of the twin continuation sign* — but along actual straight paths through a Hopfion core the phase is a continuous function of the path ranging over $[-\pi,\pi]$, with three per cent of random lines within $0.1$ of $\pm\pi$ **[V]**. So $U_{\mathcal I} = -1$ is not universal; the identification with the twin requires the meridian congruence to select paths whose polarization loop is a great circle, and an intertwining diagram showing that the core holonomy induces the existing twin action on the appropriate descended field — the theory has several $\mathbb Z_2$'s with different jobs, and this one is not identified with any of them yet **[O]**. The exchange symmetry of §XXII.11 is nonetheless most fully realized where the exterior labels fail: in the exterior $V_0\simeq V_H$ and $V_1\simeq V_{\rm mer}$ are cleanly polarized; through the core $D\mathbf n\neq0$ and the two cannot be diagonalized in the exterior basis — *the interior is where the parent symmetric structure is manifest.* And the branch symmetry of the invariant itself is exact: if the backtransform acts on the target sphere as a rotation, $H[\mathfrak B\cdot\mathbf n] = H[\mathbf n]$, reversed only by an orientation-reversing action **[T]** — *the parent Hopf invariant survives while "Hopf" and "meridian" exchange interpretations*, which is the author's "same stuff" as an invariant statement.

**The exterior-to-interior switch, made invariant, and what it demands [V/D].** "As much matter away from the center as toward it" depends on how distance and matter are weighted on a compact curved space; the invariant form uses the transverse Jacobi map of the meridian congruence and its expansion $\Theta = {\rm tr}(\dot JJ^{-1})$, with three transverse modes: for the great-circle pencil from the equator, $J(s) = \cos s\,I_3$, $\Theta = -3\tan s$, $\det J = \cos^3s$, vanishing at $s = \pi/2$ — the pole is a caustic, all meridians through one point **[V]**. Remove the tidal focusing in a core of half-width $0.4$ and the caustic dissolves, $\min|J| = 0.027>0$, with $\Theta$ passing continuously from the focusing exterior branch to the expanding interior branch **[V, toy]** — a proof of geometric possibility, not a derivation from matter. Inverting the requirement is more telling: for any smooth caustic-free bridge $J$ through the core, the tidal term $K = -\ddot J/J$ that the profile requires is $+1$ outside and *negative* inside — $-33$, $-7$, $-2.4$ for cores of half-width $0.3$, $0.5$, $0.8$ **[V]** — so **a finite core requires the meridian sectional curvature to change sign: the interior must carry a defocusing tidal term of opposite sign to the exterior's.** That is the author's exterior-type/interior-type switch made invariant — a sign change of the tidal term along the meridians, its location contingent on the distribution — and the open matter calculation is which stress-energy profile, through $T_{\mu\nu}\to R_{\mu\nu}\to J$, realizes it. After resolution the histories need not end at the center but continue through the exceptional data onto the interior branch. **Two caveats.** The blow-up does not by itself fix the metric problem of the semi-free completion — the Hopf orbit shrinking on the restored meridian while the Law-I locking grows toward a source — and how $L_H$ behaves near $S^3_p$, and the ortho length under the exchanged rendering, is a genuine metric-extension theorem **[O]**. And the branch-symmetric treatment of the source is a requirement on the action, not a topological fact: an ortho-natural distribution on the exceptional stratum and a compact central source must push forward to one gravitational source on $B_{\rm grav}$, $(q_\ell)_*T_\ell = (q_\nu)_*T_\nu = T^{(g)}$ — *gravity sees the invariant, matter sees the rendering* **[S/O]**.

**v34.1 status marks and the bridge to Part XXIX (R76).** Three objects in this section have three different standings and are not to be slid between: *(a)* the oriented real **blow-up** of the pole — kinematic, exact for the ideal pencil, a $S^3$ (or $\mathbb{RP}^3$) of directions with no metric extent and no matter; *(b)* the **finite Hopfion core** — a candidate dynamical regularization carrying $H\in\pi_3(S^2)$, computed for a *polarization texture*, whose linked preimage curves are **not** shown to be meridian trajectories (an explicit intertwining map from the texture to the integral curves of Law II is the missing theorem); *(c)* the **physical interlocking interior** of Entries 157–158 — matter, metric extent and a boundary matching law, none constructed. The exterior-to-interior tidal sign change is a *scalar, isotropic Jacobi toy*, not a theorem for every congruence. What Part XXIX adds is the reason this section is now central rather than decorative: Toy C's uniform closure image depends on a directional datum at the pole that the ideal point does not supply (§XXIX.10), and the finite interior is the physical place where that datum — the core-to-base directional measure $\nu_{\mathcal I}$ of §XXIX.14 — would be determined; the first-order secondary test of §XXIX.12 likewise leaves exactly a core-internal residual. The old pole model is the ${\rm diam}\,\mathcal I\to0$ limit of this one, and only the three exterior conditions are used downstream.

## XXIII.0 The thesis, retyped [S]

Not a hidden $SU(2)_R$ gauge group added to our spacetime with a heavy $W_R$: that is the left–right-symmetric route, and it is what collider searches bound. The proposal is that **weak chirality is not a primitive asymmetry of the parent laws.** There is one parent two-mode weak algebra and one connection (§XXII.9); the rendering selector determines which Weyl chirality admits its local non-abelian realization. A solution chooses the charged-lepton rendering, in which only the left-handed realization descends locally; the complementary right-handed realization belongs to the neutrino-natural rendering $\mathcal M_\nu$ and becomes inaccessible *at the same step* by which that rendering becomes inaccessible. From our rendering, right-handed weak isospin is not a small interaction waiting at higher energy: its local support is absent. The right-handed rank-one structure of §XXII.8's target would then be the projection of a rank-two structure whose other half belongs to $\mathcal M_\nu$, not a fundamentally absent doublet.

**The right-handed charge is not inserted.** With one photon for both chiralities — required by the Dirac mass term, which demands equal charge across chiralities — and the entire traceless part gated off on the right sector in our rendering, the right-handed electron's photon coupling comes only from the central character, so $e\,Y_R/2 = -e$ forces $Y_R = -2$ **[D, conditional on the gate]**: the Standard Model's value, *forced once the electromagnetic charge $-1$, the common photon and the central normalization $Q = T_3+Y/2$ are fixed* — those remain premises, so hypercharge is constrained rather than derived geometrically; what is gained is that $Y_R$ no longer has to be assigned independently. The right-handed $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ closes upstairs in the conventional sense — as an ordinary endomorphism algebra on the common parent bundle $S_D\otimes W_{\rm bi}$ over the history package, *before* either rendering functor is applied, where $[T^+_R,T^-_R] = 2T_{3R}$ holds as usual; the two reductions then send different portions of that one algebra to different rendered categories, and it does not descend as an algebra of local endomorphisms over $B^{(\ell)}_{\rm rep}$. ## XXIII.3 Empirical invisibility: no interpolation, and an exact absence [D/O]

A first draft made the right-handed weight a continuous leakage parameter $\epsilon = \tfrac12(1+s_\varphi)$ of an "impure" selector. That is the sharp difference from left–right-symmetric models, which place $SU(2)_R$ in our spacetime with a heavy $W_R$: those experiments are applying the wrong rendering functor, and the prediction here is an exact absence, falsifiable by any observed right-handed charged current **[D/O]**.

## XXIII.4 Anomaly cancellation, rendering by rendering [T/D]

The author's stance is adopted, and the gate makes it exact. Anomaly cancellation is a condition on the local quantum theory of a rendering, summed over the fields that are local *in that rendering*; the ortho fields are not local in ours, so they do not enter, and there is no summing across renderings. With the gate, our rendering's chiral lepton content is precisely the Standard Model's — a left-handed doublet with $Y = -1$, a right-handed charged singlet with $Y = -2$, and a sterile $\nu_R$ with $Y = 0$ contributing nothing — so the arithmetic of the Standard Model applies unchanged: the $SU(2)^2U(1)$ condition reads $N_cY_Q+Y_L = 0$, i.e. $N_cY_Q = 1$ — satisfied by the observed three colors with $Y_Q = \tfrac13$, and the cubic and mixed conditions close with $u_R$, $d_R$ at $\tfrac43$, $-\tfrac23$. Anomaly cancellation alone does not derive both the color multiplicity and $Y_Q$: if $Y_Q = \tfrac13$ is independently established it demands $N_c = 3$, and if $N_c = 3$ is known it gives $Y_Q = \tfrac13$. The ortho rendering must cancel its own, with the mirror content and its own quark completion. **Consequence:** the quark sector is no longer a deferred extension but mandatory for anomaly cancellation in our rendering, the observed three-color, standard-hypercharge assignment supplying the familiar anomaly-free completion, with the derivation of the color multiplicity a separate problem — and whatever cancels the leptons is a multiplicity on quarks alone, not generation, since generations replicate leptons and quarks alike, which is the firewall $\mathbb C^3_{\rm generation}\neq\mathbb C^3_{\rm color}$ made mandatory.

## XXIII.5 Status, the four outcomes, kill tests [S/O]

Of the four outcomes the brief distinguishes — the geometry cannot support the chirality exchange; it supports it but hypercharge stays by hand; it supports chirality and the $\ell_R$ charge but fails gauge or anomaly consistency; it yields a genuinely derived chiral representation — the branch stands at the third: the gate is derived up to one $\mathbb Z_2$ sign (§XXIII.6), the $\ell_R$ charge and the sterility of $\nu_R$ follow rather than being inserted, and the vector-like alternative is excluded only by observation; gauge dynamics and the now-mandatory quark completion are untested. **Kill tests:** (1) selector-gated chirality must arise from the existing selector, connection and history geometry without a new field; (2) the cross-rendered right doublet must descend with $\ell_R$ local in $\mathcal M_\ell$ and its partner and ladders local only in $\mathcal M_\nu$; (3) the ladder operators as inter-rendering morphisms must close the full algebra upstairs; (4) no construction keeping $T_{3R}$ *as the Cartan of a claimed gauged $SU(2)_R$* with $T^\pm_R\to0$ without a genuine breaking mechanism — an autonomous gauged $U(1)_R$, as in the minimal parent of §XXIII.10, is closed and is not that construction; (5) the backtransform must never be identified with bare parity acting *within one rendering*; what §XXIII.6 permits is a sheet exchange whose spinorial intertwiner is $\gamma^0$ between parity-conjugate sheet actions, and a $\gamma^5$ gate is acceptable only from a Lorentz-covariant selector; (6) no ordinary local right-handed charged current — exactly none, by charge superselection — and no additional $Z$-coupled light neutrino, cross-rendering mixing confined to the neutrino mass term; (7) a Pauli algebra is not a gauge theory — local redundancy, dynamics, and local and global anomalies in both renderings, quarks included; (8) the backtransform relates channels, not masses, and Dirac versus Majorana is tested separately. **Theorem target:** from the existing parent history geometry and an exchange-odd rendering selector $\varphi$, derive a Lorentz-covariant connection whose non-abelian two-mode component descends as $P_L\,\mathfrak{su}(2)$ on $\mathcal M_\ell$ and $P_R\,\mathfrak{su}(2)$ on $\mathcal M_\nu$, while the selected $\mathcal M_\ell$ theory contains a charged right-handed singlet with $Q = -1$, no local right-handed charged current, and exactly the observed left-handed doublet. The goal is not a hidden right-handed force; it is to test whether the empirical absence of right-handed weak isospin in our spacetime is the observable shadow of losing the neutrino rendering.

## XXIII.6 The gate derived up to one sign: the invariant chirality projector of the two-sheet space [V/D/O]

*The route suggested at the end of §XXIII.1, tried.* Part XXII found that reversing the split part of a transport acts on Dirac spinors as conjugation by $\gamma^0$ (§XXII.8), and read that as a failure of the Lorentz test. Taken seriously instead, it says the two sheets carry *parity-conjugate* Lorentz actions: $D_\ell = D(g)$ on the charged-lepton sheet and $D_\nu = \gamma^0D(g)\gamma^0$ on the neutrino sheet, since the split sign is what distinguishes the two Weyl sectors — in the Weyl basis the boost generators are $K = \gamma^5\Sigma$, chirality times spin, so reversing the boosts is reversing the sign of $\gamma^5$ in the generators. Three things then follow, all computed.

**The Lorentz test, in its correct form, is passed by the parity-including exchange [V].** On $S_D\otimes W_{\rm bi}$ with the sheet-dependent action $\mathcal D(g) = P_\ell\otimes D(g)+P_\nu\otimes\gamma^0D(g)\gamma^0$, the exchange $\mathfrak B_{\rm full} = \sigma_x\otimes\gamma^0$ — sheet swap times the intertwiner — commutes with $\mathcal D(g)$ for random elements of $SL(2,\mathbb C)$, while the bare swap $\sigma_x\otimes1$ does not **[V]**. So the exchange that includes $\gamma^0$ is not a violation of Lorentz covariance but its *equivariant* form once the sheets carry conjugate actions; §XXII.8's verdict is refined accordingly (an erratum in spirit to the frozen part, recorded here). Consistently, the only Lorentz-covariant cross current between sheets is $\nu^\dagger\gamma^\mu\ell$ with no $\gamma^0$ in the neutrino adjoint **[V]** — the standard current of the *aligned* field $\gamma^0\nu$ — and it pairs the neutrino sheet's own-label $R$ with the charged sheet's $L$, which after alignment is our $L$ **[V]**.

**There is an exchange-invariant, Lorentz-invariant chirality projector, and it is the gate [V/D].** $\Pi = \tfrac12(1+\Gamma\otimes\gamma^5)$ is a projector that commutes with the total Lorentz action *and* with $\mathfrak B_{\rm full}$ **[V]**: on the charged-lepton sheet ($\Gamma = -1$) it is $P_L$, on the neutrino sheet ($\Gamma = +1$) it is $P_R$, in each sheet's own labeling. Expressed in the frame that aligns the neutrino sheet to ours, $U = P_\ell\otimes1+P_\nu\otimes\gamma^0$, it becomes $1\otimes P_L$ on both sheets — the left-handed doublet $(\nu_L,\ell_L)$ — and in the frame that aligns to the ortho rendering it becomes $1\otimes P_R$ on both sheets, the right-handed doublet **[V]**. Coupling the traceless connection through $\Pi$, written in our aligned frame, is exactly the $V\!-\!A$ charged current $\bar\nu\gamma^\mu P_L\ell$ **[V]**. So **one exchange-invariant parent projector reads as the left-handed doublet in our rendering and the right-handed doublet in the ortho rendering**: the gate $C_\varphi = \tfrac12(1+s_\varphi\gamma^5)$ of §XXIII.1 is $\Pi$ expressed in the frame the selector aligns. With the grading the selector's own, $\Pi_\varphi = \tfrac12(1+\Gamma_\varphi\otimes\gamma^5)$ is gauge-*covariant*, $\Pi_{U\varphi} = (U\otimes1)\Pi_\varphi(U\otimes1)^\dagger$ **[V]**, so the invariant projector is a legitimate object of the gauge theory and not a frame artifact. Covariance of the projector does not by itself make "gating the connection" a connection on the projected subbundle; the natural induced connection is $\Pi_\varphi\nabla\Pi_\varphi$, and since $\Pi\,d\Pi\,\Pi = 0$ for any projector **[T/V]** it carries no first-order selector term inside the subbundle, while its curvature carries $\Pi(d\Pi\wedge d\Pi)\Pi$ — the selector's variation entering at second order, exactly where selector dynamics, symmetry breaking or a Higgs-like covariant derivative would enter. Constructing that induced local connection and its dynamics is the next gauge-theory test **[O]**. The selector does not choose the chirality; it chooses the *frame*, and the chirality is a property of the parent structure — which is the thesis of §XXIII.0 as an invariant statement, and it dissolves the chirality tension without any selector dependence at all.

**What remains a choice, exactly [D/O].** $\Pi' = \tfrac12(1-\Gamma\otimes\gamma^5)$ is equally invariant and would give the right-handed doublet in *our* rendering, $V\!+\!A$; and coupling through $1$ is vector-like. Lorentz and exchange symmetry admit these three invariant couplings and choose none. So two questions remain, and they are not the same question: *why a proper chiral projector rather than $1$* — why chiral at all — and, conditional on that, *why $\Pi_+$ rather than $\Pi_-$*, which alone is a $\mathbb Z_2$ orientation datum, which sheet's split sign pairs with which chirality. The second is now bounded exactly by a classification: the commutant of the total Lorentz action on $S_D\otimes W_{\rm bi}$ is eight-dimensional, exchange invariance cuts it to four, and compatibility with the electric charge to exactly ${\rm span}\{1,\Gamma\otimes\gamma^5\}$ **[V]** — a commutative algebra whose projectors are $0$, $1$, $\Pi_+$, $\Pi_-$. **Among Lorentz-invariant, exchange-invariant, charge-compatible gates the only nontrivial proper projectors are $\Pi_\pm$** **[D]**. So the one principle still needed is that the weak coupling pass through a nontrivial proper invariant projector at all; given it, the remaining choice is precisely one sign, of a kind the theory carries orientations for — the Hopf class, the twin, the meridian sense — and whether an existing orientation fixes it is the question **[O]**. Everything else in Part XXIII — $Y_R = -2$, the sterility of $\nu_R$, the closure of the right-handed algebra upstairs, rendering-by-rendering anomalies — now follows from $\Pi$ rather than from a postulated gate. **Status:** the gate is derived conditional on being a proper projector, up to one sign; the vector-like alternative is excluded by observation and by that one principle, not yet by the geometry.

## XXIII.7 The hybrid pencil: up and down quarks as a hybrid complementary pair [T/V/D/S/O]

*The author's idea, in his terms: since the dimensions of space are already related to the three generations, how possible is a "hybrid" space between the apparent middle space and the ortho-middle space — not heuristically two space axes from one and one from the other, since these are two quotient spaces, but rotating the flavors themselves between them, or perhaps the axes — and can one such space and its complement be the counterparts of the up and down quarks?*

**The pencil exists, and gravity does not see it [D].** On the regular stratum the canonical two-plane $\mathcal D = V_H\oplus\widetilde V^{\rm hor}_{\rm mer}$ admits a whole family of complementary line pairs: in its orthonormal frame, $V_\theta = {\rm span}(\cos\theta\,\hat K_H+\sin\theta\,\hat K_{\rm mer})$ and $V_{\theta^\perp}$, a point $[V_\theta]$ of $\mathbb{RP}^1$ since a line has no orientation, with the two familiar renderings the endpoints, $\theta = 0$ giving $(\mathcal M_\ell,\mathcal M_\nu)$. Every complementary pair spans $\mathcal D$, so every pair has the same common reduction, $E/(V_\theta\oplus V_{\theta^\perp}) = B_{\rm grav}$: the gravitational base is untouched while the matter rendering changes — native to the theory, and the reason the idea is not a third spacetime. The caveat of §XXII.10 stands: these $\mathcal M_\theta$ are local reduction packages, not globally established spacetimes. And the hybrid pair's exchange and grading are the conjugates of the lepton pair's by the rotation of the plane, and close the Pauli algebra again **[V]**: **weak isospin is not invented twice.** If a complementary pair $(P_u,P_d)$ sits at a hybrid position, $T^{(q)}_3 = \tfrac12(P_u-P_d)$ gives $+\tfrac12$ to the up-type and $-\tfrac12$ to the down-type member — up/down as complementarity, by the same principle that gave charged lepton/neutrino, differing only in *where* the pair sits in the projective family.

**Rotate the flavors, not the axes [T].** The literal version — two spatial axes from one rendering and one from the other — is blocked by Part XXI's own firewall: the three of generation is the multiplicity space $G_{\rm gen}$ descended from the spatial carrier precisely so that rotating space does not rotate electrons into muons. The author's alternative is the safe one, and it has a rigorous form: the combined carrier $G_{\rm gen}\otimes W_{\rm render}\simeq\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^2$, which for leptons gave the six left-handed channels, is also exactly the organization of the six quark flavors as three doublets $(u,d)$, $(c,s)$, $(t,b)$; and a rendering polarization may be flavor-sector-dependent, $\mathscr P = \sum_a|g_a\rangle\langle g_a|\otimes P(\theta_a)$ with complement $I-\mathscr P$, each generation line seeing its own position in the pencil — "two from here, one from there" as rank and projector data on the internal carrier rather than a cut of physical space, with no laboratory rotation converting flavors. A complete left-quark carrier is then $S_L\otimes G_{\rm gen}\otimes C_{\rm color}\otimes W_q$, each factor with a different job, color kept separate as §XXIII.4 requires. And CKM mixing acquires the same reading PMNS has in Part XXI: two stationary operators $H_u$, $H_d$ on $G_{\rm gen}$ with different eigenbases, $U_{\rm CKM} = U_u^\dagger U_d$, a mismatch of stationary structures and not a rotation of anything spatial.

**The obstruction is hypercharge, exactly [T/V].** A hybrid rotation cannot turn lepton charges into quark charges: the charge spectrum is invariant under any rotation of the two-mode frame, $(0,-1)$ stays $(0,-1)$ **[V]**, while quarks need $(\tfrac23,-\tfrac13)$, i.e. $Q_q = T^{(q)}_3+\tfrac16 I$, the central character $Y_Q = \tfrac13$. So the hybrid position can supply the $SU(2)$ doublet but not, by itself, $Y_Q = \tfrac13$; the central character must change, and Part XXII's caution that fractional hypercharges make the global group structure nontrivial — $U(2) = (SU(2)\times U(1))/\mathbb Z_2$ and its admissible representations — applies with full force. One shortcut is closed: fractional quark charge is *not* an expectation value of superposed electron and neutrino charge eigenstates — such a superposition has $\langle Q\rangle$ between $0$ and $-1$ with nonzero variance **[V]** and is a charge-indefinite state, not a new representation. The target as first posed — a distinguished $[V_q]\in\mathbb{RP}^1$ whose position induces $Y_Q = \tfrac13$ — is superseded by §XXIII.8: the central character is not a function of the angle at all but of the full neutral parent symmetry and its descent, with the quark value fixed by anomaly cancellation given color. What the pencil must explain is only *why quarks occupy a non-endpoint complementary pair* **[O]**. Nothing here manufactures $\tfrac13$ from an angle.

**Plausibility, ranked, and the reframing [S].** Most plausible: a projective family of complementary reductions exists locally. Quite plausible: a non-endpoint pair serves as the $u/d$ doublet while $G_{\rm gen}$ supplies $(u,c,t)$ and $(d,s,b)$. Interesting but unproved: the hybrid position determines $Y_Q = \tfrac13$. Wrong: quark charge as a superposition of lepton charges. If the ambitious version holds, the earlier "quarks as a third imposed spacetime," floated in §XXII.4 and deferred, is replaced by something cleaner: **quarks are not a third spacetime; they are the nontrivial hybrid polarization of the same two-rendering geometry**, leptons at the extremal pair and quarks at a hybrid pair of one canonical reduction family, with the quark completion that §XXIII.4 made mandatory given a native place to live.

## XXIII.8 The full neutral algebra: hypercharge as what descends of the lost symmetry [T/V/D/S/O]

*The author's instinct, in his terms: for the hypercharge obstruction, look at the contribution from the charge of neutrinos and the right-handed $W$ sector — perhaps the full effective symmetry at play is not being accounted for.*

**Hypercharge is the rendering-symmetric charge [V].** The bi-electromagnetic algebra already contains it: $Q_\ell+Q_\nu = -P_\ell-P_\nu = -I$, so for the lepton doublet $Y_L = Q_\ell+Q_\nu$ — the hypercharge generator is literally the sum of the two complementary electromagnetic readouts, and $X = (Q_\ell+Q_\nu)/2 = -\tfrac12$ is the *average of the two renderings' charges*, the part that survives the rendering average **[V]**. The neutrino's ordinary charge is still exactly zero in our rendering; what contributes to the center is its ortho-electromagnetic parent charge, which our rendering normally projects away. So the obstruction of §XXIII.7 was posed one level too low: the hybrid angle cannot change charge eigenvalues, and was never supposed to.

**The parent su(2) on the two-sheet space, and why the gate respects it [V].** The ladders must carry the $\gamma^0$ intertwiner, as the exchange did in §XXIII.6: on $S_D\otimes W_{\rm bi}$ the parent algebra is $\{T_3\otimes1,\ T_\pm\otimes\gamma^0\}$, which closes, $[T_+,T_-] = 2T_3$ **[V]**, and the invariant gate $\Pi = \tfrac12(1+\Gamma\otimes\gamma^5)$ commutes with all of it **[V]** — because $\{\Gamma,T_\pm\} = 0$ and $\{\gamma^5,\gamma^0\} = 0$, the two anticommutations cancel — so the gated generators $\Pi T_a$ are well defined and close, $[\Pi T_+,\Pi T_-] = 2\Pi T_3$ **[V]**. The gate therefore splits the parent Cartan generator exactly: $T_3 = T_{3L}+T_{3R}$ with $T_{3L} = T_3\Pi$ and $T_{3R} = T_3(1-\Pi)$.

**The descent [D/V].** Let the parent charge be $Q = T_3+X$, with one *uniform* central character $X$ on the whole doublet, both chiralities — for leptons $X = -\tfrac12$ — so that $Q = -P_\ell$ on the left sector as in §XXII.7. Our rendering keeps $Q$ as its unbroken generator and keeps the gated $\mathfrak{su}(2)_L$; the charged right-handed ladders $T_\pm(1-\Pi)$ have no local support on $B^{(\ell)}_{\rm rep}$ (§XXIII.3); and the abelian generator our rendering calls hypercharge is what is left of $Q$ once the local weak isospin is removed, $Y/2 := Q-T_{3L} = X+T_{3R}$, which commutes with the gated $\mathfrak{su}(2)_L$ **[V]**. $T_{3R}$ does not descend separately — that would be the forbidden partial representation of §XXIII.2 — only the combination $X+T_{3R}$ descends, as the one-dimensional character of the combined neutral parent subgroup, and it must include $T_{3R}$ because a single photon with $Q(e_R) = -1$ demands it (§XXIII.2's derivation of $Y_R = -2$, now seen as this descent). Structurally this is the left–right relation $Q = T_{3L}+T_{3R}+\tfrac12(B-L)$ of $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R$ constructions, reproduced *without* a local $SU(2)_R$ in our spacetime:
$$SU(2)_{R,{\rm parent} }\times U(1)_X\ \xrightarrow{\ \text{rendering}\ }\ U(1)_Y,\qquad T^\pm_R\not\downarrow,\quad T_{3R}\not\downarrow\ \text{separately},\quad T_{3R}+X\downarrow.$$
In our aligned frame the eight lepton states then read, with one $X = -\tfrac12$: $\nu_L$ $(T_{3L},T_{3R},Q,Y) = (+\tfrac12,0,0,-1)$, $e_L$ $(-\tfrac12,0,-1,-1)$, $\nu_R$ $(0,+\tfrac12,0,0)$, $e_R$ $(0,-\tfrac12,-1,-2)$ **[V]**. The sterility of $\nu_R$ and the strange-looking $Y = -2$ of $e_R$ become *two complementary cancellations of one parent structure* — $X+T_{3R} = -\tfrac12\pm\tfrac12$ — rather than two separately fitted singlet assignments, which is what the author's bookkeeping intuition said should be true.

**The quark offset, and the division of labor [D].** With $X$ the rendering-symmetric charge, the anomaly condition of §XXIII.4 reads $N_cX_q+X_\ell = 0$, so with the observed $N_c = 3$, $X_q = +\tfrac16$: quark charges $T_3+X_q = (\tfrac23,-\tfrac13)$, $Y_Q = \tfrac13$, and $Y/2 = X_q+T_{3R}$ gives $u_R$, $d_R$ their $\tfrac43$, $-\tfrac23$ **[V]** — every Standard Model hypercharge from one rule, $Y/2 = X+T_{3R}$, with $X = -\tfrac12$ for leptons and $+\tfrac16$ for quarks. The division of labor is then clean: *hybrid rendering geometry* gives $T_3 = \pm\tfrac12$, up/down complementarity; *the full bi-electromagnetic central structure* gives $X$, the common neutral charge; *the ortho weak algebra* gives $T_{3R}$, the right-handed splitting; *anomaly cancellation with color* gives $X_q = \tfrac16$; and $X+T_{3R}$ is the effective hypercharge. **§XXIII.7's theorem target is accordingly replaced:** the hybrid pencil need only explain *why quarks occupy a non-endpoint complementary pair*; the hypercharge comes from the full parent symmetry and its descent, with the quark value fixed by anomaly cancellation given the color multiplicity — $N_c$ itself still a separate problem, as §XXIII.4 says. And once color enters the parent is larger than the isolated $U(2)$-shaped rendering algebra, where the global form — how the color, weak and $U(1)$ factors are glued, and the quotients that constrain hypercharge quantization — becomes restrictive beyond the Lie algebra **[O]**.

**Next calculation.** Not "can the hybrid angle give $\tfrac13$," but: can the parent bi-electromagnetic and ortho-weak structure be shown to produce the neutral descent $Y/2 = X+T_{3R}$ with $X_\ell = -\tfrac12$ and $X_q = +\tfrac16$, while the charged $T^\pm_R$ fail to descend — as a property of the rendering functor acting on the parent gauge structure, not as the bookkeeping identity verified here. §XXIII.9 takes the first step: the descent is the stabilizer of the sterile direction.

## XXIII.9 The descent as a stabilizer: the minimal parent, and hypercharge as the fossil of the lost rendering [V/D/S/O]

*The next theorem posed by §XXIII.8 — the descent $X+R\downarrow$ with nothing else of the neutral singlet-sector symmetry descending — as a property of the rendering rather than a stipulation, in its simplest form, with the parent chosen to be no larger than what the renderings see.*

**The endomorphism algebra the gate produces, and the gauge parent it points to [V/O].** Since $\Pi$ commutes with the parent realization $\{T_3\otimes1,T_\pm\otimes\gamma^0\}$ (§XXIII.8), the projected generators $\Pi T_a$ and $(1-\Pi)T_a$ each close as an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and the two copies commute **[V]**: the two-sheet structure generates a commuting $\mathfrak{su}(2)_\Pi\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)_{1-\Pi}$ *endomorphism algebra*. That is an algebra of operations, not yet a gauge group: a single parent connection $A^a_\mu T_a$ inserted with the projectors has the *same* coefficients on both sectors, and nothing any rendering sees requires the ladders $T^\pm_{1-\Pi}$ to be gauge directions — the $(1-\Pi)$ sector is weak-singlet in every rendering (§XXIII.10). What the renderings do require is that the Cartan direction $R := T_3(1-\Pi)$ be gauged, because $Y = X+R$ must be. So **the primary gauge parent is the minimal one**,
$$G_{\min} = SU(3)_c\times SU(2)_\Pi\times U(1)_R\times U(1)_X,$$
with $\mathfrak{su}(2)_\Pi\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_R\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_X$ closed, five-dimensional **[V]**: one gated weak $SU(2)_\Pi$ — left-handed in our aligned rendering, right-handed in the ortho one — plus a $U(1)_R$ in the complementary singlet sector. The firewall is then clean: *the endomorphism and history algebra may contain $T^\pm_R$ and $R$, closing as $[T^+_R,T^-_R] = 2R$; the minimal gauge algebra gauges $R$ and not $T^\pm_R$* **[V]** — the geometry contains the operations needed to complete the two-mode structure, but only its Cartan direction is promoted to an independent gauge redundancy. The fully gauged $SU(2)_R$ of the left–right-symmetric models is an *optional enlargement*, labelled as such below, not something the core argument needs; the phrases "$W_R$" and "right-handed weak isospin" belong to that enlargement and to the endomorphism algebra, and are not used for the minimal theory.

**The selector, retyped for the minimal parent [D/V].** Under $U(1)_R\times U(1)_X$ no transformation rotates $\nu_R$ into $e_R$ — they are separate weight lines — so the selector is not a doublet direction. It is an internal selector $\sigma_R$, an $SU(2)_\Pi$ singlet carrying the neutral-rendering character of $\nu_R$: $R(\sigma_R) = +\tfrac12$, $X(\sigma_R) = -\tfrac12$ — the $\nu_R$-character selector, labelled by the sterile-neutrino direction but an object the minimal gauge group can act on, a section of the internal orbit bundle and not the fermion field $\nu_R(x)\in\Gamma(S_R\otimes W_R)$. Its annihilator — of the *vector*, including its phase, not the ray — among $aR+bX$ is $a = b$, and $\mathfrak{su}(2)_\Pi$ acts on it trivially, so
$${\rm Ann}(\sigma_R) = \mathfrak{su}(2)_\Pi\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_{X+R},$$
four-dimensional **[V]**: $SU(2)_\Pi\times U(1)_R\times U(1)_X\to SU(2)_\Pi\times U(1)_Y$ with $Y/2 = X+R$, **without an independently gauged $SU(2)_R$ anywhere.** $R$ does not descend separately — that would be a second abelian field our rendering does not have — only $X+R$ does; and it must include $R$ because one photon with $Q(e_R) = -1$ demands it (§XXIII.2's derivation of $Y_R = -2$, now this descent). The omitted gauge complement is **one-dimensional**: the neutral combination orthogonal to $Y$ in the invariant inner product, $Z'_\perp\propto g_R^2R-g_X^2X$ **[V]**, the normalization set by the two couplings. There are no $W_R^\pm$ components to omit at all. So **if the loss of the ortho rendering acts on the minimal parent as a selection of the vector $\sigma_R$, then what descends is precisely its stabilizer, and the descent of §XXIII.8 follows from one vector rather than being stipulated** **[D, conditional]**. Hypercharge is, in the referee's phrase, *the observable neutral fossil of the symmetry lost with the ortho rendering*: the combination neutral on the character along which that rendering was lost.

**The optional enlargement [S].** With a fully gauged $SU(2)_R$ on the $(1-\Pi)$ sector, the selector becomes a doublet direction $n_R = (1,0)\in W_R$ labelled by $\nu_R$, its vector stabilizer is again $\mathfrak{su}(2)_\Pi\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_{X+R}$ **[V]**, and the omitted complement is three-dimensional, $W_R^\pm$ and $Z'$ — the left–right models' breaking of $SU(2)_R\times U(1)$ to $U(1)_Y$ by a right-handed doublet along the sterile-neutrino direction, reproduced as a rendering loss, with their two Higgs sectors mirrored by the electroweak selector of §XXII.14 and the loss direction. The difference from those models is sharp in either version: their broken bosons are *heavy local* fields, searched for and bounded; here the omitted directions have *no local support in our rendering at any energy*. A $W_R$ or $Z'$ ever found would falsify the rendering reading in favor of an ordinary extension, and their continued absence at all scales is what it predicts — in the minimal parent the prediction is the absence of a $Z'$ alone, there being no $W_R$ to begin with.

**What is and is not derived [O].** Derived: that the gate yields the endomorphism algebra; that the minimal gauge parent closes; that the stabilizer of the $\nu_R$-character selector is exactly the electroweak gauge algebra with the right hypercharge, with a one-dimensional omitted complement. Not derived: that the loss of the ortho rendering acts on the parent gauge structure as a selection of $\sigma_R$ — the characterization of the $\nu_R$ character as the unique one sterile here and native there is a reason to expect it, not a construction — and the dynamics by which the omitted direction loses local support rather than acquiring mass. That construction, a rendering reduction on the parent gauge bundle whose image is the stabilizer, is built on objects in §XXIII.10.

## XXIII.10 The rendering reduction, constructed on objects; the exchange; and the parent anomaly ledgers [V/D/S/O]

*The author's question: how possible is a push for the fundamental functor now — and might the electron/neutrino distinction be a special case of the Boltzmannian space-microstate concept of §XVIII, each a hint for the other? A direct route is visible, so it is taken; the microstate idea is placed where it bears.*

**The construction [D/V].** A section $s$ of a bundle associated to a principal $G$-bundle $P$, with values in an orbit $G/H$, reduces $P$ to an $H$-bundle $P_s$, and with an $H$-invariant reductive splitting a $G$-connection $\omega$ separates into an $H$-connection $\mathrm{pr}_{\mathfrak h}\omega$ and a tensorial one-form $\mathrm{pr}_{\mathfrak m}\omega$ in the complement — the geometric half of the Higgs mechanism. The rendering reduction is this with the complement *omitted from the local image* instead of kept:
$$\mathfrak R:\ (P,\omega,s)\ \longmapsto\ (P_s,\ \mathrm{pr}_{\mathfrak h}\omega),\qquad\mathfrak h = \{A\in\mathfrak g:\ As = 0\}.$$
For the minimal parent with $s = \sigma_R$: $\mathfrak h = \mathfrak{su}(2)_\Pi\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_{X+R}$, a parent connection splits as $c = c_{\mathfrak h}+c_{\mathfrak m}$ with $c_{\mathfrak m}$ orthogonal to $\mathfrak h$ in the invariant inner product, and the omitted $\mathfrak m$ is the single direction $Z'_\perp$ **[V]**; so the image connection has structure algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)_L\oplus\mathfrak u(1)_Y$ *by construction*. (For the optional enlargement with $s = n_R$ the same holds with $\mathfrak m$ three-dimensional **[V]**.) This is a **candidate rendering functor constructed on objects**: its action on morphisms — restricting to bundle morphisms and gauge transformations preserving the selected section, and checking identities and composition — is a small theorem target, probably easy, not yet done **[O]**.
