Three operations are thereby kept apart: altering the complex structure, altering its presentation, and altering the physical quantity decomposed. The condition that makes the imaginary structure objective across witnesses is real: $T^{(R)}_{CB}\mathbb J_{B\mid R} = \mathbb J_{C\mid R}T^{(R)}_{CB}$, and globally $H_\gamma\mathbb J = \mathbb JH_\gamma$ for every admissible loop of the real passage connection — nontrivial holonomy not forbidding a compatible complex presentation, only the failure of the holonomies to preserve any admissible common $\mathbb J$ obstructing it — a candidate new invariant, the holonomy or obstruction class of the real co-middle passage structure. The next section's first calculation is therefore not another Kerr solution: identify the minimal real carrier already present in the canonical and co-middle construction and determine whether it carries an intrinsically defined operator squaring to $-I$ or only a family needing selection; test its Lorentzian bivector interpretation, attestation by $B$ through an admissible passage, and whether changing $R$ changes the polarization, the labels, or the spectrum; with isolated Kerr the benchmark — curvature, angular momentum, the $+ia/-ia$ presentation and its Schwarzschild degeneracy, none defined into the construction — and with the stringent check that the frozen architecture treats the complex Hopf geometry as primitive, so that calling its complex structure emergent requires a new underlying construction and an explicit map back, failing which the idea is a relational interpretation or selection of an existing structure, not a replacement of its foundations. Two outcomes are open: the conservative one, in which the real invariant is the conformal and spinorial geometry and the imaginary direction is a witness-conditioned polarization of it, Kerr spin invariant and its doubled presentation not absolutely selected; and the radical one, in which the invariant is a real groupoid of centrade passages from which compatible complex geometries emerge as renderings — the imaginary direction not a direction but the action of a real duality, made visible as a complex pair by the chosen centrade relationships. Neither follows from the existing mathematics; the second is now a construction problem rather than a metaphysical possibility.

## XXVIII.9 Background-selected complex orientation on the quaternionic phase-plane bundle [T/V/D/O]

**Current standing (v32.15), as a ledger.** The model: the quaternionic phase planes $E_{[\mathbf n]} = {\rm span}_{\mathbb R}\{1,\mathbf n\}\subset\mathbb H$ over the unoriented axes $[\mathbf n]\in\mathbb{RP}^2$, their natural flat projected connection, and a background vector $\mathbf r$.

- *L1, the bundle.* $E\cong\underline{\mathbb R}\oplus\gamma^1$, nonorientable, $w_1(E)\neq0$; flat connection with reflection holonomy ${\rm diag}(1,-1)$ around the generator of $\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^2)$; no global ordinary $\mathbb J$, only the pair $\{\mathbb J,-\mathbb J\}$. [T/V]
- *L2, the twisted structure.* $\mathscr J = \mathbb J_{\mathbf n}\otimes\mathbf n\in\Gamma({\rm End}(E)\otimes\gamma^1)$ is global, $\mathscr J^2 = -I$, parallel; it is the canonical twisted complex structure every rank-two Euclidean bundle carries in ${\rm End}(E)\otimes\det E$, parallel under any metric connection. [T/V]
- *L3, background selection.* $\mathbb J^{(R)} = \langle\mathscr J,s_R\rangle$ on the contractible $U_R\cong\mathbb R^2$; no background selects everywhere; backgrounds glue by the $\mathbb Z_2$ cocycle $t_{RR'}$ of $\gamma^1$; for nonparallel backgrounds $U_R\cap U_{R'}$ has two contractible components on which the witness/background square commutes exactly. [T/V]
- *L4, the global-splitting obstruction.* No global ordinary real endomorphism of $E$ has two distinct non-real eigenvalues everywhere. [T]
- *L5, the toy operator.* $\mathcal K_R = xI+(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)\mathbb J_{\mathbf n}$, unique up to scale among background-linear equivariant $\gamma^1$-valued constructions; global; spectrum $x\pm i|\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r|$; scalar on $\mathbf n\perp\mathbf r$; $\nabla\mathcal K_R = df_R\otimes\mathbb J^{(R)}$ on $U_R$, parallel along the level sets of $f_R = |\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r|$; returns as $xI-\mathbb J$ around the non-contractible loop. [T/V]
- *L6, the real-first form.* On $E = \mathbb R\oplus L_{[\mathbf n]}$, $\mathcal K_R(s,\mathbf v) = (xs-\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf v,\ x\mathbf v+s\,P_{[\mathbf n]}\mathbf r)$, with no sign of $\mathbf n$ and no $i$; $N_R = \mathcal K_R-xI$ satisfies $N_R^2 = -|P_{[\mathbf n]}\mathbf r|^2I = -(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)^2I$ and $N_R^* = -N_R$ — skew-adjoint, hence normal, so the degeneracy at $\mathbf n\perp\mathbf r$ is a genuine scalar collapse and not a Jordan block (checked). The complex eigenvalues are consequences of a real quadratic identity, not inputs. [T/V]
- *L7, two kinds of background dependence.* At fixed polarization, reversal $\mathbf r\to-\mathbf r$ sends $N_R\to-N_R$ and exchanges the locally labelled channels while $\mathcal D_{-R} = \mathcal D_R$ — the unordered separation unchanged; tilting through $\mathbf r(\lambda)$ gives $d\mathcal D_R/d\lambda = -8(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)(\mathbf n\cdot\dot{\mathbf r})$ — the separation changes (checked). Some changes of reference exchange the presentation of the channels; others change the attested separation; neither is yet an observable effect of a physical centrade. [T/V]
- *L8, the coherence restriction.* For a smooth polarization map $p:W\to\mathbb{RP}^2$ on a family $W$ of witnesses, constant nonzero attested splitting under one background requires $f_R\circ p = $ const, hence $df_R|_{p(B)}\circ dp_B = 0$ and, at regular points of $f_R$, ${\rm rank}(dp_B)\le1$: *the image of the polarization map must lie in one equal-alignment level set, and a witness assignment whose polarization map has rank two cannot exhibit complete spectral coherence on an open neighbourhood.* The restriction is on the rank of the polarization map, not on the dimension of the witness population: a two-dimensional population whose polarizations depend on one coordinate — $\mathbf n(u,v) = (\sin\theta_0\cos u,\sin\theta_0\sin u,\cos\theta_0)$, rank one, $f_R\circ p = \cos\theta_0$ for every witness (checked) — agrees entirely, and a constant map agrees trivially; v32.14's "a two-dimensional family cannot agree" is withdrawn. At maximal alignment the level set is one axis and the map is locally constant (rank zero); the set $f_R = 0$ lies outside $U_R$. [T/V]
- *L9, what is established and what is not.* Established: a real operator produces complex spectral data, and its compatibility across presentations is determined exactly — real-first *algebra*. Open: that a fundamentally real centrade geometry produces the canonical complex structure itself — real-first *ontology* — since the carrier still begins from the ambient quaternionic algebra and its Euclidean metric. Open also: the physical map from witnesses to polarizations; the source data $\mathcal Q_A$; any derivation of $\mathcal K_{B\leftarrow A\mid R}$ from $(\mathcal Q_A,\Xi_{BA},R)$ with the attestation and the comparison transport obtained independently; the isolated-Kerr spin-sensitive limit and the isolated-Schwarzschild scalar degeneracy; the separation of source-intrinsic angular momentum from dragging. [D/O]

The three levels of agreement are kept apart throughout — complex-orientation compatibility (L3), spectral compatibility (equal alignment, L5), complete-operator compatibility (intertwining along admissible paths, L5) — and none is physical Kerr attestation, since $[\mathbf n]$ labels a canonical polarization and not an independently identified witnessing centrade. The quaternionic calculation has reached its stopping point: it has answered whether a globally defined, orientation-independent real operator can generate complex channels with exactly determined compatibility (yes), and more examples with the same vector and the same flat connection will not decide the physical ontology. The priority passes to the intertwiner $\mathfrak A:(\mathcal Q_A,\Xi_{BA},R)\mapsto\mathcal K_{B\leftarrow A\mid R}$ — its domain, codomain and transformation laws before any coefficient function — with the acceptance test that independently constructed witness passages carry one attestation to another, that the spectral information carries physically justified source data, and that the isolated limits work; and with L8's alternative as the informative route: not agreement as a postulate, but whether the physical history constraints themselves restrict the available polarizations to a coherence submanifold, which would tie the definition of centrades as passage-invariant structures to this mathematics. What follows is the record by which this standing was reached, with its corrections in place.

**The theorem target, as the referee set it [T].** On a real plane $E$ with $\mathbb J^2 = -I$, a real invertible $T$ commutes with $\mathbb J = \begin{psmallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{psmallmatrix}$ iff $T = \begin{psmallmatrix}u&-v\\v&u\end{psmallmatrix}$, $u^2+v^2>0$ — the group $\mathbb C^\times$ as real $2\times2$ matrices — so a real two-dimensional passage system preserves a common $\mathbb J$ iff ${\rm Hol}(E)\subseteq\mathbb C^\times$ in some basis, all such holonomies commuting, and $\subseteq SO(2)$ with unit determinant. A hyperbolic transport $H(\eta) = {\rm diag}(e^\eta,e^{-\eta})$, $\eta\neq0$, preserves no real complex structure at all, since anything commuting with it is diagonal and no real diagonal matrix squares to $-I$: nontrivial $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ boost holonomy on the carrier excludes an invariant imaginary direction — an algebraic fact, conditional on the carriers being identified, and not triggered by a scalar dilation $e^\eta I$, which commutes with every $\mathbb J$. Weakening to $T\mathbb JT^{-1} = \pm\mathbb J$ gives the group $\mathbb C^\times\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$, the reflection acting as conjugation, and a three-level hierarchy: complex-linear passages preserving $\mathbb J$ and its orientation; conjugate-linear passages preserving the unordered pair $\{\mathbb J,-\mathbb J\}$ while exchanging the sectors; and general passages preserving neither.

**[Superseded; see R1–R2] What the project's own carrier was first said to do.** The real two-plane already present in the co-middle construction is the vertical two-plane $\mathcal D = V_H\oplus\tilde V_{\rm mer}$ of §XXVI.13, with its twin-even frame $(X_H,\partial_\chi)$ trivial on the regular stratum (§XXVI.14), and the moving Hopf complex plane $\mathbb C_{\mathbf n} = {\rm span}\{1,\mathbf n\}\subset\mathbb H$ of §XXVI.9 realizes the attestation carrier over the sphere of axes, with $\mathbb J_{\mathbf n}$ left multiplication by $\mathbf n$. Three facts were offered in v32.7 for this carrier, and the first was wrong as stated; the paragraph after next corrects it. First, the natural transport of the plane is *flat* but its holonomy around the generator of $\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^2)$ is the reflection ${\rm diag}(1,-1)$, not the identity (a contractible loop gives the identity); no hyperbolic element occurs — the admissible commutants being the compact $O(2)$ or $SU(2)$ of §XXVI.13 and the Part XV scale sector acting by dilation — so the boost obstruction does not arise, but trivial holonomy was a misreading, and the identification of this plane with $\mathcal D$ was unjustified, as the correction states. Second, the obstruction is not in the transport but in the *field of complex structures*: $\mathbb C_{-\mathbf n} = \mathbb C_{\mathbf n}$ as a plane while $\mathbb J_{-\mathbf n} = -\mathbb J_{\mathbf n}$, so along the non-contractible loop of the axis $\mathbb{RP}^2$ the complex structure returns as its negative — the identity passage is conjugate-linear with respect to the structures at its two ends. A global $\mathbb J$ therefore exists on the sphere of *oriented* axes, the orientation double cover, and does not exist on the $\mathbb{RP}^2$ of unoriented axes, where only the unordered pair $\{\mathbb J,-\mathbb J\}$ is defined: this is the $O(2)$-connection of §XXVI.9 in the referee's language, $SO(2)$ on the plane and the $\mathbb Z_2$ in the sign of the structure. Third, the sign is selected by orienting the Hopf axis, which the co-middle family does not do and a conditioning background $R$ does. So the answer is the referee's second outcome in form — *an invariant $\mathbb J$ exists only after restricting passages to the orientation double cover*, or after a background selects an orientation where it can — with the two corrections of the next paragraph: no background can select it everywhere, and the pole resolution of $\mathcal D$ is a separate problem not to be identified with this obstruction. This is a result about the existing carrier and nothing more: each fiber $\mathbb C_{\mathbf n}$ is a complex plane with its own $i$, so the construction does not show the imaginary direction *emerging* — the referee's stricture stands — though, as corrected below, the bundle $E$ itself is not the realification of any complex line bundle; what the result shows is exactly which datum fails to be global, the orientation of $\mathbf n$, and that it is the datum a background would supply.

**Correction: the bundle is nonorientable and its flat connection has reflection holonomy [T/V].** The referee's correction is accepted and the verdict of this section is replaced by the referee's. The quaternionic phase planes over the unoriented axes form the real bundle $E\cong\underline{\mathbb R}\oplus\gamma^1$ over $\mathbb{RP}^2$, $\gamma^1$ the tautological line bundle, with $w_1(E) = w_1(\gamma^1)\neq0$: nonorientable. Its natural projected connection is flat — $1$ and $\mathbf n(s)$ are parallel within the plane since $d\mathbf n$ is orthogonal to both — but flat is not trivial: around the generator of $\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^2)$ the transported basis returns as $(1,-\mathbf n_0)$ against $(1,\mathbf n_0)$, holonomy $H_\gamma = {\rm diag}(1,-1)$, $\det = -1$ (recomputed against the fixed basis of the returning plane; v32.7 compared with the natural basis $(1,-\mathbf n_0)$ at the end, which absorbs the flip, and so reported the identity), while a contractible loop gives the identity. *The quaternionic phase-plane family over unoriented axes is the nonorientable real bundle $\underline{\mathbb R}\oplus\gamma^1$; its natural projected connection is flat but has reflection holonomy around the generator of $\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^2)$; the family admits a globally defined unordered pair $\{\mathbb J,-\mathbb J\}$ but no globally defined complex structure $\mathbb J$; this obstruction is distinct from the unresolved pole gluing of the vertical rendering plane $\mathcal D$, and their identification requires a new intertwiner.* Three connections that v32.7 ran together are kept apart: the vertical plane $\mathcal D$ on the regular stratum, with a trivial frame and a flat *reference* connection (§XXVI.14, not a claim that a physical connection is flat); the moving quaternionic plane over $\mathbb{RP}^2$, nonorientable with the $\mathbb Z_2$ holonomy above; and the moving $SU(2)$ selector over the oriented sphere, with $U^\dagger dU$ flat and the projected Berry line curved (§XXVI.10). The sentence deriving trivial passage holonomy from Maurer–Cartan is withdrawn as too strong, and the identification of $\mathbb C_{\mathbf n}$ with $\mathcal D$'s attestation carrier is withdrawn as open — more than open: if $\mathcal D$ is trivial over the comparison family while $E = \underline{\mathbb R}\oplus\gamma^1$ is not, their first Stiefel–Whitney classes differ and *no* global plane-bundle isomorphism exists over that base, so the identification must restrict its domain, lift to oriented axes, use a differently twisted $\mathcal D$, or change — §XXVI.13's warning that the Hopf-axis family and the internal-mode plane are different planes, now with a topological reason. The nonorientability of $\mathbb C_{\mathbf n}$ is independent of the meridian-pole gluing of $\mathcal D$; the two are separate problems and are not identified here.

**The background cannot orient every axis [T/V] — its "computable commutator" reading superseded, see R3.** The double cover $S^2\to\mathbb{RP}^2$ has no continuous section — a section would factor the identity of $\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^2) = \mathbb Z_2$ through $\pi_1(S^2) = 0$ — so no fixed background can continuously orient every unoriented axis: a background vector $\mathbf r$ selects $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r>0$ and fails on the great circle $\mathbf n\perp\mathbf r$ (checked: the selected sign jumps across it), a failure that is the global obstruction and not a coordinate inconvenience. The claim that $R$ "supplies the orientation" is therefore demoted to the theorem target it should have been: *does a physical background centrade restrict the admissible attestation family to a domain on which a consistent orientation can be selected?* The referee's new calculation was then run with the two operations made concrete on this carrier — $T_{BC}$ the flat transport of the plane along a witness path in $\mathbb{RP}^2$ from $[\mathbf n_B]$ to $[\mathbf n_C]$, and $S_{R\to R'}$ the re-selection of the orientation at a fixed axis by a new background vector $\mathbf r'$ — asking whether the orientation selected at $B$ by $\mathbf r'$ and transported continuously to $C$ equals the orientation selected at $C$ by $\mathbf r'$ directly. They agree iff the continuous lift of the witness path crosses the equator $\mathbf n\perp\mathbf r'$ an even number of times, and since a path in $\mathbb{RP}^2$ between two points has two homotopy classes whose lifts end at $\pm\mathbf n_C$, the two classes *always* give opposite answers ($194/400$ and $206/400$ agreements over random witnesses and backgrounds, the classes disagreeing in every case): one background's selection survives the passage for exactly one class of witness paths and reverses for the other. v32.8 read this as the witness/background commutator and as independent of the old background; the next paragraph corrects that reading — it is the reflection holonomy in a background-selected basis, and the genuine square commutes on its admissible domain. This is the first attestation-rule test with a definite answer, and its content is bounded exactly as the referee bounded it: it concerns only the sign and global compatibility of the imaginary unit, says nothing about the magnitude $a$ in $Z_\pm = Z_0\pm ia$, and a complete success in selecting $\mathbb J$ would not establish that $R$ determines $a_{\rm att}$ or that $B$'s attestation agrees with the physical angular momentum — that coefficient must come from an independently derived operator or invariant, lest a topological account of $+$ against $-$ be mistaken for a dynamical account of Kerr spin. What survives, unchanged and sharper, is the hierarchy the entries wanted: the real carrier is well defined over the unoriented axes; passage around a nontrivial loop returns it with its imaginary orientation reversed; a background may select an oriented lift locally or cut the family to a domain admitting a global choice; and only then could the selected orientation enter a derived operator for how $B$ attests $A$'s two channels — the first two statements mathematics, the last two the hypotheses still to be constructed, with the real carrier never disappearing when the orientation fails to glue and the hole never becoming Schwarzschild.

**Background-selected complex orientation on the quaternionic phase-plane bundle: the construction target landed as a domain theorem [T/V].** The referee's separation is adopted and it changes the interpretation. For a witness path $\gamma$ from $[\mathbf n_B]$ to $[\mathbf n_C]$ with representatives chosen at the ends, the flat transport satisfies $T_\gamma\mathbb J_{\mathbf n_B}T_\gamma^{-1} = h_\gamma\mathbb J_{\mathbf n_C}$ with $h_\gamma = \pm1$ distinguishing the two homotopy classes; a background vector $\mathbf r$ selects $\mathbb J^{(R)}_i = \epsilon_i(R)\mathbb J_{\mathbf n_i}$, $\epsilon_i(R) = {\rm sgn}(\mathbf n_i\cdot\mathbf r)$, wherever $\mathbf n_i\cdot\mathbf r\neq0$; and transporting the background-selected structure gives $T_\gamma\mathbb J^{(R)}_BT_\gamma^{-1} = \delta_R(\gamma)\,\mathbb J^{(R)}_C$ with
$$\delta_R(\gamma) = h_\gamma\,\epsilon_B(R)\,\epsilon_C(R).$$
So for one background the two classes indeed give opposite agreement — but that is the reflection holonomy written in a background-selected basis, not a new commutator; and between two backgrounds the change of agreement is $\delta_{R'}(\gamma)/\delta_R(\gamma) = \epsilon_B(R')\epsilon_C(R')\epsilon_B(R)\epsilon_C(R)$, in which $h_\gamma$ *cancels*: independent of the path class. The referee's example makes it explicit and was reproduced — $\mathbf r = \hat z$, $\mathbf r' = \hat x$, $\mathbf n_B = (1,0,1)/\sqrt2$, $\mathbf n_C = (-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$: agreements $(+1,-1)$ and $(-1,+1)$ under $(R,R')$ for the two classes, the change $-1$ for both — so v32.8's identification of the witness/background commutator with the loop holonomy, "independent of the old background," is withdrawn; two comparisons had been run together, whether one background's selection survives a chosen passage, and whether changing background and changing witness commute as operations. The second requires its own four-map square, and on the existing carrier it can be built and decided. Define the admissible domain of a background, $U_R = \{[\mathbf n]\in\mathbb{RP}^2:\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r\neq0\}$: the complement of a projective line in $\mathbb{RP}^2$, hence an affine plane $U_R\cong\mathbb R^2$, contractible, over which the orientation double cover is trivial and every loop has trivial $\mathbb Z_2$ holonomy — within $U_R$ the background's selection is a continuous complex orientation, with its price the excluded line on which the rule is undefined. For two nonparallel backgrounds, $U_R\cap U_{R'}$ is $\mathbb R^2$ minus a line: *two* components (parallel or antiparallel backgrounds exclude the same line and leave a connected domain), each the projective image of a geodesically convex lune $\{\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r>0,\ \mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r'>0\}$ (and its antipode), on which the relative sign $\epsilon_R\epsilon_{R'}$ is constant, opposite on the two components (checked over $2\times10^4$ sampled axes, exactly two values), and within which the minor great-circle arc between two witnesses stays inside by convexity. With every map defined where it is used — $T^R_\gamma$ only for $\gamma\subset U_R$, the background change $S_B$ only for $B\in U_R\cap U_{R'}$, the square only for $\gamma\subset U_R\cap U_{R'}$ — the result is a theorem: *on the admissible domain the square $T^{R'}_\gamma S_B = S_CT^R_\gamma$ commutes exactly* (every admissible case of $2000$ random configurations, $595$ admissible, commuting; $1405$ inadmissible), because the joint domain's component is contractible, so the transport carries the selected orientation without holonomy, and the relative sign $\epsilon_R\epsilon_{R'}$ is constant along the path. Outside that domain this particular pair of conditioned presentations is not simultaneously defined: witnesses in different components of $U_R\cap U_{R'}$ admit no path within the joint domain, and a path that leaves it crosses a line on which one conditioned structure does not exist (the paragraph after next says why this is a statement about charts and not yet a physical prohibition) — the referee's own example, whose witnesses sit on opposite sides of the new background's equator, which is why both classes gave the same $-1$. The $\mathbb Z_2$ of the previous version is therefore not a sign defect of the attestation rule; it is the obstruction to crossing between components with these two prescriptions, and the two-background change of agreement is the product of the component indicators. This is the construction target landed on the existing carrier, and it is the referee's reading of the entries: *the background does not create the imaginary direction or fix its sign by fiat; it determines which real relational comparisons admit a mutually compatible complex presentation* — centrades as carriers of admissibility conditions, with background selection determining the domain of admissible comparisons rather than the value of a coordinate. Its bounds are kept: the maps are the natural flat transport and a vector-selection rule, not yet the physical operations of Kerr $B$ attesting Kerr $A$ while the distant centrade changes; the orientation question is the sign of $\mathbb J$ alone, under which $\mathcal Z = xI+\alpha\mathbb J$ has its eigenvalues exchanged, its unordered spectrum and discriminant $\mathcal D = -4\alpha^2$ unchanged, so the topology can obstruct a consistent channel labelling without touching the size of the splitting; and the coefficient $\alpha_{B\leftarrow A\mid R}$, the isolated-Kerr presentation and the separation of physical change from relabelling remain to be derived, with the Kerr benchmark explicit. The section is retitled accordingly, and the discriminant-collapse and witness-agreement statements of §XXVIII.8 carry these corrections in place.

**The real invariant beneath the complex direction: a globally defined twisted complex structure [T/V].** The referee's construction answers, within the toy, the question Entry 249 asked. Let $\gamma^1$ be the tautological line bundle over $\mathbb{RP}^2$ and set, for a unit representative $\mathbf n$,
$$\mathscr J_{[\mathbf n]} = \mathbb J_{\mathbf n}\otimes\mathbf n\ \in\ {\rm End}(E_{[\mathbf n]})\otimes\gamma^1_{[\mathbf n]}.$$
Under $\mathbf n\mapsto-\mathbf n$ both factors change sign, $\mathbb J_{-\mathbf n} = -\mathbb J_{\mathbf n}$ and $-\mathbf n$, so their product does not: $\mathscr J_{[-\mathbf n]} = \mathscr J_{[\mathbf n]}$ — checked, the difference of the two tensors vanishing identically — and $\mathscr J$ is a *globally defined* section of ${\rm End}(E)\otimes\gamma^1$ over all of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, where no ordinary $\mathbb J$ exists. With the metric identifying $\gamma^1\otimes\gamma^1$ with the trivial line, $\mathscr J^2 = -I$ (checked on the plane). It is not an ordinary complex structure, since it takes values in a real line bundle, and that is the whole point: the unordered pair $\{\mathbb J,-\mathbb J\}$ of v32.8 is now one real geometric object. The background enters by contraction. On $U_R$ the vector $\mathbf r$ selects a unit section $s_R([\mathbf n]) = {\rm sgn}(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)\,\mathbf n$ of $\gamma^1$, and $\mathbb J^{(R)} = \langle\mathscr J,s_R\rangle = {\rm sgn}(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)\,\mathbb J_{\mathbf n}$ is the ordinary complex structure of §XXVIII.9's domain theorem — the sequence *globally defined real twisted structure $\to$ background section $\to$ locally defined ordinary complex structure $\to$ a possible $+i/-i$ presentation*. Several backgrounds form a consistent atlas: on overlaps $\mathbb J^{(R')} = t_{RR'}\mathbb J^{(R)}$ with $t_{RR'}([\mathbf n]) = {\rm sgn}[(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r')]$, and on triple overlaps $t_{RR'}t_{R'R''} = t_{RR''}$ (checked) — the Čech cocycle of the real line bundle $\gamma^1$, whose nontrivial class $w_1(\gamma^1)\neq0$ is exactly the statement that the local presentations are mutually consistent while no globally preferred imaginary orientation exists. This is the toy's answer to "what can be real and invariant underneath a complex direction that no individual centrade possesses absolutely": a globally defined real operation whose representation as $+i$ or $-i$ requires a choice of orientation, supplied by a relational background; the apparent objectivity of the imaginary direction is a feature of how compatible local presentations are glued, and the orientation-independent twisted structure is what persists beneath them. The background need not create an imaginary direction from nothing; it lets a real, global, relational operation be represented as multiplication by $i$. It is standard bundle geometry applied to the chosen carrier, not a derived gravitational law, and the research question it sets is the one the referee set, keeping the three arguments of $\mathcal V(B\leftarrow A\mid R)$: *can the project's real, passage-invariant co-middle structure independently supply an analogue of $\mathscr J$, with the background selecting an ordinary complex presentation and a witnessing centrade determining how that presentation is attested?* The Kerr coefficient $a$, its Schwarzschild limit, and any physical response to changing $R$ remain separate derivational targets.

**Two corollaries, and a controlled toy operator [T/V].** *Parallelism.* Under the natural projected connection $d\mathbf n$ is orthogonal to $1$ and to $\mathbf n$, so the frame $(1,\mathbf n)$ is parallel for the plane and $\mathbf n$ is parallel for the tautological line, and $\nabla\mathscr J = 0$: the twisted operator is not only globally defined but passage-invariant under this connection. The generator loop shows it directly — the plane holonomy ${\rm diag}(1,-1)$ sends $\mathbb J\to-\mathbb J$ while the line's holonomy is $-1$, so the tensor transforms by $(-1)(-1) = +1$ — a clean realization of passage-invariant structure beneath a presentation-dependent imaginary direction, under the model connection and not yet under the physically derived co-middle correspondences. *The global-splitting no-go.* If an attestation operator were an ordinary, globally defined real endomorphism $\mathcal K:E\to E$ with two distinct complex-conjugate eigenvalues at every point — discriminant $\mathcal D_{\mathcal K} = ({\rm tr}\,\mathcal K)^2-4\det\mathcal K<0$ everywhere — then $A = \mathcal K-\tfrac12({\rm tr}\,\mathcal K)I$ satisfies $A^2 = \tfrac14\mathcal D_{\mathcal K}I$ by Cayley–Hamilton and $\mathbb J_{\mathcal K} = A/\sqrt{-\mathcal D_{\mathcal K}/4}$ would be a global ordinary complex structure on $E$, which the nonorientability forbids. *No global smooth real endomorphism of $E = \underline{\mathbb R}\oplus\gamma^1$ over $\mathbb{RP}^2$ can have two distinct non-real eigenvalues everywhere*: a two-channel attestation represented by an ordinary global operator on this carrier cannot keep a nonzero complex splitting over the whole unoriented-axis space, and must restrict its domain, use the twisted operator, change the carrier, or degenerate somewhere — a constraint on the *type* of two-channel structure the preferred carrier can support, stronger than the earlier statement about labels. *The toy operator.* The degeneracy the theorem requires has an explicit, globally defined example. With a background $\mathbf r$, the section $\boldsymbol\beta_R([\mathbf n]) = (\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)\mathbf n$ of $\gamma^1$ is even in $\mathbf n$ and hence global, and
$$\mathcal K_R = xI+\langle\mathscr J,\boldsymbol\beta_R\rangle = xI+(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)\,\mathbb J_{\mathbf n}$$
is an ordinary global endomorphism with eigenvalues $\kappa_\pm = x\pm i(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)$ and discriminant $\mathcal D_R = -4(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)^2$ (checked), a genuine scalar degeneracy $\mathcal K_R = xI$ on $\mathbf n\perp\mathbf r$ — the line on which v32.9's chart failed — and, wherever the splitting is nonzero, an own complex structure $\mathbb J_{\mathcal K_R} = {\rm sgn}(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)\mathbb J_{\mathbf n}$ that is exactly the background-selected $\mathbb J^{(R)}$ (checked at three axes). So in a separately specified operator model the background-conditioned chart failure coincides with a two-channel degeneracy, and the three layers the referee drew are all present on the carrier: the passage-invariant twisted structure $\mathscr J$; its background-dependent contraction into a channel operator; and an eigenchannel splitting with its topologically required limitation. The distinctions are kept exact: v32.9's selection rule merely became undefined on the excluded line, while $\mathcal K_R$ is built to remain defined there with its splitting going to zero; the topology forbids a globally nondegenerate complex spectrum but neither determines this operator nor requires its zero set to be that line; and $\mathbf n\perp\mathbf r$ does not make a physical Kerr hole Schwarzschild, which would need gravitational physics. One wording is corrected: $E$ is *not* the realification of a complex line bundle — any such realification is orientable, and $E$ is not — so the earlier caution stands in its precise form: the twisted construction uses the pre-existing quaternionic geometry and does not establish the ontological emergence of complex structure, yet its nonorientable real phase-plane bundle is not merely the realification of a globally complex line, and the globally defined twisted operator and the locally selected ordinary complex structures are genuinely different geometric objects. What stands after this: no global ordinary imaginary orientation (obstructed); a global twisted one (constructed); preserved by the model transport (corollary); selected locally by a background (on $U_R$); compatible across backgrounds (the cocycle); and, separately, nothing about Kerr $a$, nothing establishing this as the physical sub-centrade carrier, no witness or background map derived from physical histories, and no established observable change of splitting under a change of the actual background. The research has reached the point where the mathematics imposes restrictions on the ontology rather than illustrating it, and the one bridge that may not be assumed is whether the canonical-history equations independently produce this twisted carrier and an operator of this form, with the right spin dependence and Schwarzschild limit.

**Attestation coherence: topological compatibility is not attestation compatibility [T/V/D].** The referee's example decides a question the toy operator raises. Three remarks first. The twisted structure is more general than the quaternionic example: every real rank-two Euclidean bundle has a canonical twisted complex structure $\mathscr J\in\Gamma({\rm End}(E)\otimes\det E)$ — a local orientation fixes a $90^\circ$ rotation, reversing the orientation reverses both the rotation and the orientation line, and their tensor is global — with $\det E\cong\gamma^1$ for this bundle, and it is parallel under *any* metric-compatible connection with the induced connection on $\det E$; so the parallelism is a feature of two-dimensional metric geometry and identifies no mechanism of the theory, and the physical content must sit in how the real bundle is selected, how centrade passages act on it, and how an operator is determined. Second, what $[\mathbf n]$ labels is fixed and not conflated: in the manuscript's own structures it is the co-middle Hopf axis, a *selected canonical polarization* (the rendering selector of §XXVI.2), neither a property of source $A$, nor of witness $B$, nor a history — the pair-selected sky axis of §XXVII.6 is a history datum and a different object — and the toy operator accordingly contains the selector and the background and nothing of $A$'s spin, mass or charge, nor an independently constructed role for $B$. Third, the no-go requires only that the nondegenerate non-real spectral condition fail somewhere, not that every such operator become scalar; the toy's scalar degeneracy is the stronger property. Now the coherence test. With the common background $\mathbf r = \hat z$ and two witnesses in the same admissible region, $\mathbf n_B = \hat z$ and $\mathbf n_C = (\tfrac{\sqrt3}2,0,\tfrac12)$, the operators $\mathcal K_B = xI+\mathbb J$ and $\mathcal K_C = xI+\tfrac12\mathbb J$ have spectra $\{x\pm i\}$ and $\{x\pm\tfrac i2\}$ (checked), so the flat passage, which carries the background-selected $\mathbb J^{(R)}$ correctly, cannot carry $\mathcal K_B$ to $\mathcal K_C$: $T_{CB}\mathcal K_BT_{CB}^{-1}\neq\mathcal K_C$. Two kinds of compatibility are thereby separated — the witnesses admit consistently oriented imaginary structures (yes) and their channel operators have the same eigenvalues (no) — and the toy extends to a statement of exactly which polarizations agree — polarizations, not yet witnesses, since no map from physical witnesses to selected polarizations has been constructed. Under one common background the unordered spectra coincide precisely on the level sets $f_R = |\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r| = {\rm const}$, the cones of equal alignment about the background (five polarizations on one cone share the spectrum $\{0.4\pm0.765i\}$); and the exact form is a covariant derivative: on $U_R$, with $\mathcal K_R = xI+f_R\mathbb J^{(R)}$ and $\nabla\mathbb J^{(R)} = 0$ under the natural flat connection,
$$\nabla\mathcal K_R = df_R\otimes\mathbb J^{(R)},$$
so $\nabla_X\mathcal K_R = 0$ exactly for $X$ tangent to a level set (checked: along a meridian the derivative is $(df_R/d\theta)\,\mathbb J$ to machine precision, along a latitude it vanishes) — the operator is parallel along its equal-alignment level sets within the admissible region, and the whole of its variation comes from the alignment scalar. The complete-operator statement is path-dependent, which the referee's counterexample makes exact: at $[\hat z]$ with $\mathbf r = \hat z$ the operator $xI+\mathbb J$ transported around the non-contractible loop returns as $H\mathcal K_RH^{-1} = xI-\mathbb J\neq\mathcal K_R$ (checked), equal spectra and unequal operators, because the loop leaves $U_R$; so *equal-alignment axes have matching spectra, and their operators intertwine under the natural flat transport when the comparison path is restricted to the admissible homotopy class*. Agreement off a level set cannot be produced by any change of basis, since similarity preserves spectra — the mismatch is real within the model. What co-transporting the background does is decided by an active/passive distinction the previous draft blurred: if a rotation $G$ carries both the selected axis and the *coordinate representation* of the same background, $\mathbf n_C\cdot G\mathbf r = \mathbf n_B\cdot\mathbf r$ describes one geometric background in two comparison frames, not a change of reference; if the axes are physically distinct in one shared frame, actively rotating $\mathbf r$ changes the configuration tested. Whether transporting $\mathbf r$ preserves one physical background or replaces it with another is therefore decided by the independently defined witness-comparison map, and not by the algebra — the distinction that keeps a change of reference description from being mistaken for a physical change in the distant centrade. The construction is not arbitrary: among $SO(3)$-equivariant maps quadratic in $\mathbf n$ (hence even) and linear in $\mathbf r$, ${\rm Sym}^2(\mathbf 3)\otimes\mathbf 3 = \mathbf 3\oplus\mathbf 3\oplus\mathbf 5\oplus\mathbf 7$ contains the vector representation twice, giving $(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r)\mathbf n$ and $(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf n)\mathbf r = \mathbf r$, of which only the first is a section of $\gamma^1$; so within background-linear, rotationally equivariant, $\gamma^1$-valued sections, $\boldsymbol\beta_R$ is unique up to scale, and the operator's form is a conditional uniqueness result rather than one convenient formula — symmetry supplying the form and not the missing source law. What the calculation establishes is that the operator depends spectrally on the selected polarization; it has not established that two physical centrades disagree about Kerr $A$, which needs an actual role for $A$. The theorem target that the entries' objectivity claim now requires is $\mathcal K_{B\leftarrow A\mid R} = \mathfrak A(\mathcal Q_A,\text{history}_{BA},R)$ built from a source section or operator $\mathcal Q_A$ and the available history data, compared through a passage map specified by the geometry, $T^{(R)}_{CB}\,\mathcal K_{B\leftarrow A\mid R}\,(T^{(R)}_{CB})^{-1}\overset?=\mathcal K_{C\leftarrow A\mid R}$, with $\mathfrak A$ and $T$ obtained independently so that agreement is not programmed into their definitions: agreement would explain apparent objectivity from the common background, and disagreement would have to be judged physical, representational, or disqualifying for the operator. The physical restrictions are stated as the criteria they are: the toy splits even when the intended source has zero spin, so it cannot meet the Schwarzschild acceptance condition, and inserting $a_A$ by hand would defeat the reconstruction; the dimensionless alignment $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r$ carries no length and cannot by itself reproduce a displacement of magnitude $a = J/M$; and the source-sensitive coefficient must come from the passage and attestation structure itself. The distinction that organizes the next work is the referee's: *topological compatibility $\neq$ attestation compatibility $\neq$ physical Kerr derivation*, each now testable separately on the carrier, and the breakthrough the branch needs is an independently derived law that makes complete attestations agree across witnesses while responding, in a controlled way, to changes of the conditioning background.

**Chart or prohibition: the interpretive hurdle stated [D/O].** Two of the domain theorem's phrases are corrected. The two-component structure of $U_R\cap U_{R'}$ requires $\mathbf r$ and $\mathbf r'$ nonparallel; for parallel or antiparallel backgrounds the excluded lines coincide and the common domain is connected. And "the only failure is inadmissibility" claimed too much: what is established is that *the comparison square is defined and commutes on the prescribed joint domain; outside it, this particular pair of conditioned presentations is not simultaneously defined* — the underlying real bundle and its flat connection remain well defined everywhere, and a third background $R''$ may supply a valid chart across the excluded region, so witnesses in different components of $U_R\cap U_{R'}$ cannot be compared continuously *using those two prescriptions*, which is not a prohibition on the physical comparison. This is the principal conceptual hurdle, and it is recorded as such: the rule $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r>0$ is a chosen way of obtaining a local orientation, derived from no centrade inventory and no canonical history equation, and if changing $R$ changes only the chart then nothing measurable changes. A Machian result requires the background to select a physically distinguished domain or attestation law and not merely a convenient trivialization of $\gamma^1$ — the difference between a failed chart and a physical obstruction being exactly what the native intertwiner, when built, would have to decide.

**Corrections carried into §XXVIII.8 [T].** The discriminant $\mathcal D = 0$ does not by itself mean collapse to a scalar action — $\begin{psmallmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{psmallmatrix}$ has $\mathcal D = 0$ and one eigenvector — so the Schwarzschild acceptance condition for the simple model is the scalar degeneracy $\alpha\to0\Rightarrow\mathcal Z\to xI$, which the operator $xI+\alpha\mathbb J$ satisfies. Witness agreement $\mathcal K_C = T_{CB}\mathcal K_BT_{CB}^{-1}$ may not be imposed, since it would build the apparent objectivity into a definition; the theorem to prove is that independently constructed attestation operators and independently constructed passages agree in transported form under stated conditions. The Hodge star presupposes the metric and orientation, so its complex structure is a model of an imaginary operation arising from real geometry and not evidence that the bivector space is prior to the canonical complex space; the genuinely new result would derive the conformal structure, or its duality, from the project's real passage data; and a real carrier that merely realifies a complex carrier renames the imaginary direction rather than explaining it — the status of the fibers above, though not of the bundle $E$, which being nonorientable is no complex line bundle's realification. The Will coefficient $\partial\Omega_H/\partial J_R = 2/R^3$ is a perturbatively exact leading-order result, not a law for arbitrary rings and spins. Three result types are kept explicit throughout Part XXVIII: reproduced literature (Will, Cabrera-Munguia, Astorino–Torresan, Brill–Lindquist, Couch–Torrence), independently checked algebra (the cubic's limits, the Kerr splitting, $\star^2 = -I$, the end invariants, the $S_3\to S_2$ hierarchy, the flat holonomy and the $\mathbb Z_2$ above), and Projective-Gravity-native derivation — of which there is, as yet, none in this Part, the commutator result above being checked algebra on an existing carrier. The experiment that would produce one is the referee's: a real carrier defined without borrowing the Hopf complex structure, two passage maps from the existing geometry (a change of witness and a change of background), and the compatibility equations $T\mathbb J = \mathbb JT$ solved for $\mathbb J^2 = -I$, possibly up to sign; the six-dimensional bivector representation, where non-abelian complex-linear holonomy is possible, is the richer candidate if the two-plane proves too small.

## XXVIII.10 Toward the attestation law from the frozen primitives [D/S/O]

**The toy closed, with two last corollaries [T/V].** §XXVIII.9 is closed as a completed toy-model investigation, its ledger L1–L9 standing with two additions. *L10, two-background rigidity.* If a connected population of witnesses with one background-independent polarization map $p$ attests one common splitting under two nonparallel backgrounds $\mathbf r$ and $\mathbf s$, then $|\mathbf n_B\cdot\mathbf r| = c$ and $|\mathbf n_B\cdot\mathbf s| = d$ for every witness; for each choice of signs these are two independent linear conditions whose solution line meets the sphere in at most two points, so at most four projective axes satisfy both (two in a checked instance), and a continuous $p$ from a connected region into a finite set is constant: *spectral coherence under two nonparallel backgrounds with a fixed polarization map forces the map to be constant on each connected witness region* — under one background a whole level circle may share a splitting, under two the population cannot explore even that circle. The qualification governs its use: the theorem assumes $p$ does not change when $R$ changes, and a physical theory of background-conditioned polarizations may have $p = p_R$, in which case it does not apply directly. *L7, strengthened.* Reversal is an orthogonal conjugacy and not merely an isospectrality: with the global bundle automorphism $F(s,\mathbf v) = (s,-\mathbf v)$, $F\mathcal K_RF^{-1} = \mathcal K_{-R}$ exactly (checked) — and whether $F$ is an admissible physical equivalence is a question for the centrade passage theory, so reversal is not yet declared a relabelling. The investigation has established, in its model, *real geometry $\to$ real operator $\to$ complex spectral presentation*, with global topology and background selection governing the compatibility of presentations; it has not established that the passage-invariant reality of centrades is the physical structure generating Kerr's imaginary-worldline description, and no further example with the same vector and connection would.

**Three questions before any coefficient [D/O].** The next construction is the intertwiner $\mathfrak A:(\mathcal Q_A,\Xi_{BA},R)\mapsto\mathcal K_{B\leftarrow A\mid R}$, and its domain, codomain and transformation laws come before any function resembling $a$. The frozen primitives answer the three questions this far and no further. *What is $\mathcal Q_A$?* The source data independently available in the frozen architecture are the inventory of §XIII.5 — $(M_A,J_A,Q_A,A_A,\ldots)$ with its nonextremality gap $\Delta_A = M_A^2-a_A^2-Q_A^2$ and the distinction between a formal repacking at fixed $\Delta$ and a physical process at fixed irreducible mass — together with the quasi-local horizon spin of §XXVIII.7, defined once a rotational field on the horizon is specified, and the mass-current multipoles that carry the invariant content of $a_A = J_A/M_A$; none of these contains a complex separation, so $\mathcal Q_A$ built from them does not build the desired answer into its definition — and since the inventory already contains $J_A/M_A$, the ambition is not to obtain the value of $a$ from nothing but to derive why that real, independently established source datum appears as a particular complex separation and why different witnesses attest it coherently, which is an achievement in its own right. *What is an admissible $\Xi_{BA}$?* Not a path in $\mathbb{RP}^2$ but an actual correspondence already in the manuscript: the common wavefront of §XXVII.5 and its branches, the admissibility filter A–J of §XXVI.3 on co-middle passages, and the commuting-quaternion criterion of §XXVII.9 on paired histories — the objects that decide whether two histories belong to one class, with the round-sphere lemma and the Berger pair's non-commutation as the first instances of inadmissibility. *What does $R$ contribute?* Three different things with different consequences, to be kept apart: a frame, as the orientation selection $s_R$ of §XXVIII.9 supplies locally; an admissibility condition, as the domain $U_R$ and its components supply; or an actual interaction, as the Will ring of §XXVIII.7 supplies to the horizon's rotation — and in the frozen architecture the candidates for $R$ are the twin end of the arena, the meridian, and the co-middle axis family, each of which realizes a different one of these roles. *Transformation laws.* Under a change of witness, $\mathcal K$ must transform by conjugation with the independently constructed passage transport, $\mathcal K_{C\leftarrow A\mid R} = T^{(R)}_{CB}\mathcal K_{B\leftarrow A\mid R}(T^{(R)}_{CB})^{-1}$, which is the equality to be *derived*; under a change of background, the orientation part transforms by the cocycle $t_{RR'}$ while any change of splitting must be a derived response and not a chart; and under the rendering covariance of Part XIX, Law I, $\mathfrak A$ must be equivariant, so that the attestation is a property of the history class and not of a presentation. The codomain is an endomorphism bundle over a real two-plane not to be declared categorically different from the toy's before it is constructed — what is known is that a *global* identification with the separately trivialized vertical plane $\mathcal D$ of §XXVI.13 is obstructed over the same comparison base (R2), while local maps, pullbacks and differently twisted carriers remain possibilities — with the global-splitting obstruction L4 applying to whichever nonorientable carrier is chosen. The acceptance test is the referee's and is not negotiable: independently constructed witness passages carry one attestation to another; the spectral information carries physically justified source data; the isolated Kerr limit retains the content of $a = J/M$; the isolated Schwarzschild limit removes the spin-induced splitting without removing the real carrier; and source-intrinsic angular momentum is distinguished from environmental dragging, with Will's $J_H = 0$, $\Omega_H\neq0$ as the benchmark that any such law must reproduce. The informative route remains L8's: rather than agreement as a postulate, whether the physical history constraints themselves restrict the available polarizations to a coherence submanifold — which would be the first place the definition of centrades as passage-invariant structure across co-middle spaces does work in the mathematics, and the step with the greatest potential to change the theory's physical standing.

## XXVIII.11 The real-first reconstruction problem: from passage geometry to complexified canonical transport [T/V/D/O]

**The ambition, stated carefully [S].** The author's proposal of 10 October: discharge every place in the theory that refers to the underlying complexified spacetime — the bi-connections among them — through the newly established rendition of what complexification is. The document of the same day agrees with the direction and fixes its formulation: v32 has established a real-first mathematical model of *complex spectral presentation*; it has not established what the theory's complexified spacetime physically is, and an elegant construction must not be used to justify earlier assumptions it does not entail. Several different things are called complex in the manuscript and cannot be identified by fiat: the toy's rank-two polarization plane locally equipped with $\mathbb J$; Part I's complexified rest space and complex source worldline; Part XV's analytic continuation of histories into complexified directions $z^j = x^j+iy^j$, whose imaginary directions are *additional tangent directions*, not $90^\circ$ rotations within the real tangent space; Part XVII's two real structures on phase-and-scale transport; Part XIX's complex axial datum $\zeta = \delta+ia$; Part XXVI's complexified vertical doublet; and the self-dual bivectors, complex eigenspaces of Hodge duality on six real dimensions. The research question is accordingly not "can the new construction replace all complexified spacetime" but *can each formerly assumed complex operation be recovered as a functorial representation of a real passage structure, with the correct geometry, connection, holonomy and physical readout* — the backward direction, real passage structure $\to$ compatible complex presentations $\to$ existing constructions, which is the stronger test and which has exact theorems, obstructions and failure conditions from the start. The audit's working classification, for each earlier construction: *derived*, *algebraically re-expressed; physical identification not discharged*, or *additional ingredient indispensable*. The dangerous shortcut is named and forbidden: writing an operator squaring to $-I$ beside each old complex expression and calling the complexification derived would move the assumptions into new notation.

**First exact target, achieved: Part XVII's compact/split diamond from real operators [T/V].** On a real plane with $\mathbb J^2 = -I$ every complex scalar has the real representation $\Phi_{\mathbb J}(u+iv) = uI+v\mathbb J$, multiplicative because $\mathbb J^2 = -I$ (checked), and a nonzero complex number $e^{\eta+i\phi}$ becomes the single real operator $G(\eta,\phi) = e^\eta(\cos\phi\,I+\sin\phi\,\mathbb J)$ — $I$ generating dilation, $\mathbb J$ rotation: one real carrier with both phase and scale, the fiberwise $\mathbb C^\times$ of Parts X, XV and XVII without a complex coordinate. Two involutions are then available, $\sigma(G) = FGF^{-1}$ with $F = {\rm diag}(1,-1)$ and $\rho(G) = (G^T)^{-1}$, and they act differently: $\sigma:G(\eta,\phi)\mapsto G(\eta,-\phi)$, $\rho:G(\eta,\phi)\mapsto G(-\eta,\phi)$ (both checked), with ${\rm Fix}(\sigma)\cong\mathbb R^\times$ and ${\rm Fix}(\rho)\cong U(1)$ — the fiberwise group theory of the compact/split diamond of Part XVII, recovered from real operations. Both involutions globalize on the twisted carrier: $F$ is the global bundle automorphism of L7, and the inverse transpose is defined by the Euclidean metric, so the diamond's algebra lives on $E$ over the unoriented axes — with the subtlety that $E$ has no globally chosen $\mathbb J$, so the $U(1)$ structures are local and glued by the reflection acting as conjugation: the involutions are global, a globally preferred complex trivialization is not. The decisive refinement comes free, with the active/passive distinction of §XXVIII.9 kept explicit: reversing the imaginary orientation *at fixed $(\eta,\phi)$*, $G_{-\mathbb J}(\eta,\phi) = G_{\mathbb J}(\eta,-\phi) = FG_{\mathbb J}(\eta,\phi)F^{-1}$, is the active reflection-conjugation and implements $\sigma$ — it does *not* implement $\rho$ (checked) — whereas describing the *same* operator in the opposite convention changes its angular coordinate too, $G_{\mathbb J}(\eta,\phi) = G_{-\mathbb J}(\eta,-\phi)$ (checked), and nothing happens to the operator; a change of imaginary notation is not a transformation. So the background-orientation operation of §XXVIII.9, taken actively, is the *phase conjugation*, and Part XV's conjugate-history exchange, which reverses the *scale* while preserving the phase, is a different operation that the orientation sector cannot supply; two distinct operations are required, and the real-matrix language makes this unusually clear. Its limits are exact: this recovers the algebra of Part XVII, not its holomorphic connection, its nonzero curvature, or its action on spacetime histories. Part X's complex meridian parameter $w = e^{i(\chi+i\mu)} = e^{-\mu}e^{i\chi}$ likewise has the real representation $W = e^{-\mu}(\cos\chi\,I+\sin\chi\,\mathbb J)$, phase and modulus together without a new physical coordinate — algebraically re-expressed, with why the scale $\mu$ should control Reissner–Nordström chiral weights not discharged, as Part X itself left it.

**First serious obstruction, proved: the flat phase plane is not the Hopf phase bundle [T/V].** Pull the carrier back to the oriented-axis sphere, $\pi:S^2\to\mathbb{RP}^2$. There the tautological line has the global unit section $\mathbf n$, so $\pi^*E\cong\underline{\mathbb R}^2$ — a trivial bundle which, with its chosen ordinary complex structure, is a trivial complex line bundle with $c_1(\pi^*E) = 0$; the Hopf line bundle of the frozen architecture has $c_1(L_H) = \pm1$ (checked: the Berry flux of the spin-$\tfrac12$ coherent state over the sphere is $2\pi\times1.003$ against the flat plane's $0$). Hence $\pi^*E\not\cong L_H$ as complex line bundles — an obstruction no choice of connection can repair, since the characteristic classes differ, and the sharpest fact of the branch so far: the projected connection of §XXVIII.9 is flat and the Hopf connection carries the monopole curvature Part XV needs, so a direct identification would erase exactly that curvature. The real-first approach is not abandoned by this; it is told what it must build — a construction relating two different bundles, through a larger real carrier, a nontrivial associated bundle, an intertwiner, or a reconstruction of the Hopf principal bundle from additional real data. One such datum is identified exactly: the oriented tangent plane of the axis sphere, real rank two, has Euler number $c_1(TS^2) = 2$ (Gauss–Bonnet, $\int K\,dA = 4\pi$), and the Hopf line with $c_1 = 1$ is its square root — the *spin structure* of the axis sphere. A real-first reconstruction of the Hopf phase must therefore supply the spin structure of the co-middle axis sphere, which the flat quaternionic plane does not, and which the real tangent geometry of the axis sphere does. The rank-two toy has provided an algebraic mechanism; it has not reproduced the topology of the canonical geometry, and that is why it may not be said to have told us what all complexified spacetime is.

**The decisive test, posed: Part XV's bi-connection [D/O].** The frozen manuscript's exchange-related Weyl-type connections $\nabla^\pm_ah_{bc} = \mp2A_ah_{bc}$, mean Levi-Civita, were later reinterpreted: the nontrivial scale response arises from one analytically continued $\mathbb C^\times$-connection $\mathcal A_{\mathbb C} = i\,b_j(z)\,dz^j$ evaluated on conjugate complex histories, with $\mathcal A_H = b_j\,dx^j$ and $A = -b_j\,dy^j$ at the real locus and the mixed-curvature identity $F_A(v,J_{\rm base}w) = -F_H(v,w)$, the scale component vanishing on the real locus and the descent into the middle-space connection conditional. The real-first attempt has a definite form. On a real rank-two bundle furnished by the physical co-middle structure, on a domain with a selected $\mathbb J$, a complex-linear connection is a real matrix one-form $\mathbb B = \alpha I+\beta\mathbb J$ with $\alpha,\beta$ real one-forms; the generators commute, so $\mathbb B\wedge\mathbb B = 0$ (checked) and the curvature is $\mathbb F = d\alpha\,I+d\beta\,\mathbb J$ when the frame makes $\mathbb J$ parallel — an exact separation of scale curvature from phase curvature, local in scope: on the nontrivial Hopf bundle $\beta$ cannot be one globally defined one-form whose exterior derivative is the monopole curvature, since Stokes would force $\int_{S^2}d\beta = 0$; the connection is patchwise, local forms related by gauge transformations on overlaps, and on the nonorientable carrier the coefficient of $\mathbb J$ also transforms with the orientation sign — so the reconstruction is of a connection on a specified bundle, not of a matrix-valued one-form. ## XXVIII.12 The Hopf phase bundle reconstructed from the real tangent-spin geometry of the axis sphere [T/V]

**The first discharge at the level of bundle and connection.** The obstruction of §XXVIII.11 said what a real-first reconstruction of the Hopf phase must supply — the spin structure of the axis sphere — and the referee's chain supplies it from real data already in the frozen architecture: the real oriented rest space $H_u$, its unit-direction sphere $S(H_u)\cong S^2$ with its round metric, the real tangent geometry $TS^2$, the spin lift of its Levi-Civita connection, and from these the Hopf $U(1)$ bundle and its curvature. Every step was checked against the frozen canonical connection. *Bundle.* The oriented orthonormal frame bundle of the round $S^2$ is $SO(3)$; its $\mathrm{Spin}(2)$-frame bundle is the double cover $SU(2)\cong S^3$, and the projection $S^3\to S^2 = SU(2)/U(1)$ is the Hopf fibration: $P_{\mathrm{Spin}(2)}(TS^2)\cong S^3\to S^2$, the spin structure being unique on $S^2$ ($H^1(S^2;\mathbb Z_2) = 0$) and existing because the Euler number $2$ is even. *Connection.* In the frame $(e_\theta,e_\phi)$ the Levi-Civita form is $\omega = \cos\theta\,d\phi$ (checked by the structure equation $de^\phi+\omega\wedge e^\theta = 0$, with $d\omega = -\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$ giving $K = 1$), and its spin lift is half the rotation angle: the regular patch potentials are $\beta_N = \tfrac12(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi$ and $\beta_S = -\tfrac12(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi$, each equal to $-\omega/2$ up to the pieces $\pm d\phi/2$ (checked) — *locally* exact only: on a small patch where $\phi$ is single-valued they are gauge terms, but on an annulus around the axis $\oint\tfrac12d\phi = \pi$ and $e^{i\phi/2}$ is not single-valued, so the half-angle adjustments are the change from the singular polar-frame description to pole-regular spin frames, not global $U(1)$ gauge transformations; the globally valid unit-winding gauge transformation is the full northern–southern transition $\beta_N-\beta_S = d\phi$, with $e^{i\phi}$ single-valued, which is what makes the global construction legitimate — the Hopf transition $e^{i\phi}$. The overall sign of $\omega$ against $\beta$ is the orientation convention: the opposite orientation of $S^2$ gives $+\omega/2$ and the dual line, $c_1 = -1$, which is the referee's orientation/dual convention and the same sign the earlier orientation-reversal results exchange. *Comparison with the frozen connection.* With $\psi = (\cos\tfrac\theta2,\ e^{i\phi}\sin\tfrac\theta2)$ the canonical $\mathcal A_H = -i\langle\psi,d\psi\rangle$ of §XXVI.10 has $A_\theta = 0$ and $A_\phi = \tfrac12(1-\cos\theta)$: $\mathcal A_H = \beta_N$ exactly ($0.117579$ against $0.117579$ at $\theta = 0.7$); the curvatures agree, $d\beta = dA_H = \tfrac12\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$; the Chern number is $\tfrac1{2\pi}\int F = 1.0000$; and on latitude loops bounding solid angle $\Omega = 2\pi(1-\cos\theta)$ the holonomy is ${\rm Hol} = \exp(i\Omega/2)$ at every tested latitude ($0.24799$, $0.73877$, $2.00321$ against $\Omega/2$). The four acceptance conditions the referee set — transition functions, Chern class, curvature, holonomy — are met, not merely the abstract group $U(1)$. *What is real in this and what is a representation.* The principal bundle $S^3\to S^2$ and its connection are real objects built from the real tangent geometry; the complex line $L_H$ is the bundle associated to $P_{\mathrm{Spin}(2)}$ by the defining representation of $U(1)\subset\mathbb C$, so the $i$ of the Hopf phase enters only as the representation of the real circle group $\mathrm{Spin}(2)$ on a complex line, and the factor $\tfrac12$ — the monopole charge — is the geometric statement that the spin lift turns a tangent frame through half its ordinary angle. The canonical Hopf phase bundle of the frozen architecture is thereby reconstructed from a real sphere's tangent geometry and its spin lift: the first discharge of an earlier complex ingredient at the level of its bundle and connection, with no fitted parameter, from primitives the manuscript already has. It is not the discharge of its physical interpretation, nor of the entire complexified spacetime.

**Scope, and the antipodal Pin$^-$ structure [T/V].** The result is the reconstruction of the *canonical degree-one Hopf bundle and its angular Berry connection* on the oriented-axis sphere, $\mathcal A_{\rm spin} = \mathcal A_H$ on $S^2$ in the agreed gauge and orientation. It is not yet $\mathcal A_{\rm spin} = \mathcal A$ on the entire canonical-history space: §XXVI.11 distinguishes the canonical Hopf curvature from additional connection components on a shell whose physical sources have not been constructed, and a comparison there would need a bundle map from the larger canonical-history space to the axis geometry and the connection components in directions not tangent to the sphere — the spherical calculation fixes the angular curvature $F_H = \tfrac12\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$ and nothing in further history directions; the extension to the full Part XV canonical-history connection is the outstanding theorem, taken up for the angular sector in §XXVIII.13.
