| Part XII's reading (i) | apparent size changes; inferred mass kept | inferred surface density varies; velocities are the physical family's | the angular, distance and flux map |
| Entry 288 (ℓ/M), reading (ii) | one physical galaxy at apparent scale $s$ | constant apparent $M/\ell^2$; constant speed if spectral velocities are kept | a velocity rendering $\propto\sqrt s$; the surface-brightness diversity |

Combining (i) and (ii) with a size-only factor $t$ gives $M_{\rm app}/\ell_{\rm app}^2 = M_0/(t^2\ell_0^2)$, which is no longer universal when $t$ varies. The readings cannot be combined verbally while keeping every favourable conclusion of each.

The constants differ. With $v^2 = CGM/\ell$ and the strict asymptote $v^4 = GMa_0$ ($a_0 = 1.2\times10^{-10}$ m s$^{-2}$), $M/\ell^2 = a_0/(GC^2)$:
- *compact normalization*, $C = 2.998$: $95.78\,M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$;
- *the $r_d^{\rm (st)}/\ell = 0.1$ family*, $C = 2.55664$: $131.71\,M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$, which matched at $M_0 = 6\times10^{10}M_\odot$ would choose $\ell = 21.34$ kpc;
- *Entry 288's reference galaxy* ($\ell_0 = 16$ kpc): $234.375\,M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$, $2.45$ times the compact constant.

"Holds automatically" in §XXIX.42(g)(iii) means the law's *form*, with the reference galaxy's own constant. The reference point gives $M_0/v_0^4 = 35.26\,M_\odot$ (km/s)$^{-4}$. The empirical value is $47\pm6$, which McGaugh relates to $a_0$ with a disk geometry factor $\chi = 0.8$, and the strict isolated spherical asymptote gives $62.8$. At fixed mass the reference point is $7.45\%$ high in speed; at fixed speed it is $0.125$ dex low in mass *[v35.4, R253]*. These three benchmarks stay separate.

**(d) The Fourier-norm wording [V; R215].** The frozen suite's v34.10-1 print says a mode $\cos nx$ "gains $n^2$ in the exchange norm". At constant lapse the $L^2$ norm gains $|n|$ and the squared norm $n^2$; for variable lapse the lapse term mixes in. The computed fractions, and the conclusion that they differ at first order, are unaffected.

**(e) Conventions and status [D; R216].**
- *Time.* The Hubble-time examples of §XXIX.41(d) use equal endpoint lapses, or a common normalized time. Once unequal proper-clock rates are divided out of $F$, elapsed proper times at B still carry the lapse conversion.
- *Fits.* "Observational fits: none" refers to the current predictive model. Part XII's older exploratory fits (§XII.3) belong to its detached wing.
- *Checks.* Some frozen checks test consequences of imposed premises: the zero far-side luminosity, and the arena constant matched to $a_0$. They are regression checks of the premises, not derivations; 130 checks are 130 assertions, not 130 established mechanisms.
- *Darkness.* "Empty of matter" in Entry 286's paraphrase is the author's proposed reading. The mathematics uses the barren-twin readout of §§V.2–3, an empty resolved readout, not an absence of matter along the meridian, and darkness remains a selection hypothesis. Fast test orbits in a tracer-free region become observable only with a specified tracer, lensing measurement or detector response, computed with the same geometry and readout law.

The assessment's continuation brief for the v34 wing — P3's matter background, Law II, an evolving optical background, one forward image, the barren-twin selection, and the physical origin of the Tully–Fisher scaling — is recorded with the handoff of §XXIX.43(f), and none of it is attempted here.

## XXX.13 The conveyor typed globally: the axis-family obstruction and the trigonal-frame construction [T/V/D/O; v35.1, R224; v35.4, R247] *(`v35_1_global_typing()`)*

*The second review of v35.0 asked for the conveyor to be typed globally, as either a construction or a scoped no-go. This section gives one of each.*

**(a) The carrier.** The shift $S$ of §XXX.3 acts on the weight lines of the spin-one carrier at one selected axis. Equivalently it acts on the multiplicity space $G_{\rm gen}$ of §XXI.4b, whose lines are the weight lines. The matter field is $S_D\otimes G_{\rm gen}$, with Lorentz transformations acting on $S_D$ (§XXI.4b), so the question is how $S$ extends as the axis varies.

**(b) A scoped no-go over the axis family [T/V].** Over the sphere of oriented axes the three weight lines are line bundles with Chern numbers $0$, $+2$ and $-2$ for $m = 0$, $+1$, $-1$, computed here by a lattice Berry flux as §XXI.4c states. A global unitary bundle map $L_0\to L_+$ would need equal first Chern classes. Covering an invertible axis map $f$ instead, it would need $0 = 2\deg f$ with $\deg f = \pm1$. So no conveyor over the axis family cycles the three lines. The fixed-axis $S$ does not globalize there.

A consequence for the joint rendering follows. Equal unordered spectra at each axis do not make the matched renderings globally equivalent, because the eigenvalues sit on eigenline bundles of different topology.

**(c) The framed parent, and where the shift descends [V/D].** On spatial frames $Q\in SO(3)$, set $S(Q) = QS_0Q^{-1}$ and $M(Q,\theta) = QM_0(\theta)Q^{-1}$, with $S_0$ and $M_0$ the fixed-frame operators in Cartesian components. Then:
- $S(Q)^3 = I$ (to $2\times10^{-15}$);
- $S(Q)M(Q,\theta)S(Q)^{-1} = M(Q,\theta-2\pi/3)$ (to $6\times10^{-13}$);
- $M(Qh) = M(Q)$ for every rotation $h$ about the reference axis (to $10^{-13}$), so the mass operator descends to the axis;
- the shift does not. With $h_\gamma$ the rotation by $\gamma$, $S(Qh_\gamma) = e^{-i\gamma}S(Q)\,{\rm diag}(1,e^{3i\gamma},1)$ in the weight basis. The best complex coefficient $c$ (by least squares) leaves a largest-entry residual $\max|S(Qh_\gamma)-cS(Q)| = 0.39$ and $0.74$ at $\gamma = 0.37$ and $1$, and $3\times10^{-16}$ at $\gamma = 2\pi/3$ and $4\pi/3$, where $c = \omega^{\mp1}$.

Among rotations about the axis, $S$ is preserved, up to a cube root of unity, exactly by the third-turns: an axis with a *trigonal* transverse structure, the space $SO(3)/\mathbb Z_3$. With the oriented axis retained, its $SO(2)$ stabilizer preserves the projective shift exactly on the subgroup $\mathbb Z_3$. The pair consisting of the axis and the projective shift therefore descends to $SO(3)/\mathbb Z_3$. The shift alone has a larger projective stabilizer; the minimality assertion here concerns the axis-retaining pair (§XXX.14(a)). *[v35.4, R247]* On $SO(3)/\mathbb Z_3$ it is a genuine projective map on the pullback of the weight lines, equivalently of $G_{\rm gen}$. That is an explicit construction, not an argument from cohomology.

**(d) What HC space must supply [O].** The frozen geometry selects an unoriented line, the split real form of §XXI.4d. It does not select a trigonal frame. A conveyor of this kind therefore needs an extra selected datum: a reduction of the axis stabilizer $SO(2)$ to $\mathbb Z_3$, a "trigonal frame" field. HC space would have to supply it, with its rendering and descent, and say why it is selected rather than gauge. A frame whose choice is pure gauge makes no observable conversion.

**(e) Scope.** This is a scoped no-go plus one construction on an enlarged parent. It supplies no selection, no dynamics and no decay mechanism. The fixed-code reading stays a relation between descriptions: a physical conversion would need $105.15$ MeV for $e\to\mu$ at rest and $1671.27$ MeV for $\mu\to\tau$, with the exchanged energy and the other degrees of freedom identified (v35.1-3).

## XXX.14 Repairs of the v35.4 round: stabilizers, branches, spectra and scope [T/V/D; v35.4, R247–R249, R253] *(`v35_4_conveyor_stabilizers()`, `v35_4_potts_equilibrium()`, `v35_4_susceptibility_spectrum()`)*

*Two referee reports on v35.1–v35.2 found four statements of v35.1 wrong as written and several others misleading. The text above is corrected in place; this section records the checks that support the corrections. The referees' numbers are reproduced, including the six $\tau$ predictions of §XXX.11(i).*

**(a) Which object the conveyor retains [T/V; R247].** $\operatorname{Re}S_0$ and $\operatorname{Im}S_0$ commute, so the Cartesian shift has a real orthonormal eigenbasis. The rotations that permute its eigenlines with signs give the stabilizers:

| object | stabilizer in $SO(3)$ | order |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the linear operator $S_0$ | $V_4$ | $4$ |
| the projective class $[S_0]$ (up to a cube root of unity) | $A_4$ | $12$ |
| the oriented reference axis with $[S_0]$ | $\mathbb Z_3$ | $3$ |
| the mass operator $M_0(\theta)$ with $[S_0]$ | $\mathbb Z_3$ | $3$ |

The referee's counterexample is the half-turn $R_\pi = 2vv^{\sf T}-I$ about $v = (\sqrt{2/3},0,\sqrt{1/3})$. It preserves $S_0$ to $1.1\times10^{-16}$, sends $e_z$ to $(2\sqrt2/3,0,-1/3)$, and changes the mass operator by up to $1532$ MeV in its largest entry. So the shift alone descends linearly to $SO(3)/V_4$ and projectively to $SO(3)/A_4$; neither keeps the axis or its weight lines. The construction of §XXX.13 keeps the axis, and the axis-retaining pair descends to $SO(3)/\mathbb Z_3$. v35.1's "it descends to nothing coarser" holds for that pair only. [D] Which object the construction retains — the axis with its weight lines — is a choice that HC space would have to justify (§XXX.13(d)).

**(b) The selection toy's equilibrium branch [V within the toy; R248].** With $K = \beta J = \lambda h(\theta)$ the mean-field free energy is $f(s)/T = -(K/3)s^2+x_e\ln x_e+2x_o\ln x_o$, with $x_e = (1+2s)/3$ and $x_o = (1-s)/3$. Its landmarks:
- coexistence at $K_t = 4\ln2$, $\theta_t = 0.04438169$;
- the ordered spinodal at $K = 2.7456436$, $\theta = 0.04395789$;
- the disordered spinodal at $K = 3$, $\theta = 0.04794950$.

v35.1's solver returned the ordered root whenever $K$ exceeded the ordered spinodal. Between the spinodal and coexistence that root is metastable. At $\theta = 0.0442$ ($K = 2.76103528$) it gives $s = 0.47076336$ with $[f(s)-f(0)]/T = +0.00091030$; the equilibrium is $s = 0$. The suite now names both branches: the equilibrium branch (the global minimum, which jumps at $\theta_t$) and the metastable continuation (the descending-hysteresis branch, which jumps at the spinodal). No row of the table in §XXX.11(l) lies between the two, so its numbers stand; its label changes.

The exact other-code weight is $x_o = 1/(e^{Ks}+2)$. The power law $(m_{\rm min}/m_{\rm next})^\lambda = e^{-K}$ is its rigid asymptote: at coexistence $x_o = 1/6$ against $e^{-K} = 1/16$. The ratio $2.115$ at $\theta_t$ is the template's hierarchy, which sets the coupling; the rendered light-mass ratio there is $1.0310$ on the ordered side. The template spectrum and $h(\theta)$ have period $2\pi/3$, with the light pair degenerate again at $-2\pi/3$, so the mirror-code statement holds on the fundamental interval only. [D] Equilibrium and hysteresis are distinct protocols; which one a selection follows is part of the selection functional.

**(c) The susceptibility toy's spectrum [T; R249].** For $\begin{pmatrix}m_l&\varepsilon\\ \varepsilon&m_h\end{pmatrix}$ the eigenvalues are $\lambda_\pm = (m_l+m_h)/2\pm\tfrac12\sqrt{Q^2+4\varepsilon^2}$. At $\varepsilon = 1$ keV and the physical gap $Q = 105.1466$ MeV they move by $\mp0.00951$ eV (second order); at degeneracy by $\pm1$ keV (first order), a $2$ keV gap. A pure conjugation $U\,{\rm diag}(m_l,m_h)\,U^\dagger$ is exactly isospectral (to $4\times10^{-15}$) and needs compensating diagonal entries. So v35.1's "invisible in the masses" described the conjugation, not the toy.

**(d) Scope and wording [V/D; R253].** The remaining corrections of the reports are made in place:
- the drift bounds of §XXX.11(h) constrain coherent epoch differences and secular drift under fixed-scale and fixed-proton assumptions, and bound no stochastic process until one is specified;
- the invariant $I_{e\mu} = 5.024$ eV now precedes any statement about the electron's share in §XXX.11(i) and (m), with the electron-exact normalization ($m_* = m_e/f_e = 627.718461$ MeV, $\delta_e = 0$, $\delta_\mu = -1038.853$ eV) shown;
- the correction shapes are written $m_*[q_n+\varepsilon a_n]$ with $\varepsilon$ dimensionless, and the logarithmic shape's reference scale is $\mu = m_*$, absorbed by $m_*$ when changed;
- a self-energy evaluated at three masses can match any three corrections, so three masses cannot discriminate it;
- the $1889$ ratio of §XXX.11(k) is a scale benchmark;
- "about $1.3$ expected" in §XXX.11(m) is a rough density estimate;
- the arena-law reference point of §XXX.12(c) is $7.45\%$ *high* in speed at fixed mass.

The six $\tau$ predictions reproduce: $1776.969027$, $1776.966510$, $1776.967755$, $1776.967417$, $1776.967497$ and $1776.958248$ MeV.

**(e) Standing.** These repairs rescope rows of Part XXX's status table without reversing a conclusion: the global typing row (the axis-retaining pair), the selection-toy row (the equilibrium branch), the susceptibility and drift row (the spectrum; coherent drift), the corrections and scale rows (the invariant first; the benchmark) and the arena row (high in speed). The open bridges of §XXX.11(n) and §XXX.13(d) are unchanged.

## XXX.9 Register R203–R305 [D/O; v35.0–v35.8]

*The v34 register, R56–R202, is frozen in §XXIX.16. v35 continues the numbering. The section number is kept from v35.0, so the register precedes §§XXX.11–14 and Part XXXI, which it covers.*

- **R203** (§§XXX.1–2; Entries 281–285; six analyses). The entries are recorded, and the following are defined:

leaf's light serves at most two observers, the two-observer map, the cost of carrying one observer's visual space to another, the

parallax and timing against the stereographic radius; a minimal gateway kernel, as a class (screen transfer with an etendue exponent
kappa, distance duality, the brightness bound; what it postulates and what it forces) and a rotating ring through it; and what M31's Cepheids, M31's and M33's
proper-motion rotation and M33's masers already say about it, with the premises of the Cepheid bound.

v35_8_suite(): the author's note on reflectrons and its analysis: four reflectrons grouped into two centrons (the three pairings, the
order-8 relabeling group, the Hafnian of bosonic and the Pfaffian of Grassmann-odd reflectrons, with signs +, -, +); two reflectron
worldlines with matched vertices (the author's two figures as matchings, the alternation lemma, every matching through three loops);
what the matchings generate against QED's vertex diagrams (the known counts 1, 1, 7, 72 reproduced; the insertion-free 1PI diagrams
exactly through two loops, not at three); and the Born-rule regrouping as unitarity (the optical theorem in a finite unitary model).
With Entries 311-313: the inverse optical question (for an isotropic law, a metric answer unique up to a constant factor, whose fits to
matter fail, and the two-view uniqueness by the essential matrix); PG's solved rotation curves (Part XXV) read in gnomonic radius ell tan(chi), with the equatorial expansion
v^2 = v_eq^2 + A/R^2 and sharper sources settling onto the point source's curve; and what the gnomonic reading carries with it (density
pushforwards, shapes stretched by sec u, proper motions).
"""
import numpy as np
PI = np.pi
_CHECKS = []
def check(cond, msg):
    _CHECKS.append((bool(cond), msg))
    print(f"   [{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}] {msg}")

# ==================================================================================================== v35 body
# (the toy file appends everything below this line, reusing its own numpy, PI and check)
# PDG 2025 summary tables (charged leptons): masses in MeV, lifetimes in s, branching fractions
PDG_ME, PDG_MMU, PDG_MTAU = 0.51099895000, 105.6583755, 1776.93
PDG_TAU_MU, PDG_TAU_TAU = 2.1969811e-6, 290.3e-15
PDG_BE, PDG_BMU = 0.1785, 0.1737
# the inputs of Part XXI.4's time (its section XXI.4a quotes the tau mass 1776.86 MeV), for the post-freeze erratum (R211)
ERA_ME, ERA_MMU, ERA_MTAU = 0.5109989461, 105.6583745, 1776.86

def _v35_carrier(theta, mstar=1.0, alpha=PI/4):
    """Part XXI's spin-one carrier Sym^2 C^2 in the weight basis |0>, |+>, |-> of the selected axis: the clock R (rotation by 2 pi/3 about
    the axis), the shift S (|k> -> |k+1>), and the mass family M(theta) = m* [Re(e^{i theta} R) + cos(alpha) I]^2 (Part XXI.4; XXIV.26)."""
    w = np.exp(2j*PI/3)
    R = np.diag([1.0, w, w*w])
    S = np.roll(np.eye(3), 1, axis=0).astype(complex)
    U = np.exp(1j*theta)*R; H = 0.5*(U+U.conj().T)
    M = mstar*(H+np.cos(alpha)*np.eye(3)) @ (H+np.cos(alpha)*np.eye(3))
    return R, S, M

def _v35_fit(mtau=None, me=None, mmu=None):
    """Part XXI.4's fit sqrt(m_k) = sqrt(m*) (cos(theta + 2 pi k/3) + 1/sqrt2), k = 0 tau, 1 e, 2 mu, by least squares on sqrt(m)
    (PDG 2025 unless other masses are given)."""
    from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar
    rt = np.sqrt([PDG_MTAU if mtau is None else mtau, PDG_ME if me is None else me, PDG_MMU if mmu is None else mmu])
    def best(th):
        q = np.cos(th+2*PI*np.arange(3)/3)+1/np.sqrt(2); a = q @ rt/(q @ q); return a, np.sum((a*q-rt)**2)
    th = minimize_scalar(lambda t: best(t)[1], bounds=(0.15, 0.26), method='bounded', options={'xatol': 1e-12}).x
    return th, best(th)[0]**2

def _v35_fit_rules(me=PDG_ME, mmu=PDG_MMU, mtau=PDG_MTAU):
    """The phase under five fitting rules: least squares in sqrt m; exact on (e, mu) -- equivalent to weighting by the PDG
    uncertainties --, on (mu, tau) and on (e, tau); least squares in log m.  Returns {rule: (theta, m*, predicted third mass or None)}."""
    from scipy.optimize import brentq, least_squares
    r = np.sqrt([mtau, me, mmu]); q = lambda th: np.cos(th+2*PI*np.arange(3)/3)+1/np.sqrt(2)
    th, ms = _v35_fit(mtau, me, mmu); out = {'least squares in sqrt m': (th, ms, None)}
    for name, (i, j, k) in (('exact on e, mu', (1, 2, 0)), ('exact on mu, tau', (2, 0, 1)), ('exact on e, tau', (1, 0, 2))):
        t = brentq(lambda x: q(x)[i]/q(x)[j]-r[i]/r[j], 0.15, 0.26, xtol=1e-15)
        m_s = (r[i]/q(t)[i])**2; out[name] = (t, m_s, m_s*q(t)[k]**2)
    sol = least_squares(lambda p: np.log(p[1])+2*np.log(q(p[0]))-2*np.log(r), [0.2222, 627.7], xtol=1e-15, ftol=1e-15, gtol=1e-15)
    out['least squares in log m'] = (sol.x[0], sol.x[1], None)
    return out

def v35_conveyor_on_native_carrier():
    print("\n== v35.0-1. the two renderings on the native carrier: clock, shift, joint against fixed-code rendering (R203-R205) ==")
    theta, mstar = _v35_fit()
    R, S, M = _v35_carrier(theta, mstar); w = np.exp(2j*PI/3)
    m = np.real(np.diag(M)); lab = {0: '|0> tau', 1: '|+> e', 2: '|-> mu'}
    S3 = np.linalg.matrix_power(S, 3); comm = S @ R @ np.linalg.inv(S)
    _, _, Mm = _v35_carrier(theta-2*PI/3, mstar)
    joint = np.max(np.abs(S @ M @ np.linalg.inv(S)-Mm))
    print(f"   weight basis |0> (axial), |+>, |-> of the selected axis (stored as |0>, |1>, |2>); clock R = diag(1, w, w^2), shift S|k> = |k+1>:")
    print(f"     S^3 = I to {np.max(np.abs(S3-np.eye(3))):.0e}; S R S^-1 = w^2 R to {np.max(np.abs(comm-w*w*R)):.0e} (Part XXI.4's C is S^-1, with C R C^-1 = w R).")
    Kp = (PDG_ME+PDG_MMU+PDG_MTAU)/(np.sqrt(PDG_ME)+np.sqrt(PDG_MMU)+np.sqrt(PDG_MTAU))**2
    print(f"   M(theta) = m* [Re(e^(i theta) R) + I/sqrt2]^2, fitted to the PDG 2025 masses (Part XXI.4's form, least squares in sqrt m): theta = {theta:.6f}")
    print(f"     (2/9 = {2/9:.6f}), m* = {mstar:.3f} MeV.  Diagonal in the weight basis: " + ", ".join(f"{lab[k]} {m[k]:.5f}" for k in (0, 1, 2)) + " MeV")
    th_lo, th_hi = _v35_fit(PDG_MTAU-0.09)[0], _v35_fit(PDG_MTAU+0.09)[0]
    print(f"     (PDG 2025: e 0.51100, mu 105.65838, tau 1776.93; their Koide ratio {Kp:.6f}).  theta - 2/9 = {theta-2/9:.1e}, while the tau mass's")
    print(f"     +-0.09 MeV moves this unweighted rule's theta over {min(th_lo, th_hi):.6f}-{max(th_lo, th_hi):.6f} -- a sensitivity of the rule, not a confidence")
    print("     interval; the uncertainty-weighted test is v35.1-4.  The closeness to 2/9 is numerical, not derived (Part XXI.4a).")
    sp_joint = np.sort(np.real(np.linalg.eigvals(S @ M @ np.linalg.inv(S))))
    print(f"   joint transformation (excitation and code together): S M(theta) S^-1 = M(theta - 2 pi/3) to {joint:.0e}; its spectrum")
    print(f"     {', '.join(f'{v:.4f}' for v in sp_joint)} is M's own: an exact covariance of the mass spectrum.  Full physical equivalence of the matched")
    print("     renderings -- the whole interaction structure, the axial/circular distinction of Part XXI.4a-4c included -- is an HC-level theorem target.")
    e = np.array([0, 1, 0], complex); chain = []
    v = e.copy()
    for n in range(4):
        chain.append(np.real(v.conj() @ M @ v)); v = S @ v
    print("   fixed code (the excitation cycled, the background M(theta) held): <S^n e|M|S^n e> = " + " -> ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in chain) +
          " MeV: e -> mu -> tau -> e.")
    # an exact symmetry cannot do it: the commutant of a nondegenerate M is the diagonal matrices (the null space of X -> X M - M X)
    basis = [np.outer(np.eye(3)[i], np.eye(3)[j]).astype(complex) for i in range(3) for j in range(3)]
    A = np.array([(E @ M-M @ E).ravel() for E in basis]).T
    _, sv, Vh = np.linalg.svd(A)
    tol = 1e-9*sv.max(); nullity = int(np.sum(sv < tol))
    null = [Vh[k].conj().reshape(3, 3) for k in range(9) if sv[k] < tol]
    offdiag = max(np.max(np.abs(X-np.diag(np.diag(X)))) for X in null)
    gap = min(sv[sv >= tol]); mgap = min(abs(m[i]-m[j]) for i in range(3) for j in range(3) if i != j)
    SM = np.max(np.abs(S @ M-M @ S))
    # S is not a rotation of the real carrier: in no phase convention of the weight basis is its Cartesian matrix real
    Bc = np.array([[0, 1/np.sqrt(2), 1/np.sqrt(2)], [0, 1j/np.sqrt(2), -1j/np.sqrt(2)], [1, 0, 0]])   # columns: |0>, |+>, |-> in (x, y, z)
    Bi = np.linalg.inv(Bc)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(350); ims, trs = [], []
    for _ in range(200):                                                     # random phase conventions of the weight basis and overall phases
        p = rng.uniform(0, 2*PI, 4); D = np.diag(np.exp(1j*p[:3])); X = np.exp(1j*p[3])*Bc @ D @ S @ D.conj().T @ Bi
        ims.append(np.sum(X.imag**2)); trs.append(abs(np.trace(X @ X.T)))
    min_im, max_im, max_tr = min(ims), max(ims), max(trs)
    Rcart = Bc @ R @ Bi; r_real = np.max(np.abs(Rcart.imag))
    K = m.sum()/np.sqrt(m).sum()**2
    print(f"   the commutant of M: the null space of X -> X M - M X has dimension {nullity}, spanned by diagonal matrices (off-diagonal parts {offdiag:.0e});")
    print(f"     the smallest nonzero singular value is {gap:.4f} MeV, the smallest mass gap ({mgap:.4f}).  So an exact symmetry ([T, M] = 0) is a")
    print(f"     diagonal phase and never maps e to mu; S itself does not commute with M (|[S, M]| up to {SM:.1f} MeV).")
    print(f"   the clock R is a real rotation in Cartesian components (imaginary parts {r_real:.0e}); S is not: in 200 random phase conventions of the weight")
    print(f"     basis and overall phases, the squared imaginary part of its Cartesian matrix X is {min_im:.4f}-{max_im:.4f} -- exactly 1.5 in every convention, since X")
    print(f"     is unitary with tr(X X^T) = 0 (to {max_tr:.0e}) -- and never 0: S maps the real axial vector to the circular (e_x + i e_y)/sqrt2, which is no")
    print(f"     multiple of a real vector.  Koide K of the fitted masses = {K:.6f}.")
    ok = (np.max(np.abs(S3-np.eye(3))) < 1e-14 and np.max(np.abs(comm-w*w*R)) < 1e-14 and joint < 1e-10
          and np.max(np.abs(np.sort(sp_joint)-np.sort(m))) < 1e-10 and abs(chain[0]-m[1]) < 1e-12 and abs(chain[1]-m[2]) < 1e-12
          and abs(chain[2]-m[0]) < 1e-12 and abs(chain[3]-m[1]) < 1e-12 and nullity == 3 and offdiag < 1e-9 and abs(gap-mgap) < 1e-8
          and SM > 1.0 and r_real < 1e-14 and abs(min_im-1.5) < 1e-12 and abs(max_im-1.5) < 1e-12 and max_tr < 1e-12 and abs(K-2/3) < 1e-12
          and abs(m[0]/PDG_MTAU-1) < 1e-4 and abs(m[2]/PDG_MMU-1) < 1e-3 and abs(m[1]/PDG_ME-1) < 1e-2 and abs(theta-0.2222) < 2e-4)
    check(ok, "two renderings: S^3 = I; joint S M(theta) S^-1 = M(theta - 2pi/3) (same spectrum); fixed code e -> mu -> tau; commutant of M diagonal; S never real")
    print("   [T] A cycle that is an exact internal symmetry, commuting with the mass operator (v35.1-3), preserves every mass, so it cannot turn")
    print("       an electron into a muon.  [T/V] On the native carrier")
    print("       the two renderings have an exact model: jointly with its code the shift returns the same spectrum (theta -> theta - 2 pi/3); held")
    print("       against one code it carries e -> mu -> tau.  [D] Identifying the conveyor with S.  [T] S is not a rotation: the native geometry")
    print("       supplies the clock R, not the shift; its proposed home is the hyper-canonical space, where T_relative (one excitation against a")
    print("       fixed selected environment) is to be induced by T_global (complete matched worlds).")

def _v35_f(x):
    """f(x) = 1 - 8x + 8x^3 - x^4 - 12 x^2 ln x, in 60-digit decimal arithmetic (it cancels to O((1 - sqrt x)^5) near x = 1)."""
    from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
    getcontext().prec = 60
    X = Decimal(repr(float(x)))
    return float(1-8*X+8*X**3-X**4-12*X**2*X.ln())

def v35_phase_family_and_gate():
    print("\n== v35.0-2. the phase family: the degenerate point, the massless boundary, the physical phase, and the decay gate (R206, R211) ==")
    from scipy.optimize import brentq
    theta_phys, mstar = _v35_fit()
    def masses(th, ms=mstar):
        return np.array([ms*(np.cos(th+2*PI*k/3)+1/np.sqrt(2))**2 for k in range(3)])   # k = 0 axial (tau), 1 (e), 2 (mu)
    m0 = masses(0.0); deg = mstar*(1/np.sqrt(2)-0.5)**2
    _, _, M0 = _v35_carrier(0.0, mstar); ev = np.linalg.eigvalsh(M0); rank_min = int(np.sum(np.abs(ev-ev.min()) < 1e-9))
    Kc = np.diag([1.0, 0, 0]).astype(complex); Kc[1, 2] = Kc[2, 1] = 1.0           # conjugation: |+> <-> |->, |0> fixed (on real-diagonal M)
    _, _, Mp = _v35_carrier(0.1, mstar); _, _, Mn = _v35_carrier(-0.1, mstar)
    kcov = np.max(np.abs(Kc @ Mp @ Kc-Mn))
    mb = masses(PI/12)
    branch = [th for th in np.linspace(-PI/3, PI/3, 6001) if np.all(1+np.sqrt(2)*np.cos(th+2*PI*np.arange(3)/3) >= -1e-12)]
    blen = branch[-1]-branch[0]
    Ks = [masses(th).sum()/np.sqrt(masses(th)).sum()**2 for th in (0.0, 0.1, 0.2, theta_phys)]
    print(f"   m_k = m* (cos(theta + 2 pi k/3) + 1/sqrt2)^2, m* = {mstar:.3f} MeV held fixed (an illustration, not other worlds):")
    print(f"     theta = 0: masses {m0[0]:.2f}, {m0[1]:.4f}, {m0[2]:.4f} MeV -- the light pair degenerate at m* (1/sqrt2 - 1/2)^2 = {deg:.4f}; the lowest")
    print(f"     eigenspace has rank {rank_min}; the conjugation K (|+> <-> |->) maps M(theta) to M(-theta) (to {kcov:.0e}), so theta = 0 is its fixed point.")
    print(f"     theta = pi/12 = {PI/12:.6f}: the k = 1 branch is massless ({mb[1]:.1e} MeV); the common-sign branch is |theta| <= pi/12 (length {blen:.4f} = pi/6)")
    print(f"     in each third of the circle; K = 2/3 along it ({', '.join(f'{k:.6f}' for k in Ks)}).  The physical phase {theta_phys:.6f} sits at")
    print(f"     {theta_phys/(PI/12):.3f} of the way from the degenerate point to the massless boundary.")
    rules = _v35_fit_rules(); d = [t-2/9 for t, _, _ in rules.values()]; t_emu, ms_emu, mtau_pred = rules['exact on e, mu']
    me_misfit = abs(masses(theta_phys)[1]/PDG_ME-1)
    items = [f"{k} {v[0]:.7f} ({v[0]-2/9:+.1e})" for k, v in rules.items()]
    print("   the phase under five fitting rules (PDG 2025), with theta - 2/9: " + "; ".join(items[:2]) + ";")
    print("     " + "; ".join(items[2:]) + f": from {min(d):+.1e} to {max(d):+.1e}.")
    print(f"     Weighting by the PDG uncertainties fits e and mu exactly (theta = {t_emu:.8f}, m* = {ms_emu:.3f} MeV) and predicts m_tau = {mtau_pred:.3f} MeV,")
    print(f"     against {PDG_MTAU} +- 0.09 ({(mtau_pred-PDG_MTAU)/0.09:.1f} sigma).  Least squares in sqrt m, which misfits m_e by {me_misfit:.1e} of its value, is kept")
    print(f"     for continuity with Part XXI.4; the weighted fit moves theta by {theta_phys-t_emu:.1e} and m* by {ms_emu-mstar:.3f} MeV.")
    # post-freeze erratum to Part XXI.4-4a (R211): the frozen phase 0.22227 is reproduced by no fitting rule, at the inputs of its time or now
    era = _v35_fit_rules(ERA_ME, ERA_MMU, ERA_MTAU); de = [t-2/9 for t, _, _ in era.values()]
    th_era, ms_era, _ = era['least squares in sqrt m']
    need = brentq(lambda mt: _v35_fit(mt)[0]-0.22227, 1770.0, 1780.0, xtol=1e-6)
    fz = masses(0.22227, 627.68); ce = masses(th_era, ms_era)
    print(f"   Part XXI.4's frozen fit, theta = 0.22227 rad = {np.degrees(0.22227):.3f} deg with m* = 627.68 MeV, gives tau {fz[0]:.3f}, e {fz[1]:.4f}, mu {fz[2]:.3f} MeV.")
    print(f"     At the inputs of its time (m_tau = {ERA_MTAU}) least squares in sqrt m gives theta = {th_era:.6f} rad = {np.degrees(th_era):.3f} deg and m* = {ms_era:.3f}")
    print(f"     MeV -- the frozen m*, not the frozen theta -- {th_era-2/9:.1e} from 2/9, with masses tau {ce[0]:.3f}, e {ce[1]:.4f}, mu {ce[2]:.3f}; the five rules")
    print(f"     give theta - 2/9 from {min(de):+.1e} to {max(de):+.1e}.  The sqrt-m rule would need m_tau = {need:.2f} MeV to give 0.22227: the frozen")
    print("     phase is likely a transcription slip (0.22223 written 0.22227) -- an inference; see the erratum notes in XXI.4-4a and section XXX.4a.")
    # the decay gate: the heavier light lepton -> lighter + nu nubar, Gamma ~ m_h^5 f(x), x = (m_l/m_h)^2 (Fermi theory, tree level)
    def gam(th):
        mm = masses(th); ml, mh = sorted([mm[1], mm[2]])
        return 0.0 if mh-ml < 1e-12 else mh**5*_v35_f((ml/mh)**2)
    g_ph = gam(theta_phys); ths = (theta_phys, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01, 0.0)
    rel = [gam(t)/g_ph for t in ths]
    sl = np.log(gam(2e-4)/gam(1e-4))/np.log(2)
    mm = masses(1e-4); Q = abs(mm[2]-mm[1]); smallq = gam(1e-4)/(64/5*Q**5)
    print("   decay gate: Gamma(heavier -> lighter + nu nubar) / Gamma(physical) at theta = " + ", ".join(f"{t:g}" for t in ths) + ":")
    print("     " + ", ".join(f"{r:.3e}" for r in rel) + ";")
    print(f"     near theta = 0 it falls as theta^5, the energy release Q to the fifth power (local slope {sl:.3f} at theta = 1e-4, where the rate is")
    print(f"     {smallq:.4f} of the small-Q law (64/5) Q^5, Sargent's rule).")
    print("     At the degenerate point no energy is released: both light charged leptons would be stable, and neither is singled out by its mass.")
    ok = (abs(m0[1]-m0[2]) < 1e-9 and abs(m0[1]-deg) < 1e-9 and abs(deg-26.923) < 0.01 and rank_min == 2 and kcov < 1e-12 and mb[1] < 1e-20
          and abs(blen-PI/6) < 2e-3 and max(abs(k-2/3) for k in Ks) < 1e-12 and abs(theta_phys/(PI/12)-0.849) < 0.001 and rel[-1] == 0.0
          and abs(sl-5) < 0.01 and abs(smallq-1) < 0.01 and abs(rel[0]-1) < 1e-12 and max(abs(x) for x in d) < 5e-6
          and abs(mtau_pred-PDG_MTAU) < 0.09 and len(rules) == 5 and abs(th_era-0.222230) < 1e-6 and abs(ms_era-627.68) < 0.01
          and min(abs(t-0.22227) for t, _, _ in era.values()) > 3e-5 and min(abs(t-0.22227) for t, _, _ in rules.values()) > 3e-5)
    check(ok, "phase family: degenerate pair at theta = 0 (26.92 MeV, rank 2, K-fixed); massless boundary pi/12; physical 0.849 of the way, within 5e-6 of 2/9 (five rules); frozen 0.22227 reproduced by none; gate ~ theta^5")
    print("   [T/V] The mass family has a degenerate, conjugation-symmetric point and a massless boundary; the observed hierarchy lies between them, near")
    print("         the boundary.  Its decay gate is closed at the degenerate point and opens with the energy release.  [O] What selects the phase.")

def v35_dephasing_vs_decay(V=0.002, delta=0.001, N=2001):
    print("\n== v35.0-3. rendering mismatch is not decay: dephasing without loss against decay into a quasi-continuum (R207) ==")
    # Toy A (minimal, generic): two internal components of one rendered particle, scrambled by independent random phase walks
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3501); nr, nt, Dph, dt = 20000, 40, 0.5, 0.05
    phi = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, np.sqrt(2*Dph*dt), (nr, nt, 2)), axis=1)
    a = np.exp(1j*phi[:, :, 0])/np.sqrt(2); b = np.exp(1j*phi[:, :, 1])/np.sqrt(2)
    surv = np.mean(np.abs(a)**2+np.abs(b)**2, axis=0); coh = np.abs(np.mean(a*np.conj(b), axis=0))*2
    tt = dt*np.arange(1, nt+1); kfit = -np.polyfit(tt, np.log(coh), 1)[0]
    print(f"   toy A (minimal): a rendered particle with two internal components, each phase a random walk (diffusion {Dph}).  The probability of")
    print(f"     finding the particle is exactly 1 by construction (phase-only evolution; numerically {surv.min():.12f}-{surv.max():.12f}), while the coherence")
    print(f"     between its components decays at rate {kfit:.3f} (expected 2 D = {2*Dph}).")
    # Toy B (minimal, generic): a discrete state coupled uniformly to a quasi-continuum: Weisskopf-Wigner decay
    Ek = (np.arange(N)-N//2)*delta; W = (N//2)*delta
    H = np.zeros((N+1, N+1)); H[1:, 1:] = np.diag(Ek); H[0, 1:] = H[1:, 0] = V
    ev, vec = np.linalg.eigh(H); c0 = vec[0, :]
    G_gr = 2*PI*V**2/delta
    gam = PI*V**2/delta
    for _ in range(200):                                                           # the band-limited pole: gamma = (V^2/delta)(pi + 2 arctan(gamma/W))
        gam = V**2/delta*(PI+2*np.arctan(gam/W))
    G_band = 2*gam
    ts = np.linspace(0, 5/G_gr, 101); amp = np.array([np.sum(np.abs(c0)**2*np.exp(-1j*ev*t)) for t in ts]); P = np.abs(amp)**2
    G_fit = -np.polyfit(ts[10:], np.log(P[10:]), 1)[0]
    print(f"   toy B (minimal): one level coupled with V = {V} to {N} levels of spacing {delta} (band half-width {W:.3f}, Gamma/band {G_gr/(N*delta):.3f}): survival")

    print(f"     and the fit agrees with it to {abs(G_fit/G_band-1):.0e}.  Gamma = -2 Im Sigma at the pole.  The finite model's spectrum is real: the pole is a")

    print("   [T] Scrambling the hyper-canonical components of a rendered particle removes interference, not the particle.  A lifetime needs open")
    print("       channels and a coupling: Gamma = -2 Im Sigma.  'Seeing spacetime wonky' must become such a coupling to count as decay.  These are")

def v35_lifetimes_from_masses():
    print("\n== v35.0-4. the standard lepton-universality tests with one weak coupling (R208) ==")
    f = lambda x: 1-8*x+8*x**3-x**4-12*x**2*np.log(x)
    x_mu = (PDG_ME/PDG_MMU)**2; x_te = (PDG_ME/PDG_MTAU)**2; x_tm = (PDG_MMU/PDG_MTAU)**2
    tau_pred = PDG_BE*PDG_TAU_MU*(PDG_MMU/PDG_MTAU)**5*f(x_mu)/f(x_te)
    MW = 80369.2; rW = (1+0.6*(PDG_MMU/MW)**2)/(1+0.6*(PDG_MTAU/MW)**2)       # W-propagator factors (1 + 3 m^2/5 M_W^2), PDG 2025 M_W
    tau_pW = tau_pred*rW; sig = np.sqrt((0.04/17.85)**2+(0.5/290.3)**2+(5*0.09/PDG_MTAU)**2)
    ratio_B = f(x_tm)/f(x_te); ratio_B_obs = PDG_BMU/PDG_BE; sigB = ratio_B_obs*np.sqrt((0.04/17.37)**2+(0.04/17.85)**2)
    lt = PDG_TAU_MU/PDG_TAU_TAU; m5 = (PDG_MTAU/PDG_MMU)**5/PDG_BE*f(x_te)/f(x_mu)
    print(f"   Fermi theory at tree level: Gamma(l -> l' nu nubar) = G_F^2 m_l^5 f(m_l'^2/m_l^2)/(192 pi^3), f(x) = 1 - 8x + 8x^3 - x^4 - 12x^2 ln x;")
    print(f"     x_mu = m_e^2/m_mu^2, x_te = m_e^2/m_tau^2, x_tm = m_mu^2/m_tau^2: f(x_mu) = {f(x_mu):.6f}, f(x_te) = {f(x_te):.8f}, f(x_tm) = {f(x_tm):.6f}.")
    print(f"   one G_F, fixed by the muon; the tau lifetime given its measured leptonic branching fraction (the standard g_tau/g_mu test):")
    print(f"     tau_tau = B(tau -> e nu nu) tau_mu (m_mu/m_tau)^5 f(x_mu)/f(x_te) = {tau_pred*1e15:.1f} fs against {PDG_TAU_TAU*1e15:.1f} fs ({100*(tau_pred/PDG_TAU_TAU-1):+.2f}%;")
    print(f"     {100*(tau_pW/PDG_TAU_TAU-1):+.2f}%, {(tau_pW/PDG_TAU_TAU-1)/sig:.1f} sigma, with the W-propagator factors, against an input uncertainty of {100*sig:.2f}% from B_e,")
    print(f"     tau_tau and m_tau^5).  Written as the lifetime ratio, the same relation reads tau_mu/tau_tau = {m5:.4g} against {lt:.4g}.")
    print(f"   the two leptonic branching fractions, by phase space alone: B(mu)/B(e) = f(x_tm)/f(x_te) = {ratio_B:.4f} against {ratio_B_obs:.4f} +- {sigB:.4f}")
    print(f"     (the two treated as uncorrelated): {(ratio_B-ratio_B_obs)/sigB:+.1f} sigma.")
    ok = abs(tau_pW/PDG_TAU_TAU-1) < 1.5*sig and abs(ratio_B-ratio_B_obs) < sigB and abs(m5/lt*tau_pred/PDG_TAU_TAU-1) < 1e-12
    check(ok, "lepton universality: the tau lifetime given its measured B_e (+0.36% with the W factors, 1.3 sigma) and B(mu)/B(e) (0.2 sigma), with one G_F")
    print("   [V, standard physics with measured inputs] The muon's and the tau's very different lifetimes are consistent with one weak coupling and")
    print("       their masses and open channels, at the few-per-mille level.  Any reading -- economical or broader -- must reproduce this.")

def v35_generation_transport():
    print("\n== v35.0-5. generation transport: an aligned identity, a global cycle, and the clock-shift group (R209) ==")
    from scipy.linalg import expm, logm
    R, S, _ = _v35_carrier(0.0)
    theta, mstar = _v35_fit(); _, _, M = _v35_carrier(theta, mstar)
    L = logm(S); G = lambda a: expm(a*L)
    al = np.linspace(0, 1, 11); ov = [abs(G(a)[2, 1])**2 for a in al]            # |<mu|G_alpha|e>|^2 with e = |+> = |1>, mu = |-> = |2>
    uni = max(np.max(np.abs(G(a) @ G(a).conj().T-np.eye(3))) for a in al)
    ends = (np.max(np.abs(G(0)-np.eye(3))), np.max(np.abs(G(1)-S)))
    # the group generated by the clock R and the shift S (with the phases they produce): the Weyl-Heisenberg group of order 27
    def key(Mx): return tuple(np.round(Mx, 9).ravel())
    grp = {key(np.eye(3)): np.eye(3, dtype=complex)}; frontier = [np.eye(3, dtype=complex)]
    while frontier:
        new = []
        for A in frontier:
            for g in (R, S):
                Bm = g @ A; k = key(Bm)
                if k not in grp: grp[k] = Bm; new.append(Bm)
        frontier = new
    hol = np.max(np.abs(S @ M @ np.linalg.inv(S)-M))
    print(f"   G_alpha = exp(alpha log S): G_0 = I to {ends[0]:.0e} (the aligned comparison), G_1 = S to {ends[1]:.0e} (the global cycle), unitary to {uni:.0e};")
    print("     |<mu|G_alpha|e>|^2 at alpha = 0, 0.1, ..., 1: " + ", ".join(f"{o:.3f}" for o in ov) + ".")
    print("     This is the principal logarithm's path, a chosen path in the group (other branches differ, v35.1-3), not an invariant: a fixed flat")
    print("     connection's holonomy is constant on homotopy")
    print("     classes, so a continuous degree of alignment needs curvature, or a change of endpoints, frames, background or connection.")
    print(f"   clock R and shift S generate a group of order {len(grp)} (the Weyl-Heisenberg group of Z3: S R S^-1 = w^2 R, its centre the cube roots of unity).")
    print("   A flat connection whose holonomy around a loop of order three is S would be trivial on contractible loops -- in a parallel frame, local")
    print("   transport is the identity: the aligned assignment -- and the cycle only around the loop.  The order-three cycle cannot be the holonomy")
    print("   of the frozen canonical transport (diagonal on the sectors, XXI.4b-4c), nor of any transport commuting with a covariantly constant")
    print(f"   nondegenerate mass operator (such holonomy is diagonal; S moves M by up to {hol:.1f} MeV), nor of a flat connection on spatial sections")
    print("   S^3 or RP^3 (fundamental group 1 or Z2; a curved connection can have holonomy S around a contractible loop).  Other spacetime transports")
    print("   need a dynamical construction, and their flavour-changing channels computed -- for mu -> e gamma, a dipole amplitude to compare with")
    print("   B(mu+ -> e+ gamma) < 1.5e-13 (90% C.L., MEG II 2021-2022).  The HC configuration space is the proposed home, not a proven one.")
    ok = (ends[0] < 1e-12 and ends[1] < 1e-10 and uni < 1e-10 and ov[0] < 1e-20 and abs(ov[-1]-1) < 1e-10 and all(np.diff(ov) >= -1e-12)
          and len(grp) == 27 and np.max(np.abs(np.linalg.matrix_power(S, 3)-np.eye(3))) < 1e-14 and hol > 1.0)
    check(ok, "generation transport: G_0 = I, G_1 = S, monotone e -> mu overlap; clock and shift generate the order-27 Weyl-Heisenberg group; S does not commute with M")
    print("   [S] The local, aligned assignment and the global cycle as two regimes of one transport, proposed as a flat connection.  [T] Not the")
    print("       frozen transport's holonomy, not one commuting with a covariantly constant mass, not a flat spatial loop.  [O] A spacetime coupling would")
    print("       need its amplitudes computed; whether a loop in the hyper-canonical space carries S (the Hopf third-turn gives the clock) is open.")

def _v35_far_hemisphere(alpha, ell_kpc=16.0, Msun=6e10):
    """Part XXIX.42(g)'s far-hemisphere continuation, solved independently of the frozen suite (post-freeze controls, R212-R213): the rigid
    closure's radial equation y'' + 4 y = -2 pi rho_eff(x) sin x for y = psi sin x on the unit S^3, by initial-value integration of a
    particular solution with y(0) = y'(0) = 0 plus A sin 2x fixed by y'(pi/2) = 0 (the twin-symmetric even sector); the source is
    exp(-tan(x/2)/alpha), normalised as in Part XXV.  Returns v(x) in km/s, the plateau, psi''(pi/2) per unit mu, the radial stiffness, (psi, psi') per unit mu,
    and mu = G M/(c^2 ell) (the last two used by v35.2)."""
    from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp, quad
    G, C, MS, KP = 6.67430e-11, 299792458.0, 1.98847e30, 3.085677581491367e19
    raw = lambda x: np.exp(-np.tan(x/2)/alpha) if x < PI-1e-12 else 0.0
    mass = 4*PI*quad(lambda x: raw(x)*np.sin(x)**2, 0, PI, epsabs=1e-15, epsrel=1e-12, limit=400, points=[0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0])[0]
    rho_eff = lambda x: (raw(x)+raw(PI-x))/mass
    sol = solve_ivp(lambda t, Y: [Y[1], -2*PI*rho_eff(t)*np.sin(t)-4*Y[0]], (0, PI/2), [0.0, 0.0], method='DOP853', rtol=1e-13, atol=1e-16,
                    dense_output=True)
    A = sol.sol(PI/2)[1]/2
    def psi_dpsi(x):
        x = np.asarray(x, float); xx = np.where(x <= PI/2, x, PI-x); sg = np.where(x <= PI/2, 1.0, -1.0)
        Y = sol.sol(xx); y = Y[0]+A*np.sin(2*xx); dy = (Y[1]+2*A*np.cos(2*xx))*sg; s, c = np.sin(x), np.cos(x)
        return y/s, (dy*s-y*c)/s**2
    mu = G*Msun*MS/(C**2*ell_kpc*KP)
    def v(x):
        _, dp = psi_dpsi(x)
        return np.sqrt(np.maximum(-2*np.tan(x)*dp, 0)*mu)*C/1e3
    d2_eq = -3*psi_dpsi(PI/2)[0]-2*PI*rho_eff(PI/2)               # psi'' + 2 cot psi' + 3 psi = -2 pi rho_eff at the equator
    def stiff(x):
        p, dp = psi_dpsi(x); d2 = -2/np.tan(x)*dp-3*p-2*PI*rho_eff(x)
        return d2+dp*(np.tan(x)+3/np.tan(x))
    return v, np.sqrt(2*d2_eq*mu)*C/1e3, d2_eq, stiff, psi_dpsi, mu

def v35_1_far_hemisphere_postfreeze(ell_kpc=16.0):
    print("\n== v35.1-1. post-freeze controls on Part XXIX.42(g): the finite-core far side and the equatorial orbits (R212, R213) ==")
    Gk = 4.300917270e-6                                                   # G in kpc (km/s)^2 / M_sun
    chi = lambda r: 2*np.arctan(r/(2*ell_kpc))                            # stereographic radius rho = 2 ell tan(chi/2), far side chi > pi/2
    rs = [103.45, 450.8, 1000.0, 10000.0]; out = {}
    for al in (0.1, 0.04, 0.02):
        out[al] = _v35_far_hemisphere(al, ell_kpc)
    print("   An independent solution of the rigid closure's radial equation (initial-value integration and matching at the equator, not the frozen")
    print("   suite's Green-function quadratures) gives the plateaus " + ", ".join(f"{out[a][1]:.3f}" for a in (0.1, 0.04, 0.02)) +
          " km/s at r_d/ell = 0.1, 0.04, 0.02, as Part XXIX.42(g).")
    tab = {}
    for al in (0.1, 0.02):
        v = out[al][0]; tab[al] = [float(v(chi(r))) for r in rs]
        print(f"   r_d/ell = {al}: far-side speeds at rho = " + ", ".join(f"{r:g}" for r in rs) + " kpc: " + ", ".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x in tab[al]) + " km/s")
    slopes = {al: float(np.log(out[al][0](chi(1e6))/out[al][0](chi(1e5)))/np.log(10.0)) for al in (0.1, 0.02)}
    Meff = {al: [r*float(out[al][0](chi(r)))**2/Gk for r in (1000.0, 10000.0)] for al in (0.1, 0.02)}
    print(f"     Every finite core declines at last: near a regular centre v ~ rho_near, so by the mirror v ~ 1/rho_far (d ln v/d ln rho between 1e5 and 1e6")
    print(f"     kpc: {slopes[0.1]:.4f}, {slopes[0.02]:.4f}).  The mirrored peak is finite: rising above the plateau toward the antipode, then falling to zero.")
    print(f"     Forced into a Euclidean spherical Newtonian estimator, M_eff = rho v^2/G falls with radius out there ({Meff[0.1][0]:.3e} -> {Meff[0.1][1]:.3e} and")
    print(f"     {Meff[0.02][0]:.3e} -> {Meff[0.02][1]:.3e} M_sun from 1000 to 10000 kpc): no non-negative spherical density does that, so the model gives a")
    print("     finite-range apparent mass discrepancy, not an interchangeable ordinary halo.  (These radii are checks of the assigned map, not distances.)")
    v1, veq1, d2, stiff = out[0.1][:4]
    # equatorial circular orbits: U = Phi + L^2/(2 ell^2 sin^2 chi), Phi = -2 c^2 psi; at the equator U' = 0 for every L, and
    # U''(pi/2) = -2 c^2 psi''(pi/2) + L^2/ell^2 (per unit mu c^2: -2 psi'' + l^2), with the continuous branch's limit l^2 = 2 psi''(pi/2)
    l2 = 2*d2; U2 = {k: -2*d2+(k**2)*l2 for k in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0)}
    q = [stiff(PI/2-dd)/dd**2 for dd in (0.0208, 0.01)]
    print(f"   Equatorial orbits (r_d/ell = 0.1): psi''(pi/2) = {d2:.5f} per unit mu, so the plateau v^2 = 2 psi'' mu c^2 ({veq1:.3f} km/s).  At the equator")
    print("     U' = 0 for every angular momentum L: circularity there fixes no speed.  U''(pi/2) = -2 c^2 psi'' + L^2/ell^2 is " +
          ", ".join(f"{U2[k]:+.4f}" for k in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0)) + " (per unit mu c^2)")
    print("     at half, once and twice the continuous branch's speed: the branch's limit is linearly marginal, slower equatorial circular orbits are")
    print(f"     radially unstable and faster ones stable.  Off the equator the branch's stiffness vanishes as {-q[-1]:.4f} (chi - pi/2)^2 per unit mu.")
    ok = (abs(out[0.1][1]-203.066) < 0.005 and abs(out[0.04][1]-216.184) < 0.005 and abs(out[0.02][1]-218.945) < 0.005
          and max(abs(a-b) for a, b in zip(tab[0.1], (174.35, 77.07, 39.51, 4.36))) < 0.01
          and max(abs(a-b) for a, b in zip(tab[0.02], (215.28, 287.32, 236.98, 39.45))) < 0.01
          and abs(slopes[0.1]+1) < 0.01 and abs(slopes[0.02]+1) < 0.01 and Meff[0.1][1] < Meff[0.1][0] and Meff[0.02][1] < Meff[0.02][0]
          and abs(U2[1.0]) < 1e-12 and U2[0.5] < 0 < U2[2.0] and d2 > 0 and abs(q[-1]+3.0946) < 0.001 and abs(2*d2-2.55664) < 1e-4)
    check(ok, "post-freeze: far-side speeds (174.35..4.36; the 287.32 peak) decline as 1/rho, M_eff falls; equatorial branch marginal, slower orbits unstable")
    print("   [V] The far-hemisphere continuation has a finite near-flat band and an eventual decline for every finite core; the equatorial limit of the")
    print("       circular branch is linearly marginal, and equatorial circularity alone permits other speeds and either stability sign.")

          and abs(l_match-21.34) < 0.01 and abs(A_ref-35.26) < 0.01 and abs(off_v-0.0745) < 0.001 and abs(off_dex-0.125) < 0.001
