v36_7_suite(): the review of v36.6, Entry 349 and the two responses on it.  The penalties of the admissibility geometry as functions of the full
two-sector configuration, through S = (n_L + n_R)/2 and D = (n_L - n_R)/2: v36.6's scalar, with the review's cone at the aligned vacuum
(alpha0^2/2 - (alpha0/2)|u_L - u_R| + O(u^2)), one point of a non-differentiable set that contains the whole coincidence set n_L = n_R; Entry 349's sine (|D| - sin alpha0)^2/2 --
in the responses' reading sin theta = |n_L - n_R|/2 a function of n_L.n_R alone, blind to the normal, zero again at pi - alpha0, quartic in the
twist -- and the response's 1 - cos(theta - alpha0), both conical at alignment in every exchange-even reading; the response's smooth form and the
review's |n_L + n_R - 2 cos alpha0 k|^2 (polynomials in S, smooth, zero exactly on the family; these lowest-order forms have about a quarter of the
gap at the same curvature, a smooth form with higher terms can have more); all blind to the fibre phases.  The localization model of v36.6-1 with
each, the probe's potential alone and the pinning with it, at the same coupling and at the same gap: the cone penalties' tilt follows the column
density, the smooth forms' (exchange-even, so flat at alignment) is confined to a patch where the matter is dense; the sine and 1 - cos keep
v36.6's modes and, isotropically, its scales (at the same gap the probe-only sine binds more strongly, V_sin <= V_old; at the same coupling more
weakly); with their pinning the lowest-order smooth forms lose the mode at the same coupling and regain one, weakly bound, at the same gap,
while a smooth form with a quartic term and v36.6's gap binds two (smoothness forbids the tail-following, not localization); the exterior
obstruction holds for every gapped penalty.  Off the ansatz: the mirror solution is a critical point of the full two-sector energy and, block by
block, a stable one, with one zero mode (the rotation about k, sin alpha), gapless along the disk for v36.6's scalar, the sine and 1 - cos and
gapped for the response's smooth form; a multi-start local search finds no lower state; from the sine's second zero the run stops at a wall held
by the grid, and the wall held at R_w has an energy with one maximum and no minimum, so the second zero leaves no metastable state.

v36_7_quick(): v36_6_quick plus v36.7's penalties.

v36_8_suite(): Part XXXIV, opened in v36.8 for Entries 351-353 and the three responses.  The complement of a Cartesian fibration: on the reading
of the two families as orthonormal bases of one complex carrier, Entry 352's rule (no fiber of one family privileges a fiber of the other) is
mutual unbiasedness, one condition, with its information content (one fiber blurs the other family; deleting a fiber keeps 2/3 of each;
H_X + H_F >= ln 3); no real pair realizes it (in every real pair some squared overlap is at least 4/9, a theorem whose proof is printed, attained
by the 96 rotations with entries +-1/3, +-2/3; a shell's left- and right-invariant frames are related by Ad_g); the weight basis of an axis is
unbiased to a frame exactly when the axis is a body diagonal, the frame's cyclic shift then the archive's clock R and its clock the conveyor S; the
circular lines meet the real slice only at 0, casting circles about the diagonal; unbiasedness alone leaves a torus of complements, the
weight-basis condition four, oriented fibers one; the selected axis fixes the frame only up to a circle, which keeps the lines and the mass
operator and moves the conveyor except at third-turns (relative Frobenius residual (2 sqrt2/3)|sin(3 gamma/2)|; the trigonal frame of XXX.13);
the dephasings commute and depolarize, the projectors do not.  The mass operator read on the Cartesian fibers: a circulant on a three-site ring,
the mean mass on every fiber; the archive's H the covariant central difference with a flux, the sine difference the spectrum of
D_F = sqrt(m*)(H + cos alpha I), M = A I + 2|c| d a one-hop operator, the dual factors the real and imaginary parts of one hop; the ring's holonomy
spectral data, invariant under rephasing and cyclic relabellings and conjugated by odd ones, the spectrum degenerate iff it is real; the e-mu
distinction the part odd under complex conjugation in the real frame (XXI.4a's K); the octants' Pancharatnam phases (spin one-half and spin one)
not the holonomy phase; Koide's relation the light cone of the trace-reversed Hilbert-Schmidt form on sqrt M, on the common-sign branch (D_F null
for every theta); the Fourier interchange, and trimaximal mixing excluded (NuFIT 6.0, without and with SK-atm).  The bare Dirac toy: the kinetic
term U(3)-invariant, the mass a Lorentz scalar (a spinor Lorentz transformation preserving the Dirac adjoint); the parent operator with an
anticommuting insertion, its square p^2 - Mint^2, the 7-d Clifford form, the mode reduction, det_F(p^2 - Mint^2) = prod (p^2 - m^2); the
interchange spinor of the flat parent, broken by the shells of a compact T^3 or by the three-site ring, whose constant term shifts the internal
momentum (not a 5-d bulk mass); the ring's masses Koide's amplitudes, linear against quadratic.  Residuals are printed in coarse bins (_v36_8_r),
so that the output does not depend on the machine's BLAS kernel.

_V36_GK = 4.300917270e-6                        # G in kpc (km/s)^2 / Msun
_V36_A0 = 1.2e-10*3.0856775814913673e19/1e6     # a0 = 1.2e-10 m/s^2 in (km/s)^2/kpc (3702.8)
_V36_K = 4.740470463                            # km/s per (mas/yr kpc)
# McMillan 2017 (MNRAS 465, 76), best-fitting model: disks (Sigma0 [Msun/pc^2], R_d [kpc], R_m [kpc]; Sigma = Sigma0 exp(-R_m/R - R/R_d)),
# and the bulge (rho ~ (1 + r/r0)^-alpha exp(-(r/r_cut)^2), mass 9.23e9 Msun), treated here as spherical with that mass.
_V36_MCM_DISKS = {"thin": (896.0, 2.50, 0.0), "thick": (183.0, 3.02, 0.0), "HI": (53.1, 7.0, 4.0), "H2": (2180.0, 1.5, 12.0)}
_V36_MCM_BULGE = (9.23e9, 0.075, 2.1, 1.8)

def _v36_table(txt):
    return np.array([[float(x) for x in l.split()] for l in txt.strip().splitlines()])

def _v36_mw_data():
    e, o = _v36_table(_V36_EILERS_TXT), _v36_table(_V36_OU_TXT)
    return (dict(name="Eilers et al. 2019", R=e[:, 0], v=e[:, 1], s=0.5*(e[:, 2]+e[:, 3]), R0=8.122, vsun=(11.1, 245.8)),
            dict(name="Ou et al. 2024", R=o[:, 0], v=o[:, 1], s=0.5*(o[:, 2]+o[:, 3]), R0=8.178, vsun=(5.1, 247.3)))
# (the radial component of the solar velocity enters the azimuthal speeds as U sin(Phi), odd about the centre-anticentre line, and cancels in
#  the symmetric wedge and tracer weights used here)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ PG's field on the leaf (rigid closure)
def _v36_gl_cumulative(f, xs, n=8):
    """Cumulative integral of the vectorized f over the sorted nodes xs (from xs[0]), Gauss-Legendre with n points per interval."""
    g, w = np.polynomial.legendre.leggauss(n)
    a, b = xs[:-1], xs[1:]
    t = 0.5*(b-a)[:, None]*g[None, :] + 0.5*(b+a)[:, None]
    return np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(0.5*(b-a)*np.sum(w[None, :]*f(t), axis=1))])

def _v36_gl_integrate(f, edges, n=16):
    """Integral of the vectorized f over the sorted edges' span, Gauss-Legendre with n points per piece."""
    return float(_v36_gl_cumulative(f, np.asarray(edges, float), n)[-1])

def _v36_sphere(rho, ell, M, n_lin=4000):
    """A spherical source on the leaf (Part XXV's rigid closure), twin-symmetrized: rho_eff(t) = rho(t) + rho(pi - t), rho vectorized on
    [0, pi), normalized here to unit single-copy mass.  y = psi sin x solves y'' + 4y = -2 pi rho_eff sin x with y(0) = 0 and y'(pi/2) = 0:
    y = (1/2)(sin 2x C - cos 2x S) + A sin 2x, C = int cos 2t f, S = int sin 2t f, A = -C(pi/2)/2.  Returns the grid, v (km/s), psi and v_eq
    (the equator by l'Hopital, v_eq^2 = 2 psi''(pi/2) G M/ell with psi''(pi/2) = -3 psi - 2 pi rho_eff)."""
    xn = np.concatenate([np.geomspace(1e-7, 1e-2, 400), np.linspace(1e-2, PI, 2*n_lin)[1:]])
    mass = 4*PI*_v36_gl_cumulative(lambda t: rho(t)*np.sin(t)**2, np.concatenate([[0.0], xn]))[-1]
    reff = lambda t: (rho(t) + rho(PI - t))/mass
    xs = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.geomspace(1e-7, 1e-2, 400), np.linspace(1e-2, PI/2, n_lin)[1:]])
    C = _v36_gl_cumulative(lambda t: -2*PI*reff(t)*np.sin(t)*np.cos(2*t), xs)
    S = _v36_gl_cumulative(lambda t: -2*PI*reff(t)*np.sin(t)*np.sin(2*t), xs)
    xs, C, S = xs[1:], C[1:], S[1:]
    A = -C[-1]/2
    y = 0.5*(np.sin(2*xs)*C - np.cos(2*xs)*S) + A*np.sin(2*xs)
    yp = np.cos(2*xs)*C + np.sin(2*xs)*S + 2*A*np.cos(2*xs)
    psi = y/np.sin(xs); dpsi = (yp*np.sin(xs) - y*np.cos(xs))/np.sin(xs)**2
    v2 = (_V36_GK*M/ell)*(-2*np.tan(xs)*dpsi)
    d2eq = -3*psi[-1] - 2*PI*float(reff(np.array([PI/2]))[0])
    veq = np.sqrt(2*d2eq*_V36_GK*M/ell)
    v = np.sqrt(np.maximum(v2, 0)); v[-1] = veq
    return xs, v, psi, veq

def _v36_partXXV(alpha):
    """Part XXV.3's source exp(-tan(t/2)/alpha), alpha = r_d/ell."""
    return lambda t: np.where(t < PI-1e-12, np.exp(-np.tan(np.minimum(t, PI-1e-12)/2)/alpha), 0.0)

_V36_NPHI, _V36_NGL = 64, 32
_V36_PHI = (np.arange(_V36_NPHI) + 0.5)*(2*PI/_V36_NPHI)
_V36_GLX, _V36_GLW = np.polynomial.legendre.leggauss(_V36_NGL)

def _v36_ring_kernel(x, xp, kern="twin"):
    """K(x, x') = int_0^2pi G_twin(theta) dphi', G_twin = cos 2theta/(4 pi sin theta), split into the two chords' elliptic integrals,
    1/(4 pi c) + 1/(4 pi cbar), and the bounded remainder g_rr = [cos 2theta - cos(theta/2) - sin(theta/2)]/(4 pi sin theta).  As controls,
    kern = "chords" keeps the two chord terms alone (a strictly positive kernel) and kern = "chord" the first alone (no twin)."""
    from scipy.special import ellipkm1
    sp, sm, cp, cm = np.sin((x+xp)/2), np.sin((x-xp)/2), np.cos((x+xp)/2), np.cos((x-xp)/2)
    p1 = np.maximum((sm/sp)**2, 1e-300); p2 = np.maximum((cp/cm)**2, 1e-300)
    if kern == "chord": return ellipkm1(p1)/np.abs(sp)/(2*PI)
    sing = (ellipkm1(p1)/np.abs(sp) + ellipkm1(p2)/np.abs(cm))/(2*PI)
    if kern == "chords": return sing
    th = np.arccos(np.clip(np.cos(x)*np.cos(xp)[:, None] + np.sin(x)*np.sin(xp)[:, None]*np.cos(_V36_PHI)[None, :], -1, 1))
    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
        g = (np.cos(2*th) - np.cos(th/2) - np.sin(th/2))/(4*PI*np.sin(th))
    g = np.where((th < 1e-6) | (th > PI-1e-6), -1/(8*PI), g)
    return sing + g.mean(axis=1)*2*PI

def _v36_graded(a, b, ga, gb, p=3):
    u = 0.5*(_V36_GLX + 1); w = 0.5*_V36_GLW
    if ga: return a + (b-a)*u**p, (b-a)*p*u**(p-1)*w
    if gb: return b - (b-a)*u**p, (b-a)*p*u**(p-1)*w
    return a + (b-a)*u, (b-a)*w

def _v36_disk_psi(Sig, x, xmax, brk, nref=12, kern="twin"):
    """psi(x) (unnormalized) of a thin disk Sigma on the great 2-sphere: Gauss-Legendre on pieces between the breakpoints and a geometric
    ladder x +- x 2^-k about the logarithmic singularity at x' = x, the two pieces touching x graded toward it."""
    dmin = x*2.0**(-nref)
    pts = [0.0, xmax] + [p for p in brk if 0 < p < xmax and abs(p-x) > dmin]
    pts += [x + s*x*2.0**(-k) for k in range(1, nref+1) for s in (-1, 1) if 0 < x + s*x*2.0**(-k) < xmax]
    if 0 < x < xmax: pts.append(x)
    e = sorted(set(pts)); T, W = [], []
    for a, b in zip(e[:-1], e[1:]):
        t, w = _v36_graded(a, b, abs(a-x) < 1e-15*x, abs(b-x) < 1e-15*x); T.append(t); W.append(w)
    t, w = np.concatenate(T), np.concatenate(W)
    return 2*PI*np.sum(w*Sig(t)*np.sin(t)*_v36_ring_kernel(x, t, kern))

def _v36_disk_v2(Sig, ell, M, xs, xmax=PI/2, brk=(), rel_h=0.02, hmax=1e-4, kern="twin"):
    """v^2 [(km/s)^2] in the disk plane, at the polar angles xs, of a thin axisymmetric disk of mass M and profile Sigma (vectorized, on the
    unit S^3) on a leaf of radius ell: v^2 = (G M/ell)(-2 tan x psi'), psi normalized to unit mass, psi' by central differences."""
    brk = list(brk)
    e = sorted(set([0.0, xmax] + [p for p in brk if 0 < p < xmax])); norm = 0.0
    for a, b in zip(e[:-1], e[1:]):
        t, w = _v36_graded(a, b, False, False); norm += np.sum(w*Sig(t)*np.sin(t))
    norm *= 2*PI
    out = np.empty(len(xs))
    for i, x in enumerate(xs):
        h = min(hmax, rel_h*x)
        out[i] = (_V36_GK*M/ell)*(-2*np.tan(x)*(_v36_disk_psi(Sig, x+h, xmax, brk, kern=kern) - _v36_disk_psi(Sig, x-h, xmax, brk, kern=kern))/(2*h)/norm)
    return out

def _v36_disk_v2_spectral(Sig, ell, M, xs, lmax=1200, npan=240):
    """A control on _v36_disk_v2 by another method: the Funk-Hecke expansion on the great 2-sphere.  psi = 2 pi sum_l lam_l sig_l P_l(cos x), with
    lam_l = (1/2) int_0^pi cos 2t P_l(cos t) dt = (pi/2) a_{(l-2)/2} a_{(l+2)/2} for even l >= 2 and 0 otherwise (a_k = C(2k, k)/4^k), and
    sig_l = (2l+1)/2 int Sigma P_l(cos x) sin x dx for Sigma normalized to 2 pi int Sigma sin x dx = 1 (the disk on the near hemisphere)."""
    a = np.ones(lmax//2 + 2)
    for k in range(1, len(a)): a[k] = a[k-1]*(2*k - 1)/(2*k)
    lam = np.zeros(lmax + 1)
    for l in range(2, lmax + 1, 2): lam[l] = 0.5*PI*a[(l-2)//2]*a[(l+2)//2]
    g, w = np.polynomial.legendre.leggauss(24); e = np.linspace(0.0, PI/2, npan + 1)
    xq = (0.5*(e[1:]-e[:-1])[:, None]*g[None, :] + 0.5*(e[1:]+e[:-1])[:, None]).ravel(); wq = (0.5*(e[1:]-e[:-1])[:, None]*w[None, :]).ravel()
    sq = Sig(xq)*np.sin(xq)*wq; sq /= 2*PI*np.sum(sq)
    def legendre_rows(u):
        P = np.empty((lmax + 1, len(u))); P[0] = 1.0; P[1] = u
        for l in range(1, lmax): P[l+1] = ((2*l + 1)*u*P[l] - l*P[l-1])/(l + 1)
        return P
    sig = (2*np.arange(lmax + 1) + 1)/2*(legendre_rows(np.cos(xq)) @ sq)
    u = np.cos(xs); P = legendre_rows(u); l = np.arange(lmax + 1)[:, None]
    dP = np.zeros_like(P); dP[1:] = -l[1:]*(P[:-1] - u*P[1:])/np.sin(xs)          # d P_l(cos x)/dx
    dpsi = 2*PI*np.sum((lam*sig)[:, None]*dP, axis=0)
    return (_V36_GK*M/ell)*(-2*np.tan(xs)*dpsi)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ the view from inside
def _v36_observe(ell, chi_sun, vsun_true, chi, phi, vc):
    """The Sun at polar angle chi_sun on the disk's great 2-sphere (azimuth pi), stars at (chi, phi) rotating at vc in the sense e_phi;
    light on the leaf's great circles.  Returns, in the Sun's frame (toward the centre, toward rotation), the direction n, D_A, the line-of-sight
    velocity, the proper-motion velocity D_A mu (the star's transverse motion at D_A, the Sun's at D_par) and the transverse direction w."""
    P = np.array([np.cos(chi_sun), -np.sin(chi_sun), 0.0])
    xO = np.array([np.sin(chi_sun), np.cos(chi_sun), 0.0]); yO = np.array([0.0, 0.0, -1.0])
    Q = np.stack([np.cos(chi), np.sin(chi)*np.cos(phi), np.sin(chi)*np.sin(phi)], -1)
    cd = np.clip(Q @ P, -1, 1); d = np.arccos(cd)
    n = Q - cd[..., None]*P; n /= np.linalg.norm(n, axis=-1)[..., None]
    k = -P*np.sin(d)[..., None] + n*np.cos(d)[..., None]
    w = np.cross(P, n)
    vstar = vc[..., None]*np.stack([np.zeros_like(phi), -np.sin(phi), np.cos(phi)], -1)
    vS = vsun_true[0]*xO + vsun_true[1]*yO
    DA = ell*np.sin(d)
    vlos = np.sum(vstar*k, -1) - n @ vS
    vt = np.sum(vstar*w, -1) - (w @ vS)*np.cos(d)                        # D_A/D_par = cos(d)
    return np.stack([n @ xO, n @ yO], -1), DA, vlos, vt, np.stack([w @ xO, w @ yO], -1)

def _v36_pipeline(R0, vsun_pipe, n2, DA, vlos, vt, w2):
    """The Euclidean Galactocentric reduction: X = (-R0, 0) + D_A n, v = v_los n + v_t w + v_sun; R, azimuth, v_phi in the rotation sense."""
    X = np.array([-R0, 0.0]) + DA[..., None]*n2
    v = vlos[..., None]*n2 + vt[..., None]*w2 + np.array(vsun_pipe)
    Phi = np.arctan2(X[..., 1], X[..., 0])
    return np.linalg.norm(X, axis=-1), Phi, v[..., 0]*np.sin(Phi) - v[..., 1]*np.cos(Phi)

def _v36_inside(ell, D, xs, vref, wedge=30.0, hR=3.0, U=None, nchi=1500, nphi=181, hw=0.25):
    """Linear response L and the Sun's offset S of the inferred curve at the data radii (inferred v = sqrt(f) L + S), and the bins reached by
    near-hemisphere tracers (exponential in arc length, scale hR, in the wedge |Phi - pi| <= wedge); the Sun's true speed is set by the
    measured Sgr A* proper motion, v_sun,true = v_y,pipeline/cos(chi_sun), chi_sun = arcsin(R0/ell).  A bin counts as reached when its centre lies
    within the reach R0 + sqrt(ell^2 - R0^2)."""
    U = D['vsun'][0] if U is None else U
    chi_sun = np.arcsin(D['R0']/ell); vS = (U, D['vsun'][1]/np.cos(chi_sun))
    smax = min(ell*PI/2, 60.0)
    CH, PH = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(0.02/ell, smax/ell - 1e-9, nchi), np.linspace(PI-np.radians(70), PI+np.radians(70), nphi), indexing='ij')
    out = []
    for vc in (np.interp(CH, xs, vref), 0*CH):
        n2, DA, vlos, vt, w2 = _v36_observe(ell, chi_sun, vS, CH, PH, vc)
        out.append(_v36_pipeline(D['R0'], (U, D['vsun'][1]), n2, DA, vlos, vt, w2))
    (R, Phi, vphi), (_, _, vphi0) = out
    wgt = np.exp(-ell*CH/hR)*np.sin(CH); sel = np.abs(np.angle(np.exp(1j*(Phi-PI)))) <= np.radians(wedge)
    L = np.full(len(D['R']), np.nan); S = np.full(len(D['R']), np.nan)
    reach_max = D['R0'] + np.sqrt(max(ell**2 - D['R0']**2, 0.0))
    for i, Rc in enumerate(D['R']):
        m = sel & (np.abs(R-Rc) <= hw)
        if Rc <= reach_max and m.sum() > 3:
            S[i] = np.sum(wgt[m]*vphi0[m])/np.sum(wgt[m]); L[i] = np.sum(wgt[m]*(vphi[m]-vphi0[m]))/np.sum(wgt[m])
    return L, S, ~np.isnan(L), vS[1]

def _v36_fit_f(L, S, D):
    """The mass factor f (all baryons scaled) minimizing chi^2 for v = sqrt(f) L + S; returns f, chi^2(f), chi^2(1)."""
    m = ~np.isnan(L); v, s = D['v'][m], D['s'][m]
    a = max(np.sum(L[m]*(v-S[m])/s**2)/np.sum(L[m]**2/s**2), 0.0)
    return a*a, float(np.sum(((a*L[m]+S[m]-v)/s)**2)), float(np.sum(((L[m]+S[m]-v)/s)**2))

def _v36_mw_leaf(ell, n=90):
    """McMillan 2017's baryons on a leaf of radius ell, placed by arc length s = ell chi from the centre and truncated at the equator: thin
    disks by the twin Green function, the bulge spherical.  Returns the angles, v^2 per component and the masses on the leaf."""
    xs = np.geomspace(0.05, min(40.0, ell*PI/2*0.999), n)/ell
    xs = np.unique(np.concatenate([xs, [s/ell for s in (8.2, 15.0, 20.0) if s < ell*PI/2*0.999]]))      # the quoted arcs, solved exactly
    comps, masses = {}, {}
    for nm, (S0, Rd, Rm) in _V36_MCM_DISKS.items():
        Sig = (lambda t, S0=S0, Rd=Rd: S0*1e6*np.exp(-ell*t/Rd)) if Rm == 0 else \
              (lambda t, S0=S0, Rd=Rd, Rm=Rm: S0*1e6*np.exp(-Rm/np.maximum(ell*t, 1e-12) - ell*t/Rd))
        brk = [r/ell for r in (0.5*Rd, Rd, 3*Rd, 10*Rd) if r/ell < PI/2]
        e = sorted(set([0.0, PI/2] + brk)); M = 0.0
        for a, b in zip(e[:-1], e[1:]):
            t, w = _v36_graded(a, b, False, False); M += np.sum(w*Sig(t)*np.sin(t))
        masses[nm] = 2*PI*ell**2*M
        comps[nm] = _v36_disk_v2(Sig, ell, masses[nm], xs, PI/2, brk)
    Mb, r0, rc, al = _V36_MCM_BULGE
    rho = lambda t: np.where(t < PI/2, (1 + ell*t/r0)**(-al)*np.exp(-(ell*np.minimum(t, PI/2)/rc)**2), 0.0)
    xg, vb, _, _ = _v36_sphere(rho, ell, Mb)
    comps["bulge"], masses["bulge"] = np.interp(xs, xg, vb**2), Mb
    return xs, comps, masses

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ SPARC under the gnomonic premise
def _v36_sparc(name):
    D, Inc, L36, Rdisk, MHI, Vflat, eVf, Q = _V36_SPARC_T1[name]
    R, Vobs, eV, Vgas, Vdisk, Vbul, SBd, SBb = _v36_table(_V36_SPARC_ROT[name]).T
    return dict(name=name, L36=L36, Rdisk=Rdisk, MHI=MHI, Vflat=Vflat, Q=Q, R=R, Vobs=Vobs, eV=eV, Vgas=Vgas, Vdisk=Vdisk, Vbul=Vbul,
                SBd=SBd, SBb=SBb)

def _v36_freeman(R, h):
    from scipy.special import i0, i1, k0, k1
    y = np.maximum(R, 1e-9)/(2*h)
    return 4*PI*_V36_GK*h*y**2*(i0(y)*k0(y) - i1(y)*k1(y))

def _v36_basis(R, h, k):
    """Euclidean Newtonian v^2 of Sigma = (R/h)^k exp(-R/h): Freeman's formula and its h-derivatives (R e^{-R/h} = h^2 d_h e^{-R/h})."""
    if k == 0: return _v36_freeman(R, h)
    dh = 1e-4*h; f0, fp, fm = _v36_freeman(R, h), _v36_freeman(R, h+dh), _v36_freeman(R, h-dh)
    d1, d2 = (fp - fm)/(2*dh), (fp - 2*f0 + fm)/dh**2
    return h*d1 if k == 1 else h**2*(d2 + 2*d1/h)

def _v36_sparc_sources(g, ups_d=0.5, ups_b=0.7, he=1.33, hmax=2.0, pen=30.0):
    """The observed baryons: the stellar disk 0.5 SBdisk (log-linear between the radii, flat inside, exponential with Rdisk outside); the gas
    disk as a nonnegative sum of (R/h)^k exp(-R/h) fitted to SPARC's Vgas|Vgas| with the total fixed to 1.33 M_HI; the bulge spherical,
    M(<r) = 0.7 r Vbul^2/G.  Returns the two surface densities (Msun/kpc^2), their masses, the bulge profile and the gas fit's rms.  v36.1: the
    basis's largest scale length (hmax R_last) and the mass penalty's weight (pen) are options, for the family of v36.1-4; the defaults are v36.0's."""
    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    from scipy.interpolate import PchipInterpolator
    R = g['R']; m = g['SBd'] > 0; Rs, lg = R[m], np.log(g['SBd'][m]*ups_d*1e6)
    Rd = g['Rdisk']
    Sst = lambda r: np.exp(np.where(np.asarray(r) <= Rs[0], lg[0], np.where(np.asarray(r) >= Rs[-1], lg[-1] - (np.asarray(r) - Rs[-1])/Rd,
                                                                               np.interp(r, Rs, lg))))
    Mst = 2*PI*_v36_gl_integrate(lambda r: r*Sst(r), np.concatenate([[0.0], Rs, R[-1] + Rd*np.arange(1, 81)]))
    target = g['Vgas']*np.abs(g['Vgas']); Mgas = he*g['MHI']*1e9; Rl = R[-1]
    specs = [(h, k) for h in np.geomspace(0.05*Rl, hmax*Rl, 10) for k in (0, 1, 2)]
    A = np.array([_v36_basis(R, h, k) for h, k in specs]).T; mass = np.array([2*PI*h**2*(1.0, 2.0, 6.0)[k] for h, k in specs])
    sc = max(np.max(np.abs(target)), 1.0)
    w, _ = nnls(np.vstack([A/sc, pen*mass/Mgas]), np.concatenate([target/sc, [pen]]), maxiter=5000)
    Sg = lambda r: sum(wi*(np.asarray(r, float)/h)**k*np.exp(-np.asarray(r, float)/h) for wi, (h, k) in zip(w, specs) if wi > 0)
    bul = None
    if np.any(g['Vbul'] != 0):
        Rb = np.concatenate([[0.0], R]); Mb = np.maximum.accumulate(np.concatenate([[0.0], R*ups_b*g['Vbul']**2/_V36_GK]))
        bul = (PchipInterpolator(Rb, Mb, extrapolate=False), Mb[-1], Rb[-1])
    return Sst, Mst, Sg, float(mass @ w), bul, float(np.sqrt(np.mean((A @ w - target)**2))/sc)

def _v36_sparc_pg(name, ell_factor=1.0, ups_d=0.5, ups_b=0.7, ngrid=None, zoom=(1.0, 1.0), kern="twin", src=None, Rx=None):
    """PG's curve under the gnomonic premise (R = ell tan chi; mass pushforward Sigma_leaf = Sigma_obs(ell tan chi)/cos^3 chi; Doppler speeds
    the leaf's speeds) with the arena law ell = 3 sqrt(G M_b/a0) (times ell_factor), against Vobs; with SPARC's Newtonian baryons and the
    empirical radial acceleration relation (McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert 2016) as references.  zoom = (lambda, zeta), the author's zoom labels
    in the analysis's dictionary: the image radius R = lambda R_phys, so the leaf's radius is the mapping scale over lambda, and the
    gravitating mass zeta/lambda^2 times the image's mass.  v36.1: src passes options to _v36_sparc_sources; Rx asks for the curve at extra radii
    (returned as 'Rx', 'v2x'), for the field near the equator."""
    lam, zeta = zoom
    g = _v36_sparc(name)
    Sst, Mst, Sg, Mg, bul, grms = _v36_sparc_sources(g, ups_d, ups_b, **(src or {}))
    Mbul = bul[1] if bul else 0.0
    Mb = Mst + Mg + Mbul
    ell = 3*np.sqrt(_V36_GK*Mb/_V36_A0)*ell_factor
    R = g['R']; t = np.arctan(R/ell)
    Rx = None if Rx is None else np.asarray(Rx, float); tx = None if Rx is None else np.arctan(Rx/ell)
    Re = R if ngrid is None else np.geomspace(R[0], R[-1], ngrid)             # a coarse grid, interpolated in log R, for scans
    te = np.arctan(Re/ell)
    brk = sorted(set(np.arctan(np.concatenate([R, [0.5*R[-1], 2*R[-1], 5*R[-1], 20*R[-1]]])/ell)))
    comps, compx = {}, {}
    for lab, S, M in (("stars", Sst, Mst), ("gas", Sg, Mg)):
        SL = lambda x, S=S: np.where(x < PI/2-1e-9, S(ell*np.tan(np.minimum(x, PI/2-1e-9)))/np.cos(np.minimum(x, PI/2-1e-9))**3, 0.0)
        v2e = _v36_disk_v2(SL, ell/lam, M*zeta/lam**2, te, PI/2, brk, kern=kern)
        comps[lab] = v2e if ngrid is None else np.interp(np.log(R), np.log(Re), v2e)
        if Rx is not None: compx[lab] = _v36_disk_v2(SL, ell/lam, M*zeta/lam**2, tx, PI/2, brk, kern=kern)
    if bul:
        Mi, Mt, Rmax = bul; dM = Mi.derivative()
        def rho(x):
            r = ell*np.tan(np.minimum(x, PI/2-1e-9))
            ok = (x < PI/2-1e-9) & (r > 0) & (r < Rmax)
            val = np.where(ok, np.nan_to_num(dM(np.where(ok, r, 0.5*Rmax))), 0.0)
            return val*ell/np.cos(np.minimum(x, PI/2-1e-9))**2/np.maximum(np.sin(x), 1e-300)**2
        xg, vb, _, _ = _v36_sphere(rho, ell/lam, Mt*zeta/lam**2)
        comps["bulge"] = np.interp(t, xg, vb**2)
        if Rx is not None: compx["bulge"] = np.interp(tx, xg, vb**2)
    v2 = sum(comps.values()); vpg = np.sqrt(np.maximum(v2, 0))
    v2x = None if Rx is None else sum(compx.values())
    vbar2 = g['Vgas']*np.abs(g['Vgas']) + ups_d*g['Vdisk']*np.abs(g['Vdisk']) + ups_b*g['Vbul']*np.abs(g['Vbul'])
    gbar = np.maximum(vbar2, 1e-9)/R
    vrar = np.sqrt(gbar/(1 - np.exp(-np.sqrt(gbar/_V36_A0)))*R)
    eV = np.maximum(g['eV'], 1e-3)
    edges = np.unique(np.concatenate([[ell], R[R > ell], ell*np.geomspace(1, 60, 200)]))
    out_mass = lambda S: 2*PI*_v36_gl_integrate(lambda r: r*S(r), edges)
    beyond = (out_mass(Sst) + out_mass(Sg) + (Mbul - float(np.nan_to_num(bul[0](min(ell, bul[2]))) if bul else 0.0)))/Mb
    return dict(beyond=beyond, Rx=Rx, v2x=v2x, name=name, ell=ell, Mb=Mb, Mst=Mst, Mgas=Mg, Mbul=Mbul, gas_rms=grms, veq=(_V36_GK*Mb*_V36_A0)**0.25, Vflat=g['Vflat'],
                Q=g['Q'], R=R, Vobs=g['Vobs'], eV=g['eV'], vpg=vpg, v2pg=v2, vbar=np.sqrt(np.maximum(vbar2, 0)), vrar=vrar, comps=comps,
                chi2_pg=float(np.sum(((vpg-g['Vobs'])/eV)**2)), chi2_rar=float(np.sum(((vrar-g['Vobs'])/eV)**2)), N=len(R))

# ==================================================================================================== v36.0 (15 October 2026): sections
def v36_0_data():
    print("\n== v36.0-1. The data: two Milky Way curves with their pipelines, and eight SPARC galaxies (R306, R307) ==")
    eil, ou = _v36_mw_data()
    fits = []
    for D in (eil, ou):
        w = 1/D['s']**2; A = np.vstack([np.ones_like(D['R']), D['R']-D['R0']]).T
        p = np.linalg.solve(A.T @ (A*w[:, None]), A.T @ (w*D['v'])); fits.append(p)
        print(f"   {D['name']}: {len(D['R'])} radii, {D['R'][0]:.2f}-{D['R'][-1]:.2f} kpc; R_sun = {D['R0']} kpc, v_sun,y = {D['vsun'][1]} km/s (Sgr A*'s proper"
              f" motion times R_sun); weighted line v_c(R_sun) = {p[0]:.2f} km/s, slope {p[1]:+.3f} km/s/kpc")
    print("   Eilers et al. publish v_c(R_sun) = 229.0 +- 0.2 km/s and a slope of -1.7 +- 0.1 km/s/kpc (systematics 2-5%, slope 0.46).")
    print("   SPARC (Lelli, McGaugh & Schombert 2016): eight galaxies, from the gas-rich dwarf DDO 154 to the giant UGC 2885 (baryonic masses in v36.0-4):")
    for nm, (D, Inc, L36, Rd, MHI, Vf, eVf, Q) in _V36_SPARC_T1.items():
        g = _v36_sparc(nm)
        print(f"     {nm:9s} D = {D:5.2f} Mpc, i = {Inc:4.1f} deg, L[3.6] = {L36:7.3f}e9, R_disk = {Rd:5.2f} kpc, M_HI = {MHI:6.3f}e9, V_flat = {Vf:5.1f}"
              f" +- {eVf:3.1f}, Q = {Q}; {len(g['R'])} radii to {g['R'][-1]:.1f} kpc")
    ok = abs(fits[0][0]-229.0) < 0.2 and abs(fits[0][1]+1.7) < 0.1 and len(eil['R']) == 38 and len(ou['R']) == 37
    check(ok, "the Milky Way data: Eilers et al.'s published line (229.0, -1.7) reproduced from the embedded table; 38 and 37 radii")
    print("   [V] The tables' transcription (two independent copies each, identical) and the published line.  [T] The pipelines as published.")
    return eil, ou

def v36_0_inside_view():
    print("\n== v36.0-2. The Milky Way seen from inside a PG leaf, with the leaf's own light (R308) ==")
    # (a) on the round leaf an observer's own transverse motion moves a source at s by v/(ell tan(s/ell)) = v/D_par, the source's by v/D_A
    eps, res = 1e-7, []
    dirn = lambda P, Q: (Q - (Q @ P)*P)/np.linalg.norm(Q - (Q @ P)*P)
    for chi in (0.3, 0.8, 1.2, 2.0):
        P, Q = np.array([1.0, 0, 0]), np.array([np.cos(chi), np.sin(chi), 0])
        P2 = np.array([np.cos(eps), 0, np.sin(eps)]); n2 = dirn(P2, Q)
        ang_obs = np.arctan2(n2 @ np.array([-np.sin(eps), 0, np.cos(eps)]), n2 @ np.array([0, 1.0, 0]))/eps
        Q2 = Q + eps*np.array([0, 0, 1.0]); Q2 /= np.linalg.norm(Q2); n3 = dirn(P, Q2)
        res.append((abs(ang_obs + 1/np.tan(chi))*np.tan(chi), abs(np.arctan2(n3[2], n3[1])/eps*np.sin(chi) - 1)))
    res = np.array(res)
    cal = [1/np.cos(s/16.0) - 1 for s in (1.0, 2.0)]
    print(f"   (a) Proper motions on the leaf: the observer's motion moves a source at distance s by v/(ell tan(s/ell)) = v/D_par, the source's own")
    print(f"     motion by v/(ell sin(s/ell)) = v/D_A (finite displacements on the embedded sphere, relative residuals {res.max():.0e}).  The two reductions")
    print("     used here convert proper motions with spectrophotometric distances, candle-like, so on the leaf with D_A (a premise: trained on parallaxes")
    print(f"     at 1-2 kpc, their scale would exceed D_A by {cal[0]:.1%}-{cal[1]:.1%} on a 16 kpc leaf).  The proper motions then carry the Sun's reflex only in the")
    print("     fraction D_A/D_par = cos(s/ell), while the reduction adds back the full solar velocity: the reflex is over-corrected by v_sun [1 - cos(s/ell)].")
    # (b) Sgr A*'s proper motion fixes the Sun's true speed
    eil, ou = _v36_mw_data()
    print("   (b) Sgr A*'s proper motion is the Sun's reflex at D_par (a premise: the quasar frame of the proper motions neither rotates against the")
    print("     leaf's parallel transport nor carries a solar reflex), and R_sun = D_A (S2's orbit, GRAVITY), so v_sun,y(pipeline) = 4.74 mu R_sun =")
    print("     v_sun,true cos(chi_sun):")
    rows = []
    for ell in (16.0, 20.0, 25.0, 30.0, 50.0, 100.0):
        cs = np.sqrt(1 - (eil['R0']/ell)**2); vt = eil['vsun'][1]/cs
        rows.append((ell, np.degrees(np.arcsin(eil['R0']/ell)), vt, 229.0 + vt - eil['vsun'][1], ell*np.arcsin(eil['R0']/ell)))
        print(f"     ell = {ell:5.0f} kpc: chi_sun = {rows[-1][1]:5.2f} deg (the Sun at arc length {rows[-1][4]:5.2f} kpc), true solar speed {vt:6.1f} km/s; for local stars to"
              f" read 229 km/s the leaf must turn at 229 + v_sun,y (sec chi_sun - 1) = {rows[-1][3]:6.1f} km/s at the Sun")
    # (c) the centre and anticentre directions in closed form, and the Euclidean control
    ell, R0, vy = 16.0, eil['R0'], eil['vsun'][1]
    cs = np.arcsin(R0/ell); vS = (eil['vsun'][0], vy/np.cos(cs)); worst = 0.0
    for sgn in (+1, -1):
        dd = np.linspace(0.02, (PI/2 - cs if sgn > 0 else cs) - 1e-3, 9)
        chi = cs + sgn*dd; phi = np.full_like(chi, PI); vc = np.full_like(chi, 229.0)
        n2, DA, vlos, vt_, w2 = _v36_observe(ell, cs, vS, chi, phi, vc)
        R, Phi, vphi = _v36_pipeline(R0, (eil['vsun'][0], vy), n2, DA, vlos, vt_, w2)
        worst = max(worst, np.max(np.abs(vphi - (229.0 + vS[1]*(np.cos(cs) - np.cos(dd))))), np.max(np.abs(R - (R0 + sgn*ell*np.sin(dd)))))
    chi = np.linspace(0.05, 2.0, 40)/1e6; phi = PI + np.linspace(-0.4, 0.4, 40)
    CH, PH = np.meshgrid(chi + np.arcsin(R0/1e6), phi, indexing='ij')
    n2, DA, vlos, vt_, w2 = _v36_observe(1e6, np.arcsin(R0/1e6), (eil['vsun'][0], vy/np.cos(np.arcsin(R0/1e6))), CH, PH, np.full_like(CH, 229.0))
    _, _, vphi = _v36_pipeline(R0, (eil['vsun'][0], vy), n2, DA, vlos, vt_, w2)
    ctrl = np.max(np.abs(vphi - 229.0))
    dd = np.array([0.0, cs, 0.75, 1.0]); vself = 229.0 + vy*(1/np.cos(cs) - 1)
    print("   (c) On the Sun's side of the centre (toward the centre and toward the anticentre, the side the wedge selects) the reduction gives exactly")
    print(f"     v_inf = v_true + v_sun,true [cos(chi_sun) - cos(s/ell)] at R_inf = R_sun +- ell sin(s/ell) (residual {worst:.0e}): under-corrected for stars nearer")
    print(f"     than the centre, exact at s = s_sun, that is at R_inf = 2 R_sun = {2*R0:.2f} kpc on every leaf, over-corrected beyond.  For ell = 16 kpc, at s = 0,")
    print("     s_sun, 12, 16 kpc, a flat true 229 km/s is read as " + ", ".join(f"{229.0 + vS[1]*(np.cos(cs)-np.cos(x)):.1f}" for x in dd) + " km/s, and a flat")
    print(f"     {vself:.1f} km/s, the leaf's speed for which local stars read 229, as " + ", ".join(f"{vself + vS[1]*(np.cos(cs)-np.cos(x)):.1f}" for x in dd)
          + " km/s: the curve read from inside rises once")
    print(f"     the stars are farther from the Sun than the centre is.  With ell = 1e6 kpc the reduction returns the true speeds (to {ctrl:.0e} km/s).")
    # (d) reach of near-hemisphere tracers
    reach = [(ell, R0 + np.sqrt(ell**2 - R0**2)) for ell in (16.0, 18.0, 20.0, 25.0)]
    lmin = [np.hypot(D['R0'], D['R'][-1] - D['R0']) for D in (eil, ou)]
    print("   (d) Reach: tracers on the near hemisphere (the barren-twin readout) appear at most at R_sun + sqrt(ell^2 - R_sun^2) toward the anticentre:")
    print("     " + ", ".join(f"{r:.2f} kpc for ell = {l:.0f}" for l, r in reach) + f"; the last radii, {eil['R'][-1]} and {ou['R'][-1]} kpc, need ell >= {lmin[0]:.2f}"
          f" and {lmin[1]:.2f} kpc.")
    ok = res.max() < 1e-5 and worst < 1e-9 and ctrl < 1e-3 and abs(lmin[0] - 18.57) < 0.01 and abs(vself + vS[1]*(np.cos(cs) - 1) - 229.0) < 1e-9
    check(ok, "the view from inside: proper motions at D_A (source) and D_par (observer); the line formula exact; the Euclidean limit returns the truth")
    print("   [T] The geometry.  [V] The reduction applied to the leaf's own light.  [D] The barren-twin reach.  [S] The distances and the proper-motion frame.")
    return dict(vsun_rows=rows, reach=reach, lmin=lmin)

def v36_0_milky_way():
    print("\n== v36.0-3. The Milky Way's baryons on the leaf, and the curve seen from inside, against Eilers et al. and Ou et al. (R309) ==")
    from scipy.special import i0, i1, k0, k1
    from scipy.optimize import least_squares
    # (a) the thin-disk solver: two limits, whose small residuals are physical (the leaf's curvature, the disk's size), and another method
    Rd, M = 3.0, 5e10
    R = np.array([1.0, 3.0, 6.6, 10.0]); dev = []
    for ell in (2000.0, 4000.0):
        v2 = _v36_disk_v2(lambda t, ell=ell: np.exp(-ell*t/Rd), ell, M, R/ell, 60*Rd/ell, [Rd/ell*k for k in (0.25, 1, 3, 8, 20)], rel_h=1e-3)
        y = R/(2*Rd); v2F = 4*PI*_V36_GK*(M/(2*PI*Rd**2))*Rd*y**2*(i0(y)*k0(y) - i1(y)*k1(y))
        dev.append(np.max(np.abs(np.sqrt(v2/v2F)-1)))
    x = np.array([0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 1.4]); devp = []
    for hd in (0.01, 0.02):
        v2p = _v36_disk_v2(lambda t, hd=hd: np.exp(-16.0*t/hd), 16.0, 6e10, x, 40*hd/16, [hd/16, 5*hd/16])
        devp.append(np.max(np.abs(v2p/(_V36_GK*6e10/16*(1/np.sin(x) + 2*np.sin(x))) - 1)))
    Sig = lambda t: np.exp(-16.0*t/2.5)
    ve = _v36_disk_v2(Sig, 16.0, 5e10, x, PI/2, [2.5/16*k for k in (0.5, 1, 3, 10)])
    espec = np.max(np.abs(_v36_disk_v2_spectral(Sig, 16.0, 5e10, x, lmax=2000, npan=400)/ve - 1))
    print("   (a) The thin-disk solver (twin Green function, elliptic ring integrals): on a 2000 kpc leaf an exponential disk gives Freeman's curve to")
    print(f"     {dev[0]:.1e} in v ({dev[1]:.1e} on a 4000 kpc leaf: the leaf's curvature, falling as ell^-2); a 0.01 kpc disk on the 16 kpc leaf gives the point")
    print(f"     source csc x + 2 sin x to {devp[0]:.1e} in v^2 ({devp[1]:.1e} for a 0.02 kpc disk: the disk's size, growing as its square).  By another method, a")
    print(f"     Funk-Hecke (Legendre) expansion on the great 2-sphere, an exponential disk of 2.5 kpc on the 16 kpc leaf agrees to {espec:.0e} in v^2.")
    # (b) McMillan's baryons on leaves of several radii (32.3 kpc: the maser R_0 bound; 48.5 kpc: the cap's bound from the LMC, R255)
    ells = [16.0, 20.0, 25.0, 28.0, 30.0, 32.3, 34.0, 37.0, 40.0, 48.5, 60.0, 100.0, 1e5]
    tag = {32.3: "  (the maser bound)", 48.5: "  (the cap's LMC bound)"}
    leaves = {}; eil, ou = _v36_mw_data()
    print("   (b) McMillan 2017's baryons (thin and thick stellar disks, HI and H2, bulge), their surface densities placed by arc length; the leaf's own curve:")
    for ell in ells:
        xs, comps, masses = _v36_mw_leaf(ell); leaves[ell] = (xs, comps, masses)
        vt = np.sqrt(np.maximum(sum(comps.values()), 0)); s = xs*ell
        ssun = ell*np.arcsin(eil['R0']/ell)
        print(f"     ell = {ell:7.1f} kpc: mass on the near hemisphere {sum(masses.values()):.3e} Msun; v = {np.interp(8.2, s, vt):6.1f}, {np.interp(15.0, s, vt):6.1f},"
              f" {np.interp(20.0, s, vt) if s[-1] > 20 else float('nan'):6.1f} km/s at 8.2, 15, 20 kpc of arc; the Sun at arc {ssun:5.2f} kpc, where the thin disk is"
              f" {np.exp(-(ssun - eil['R0'])/2.5):.2f} of McMillan's density at R_sun")
    # (c) the curve seen from inside, one free number f (every baryonic component scaled)
    fits = {}
    print("   (c) Seen from inside with the leaf's own light, fitted with one mass factor f (f = 1: McMillan's surface densities, placed by arc length):")
    for D in (eil, ou):
        print(f"     {D['name']} ({len(D['R'])} radii):  ell   f_best  chi2(f_best)  chi2(f = 1)  unreached")
        for ell in ells:
            xs, comps, masses = leaves[ell]
            vref = np.sqrt(np.maximum(sum(comps.values()), 0))
            L, S, reach, vst = _v36_inside(ell, D, np.append(xs, PI/2), np.append(vref, vref[-1]))
            f, c2, c21 = _v36_fit_f(L, S, D)
            fits[(D['name'], ell)] = (f, c2, c21, int((~reach).sum()), L, S)
            print(f"       {ell:9.1f} {f:7.3f} {c2:12.1f} {c21:12.1f}  {int((~reach).sum()):3d}{tag.get(ell, '')}")
    # (d) references: Newtonian gravity with McMillan's baryons and an NFW halo; PG's own curve read at arc length (perfect optics)
    xs, comps, masses = leaves[1e5]; sN = xs*1e5; vb2 = sum(comps.values())
    ref = {}
    def nfw(D, s):
        vb2d = np.interp(D['R'], sN, vb2)
        def resid(p):
            x = D['R']/10**p[1]
            vh2 = 4*PI*_V36_GK*10**p[0]*10**(3*p[1])*(np.log(1+x) - x/(1+x))/D['R']
            return (np.sqrt(vb2d + vh2) - D['v'])/s
        return min((least_squares(resid, [7.0, l0], bounds=([4.0, -1.0], [10.0, 2.5])) for l0 in (0.8, 1.2, 1.5)), key=lambda r: r.cost)
    for D in (eil, ou):
        best = nfw(D, D['s'])
        cf = []
        for ell in ells[:-1]:
            xs2, comps2, _ = leaves[ell]; s2 = xs2*ell; v = np.sqrt(np.maximum(sum(comps2.values()), 0)); m = D['R'] < s2[-1]
            vt = np.interp(D['R'][m], s2, v); a = np.sum(vt*D['v'][m]/D['s'][m]**2)/np.sum(vt**2/D['s'][m]**2)
            cf.append((ell, a*a, float(np.sum(((a*vt-D['v'][m])/D['s'][m])**2)), int(m.sum())))
        bcf = min(cf, key=lambda r: r[2] if r[3] == len(D['R']) else 1e99)
        bi = min((k for k in fits if k[0] == D['name']), key=lambda k: fits[k][1])
        # a 2% systematic floor in quadrature, refitted on every leaf, for PG and for the reference
        ss = np.sqrt(D['s']**2 + (0.02*D['v'])**2); Ds = dict(D, s=ss)
        sysf = {e: _v36_fit_f(fits[(D['name'], e)][4], fits[(D['name'], e)][5], Ds) for e in ells}
        es = min(ells, key=lambda e: sysf[e][1]); best_sys = nfw(D, ss)
        cap = fits[(D['name'], 48.5)]
        ref[D['name']] = (2*best.cost, 10**best.x[0], 10**best.x[1], bcf, bi, sysf[es][1], 2*best_sys.cost, cap, es, sysf[es][0])
        print(f"   (d) {D['name']}: best seen from inside, ell = {bi[1]:.0f} kpc with f = {fits[bi][0]:.2f}, chi2 = {fits[bi][1]:.0f}; Newtonian with McMillan's baryons"
              f" and an NFW halo (rho_s = {10**best.x[0]:.2e} Msun/kpc^3, r_s = {10**best.x[1]:.1f} kpc), chi2 = {2*best.cost:.0f} (ratio {fits[bi][1]/(2*best.cost):.1f});"
              f" with a 2% systematic floor, refitted on every leaf, best ell = {es:g} kpc with f = {sysf[es][0]:.2f}, chi2 = {sysf[es][1]:.0f} against {2*best_sys.cost:.1f}"
              f" (ratio {sysf[es][1]/(2*best_sys.cost):.1f}); at the cap's bound, ell = 48.5 kpc, f = {cap[0]:.2f} and chi2 = {cap[1]:.0f}"
              f" ({cap[1]/(2*best.cost):.0f} times); PG's own curve read at arc length (as if the optics returned it), best ell = {bcf[0]:.0f} kpc with f = {bcf[1]:.2f},"
              f" chi2 = {bcf[2]:.0f}")
    worst_f1 = min(fits[k][2] for k in fits)
    ok = (worst_f1 > 5e4 and all(fits[k][0] > 1.3 for k in fits)
          and min(fits[k][1] for k in fits if k[0] == eil['name']) > 4*ref[eil['name']][0]
          and min(fits[k][1] for k in fits if k[0] == ou['name']) > 4*ref[ou['name']][0] and devp[0] < 1e-4 and espec < 1e-4
          and dev[1] < dev[0] and devp[1] > devp[0] and all(ref[n][5] > 3*ref[n][6] for n in ref))
    check(ok, "the Milky Way from inside (a cold-tracer proxy, v36.1-5): at McMillan's surface densities chi^2 > 5e4 on every scanned leaf; the best needs f > 1.3 and stays > 4x the baryons + NFW chi^2")
    print("   [V] The fits, under the stated premises (cold tracers standing in for the published Jeans estimator -- a proxy, v36.1-5; the published pipelines")
    print("       and their distances, the proper-motion frame, direct rays only,")
    print("       McMillan's surface densities by arc length, the barren-twin readout).  [D] What fails: the reflex, over-corrected beyond 2 R_sun, on small")
    print("       leaves; the missing mass on large ones, where PG becomes Newton.")
    return dict(ells=ells, leaves=leaves, fits=fits, ref=ref, data=(eil, ou))

def _v36_fit_amp(o):
    """The amplitude on v in closed form (its square is the factor zeta/lambda on v^2) and chi^2/N."""
    e = np.maximum(o['eV'], 1e-3); vp = o['vpg']
    a = max(np.sum(vp*o['Vobs']/e**2)/max(np.sum(vp**2/e**2), 1e-300), 0.0)
    return a*a, float(np.sum(((a*vp - o['Vobs'])/e)**2))/o['N']

def _v36_label_opt(nm, two, cache, src=None):
    """The mapping scale ell_eff = f ell_arena minimizing chi^2/N with one label (f) or two (f, and the factor on v^2 in closed form): a bounded
    Brent search in log f on curves computed on 16 radii, bracketed by the grid 0.4-5, then a solve on every data radius at the optimum."""
    from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar
    def curve(lf):
        k = round(float(lf), 10)
        if k not in cache: cache[k] = _v36_sparc_pg(nm, ell_factor=float(np.exp(k)), ngrid=16, src=src)
        return cache[k]
    obj = (lambda lf: _v36_fit_amp(curve(lf))[1]) if two else (lambda lf: curve(lf)['chi2_pg']/curve(lf)['N'])
    grid = np.log([0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 1.0, 1.3, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0]); vals = [obj(g) for g in grid]; i = int(np.argmin(vals))
    r = minimize_scalar(obj, bounds=(grid[max(i-1, 0)], grid[min(i+1, len(grid)-1)]), method='bounded', options=dict(xatol=0.004))
    f = float(np.exp(r.x)); o = _v36_sparc_pg(nm, ell_factor=f, src=src)
    A, c2 = _v36_fit_amp(o) if two else (1.0, o['chi2_pg']/o['N'])
    return f, A, c2, o, i in (0, len(grid)-1)

def v36_0_sparc_pilot():
    print("\n== v36.0-4. External galaxies under the gnomonic premise with the arena law: a SPARC pilot of eight galaxies (R310) ==")
    out = {}
    print("   Premise: R_obs = ell tan(chi), each annulus's light counted once (Sigma_leaf = Sigma_obs/cos^3 chi), Doppler speeds the leaf's; arena law")
    print("   ell = 3 sqrt(G M_b/a0) (the point-source reference v_arena^4 = G M_b a0, written v_eq in v36.0; an extended source's asymptote is C G M_b/ell,")
    print("   v36.1-1); stellar mass-to-light 0.5 (disk) and 0.7 (bulge); no free parameter.  RAR: the empirical relation")
    print("   on SPARC's baryonic curves; RAR*: the same relation on the reconstructed razor-thin sources PG uses.")
    print("     galaxy     M_b [Msun]  ell [kpc]  R_last/ell  gas   beyond ell  v_arena/Vfl  v(R_last)/v_ar  chi2/N: PG     RAR   RAR*   control rms")
    for nm in _V36_SPARC_T1:
        o = _v36_sparc_pg(nm); c = _v36_sparc_pg(nm, ell_factor=1e3)
        o['control_rms'] = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((c['vpg'] - c['vbar'])**2))); o['control_max'] = float(np.max(np.abs(c['vpg'] - c['vbar'])))
        gb = np.maximum(c['v2pg'], 1e-9)/o['R']; vr = np.sqrt(gb/(1 - np.exp(-np.sqrt(gb/_V36_A0)))*o['R'])
        o['chi2_rar_same'] = float(np.sum(((vr - o['Vobs'])/np.maximum(o['eV'], 1e-3))**2))
        out[nm] = o
        print(f"     {nm:9s} {o['Mb']:10.3e} {o['ell']:9.2f} {o['R'][-1]/o['ell']:10.2f}  {o['Mgas']/o['Mb']:5.2f} {o['beyond']:8.2f}"
              f" {o['veq']/o['Vflat']:11.3f} {o['vpg'][-1]/o['veq']:13.3f} {o['chi2_pg']/o['N']:14.1f} {o['chi2_rar']/o['N']:7.1f} {o['chi2_rar_same']/o['N']:6.1f}"
              f" {o['control_rms']:9.2f}")
    print("   Control: on a leaf 1000 times larger PG is Newton, and the reconstructed sources give SPARC's own baryonic curve to the rms above;")
    print("   inside, a razor-thin disk against SPARC's thickened ones; outside, for NGC 2841 and UGC 2885, the reconstruction's own residual, whose cause the")
    print("   disk geometry must settle (v36.1-2; v36.0 read R V_gas^2/G there as a gas mass, a spherical diagnostic, withdrawn).")
    dd = out["DDO154"]; neg = dd['R'][dd['v2pg'] < 0]; ic = out["IC2574"]; negi = ic['R'][ic['v2pg'] < 0]
    print(f"   DDO 154: v^2 < 0 at R = {neg.min():.2f}-{neg.max():.2f} kpc (gas fraction {dd['Mgas']/dd['Mb']:.2f}); IC 2574: at {negi.min():.2f}-{negi.max():.2f} kpc (gas {ic['Mgas']/ic['Mb']:.2f}).")
    print(f"   The pushforward puts {dd['beyond']:.2f} of DDO 154's baryons beyond R = ell, at chi > 45 deg ({np.degrees(np.arctan(dd['R'][-1]/dd['ell'])):.0f} deg at the last radius):")
    print("   a band of gas just outside the inner orbits, whose outward pull on them -- a ring's, under a kernel whose pull weakens with distance --")
    print("   outweighs the inner mass.  The sign of G_twin beyond pi/4 is not the cause.  Controls with other kernels:")
    kc = {}
    rng = lambda a: (f"{a.min():.2f} kpc" if a.min() == a.max() else f"{a.min():.2f}-{a.max():.2f} kpc") if len(a) else "no radius"
    for kern, lab in (("chords", "the two chord terms alone (a strictly positive kernel)"), ("chord", "one chord, without the twin")):
        for nm in ("DDO154", "IC2574"):
            o = _v36_sparc_pg(nm, kern=kern); ng = o['R'][o['v2pg'] < 0]; kc[(kern, nm)] = (ng, o['chi2_pg']/o['N'])
        print(f"     {lab}: DDO 154 v^2 < 0 at " + rng(kc[(kern, 'DDO154')][0]) + f" (chi2/N {kc[(kern, 'DDO154')][1]:.0f}); IC 2574 at "
              + rng(kc[(kern, 'IC2574')][0]) + f" (chi2/N {kc[(kern, 'IC2574')][1]:.0f})")
    print("   Other leaf radii for DDO 154 (no arena law):")
    free = []
    for fct in (0.5, 2.0, 4.0):
        o = _v36_sparc_pg("DDO154", ell_factor=fct); free.append((fct, o['ell'], o['chi2_pg']/o['N'], o['vpg'][-1]))
        print(f"     ell = {o['ell']:5.2f} kpc ({fct} x the arena value): chi2/N = {o['chi2_pg']/o['N']:8.1f}; v at the last radius {o['vpg'][-1]:5.1f} km/s (observed {o['Vobs'][-1]:.1f})")
    # one free parameter: the leaf radius (the arena law dropped), optimized
    print("   The leaf radius as a free parameter (the arena law dropped; a bounded search bracketed by a grid of 0.4-5 times the arena value on curves")
    print("   computed on 16 radii, then a solve on every data radius at the optimum):")
    scan, caches = {}, {}
    for nm in ("NGC7814", "NGC2841", "UGC02885", "NGC6503", "NGC3198", "NGC2403", "IC2574", "DDO154"):
        caches[nm] = {}
        f, _, c2, o, edge = _v36_label_opt(nm, False, caches[nm])
        scan[nm] = (f, o['ell'], c2, out[nm]['chi2_rar']/out[nm]['N'], out[nm]['Mgas']/out[nm]['Mb'], edge)
        print(f"     {nm:9s} gas {scan[nm][4]:.2f}: best ell = {o['ell']:6.2f} kpc ({f:.2f} x arena; (v_arena/V_flat)^2 = {(out[nm]['veq']/out[nm]['Vflat'])**2:.2f}),"
              f" chi2/N = {c2:8.1f} (the empirical relation {scan[nm][3]:5.1f})")
    gas = np.array([scan[n][4] for n in scan]); q = np.array([scan[n][2] for n in scan])
    rk = lambda a: np.argsort(np.argsort(a)).astype(float)
    rs = np.corrcoef(rk(gas), rk(q))[0, 1]
    print(f"   With the leaf free the quality trends with the gas fraction (rank correlation {rs:.2f}).  For NGC 7814 and NGC 2841, the most gas-poor, the")
    print("   optimum sits at ell = (v_arena/V_flat)^2 ell_arena, where the plateau's level (their C is within 1.4% of 3, v36.1-1) reaches V_flat: there the arena law misses the plateau's level, not")
    print("   its approach (at the arena radius their curves are already within 2% of v_eq at the last radius).")
    print(f"   If surface brightness were kept instead, the image would not fix the leaf's radius; the arena law would fix the near hemisphere's mean")
    print(f"   surface density, M_b/(2 pi ell^2) = a0/(18 pi G) = {_V36_A0/(18*PI*_V36_GK)/1e6:.1f} Msun/pc^2.")
    # the point source's interpolation function against the empirical radial acceleration relation
    yv = np.geomspace(1e-3, 1e2, 2001)
    nu_pg = (1 + 1/(3*yv))/np.sqrt(1 + 1/(9*yv)); nu_rar = 1/(1 - np.exp(-np.sqrt(yv)))
    r = nu_pg/nu_rar; i = int(np.argmin(r)); yc = yv[np.argmax(r > 1)]
    print(f"   A point source in this premise gives g = g_N nu_PG(g_N/a0), nu_PG(y) = (1 + 1/(3y))/sqrt(1 + 1/(9y)) (-> 1 and -> y^-1/2): below the empirical")
    print(f"   relation 1/(1 - exp(-sqrt y)) for y < {yc:.1f}, most at y = {yv[i]:.2f} ({r[i]-1:+.3f}), and above it beyond, by at most {r[yv > yc].max()-1:.3f};")
    print("   at y = 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10: " + ", ".join(f"{(1+1/(3*q_))/np.sqrt(1+1/(9*q_))*(1-np.exp(-np.sqrt(q_)))-1:+.3f}" for q_ in (0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0)) + ".")
    rec_rms = {"DDO154": 0.57, "IC2574": 1.36, "NGC2403": 4.90, "NGC3198": 3.83, "NGC6503": 2.36, "NGC2841": 8.68, "UGC02885": 6.73, "NGC7814": 1.17}
    ok = (all(out[n]['chi2_pg'] > max(20.0, out[n]['chi2_rar']) for n in out) and all(abs(out[n]['control_rms'] - rec_rms[n]) < 0.05 for n in rec_rms)
          and all(f[2] > 1000 for f in free) and scan["NGC7814"][2] < 10 and scan["UGC02885"][2] < 10 and scan["NGC3198"][2] > 50
          and scan["NGC2403"][2] > 100 and scan["DDO154"][2] > 1000 and scan["IC2574"][2] > 100 and rs > 0.8 and not any(scan[n][5] for n in scan)
          and len(kc[("chords", "DDO154")][0]) > 0 and len(kc[("chords", "IC2574")][0]) > 0 and len(kc[("chord", "IC2574")][0]) > 0
          and abs(nu_pg[-1] - 1) < 0.01 and abs(nu_pg[0]*np.sqrt(yv[0]) - 1) < 0.01 and np.all(r[yv < yc] < 1) and r.min() < 0.8)
    check(ok, "the SPARC pilot: with the arena law PG misses all eight (chi2/N > 20, above the empirical relation's); the Newtonian control's rms reproduced to 0.05 km/s (v36.1: in place of 'rms < 10'); the dwarfs' v^2 < 0 under positive kernels too; with the leaf free the quality trends with the gas fraction")
    print("   [V] The curves, under the stated premise.  [D] Why: the pushforward compresses extended gas into a band near the equator, just outside the")
    print("       inner orbits, which it pulls outward; for the gas-poor, the plateau's level.  [O] Other premises: surface brightness kept, the stereographic reading.")
    return dict(pilot=out, free=free, scan=scan, caches=caches, kern=kc, nu=(yv, nu_pg, nu_rar))

def v36_0_zoom_labels(pilot):
    print("\n== v36.0-5. The author's zoom labels (the note of 15 October), against the pilot (R315) ==")
    # (a) the analysis's dictionary: R_vis = lambda R_phys, M_app = lambda^2 M_inst (a fixed photometric calibration), M_grav = zeta M_inst;
    #     PG's plateau v_eq^2 = C G M_grav/ell; v_eq^4 = G a0 M_app needs lambda^4 ell^2/zeta^2 = (C^2 G/a0) M_app
    lam = np.array([0.7, 1.0, 1.6]); zeta = np.array([0.8, 1.0, 1.3]); ell = np.array([10.0, 20.0, 40.0]); C = 3.0
    Mapp = lam**4*ell**2/zeta**2*_V36_A0/(C**2*_V36_GK)
    veq2 = C*_V36_GK*(zeta*Mapp/lam**2)/ell
    e1 = np.max(np.abs(veq2**2/(_V36_GK*_V36_A0*Mapp) - 1))
    e3 = np.max(np.abs((zeta/lam)/(lam*ell/(3*np.sqrt(_V36_GK*Mapp/_V36_A0))) - 1))   # the condition in fitted labels: zeta/lambda = ell_eff/ell_arena
    print("   (a) The analysis's dictionary: R_vis = lambda R_phys, M_app = lambda^2 M_inst under a fixed photometric calibration, M_grav = zeta M_inst;")
    print(f"     with the point source's v_eq^2 = 3 G M_grav/ell (an extended source's C replaces 3, and 9 becomes C^2: v36.1-3), the baryonic Tully-Fisher form")
    print(f"     v_eq^4 = G a0 M_app holds exactly when lambda^4 ell^2/zeta^2 = (9 G/a0) M_app")
    print(f"     (an identity, checked to {e1:.0e}); with ell ~ lambda and zeta fixed, lambda ~ M_app^(1/6); with ell fixed, lambda ~ M_app^(1/4).  A misassigned")
    print("     distance is one such label: R and flux-based masses scale as lambda and lambda^2, the dynamical v^2 R/G as lambda.")
    # (b) in the gnomonic premise the labels act as a free mapping scale ell_eff = lambda ell and an amplitude zeta/lambda on v^2
    g7 = _v36_sparc_pg("NGC7814", ell_factor=0.6, ngrid=8); gz = _v36_sparc_pg("NGC7814", ell_factor=0.6, ngrid=8, zoom=(1.4, 0.9))
    e2 = np.max(np.abs(gz['v2pg']/g7['v2pg'] - 0.9/1.4))
    print(f"   (b) In the gnomonic premise the labels act on PG's curve as a mapping scale ell_eff = lambda ell and a factor zeta/lambda on v^2 (an exact")
    print(f"     scaling of the closure, checked to {e2:.0e}).  A positive factor cannot lift a negative v^2, so at their arena radii DDO 154 and IC 2574")
    print("     fail under any factor; on larger leaves their gas moves off the equator and the factor acts.")
    # (c) two labels free per galaxy: ell_eff optimized, the factor in closed form; the empirical relation with the disk's mass-to-light free
    ups = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.geomspace(1e-3, 2.5, 1201)])
    def rar_free(nm, lo):
        g = _v36_sparc(nm); e = np.maximum(g['eV'], 1e-3); best = None
        for ud in np.unique(np.concatenate([[lo], ups[ups >= lo]])):
            vb2 = g['Vgas']*np.abs(g['Vgas']) + ud*g['Vdisk']*np.abs(g['Vdisk']) + 1.4*ud*g['Vbul']*np.abs(g['Vbul'])
            gb = np.maximum(vb2, 1e-9)/g['R']; vr = np.sqrt(gb/(1 - np.exp(-np.sqrt(gb/_V36_A0)))*g['R'])
            c2 = float(np.sum(((vr - g['Vobs'])/e)**2))/len(g['R'])
            if best is None or c2 < best[1]: best = (ud, c2)
        return best
    print("   (c) Two labels free per galaxy (ell_eff optimized as in v36.0-4, the factor in closed form, chi2/N on every data radius); the empirical")
    print("     relation with the disk's mass-to-light ratio free on [0.1, 2.5], and without the floor:")
    rows = {}
    for nm in pilot['scan']:
        f, A, c2, o, edge = _v36_label_opt(nm, True, pilot['caches'][nm])
        rf, ru = rar_free(nm, 0.1), rar_free(nm, 0.0)
        rows[nm] = (f, A, c2, rf[0], rf[1], ru[0], ru[1], edge)
        print(f"     {nm:9s} ell_eff = {f:.2f} x arena, zeta/lambda = {A:5.2f}: chi2/N = {c2:6.1f}  (one label: {pilot['scan'][nm][2]:7.1f}; the empirical relation"
              f" {pilot['scan'][nm][3]:5.1f}, {rf[1]:5.1f} with Y_disk = {rf[0]:.2f}{' (the floor)' if rf[0] <= 0.1 + 1e-9 else ''}, {ru[1]:5.1f} with Y_disk = {ru[0]:.3f} unbounded)")
    Mb = {nm: pilot['pilot'][nm]['Mb'] for nm in rows}
    order = sorted(rows, key=lambda n: Mb[n])
    good = [n for n in order if rows[n][2] <= 7.0]; poor = [n for n in order if rows[n][2] > 7.0]
    c2s = [rows[n][2] for n in rows]; rfs = [rows[n][4] for n in rows]
    words = {3: "three", 4: "four", 5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven", 8: "eight"}
    print(f"   With two labels free, chi2/N falls to {min(rows[n][2] for n in good):.1f}-{max(rows[n][2] for n in good):.1f} for {words.get(len(good), len(good))} of the eight (v36.0 grouped these at chi2/N <= 7 as fits; v36.1-2 gives each fit's tail")
    print(f"   probability, under which one is acceptable and one borderline) and stays {min(rows[n][2] for n in poor):.1f}-{max(rows[n][2] for n in poor):.1f} for " + ", ".join(poor) + ";")
    print(f"   the empirical relation reaches {min(pilot['scan'][n][3] for n in rows):.1f}-{max(pilot['scan'][n][3] for n in rows):.1f} at fixed mass-to-light ratios and"
          f" {min(rfs):.1f}-{max(rfs):.1f} with one ratio free on [0.1, 2.5], the two dwarfs")
    print("   at its floor.  The labels the fits need trend with mass: by increasing M_b, ell_eff/ell_arena = " + ", ".join(f"{rows[n][0]:.2f}" for n in order))
    print("   and zeta/lambda = " + ", ".join(f"{rows[n][1]:.2f}" for n in order) + ";")
    vmass = np.array([Mb[n] for n in order]); amp = np.array([rows[n][1] for n in order])
    rc = np.corrcoef(np.log(vmass), np.log(amp))[0, 1]
    print(f"   the amplitude's log-correlation with M_b is {rc:.2f}.  The dwarfs want larger leaves and amplitudes of {rows['IC2574'][1]:.2f} and {rows['DDO154'][1]:.2f}, a")
    print("   factor that carries their mass discrepancy as a dark-matter fraction would.  Two free numbers per galaxy predict nothing until a law fixes them.")
    # (d) the dictionary's condition written in the fitted labels: with ell_eff = lambda ell and ell_arena^2 = 9 G M_app/a0 it reads
    #     zeta/lambda = ell_eff/ell_arena -- one combination (the plateau, through the Tully-Fisher form); the turnover scale ell_eff is left

    print(f"     with the source's coefficient it reads zeta/lambda = 3f/C(f), v36.1-3): it fixes one")

    print("     against each galaxy's own (V_flat/v_arena)^2 = " + ", ".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x in off) + ", with v_arena = (G a0 M_b)^(1/4).")
    print("     For the two most gas-poor disks the misfit is the galaxy's own offset from v^4 = G a0 M_b at these mass-to-light ratios; the others need more.")

    ok = (e1 < 1e-12 and e2 < 1e-12 and e3 < 1e-12 and all(abs(rows[n][2]/rec36[n] - 1) < 0.03 for n in rec36)
          and abs(rows["DDO154"][1] - 4.30) < 0.05 and abs(rows["IC2574"][1] - 2.61) < 0.05 and abs(rc + 0.76) < 0.03 and not any(rows[n][7] for n in rows)
          and rows["DDO154"][3] <= 0.1 + 1e-9 and rows["IC2574"][3] <= 0.1 + 1e-9)
    check(ok, "zoom labels -- controls: the dictionary's Tully-Fisher condition, in fitted labels zeta/lambda = ell_eff/ell_arena (point-source form); labels as a mapping scale and a v^2 factor; recorded outcomes reproduced (v36.1: tolerances on v36.0's values, the five/three grouping no longer a condition): chi2/N = 5.71, 6.41, 20.81, 51.58, 13.84, 1.92, 1.31, 1.08 on the 16-radius optima, the dwarfs' amplitudes 4.30 and 2.61, the log-correlation -0.76, the dwarfs at the RAR floor")
    print("   [T] The dictionary's algebra and the scaling.  [V] The fits.  [D] What labels can and cannot do in this premise.")
    return rows

def v36_0_note_algebra():
    print("\n== v36.0-6. The note's flavor and mass-category analyses: their algebra checked, the program held (R314) ==")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(36)
    A = rng.normal(size=(3, 3)) + 1j*rng.normal(size=(3, 3)); H = A @ A.conj().T
    I1 = np.trace(H).real; I2 = 0.5*(np.trace(H)**2 - np.trace(H @ H)).real; I3 = np.linalg.det(H).real
    t = 0.37
    e1 = abs(np.linalg.det(t*np.eye(3) - H).real - (t**3 - I1*t**2 + I2*t - I3))/abs(I3)
    Q = np.linalg.qr(rng.normal(size=(3, 3)) + 1j*rng.normal(size=(3, 3)))[0]; Hc = Q @ H @ Q.conj().T
    e2 = np.max(np.abs(np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(Hc)) - np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(H))))/np.max(np.linalg.eigvalsh(H))
    print(f"   (a) For a 3x3 Hermitian H, (tr H, [(tr H)^2 - tr H^2]/2, det H) fix det(tI - H) = t^3 - I1 t^2 + I2 t - I3 (to {e1:.0e}); conjugation keeps the")
    print(f"     spectrum (to {e2:.0e}), so a change of flavor basis, like the frozen conveyor (Part XXX), relates descriptions and converts no mass.")
    th = (np.arange(4096) + 0.5)*(2*PI/4096); kk = np.array([-1, 0, 1])
    worst = 0.0
    for a in (0.0, 0.35, 0.7):
        w = (1 + a*np.cos(th))/(2*PI)
        K = np.array([[np.sum(w*np.exp(1j*(kj - ki)*th))*(2*PI/4096) for kj in kk] for ki in kk]).real
        ev = np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(K)); tot = np.sum(w)*(2*PI/4096)
        worst = max(worst, np.max(np.abs(ev - np.array([1 - a/np.sqrt(2), 1.0, 1 + a/np.sqrt(2)]))), abs(tot - 1),
                    abs(np.trace(K @ K) - (3 + a*a)), abs(np.linalg.det(K) - (1 - a*a/2)))
    print(f"   (b) The third analysis's meridian toy: w_a = (1 + a cos theta)/2pi keeps its total 1 while the three-mode response K_ij = int w phi_i* phi_j")
    print(f"     (phi = e^-i theta, 1, e^i theta) has eigenvalues 1 - a/sqrt2, 1, 1 + a/sqrt2, tr K^2 = 3 + a^2, det K = 1 - a^2/2 (to {worst:.0e}): one total,")
    print("     three moving modes.  An illustration, not a lepton fit; its caveat stands -- changed masses change energy, which gravitates.")
    print("   (c) Held for its own piece: a three-mode operator and a history-dependent connection from PG's complex/Hopf structure, with its")
    print("     spectral invariants and holonomy, and the action-level audit of where m/hbar must be restored (Entry 319).")
    ok = e1 < 1e-10 and e2 < 1e-10 and worst < 1e-12
    check(ok, "the note's algebra: three invariants fix a 3x3 spectrum; conjugation keeps it; the meridian toy's fixed total and moving spectrum")
    print("   [T] Standard algebra.  [V] The toy.  [O] The flavor substrate and the categories of mass, as a program.")

def v36_0_selfconsistent_source():
    print("\n== v36.0-7. The review's self-consistent source: leaf densities whose gnomonic image is exactly exponential, solved again (R311) ==")
    from scipy.integrate import quad
    from scipy.special import i0, i1, k0, k1
    ell, h = 16.0, 3.0
    xs = np.array([0.3, 0.8, 1.2, 1.5])
    dsk = [2*PI*ell**2*quad(lambda x: np.exp(-ell*np.tan(x)/h)/np.cos(x)**3*np.sin(x), 0, X, limit=200)[0] for X in xs]
    dsk_o = [2*PI*h**2*(1 - (1 + ell*np.tan(X)/h)*np.exp(-ell*np.tan(X)/h)) for X in xs]
    sph = [4*PI*ell**3*quad(lambda x: np.exp(-ell*np.tan(x)/h)/np.cos(x)**4*np.sin(x)**2, 0, X, limit=200)[0] for X in xs]
    sph_o = [4*PI*h**3*(2 - np.exp(-ell*np.tan(X)/h)*((ell*np.tan(X)/h)**2 + 2*ell*np.tan(X)/h + 2)) for X in xs]
    e1 = max(np.max(np.abs(np.array(dsk)/np.array(dsk_o) - 1)), np.max(np.abs(np.array(sph)/np.array(sph_o) - 1)))
    print(f"   (a) Sigma_B = Sigma_0 sec^3 chi exp(-ell tan chi/h) (thin disk) and rho_B = rho_0 sec^4 chi exp(-ell tan chi/h) (sphere) push forward to exact")
    print(f"     exponentials in R = ell tan chi (enclosed masses to {e1:.0e}); the image's light is exponential if light follows mass annulus by annulus.")
    Rs = np.array([1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 16, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200.0]); M = 6e10
    Rf = np.geomspace(12.0, 200.0, 61)
    curves, fine = {}, {}
    for ell in (16.0, 25.0):
        S = lambda t, ell=ell: np.where(t < PI/2-1e-9, np.exp(-ell*np.tan(np.minimum(t, PI/2-1e-9))/h)/np.cos(np.minimum(t, PI/2-1e-9))**3, 0.0)
        brk = sorted(np.arctan(np.array([h, 3*h, 10*h, 30*h])/ell))
        v = np.sqrt(np.maximum(_v36_disk_v2(S, ell, M, np.arctan(Rs/ell), PI/2, brk), 0)); curves[ell] = v
        fine[ell] = np.sqrt(np.maximum(_v36_disk_v2(S, ell, M, np.arctan(Rf/ell), PI/2, brk), 0))
    y = Rs/(2*h); vN = np.sqrt(4*PI*_V36_GK*(M/(2*PI*h**2))*h*y**2*(i0(y)*k0(y) - i1(y)*k1(y)))
    light = (1 + Rs/h)*np.exp(-Rs/h)
    print(f"   (b) A thin disk of 6e10 Msun, h = 3 kpc, solved on the leaf and read at R (kpc): R, v (ell = 16), v (ell = 25, the arena value), v (Newton,")
    print("     Euclidean), light beyond R:")
    for i in range(len(Rs)):
        print(f"       {Rs[i]:6.0f} {curves[16.0][i]:7.1f} {curves[25.0][i]:7.1f} {vN[i]:7.1f}   {light[i]:.1e}")
    rho = lambda t: np.where(t < PI/2-1e-9, np.exp(-25.0*np.tan(np.minimum(t, PI/2-1e-9))/h)/np.cos(np.minimum(t, PI/2-1e-9))**4, 0.0)
    xg, vs, _, veq = _v36_sphere(rho, 25.0, M)
    print("   (c) The sphere (ell = 25): " + ", ".join(f"{R:.0f}: {np.interp(np.arctan(R/25.0), xg, vs):.1f}" for R in (2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100)) + f" km/s; v_eq = {veq:.1f}.")
    ip = int(np.argmax(fine[16.0])); Rp = np.linspace(Rf[max(ip-1, 0)], Rf[min(ip+1, len(Rf)-1)], 41)
    S16 = lambda t: np.where(t < PI/2-1e-9, np.exp(-16.0*np.tan(np.minimum(t, PI/2-1e-9))/h)/np.cos(np.minimum(t, PI/2-1e-9))**3, 0.0)
    vp = np.sqrt(np.maximum(_v36_disk_v2(S16, 16.0, M, np.arctan(Rp/16.0), PI/2, sorted(np.arctan(np.array([h, 3*h, 10*h, 30*h])/16.0))), 0)); jp = int(np.argmax(vp))
    flat16 = max(np.max(np.abs(fine[16.0]/curves[16.0][-1] - 1)), vp[jp]/curves[16.0][-1] - 1); inner = np.max(np.abs(curves[16.0][Rs <= 2]/vN[Rs <= 2] - 1))
    drop25 = 1 - curves[25.0][Rs == 50][0]/curves[25.0][Rs == 8][0]
    print(f"   (d) The review's four requirements: exponential in the image (exact for the mass); a realistic central curve (within {inner:.1%} of Newton inside")
    print(f"     2 kpc); a plateau: for ell = 16, within {flat16:.1%} of its value at 200 kpc from 12 kpc out (on a fine grid; its peak {vp[jp]:.1f} km/s at {Rp[jp]:.1f} kpc),")
    print(f"     while on the arena leaf, ell = 25, the curve first falls by {drop25:.0%} from 8 to 50 kpc; tracers: stellar light traces only the plateau's inner")
    print(f"     part ({light[Rs == 12][0]:.3f} of it beyond 12 kpc, {light[Rs == 20][0]:.3f} beyond 20, {light[Rs == 30][0]:.0e} beyond 30 and {light[Rs == 50][0]:.0e} beyond 50); the gas")
    print("     that traces outer plateaus in real galaxies is the source that fails in v36.0-4.")
    ok = e1 < 1e-8 and flat16 < 0.05 and inner < 0.03 and light[Rs == 30][0] < 1e-3 and drop25 > 0.05
    check(ok, "the self-consistent source: exact exponential pushforwards; a central curve near Newton and, on a 16 kpc leaf, a plateau to infinity; its far part almost without light")
    print("   [T] The pushforwards.  [V] The curves.  [D] Three of the four requirements met by a stellar disk on a 16 kpc leaf; the fourth, tracers, is a reach")
    print("       to be quantified (v36.1-6), not a categorical failure.")
    return dict(Rs=Rs, curves=curves, vN=vN, light=light)

def v36_0_orbits():
    print("\n== v36.0-8. Orbits through the equator in PG's twin-symmetric field: the held note's first calculation (R312) ==")
    from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
    from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
    ell, M = 16.0, 6e10
    xs, v, psi, veq = _v36_sphere(_v36_partXXV(0.1), ell, M)
    m = xs < PI/2 - 1e-12
    X = np.concatenate([xs[m], [PI/2], PI - xs[m][::-1]]); P = np.concatenate([psi[m], [psi[-1]], psi[m][::-1]])
    Phi = CubicSpline(X, -2*(_V36_GK*M/ell)*P)
    d2 = float(Phi(PI/2, 2))
    U = lambda x, L: Phi(x) + L**2/(2*ell**2*np.sin(x)**2)
    print(f"   (a) The benchmark field (r_d/ell = 0.1, ell = 16 kpc, 6e10 Msun): v_eq = {veq:.2f} km/s.  Since Phi' = v_c^2 cot x, l'Hopital gives")
    print(f"     Phi''(pi/2) = -v_eq^2 (the spline: {d2:.1f} against {-veq**2:.1f}); U_eff(x) = Phi(x) + L^2/(2 ell^2 sin^2 x) is symmetric about the equator, with")
    print("     U_eff''(pi/2) = L^2/ell^2 - v_eq^2: a barrier at the equator for L < ell v_eq, a single well for L > ell v_eq.")
    rows = []
    print("   (b) From a circular orbit at chi_c, the radial speed that crosses the barrier:")
    for deg in (40, 50, 60, 70, 75, 80, 85):
        xc = np.radians(deg); vc2 = np.tan(xc)*Phi(xc, 1); L = ell*np.sin(xc)*np.sqrt(vc2); dE = U(PI/2, L) - U(xc, L)
        rows.append((deg, ell*np.tan(xc), np.sqrt(vc2), np.sqrt(max(2*dE, 0))))
        print(f"     chi_c = {deg:2d} deg (R = {ell*np.tan(xc):6.1f} kpc): v_c = {np.sqrt(vc2):6.1f}, kick {np.sqrt(max(2*dE, 0)):6.1f} km/s = {np.sqrt(max(2*dE, 0)/vc2):.3f} v_c")
    def orbit(x0, L, vr0, T=6.0):
        f = lambda t, Y: [Y[1], np.sin(Y[0])*np.cos(Y[0])*(L/(ell**2*np.sin(Y[0])**2))**2 - Phi(Y[0], 1)/ell**2, L/(ell**2*np.sin(Y[0])**2)]
        s = solve_ivp(f, (0, T), [x0, vr0/ell, 0.0], method='DOP853', rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14, t_eval=np.linspace(0, T, 30001))
        E = 0.5*ell**2*s.y[1]**2 + U(s.y[0], L)
        return s.t, s.y, float(np.ptp(E)/abs(E[0]))
    cases = [("L = 1.1 ell v_eq from 50 deg at rest", np.radians(50), 1.1*ell*veq, 0.0),
             ("L = 0.8 ell v_eq from 60 deg, 60 km/s outward", np.radians(60), 0.8*ell*veq, 60.0),
             ("L = 0.5 ell v_eq from 30 deg at rest", np.radians(30), 0.5*ell*veq, 0.0)]
    orbs = []
    print("   (c) Three orbits (time in kpc/(km/s) = 0.978 Gyr; by the symmetry a crossing orbit spends half of each radial period beyond the equator --")
    print("     v36.1-7 integrates one period; a finite window gives the fractions below):")
    for lab, x0, L, vr in cases:
        t, Y, dE = orbit(x0, L, vr); a, b = Y[0].min(), Y[0].max(); cross = b > PI/2
        far = np.mean(Y[0] > PI/2); vphi = L/(ell*np.sin(x0))/np.sqrt(np.tan(x0)*Phi(x0, 1))
        orbs.append((lab, t, Y, a, b, cross, dE, L))
        print(f"     {lab} (v_phi = {vphi:.2f} v_c there): chi from {np.degrees(a):8.4f} to {np.degrees(b):8.4f} deg; crosses: {cross}; pi - chi_max = {np.degrees(PI-b):8.4f} deg;"
              f" time beyond the equator over the window {far:.2f}; energy to {dE:.0e}")
    t, Y = orbs[0][1], orbs[0][2]; Rg = ell*np.tan(Y[0])
    big = np.mean(np.abs(Rg) > 5*ell)
    print(f"   (d) In gnomonic radius the first orbit runs out to +infinity and returns from -infinity; R(P) = R(-P), so its far-side arc is drawn through")
    print(f"     the near galaxy's own image, down to ell tan(chi_min) = {ell*np.tan(orbs[0][3]):.1f} kpc; it spends {big:.2f} of its time beyond 5 ell = 80 kpc.")
    print("     Whether the star fades there is a statement about photons, not coordinates: the transfer law is open (the review's section 6).")
    cr = [o for o in orbs if o[5]]
    ok = (abs(d2/(-veq**2) - 1) < 1e-3 and len(cr) == 2 and all(abs(o[4] - (PI - o[3])) < 1e-6 for o in cr) and not orbs[2][5]
          and all(o[6] < 1e-8 for o in orbs))
    check(ok, "orbits through the equator: Phi''(pi/2) = -v_eq^2; crossing orbits have chi_max = pi - chi_min (to 1e-6); a low-L orbit is trapped")
    print("   [T] The symmetry.  [V] The orbits.  [D] In this benchmark field every orbit with L > ell v_eq crosses (its circular angular momentum rises to the")
    print("       equator, v36.1-7), though such orbits are far from circular disk orbits; from a")
    print("       circular orbit, radial kicks of 0.1-0.2 v_c cross from beyond about 60-70 deg.")
    return dict(rows=rows, orbs=orbs, Phi=Phi, veq=veq, ell=ell)
