> **v34.0 — what this version is, and the second clarification (Law II).** Version 34.0 merges the referee's v33.6 "middle-space source reset" of v33.5 (the governing paragraph above, the corrected Law I in Part III, the rescoped twin, charge, closure and galactic passages, and §XXIX.8) with the Part XXIX work of v33.6–v33.7 (§§XXIX.6–7, corrections R41–R44); the referee's register entries are renumbered R45–R49 here. It adds the author's second clarification of 11 October: **Law II is a universal, matter-responsive meridian law, sought and not yet constructed.** The whole middle-space matter distribution is to select the meridian line distribution $U_{\rm mer}$ and its singular structure; a *primary* is a concentration that dominates that selection over a region and a range of scales — a property of the solution, never a privileged entry in the law — and when one does, the meridians near it should approach the primary-centred radial great-circle pencil of §VIII.1, so that the pencil is a dominant-mass *solution branch*, not an axiom; secondaries participate in the same law and keep their full local gravitational response, including the weak-field Keplerian limit. Law I's fiber reduction then runs along the meridians Law II selects, so $q$ is endogenous and the two laws are a coupled system with backreaction (§XXIX.8, coupling paragraph). For $n$ separated primary-sized concentrations in a middle space vastly larger than one local representational three-sphere, the same law should produce a locally primary-centred germ with its own $S^3$-type readout around each, with transitions between basins; this is a stringent *validation* test, while the origin of a universal $G$ is to be attempted in the $n = 1$ dominant-primary branch only (§XXIX.9). Two geometric facts guard the intention: at the equatorial leaf the great-circle tangent is *normal* to the leaf, so "radial on the leaf" is a separate derived readout, not the meridian tangent; and one round $S^4$ with one equatorial $S^3$ does not by itself realize the scale separation $L_{\rm middle}\gg a_i$ of the multi-primary picture. The author's third clarification — that gravity is quotient-first, the Einstein equations living on $B_{\rm grav}^4$ with the base metric pulled back as a vertically degenerate, meridian-constant horizontal tensor, and Law I never a line integral of mass inserted into a five-dimensional metric — is stated as the governing hierarchy in §XXIX.8. §XXIX.9 executes the three toys the handoff asked for — the fiber-kernel control, a variational full-fiber source with its exact conservation identity, and the geometric disintegration of the great-circle pencil, under which a pole-concentrated primary reduces to a *uniform* base source and an equatorial body to the two-crossing rule — and sets out the $n$-primary regression, the falsifiers and the register R50–R55.

> **v34.1 — the double referee round (12 October 2026) and what now governs.** Two reports were received on v34.0: the standing referee's execution brief with the author's archival Entries 156–158 of 30 September, and an independent blind report (18 findings, reproduced calculations, an analytic counterexample and replacement core text). Every definite finding is implemented in this version; the new work is in §§XXIX.10–16, the local corrections carry *v34.1* tags, and the register runs R56–R79 (§XXIX.16). The controlling statements, which supersede any passage below that says otherwise, are these. **(1) Geometry.** The family of great circles through $\pm p$ is *parameterized* by $\mathbb{RP}^3$; those circles share the poles and are therefore **not** the disjoint fibers of a quotient of the original $S^4$. On the regular stratum $S^4\setminus\{\pm p\}\simeq(0,\pi)\times S^3$ the connected meridian leaves are indexed by $S^3$; the regular map to $\mathbb{RP}^3$ has *two open arcs* per fiber and adds the pairing $n\sim-n$, which the line field does not supply; a space with genuine disjoint complete fibers exists only after a resolution — the control $\widetilde X=(S^3\times S^1)/((n,\theta)\sim(-n,-\theta))$ of §XXIX.10 is one, non-orientable, with directional core sections, and is not asserted to be physical. The pulled-back base metric $q^*g_G$ is regular on the regular stratum only; at an original pole it diverges as $r^{-2}$. **(2) The pole primary.** The coarea reduction of a *smooth* density axisymmetric about the poles is uniform on the base (Toy C, retained); a *point mass at the pole* has **no canonical reduction** — shrinking annuli with different even angular profiles converge to the same $M\delta_p$ in the middle space and to different base measures (§XXIX.10, computed). The uniform closure image is therefore an **isotropic-core prescription**, extra data to be derived from the core's dynamics, not a consequence of zero volume weight; R55 is rewritten accordingly. **(3) The finite core (Entries 156–158).** The author's primary never required the meridians to meet at a point: a finite, matter-conditioned interlocking interior with a smooth transition to an exterior in which the meridians approximate the radial, antipodal pencil — the round point-pencil is the **zero-core limit**, and the gravitational seed needs only three *exterior* conditions: near-normal crossings of the selected $S^3$, radial organization of the congruence, approximately antipodal return (§XXII.12; §XXIX.14). The core-to-base directional measure of that interior is exactly the datum (2) leaves open. **(4) Source and conservation.** $T^{(g)}$ is the response of the *complete* source action (matter, meridian variable, constraints, core) to the base metric with the independent variables fixed; conservation follows from covariance and the complete equations of motion; Toy B's obstruction term is the Lie-derivative of the action in the fiber-length field, and an auxiliary (non-propagating) fiber-length sector restores conservation of the total — no radion is logically forced (§XXIX.11). **(5) The static benchmark.** The first-order lapse relation is exact, $\nu=-2\psi+2\psi(0)$; the plateau has the closed form $v_{\rm eq}^2=12\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\rho_{\rm eff}\sin^2x\cos x\,dx-4\pi\rho_{\rm eff}(\pi/2)$; the printed table's compact entry becomes $2.9929$ (the old $0.1$–$1\%$ "full-system correction" was shooting error); the rigid closure is *sufficient*, not unique — a finite slope $s=dp/d\rho>1/5$ gives a nonoscillatory compact Green function with $v_{\rm eq}^2/\mu=-(3+1/s)/\cos(\tfrac\pi2\sqrt{4+1/s})$ ($4.2917$ at $s=1$), and $p/\rho$ is not $dp/d\rho$ (§XXIX.13). **(6) The two-source test, first executed step.** In the kinematic control the first-order meridian response to an extended secondary redistributes the pole primary's base image by $-\kappa(\rho_S-\langle\rho_S\rangle)$ with $\kappa\simeq0.72$–$0.86$ — the same order as the secondary's own source — but that redistribution is a *relabeling* of a uniform measure *[the rest of this item is **withdrawn in v34.2 (R80)**: the transport is a mass-form statement, not a proper-density one, a changed quotient is not a strict relabeling, and the survival of the Keplerian field is open — see the v34.2 paragraph and §XXIX.12; the residual's falloff is author-reported numerical behaviour over three widths]*; had the base metric been pinned to the leaf's labels the plateau would change by $-71\%$ with a size-dependent coupling (§XXIX.12). What is not settled is the primary's stress response (fixed measure versus rigid proper density), which is the Theorem I/III target and now carries the budget test of §XXIX.17. **(7) Labels.** The status tags [T/V/D/S/O/R] are kept for the archive and supplemented, in Part XXIX from §XXIX.10 on and in the register, by the evidence system both referees asked for: *standard result*, *proved here (under stated assumptions)*, *conditional calculation reproduced*, *numerical claim not independently reproduced*, *model premise*, *open construction*, *withdrawn* (§XXIX.16). **(8) Masses.** $M_{\rm bg}=\pi c^2\ell/4G=2.626\times10^{17}M_\odot$ at $\ell=16$ kpc is the base closure mass; $M_c=2M_{\rm bg}=5.252\times10^{17}M_\odot$ is its mathematical cover lift; a candidate pole primary under Toy C's same-total convention carries the **base** mass. Branch symmetry (§XXII.11) is retained as a parent-level requirement, with the exchange test stated for the full-middle-space ontology (§XXIX.14); the optical-frame coefficient $N^2$ is a frame coefficient, not a matter-dependent coupling; the Brans–Dicke negative result is scoped to the tested ansätze; the Higgs data verdict awaits a model-consistent joint fit; the Johnston citation is corrected (§XXIX.15).

> **v34.2 — the second double round (12 October 2026): what is withdrawn, what is proved, what is new.** Two further reports arrived on v34.1 — the standing referee's assessment with a note on the Boltzmannian core, and the blind referee's follow-up — together with the author's Entries 267–268 and a referee analysis of them. **Withdrawn (R80).** §XXIX.12's Result 3 claimed that the first-order meridian backreaction is a relabeling with no invariant content and marked the survival of the secondary's near field and plateau as proved. That was too strong: a transported mass *form* is not a transported *proper density* unless the metric volume element is transported with it ($\delta m_P = (\delta\rho_P+\tfrac{\bar\rho}2{\rm tr}\,\delta h)\,dV_0$, so a pure pullback has $\delta\rho_P = 0$ only together with $\delta h = \mathcal L_\xi h_0$); a changed quotient is not a strict relabeling $q_\epsilon = \Phi_\epsilon\circ q_0$ of the old one; and H1–H3 supply neither the total stress nor the readout. The kinematic transport stands; its physical content — "harmless relabeling" or "physical cancellation" — is **open**, decided by the primary's constitutive response, which is the Theorem III target. The smooth-core angular displacement is also not finite at the old pole ($\eta\sim-4V_S'\sin\varphi/((\rho_c-\langle\rho\rangle)\theta)$, the coordinate breakdown about a *moved* critical point; the antipodal maximum moves too, by $(8/3)\epsilon$ in the point limit), so the point-core and finite-core limits do not commute and a moving-core chart is required; the finite-core residual is author-reported numerical behaviour over three widths, not an asymptotic law. **Proved (R81, §XXIX.17).** On the closed static base in the conformal gauge the Hamiltonian constraint fixes the total base rest mass at its background value at first order — $\int R\,dV$ and $2\Lambda V$ both shift by $12\int\psi$ — so *any* static closure surrenders exactly $M_S$ of rest mass when a secondary of mass $M_S$ is present ($\int(\delta\rho_{\rm cl}+6\bar\rho\psi) = -M_S$ for every constitutive law; the rigid branch does it through volume, a barotropic branch of slope $s$ through density $-M_S/(3s+1)$ and volume $-3sM_S/(3s+1)$); a **conserved-number** medium — fluid or solid, any bulk or shear modulus — cannot do it and admits **no static solution** (the even-sector matching matrix is singular and the sourced solution misses the common condition by exactly $M_S$, computed) *[narrowed in v34.3, R95: this holds for a closure sector whose separate charge is held fixed while an independent secondary is added; number conservation as a material law is not excluded, and the identity constrains integrated source energy, not rest mass]*; the fixed-measure pressureless image fails the Laplacian's zero mode ($\Delta\psi = -2\pi\rho_S$ integrates to $-2\pi M_S\neq0$). The primary's base image must therefore lose $M_S$ — most naturally because the secondary is drawn from the arena's fixed content, $M_P^{\rm image}+M_S = M_{\rm bg}$ — and this integrated budget, with the hydrostatic law, is the acceptance test for Theorem III; the zero-total fiber transport of §XXIX.12 cannot supply the monopole and is not the mechanism. **Corrected (R84–R88).** The core-anisotropy "tolerance $a\lesssim15\mu$" is replaced by the transfer function $\delta v_{\rm eq}^2/c^2 = 8a/15$ for $Y_2 = (4\cos^2\chi-1)/3$ and the observable-specific bound $\vert a\vert\le\tfrac{45}{8}f\mu$ ($1.0\times10^{-8}$ for a one-percent tolerance in $v^2$; at $a = 15\mu$ the change is $8/3$ of the compact plateau); the convexity lemma carries its hypotheses (convex admissible domain closed under $SO(4)$ averaging, existence of a minimizer) and a strictly convex *forced* functional has an anisotropic minimizer $a = \epsilon j/8K$; the SI stress convention is $T^{\rm phys}_{\mu\nu} = -(2c/\sqrt{-g})\,\delta S/\delta g^{\mu\nu}$ with $x^0 = ct$; the coefficient comparison is $16\pi F/c^3$ against $2M_c/\pi c^2\ell$; "shooting error" becomes "a discrepancy incompatible with the exact equations, attributed by the author to the shooting calculation"; resonances are at even $n\ge2$; the finite-$s$ statement concerns the static Green function, not dynamical stability. **Evidence (R86).** Neither referee received the numerical suite, so every $\kappa$ fit, residual and critical-point claim is **author-reported** until the standalone file `pg_v34_numerics.py` delivered with this version is run; the labels in §§XXIX.12, 16 and in the current manuscript are downgraded accordingly. **New.** §XXIX.18 executes the minimal optical test on the leaf carrying the pulled-back base metric: near-field lensing is standard ($\alpha b/4\mu\to1$, excess $\simeq6b^2/\ell^2$), the Fermat potential is exactly twice the dynamical one — **zero gravitational slip**, as in GR — the full-circuit deflection vanishes, and the antipodal refocusing at $\pi\ell$ ($164$ kyr light time at $16$ kpc) remains *[v34.3, R96–R97: the asymptote is logarithmic, $1+\beta^2(2\ln(2/\beta)-\tfrac13)$; the circuit statement concerns the signed gradient integral only — the forced-Jacobi return direction changes; the slip relation is conditional on a common metric readout]*. §XXIX.19 records the Boltzmannian core program: isotropy as typicality, $\log\Omega\simeq N\log K-Na^2/18$ for the quadrupole, so the referee's tolerance ladder demands $N_{\rm eff}\gtrsim18/a^2 = 10^{13}$–$10^{17}$ compatibility units — the entropy is the convex functional of §XXIX.10(g) with stiffness $N_{\rm eff}$. §XXIX.20 records the author's **representation-stretch branch** (Entries 267–268): Option A, $d\hat s^2 = \ell^2\sec^4(\chi/2)d\chi^2+\ell^2\sin^2\chi\,d\Omega^2$, puts the antipode at infinite proper distance $D = 2\ell\tan(\chi/2)$ while leaving every circular speed unchanged ($v^2 = RN'/NR'$ is independent of the radial coefficient) and makes the stereographic exponential an exact exponential in $D$; it is realized as the leaf's *inclination* into the meridian direction, $\hat\gamma = \gamma+d\Phi\otimes d\Phi$ with an unbounded meridian height $\Phi\sim2\ell\tan(\chi/2)$ — the author's "meeting your own fiber" made literal — and a four-centre regularization makes all distances finite with $D_{\rm antipode}\simeq2\ell/\sqrt{\epsilon}$; its costs and tests (a horn with divergent cross-sectional curvature, no Hubble law from a static stretch, the azimuth advance $\pi(1+\ell^2/b^2)$ that replaces point refocusing by spiralling, the epicyclic ratio $\kappa/\Omega$ reduced by $\cos^2(\chi/2)$ — $1.449\to1.352$ at $8$ kpc in the $\alpha = 0.1$ model) are stated *[v34.3: the angular-diameter cap is a central-observer special case, R99; the exact epicyclic formula, R98]*; Law I is unchanged (minimal interpretation). The register runs R80–R92 (§XXIX.16).

> **v34.3 — the third double round (12 October 2026), and the author's centering requirement.** The long v34.2 title is retired for the short one above; what it listed now lives in these status paragraphs. The Boltzmann toy's entropy Hessian is local and matches the Dirichlet stiffness only mode by mode ($K = N/8$ for the quadrupole); at $N = 18/a_{\rm tol}^2$ the tail probability is ${\rm erfc}(1) = 0.157$. **The author's requirement (R102, §XXIX.20).** *The inclination must be selected covariantly by the full middle-space stress-energy and its meridian structure; no centre, origin or primary label may be prescribed independently of it; in the stationary isotropic one-primary limit the stretch is radial about the dynamically selected centre of energy and approaches Option A outside the finite core; moving the matter moves the stretch; several concentrations regularize one another through the same law.* A symmetry lemma makes centering automatic for any covariant law with a unique solution, and the simplest such law — a Poisson-type coupling $\Delta_B\Phi = \kappa(\rho-\langle\rho\rangle)$ — is computed: it centres correctly and is **not** Option A (bounded stretch, $1.02$ at most, antipodal distance $3.16\ell$), because Option A grows *away* from matter toward the meridian's return point; so the centre comes from the matter potential's minimum while the profile must come from the return/closure structure, and since no smooth regular inclination field on a compact $S^3$ is exactly infinite, the universal law must produce Option A only as the singular isolated-source limit. The embedding of the inclined leaf as the bisection of the resolved middle space is recorded as the branch's first open theorem. *[v34.4: the template $\Phi_A(d(x,c_V))$ and "centering is automatic" are withdrawn (R106); "no Poisson-type coupling" is restricted and replaced by the divergence-form theorem (R107); the return-point mechanism is in §XXIX.26.]*

The closure energy identity $\delta E_c = \mu_c\delta\mathcal N_c-\bar p\,\delta V$ makes the first-order source-energy budget, on the dust background, identical to combined particle-number conservation when the galaxy is made of the closure's species: the transfer law v34.3 recorded as missing is the budget itself at first order; every barotropic closure has the Keplerian near field with $G_{\rm eff} = G$ (§XXIX.23). **The decisive new result (R111).** In the kinematic control with the primary's density frozen, the first-order redistribution of its image removes *exactly* the monopole of a compact secondary at the secondary's position: $\kappa\to1$ as $\delta_S\to0$ ($1-\kappa\simeq2.1\,\delta_S/\ell$, $\kappa = 0.9867$ at $\delta_S = \ell/160$), by a kink-and-flux mechanism derived in the point limit; a point secondary would have no Keplerian field on the base. no uniformly elliptic divergence-form law sourced at the galaxy can produce the horn (theorem); the return-image law with the Entry 156–158 normal-crossing condition imposed at the matter forces a uniform compensating charge and produces it, with finite horns for smooth images and the exact end as the point-image limit; a linear law gives no muffling of four tetrahedral masses; the coupling must be $2.8\times10^8$ times gravitational strength or a universal unit charge per return point (§XXIX.26). **The relational toy and its interface (R116–R117).** The three-anchor compatibility model is computed in full; along a meridian fiber of the resolved pencil every flat $U(1)$ structure has loop holonomy in $\{0,\pi\}$ ($\pi_1 = D_\infty$), the orientation character gives $\pi$, and a continuous phase needs a non-flat Hopf connection — the smallest missing datum (§XXIX.27). **Next.** The one calculation that can end the gravitational program: a finite core with a transported directional measure, matched to the exterior pencil, under which the alignment deficit vanishes and the forced anisotropy stays within tolerance. *[v34.5: several statements of this paragraph are corrected by R121–R129 — the rigidity lemma, the "iff", P2 as "the fibration as a variable", the orientation assignment of $\pi$, "a continuous phase needs a non-flat connection", "no muffling" in a linear law, and "can end the gravitational program"; > **v34.6 — the author's Entries 275–276 and two reports on v34.5 (13 October 2026).** The author refined the readout: the infinite apparent distance belongs only to histories passing *through* the antipode, and skew should soften it continuously (275). The grade is chosen as the image opposition $\alpha = -\hat n_1\cdot\hat n_2$, computed and not fitted; a symmetric return lens keeps $\alpha = 1$. *[v34.7, R150: image opposition is a detector observable, not the passage criterion; the history-level grade is the return near-miss $\alpha_R = \cos\beta_R$, conserved as $\lvert L\rvert = \sin\beta_R$ (§XXIX.34(e))]* **Propagation and the consistency (R134, R137, R138; §XXIX.32).** The histories are null geodesics of the complete matter geometry $H_{\mathcal M}$. > **What is new in version 20 — the bi-connection substrate, adopted by decision.** Part XV states the author's Universal Null-History Principle — light and gravitational waves share one characteristic cone, one Jacobi gate and one history class, differing only as representations — and adopts, as a decision, the middle geometry as the symmetric resolution of two exchange-related Weyl-type connections sharing one null geometry. What the pair does is verified: its mean is Levi-Civita, all three connections share every unparametrized null geodesic, and its relative holonomy around a two-history loop is a homothety, $e^{-2\int_\Sigma F_A}$ — abelian, Stokes-expressible, non-exact and additive *(this real-loop mechanism is superseded by 20.2: on the real middle space the scale flux vanishes, and the scale character lives on the conjugate complex lifts of a class)*. It is *not* the Jacobi squeeze of §XIV.9, and cannot be: the two are the $\mathbb R_+$ and $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ factors of one relative transport, scale and shape, which moves the redshift candidate into the homothety and dissolves the reciprocal-branch problem. The enclosed flux is first order in a class's width, so redshift becomes a property of finite classes; its sign rule, magnitude and universality are open, the recurrence-age bound survives for cumulative readings, and the multi-messenger requirement $\eta_{\rm EM} = \eta_{\rm GW}$ is anchored by GW170817. The fiber-product deepening of the middle space is stated as a target, not adopted. Added in the same version: the branch's model-independent foundation — the conjugate-point theorem with its local and global halves (§XV.0) — and §XV.6, the author's larger ambition made precise: the two Born paths and the two connections as one doubled transport, by the closed-time-path dictionary; > **What is new in version 19 — a deliberately ambitious branch, Part XIV.** From two research briefs: modular return optics, in which other galaxies would be recurrent photon-history classes of the one arena rendered with a unitary multiplicative redshift, and the galactic well as the scale of that redshift. Everything in it is provisional, and its first calculations already prune it. Secondaries do break the round antipodal family, into about two first-order stationary members each — not a galaxy count. The addendum's literal well fails its own first null test: the flux through the hemisphere separating source from twin vanishes by symmetry, and the arena-scale depth is dominated by the galaxy's own central self-potential. The coincidence $M_{\rm gal}\sim cH_0\ell^2/G$ encodes the arena radius, and its heuristic coefficient $1/4$ selects 7 kpc, against 13–16 kpc from Part IV and 25 kpc from the detached wing. Returned starlight would exceed the measured optical background twenty- to two-hundredfold, so the readout must send nearly all of it into its kernel; the branch's sharpest construction test is the invariant that puts the observer's own return there. What survives is stated as proposals with a falsification ledger and a single deciding question (§XIV.10). Parts 0–XIII are unchanged. *(19.1: the ledger corrected after review — the member count is not a galaxy count, the starlight budget overshoots the background, both return times are given with their dependence on $\ell$, and the self-return test is stated as a construction tool. 19.2: the opening synchronized with Part XIV, the flux-suppression factor made conditional on $D_{\rm app}$ acting as a luminosity distance, the Morse count's smoothing stated, the brightness budget sourced in its own box, and the next calculation named. 19.3: the history-dependent functional computed — the boost holonomy vanishes in the static arena and reduces to the tidal integral for the null loop; the tidal integral is sign-indefinite; and the null focusing column gives the Hubble scale to within a factor $1$–$1.6$, independently of $\ell$, for classes centred on the Galaxy — the coincidence becoming $M_{\rm gal}/h^2\approx2cH_0/G$. 19.4: the focusing functional made affine-invariant and explicitly background-subtracted, and renamed; the pivot stated — $\ell$ sets recurrence, $GM/h^2$ the dilation scale; the off-centre observer made the decisive problem; and §XIV.9 added, deriving from the relative Jacobi monodromy a noncompact squeeze with coefficient $1/4$, to which the background contributes nothing, and defining the collective class as a return-map island. 19.5: the focusing functional normalized by the Killing energy; the derived sector named the isotropic $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ block of the full $Sp(4,\mathbb R)$ monodromy, which is then computed, separating a screen-invariant $\eta_{\rm iso}$ from a shear $\gamma_{\rm aniso}$; the $1/4$ restricted to localized lumps; a positive squeeze distinguished from a positive redshift, which is now the bridge to build; the island observer-conditioned with the Liouville measure; and a recurrence-age bound added, $\ell$ cancelling, which caps the cumulative reading of $z$ at about $0.1$.)*

> **What is new in version 18 — two additions.** *Conjugate-path optics* (§XIII.10), from the author's brief: the isolated ray replaced by the Jacobi-critical class it belongs to, with conjugacy as the gate. Four calculations are done — on the round arena the release points are $L = n\pi\ell$ and the first is the twin, with the antipodal family a critical manifold; a weak secondary splits it by the point-lens shear; the theory's static metric has the standard Fermat form; and within the solar system the gate stays shut, the solar focus lying at 548 AU. Standard theory already sums stationary rays, so the proposal is placed in the readout, as a Photon History Postulate, with a first acceptance test: on the gravity slice every source refocuses on itself after $\pi\ell/c$ from every direction, and that family must not render as an image — quantified: the Sun's own light would return at the solar constant from every direction, so canonical position cannot be visual position for returning light. A proposed modular-return branch, in which returns render as other galaxies, is opened as a ledger of requirements on that condition, with its pros and cons recorded. And the canonical metric in bundle form, below.
>
> **What is new in version 18 — the canonical metric in bundle form.** Of the recommendations on the Berry-phase analogy, one was worth adopting for its parsimony: the bundle form $\hat g = \pi_H^*g_{\mathcal M}+R_H^2(d\chi+\mathcal A_H)^2$, which packages the frozen $3+1+2$ blocks into a single object with standard curvature formulas, and turns the action target into one question — what condition on $\hat g$ makes the quotient obey Law I? (§IX.1). It gives Berry's phase a size, $\Delta s_H = (L_H/2\pi)\Delta\chi$: the connection says how far around the fiber a loop goes, the locking says how far that is. And the first candidate condition is tested and excluded: Einstein's vacuum equations on $E$ make each source a Kaluza–Klein monopole whose fiber shrinks toward the source while the locking's grows — Obstruction 1 as a sign — and would make the fiber's absolute size observable, a galactic fiber exceeding solar gravity at 1 AU by $5\times10^{26}$. The fork that leaves is recorded. Parts 0–IX remain frozen; §IX.1 is a target, not a law.
>
> **What is new in version 17.6 — the completion's price, and a freeze.** The smooth local completion of §II.2 has a metric consequence: the circle's generator vanishes on the restored meridian, so any smooth metric collapses the fiber there, $L_H = O(\sqrt\rho)$, while Law I's locking grows it toward a source. The Taub–NUT nut is the smooth example — the reciprocal warping already recorded as Obstruction 1 (§XI.3), now forced into the core. So the locking and the principal connection are laws on the *regular stratum* $E^\circ$, and the orbit's behaviour at an exceptional stratum is a separate question; §0.1, the primitive data, Law 0, §III.2, Structure III and the action target are synchronized to this. Canonical optics is typed on $E$, Rule A is labelled an Aethic stipulation rather than a requirement of quantum mechanics, and optical non-closure is phrased as integrated holonomy rather than large curvature. With these, Parts 0–IX are frozen.
>
> **What is new in version 17.5 — the author's latest considerations, audited and made explicit.** The author's entries of 22 September were checked against the document. Two were misrepresented and are repaired: the author's own cut-and-flip of a rosette, which gives two point-symmetric spirals (§XIII.7), and the ordering argument that the normal's special treatment precedes gravity's quotient, so gravity must inherit a correspondent of it (§XIII.9). Several were missing and are added: the Machian motivation for renderings and the rooted form of the complexity criterion (§XIII.0, §XIII.6); visual space as built from pairs, with a blur reading of the circumgalactic boundary (§XIII.8); the author's framing of the gravitational firewall (§XIII.9); and the recurring budget motif. The branch's research program is now stated explicitly, as a numbered list at the end of §XIII.0.
>
> **What is new in version 17.4 — targets, not mechanisms, and an existing budget.** The Reissner–Nordström factorization is recorded as a *target* for an unpacking theory rather than a mechanism: its two weights are internal, and best read as outputs of an unpacking, not objects upstairs; unifying them with Kerr's displacement is posed as an open problem (§X.0). Black-hole physics already has a budget of this kind: the horizon radii multiply to $a^2+Q^2$, and the Christodoulou–Ruffini formula splits mass into an irreducible, area-fixed part and extractable charge and spin energy. The rapidity, though, holds $\delta$ fixed rather than the area — unpacking charge that way shrinks the horizon, so it can be a change of rendering but not a physical process (§XIII.5). The branch's one-sentence thesis, the family of renderings, and a rule against using the dipole to build an axis are added.
>
> **What is new in version 17.3 — the corrections asked for before a conceptual freeze, and one construction.** The shell's circle is identified with the spinor's overall phase through the Hopf bundle's principal *right* action, not the spin group's left action (§I.6). Maps from substrate to rendering are typed branchwise throughout, with the optical connection living on the correspondence itself (§XIII.2). Curvature odd under the plane reflection makes the plane's connection *flat*, which is not yet trivial holonomy on the projective plane; and the descended reflection also fixes an isolated point on the normal axis (§XIII.9). Only *generic* distinct light paths are too far apart in time to interfere (§XIII.8). The charge branch's rapidity is now a *chiral weight rapidity*, acting on gauge-invariant weights rather than on spinor representatives (§XIII.5). The lunar bound is tagged conditional, and the density convention and the Grassmann sentence are corrected. And one construction: **a smooth local model of $E$ near each meridian**, whose circle action is free away from the meridian, whose quotient restores the meridian, and which produces Structure III's unit Hopf class on every linking sphere (§II.2).
>
> **What is new in version 17.2 — two refinements to the branch.** §XIII.9 adds a gravitational firewall and prospect holonomy. The firewall: centrades carry localization, propagation carries relations, and centrade-free sectors would carry no *autonomous* Weyl datum. The stronger rule $C_{abcd} = 0$ fails, since the Bianchi identity sources Weyl curvature from stress gradients, and electromagnetic plane waves are conformally flat only when their profile is isotropic; the weaker rule needs a local split of Weyl curvature that general relativity does not supply. Prospect holonomy moves the normal-direction effect out of optics and into the lift, since gravity along the normal is measured. No flat bundle can close in the plane yet fail along the normal, but curvature odd under the plane reflection makes the plane's connection flat while opening loops along the normal — the geometric shape of a mechanism, with its free choices named.
>
> **What is new in version 17.1 — corrections before a freeze.** A referee's review of version 17 is applied throughout. Coherence is governed by what the detector and environment can distinguish, not by literal identity of endpoints, so phase holonomy is the cleanest carrier of the optical proposal but not the only one (§XIII.3). The incidence correspondence becomes the global primitive of canonical optics, with the old optical map surviving branch by branch (§XIII.2). The "veering normal" is repaired as a canonical line field (§XIII.8). The relative-modulus gauge trap resolves in one direction: in any construction that reproduces Reissner–Nordström, the rapidity cannot be the spinor pair's gauge freedom, and the one rescaling gravity cannot see is the swap $Q\to-Q$ (§X.0). Darkness gains three candidate routes — non-unitary leakage, unitary mode conversion, and *closure obstruction*, in which no rendered endpoint satisfies both legs at once — and none is yet derived (§XIII.8). The involution claims are qualified, the dipole coincidence keeps its geometry but loses its probability, and the complexification of $E$ and the regular locus of the Hopf bundle are stated consistently (§0.4, §II.2).
>
> **What is new in version 17 — a branch, on a frozen architecture.** Version 16's architecture is frozen as Parts 0–XII. Part XIII opens a new branch from the author's newer intuitions: canonical optics, in which an observed event is rigid downstairs while its canonical realizations are flexible upstairs; agreeing structure, in which one underlying point can appear twice; centrades, in which fields are unfinished reductions; and many rendered spacetimes. Its sharpest findings are constraints. Inside standard quantum mechanics coherence is governed by what the detector and environment can distinguish, and a *phase*-type holonomy is the cleanest carrier of the optical proposal (§XIII.3). Rendering one point twice needs a correspondence, not a map (§XIII.4). And neither simple reading of the orbital flip turns a symmetric disk into spirals, although a handedness flip freezes each rosette into a stationary spiral segment (§XIII.7). §0.0 now lists these intuitions beside the older ones, and §X.0's complexified-meridian modulus is refined toward a chiral weight rapidity (§XIII.5). §XIII.8 then tests whether the latest intuitions form one structure: **not yet** — no single literal involution plays all the roles, though time reversal and the plane reflection are genuinely shared; a pure phase or sign cannot dim a single ray, leaving three candidate routes to darkness, none derived; and the in-plane part of our motion relative to the cosmic background lies $3.4^\circ$ from reversed solar motion, a numerical clue whose significance is open.
>
> **What is new in version 16 — a draft branch, not a new architecture.** Parts 0–IX are version 15.7 text with **one architectural exception**, flagged where it occurs: the arena scale $\ell$ is now galactic, and the model deliberately has no cosmological slot (see the note on scale); other galaxies are moved to a detached wing (Part XII). A new Part X tests a proposal: that Reissner–Nordström is the small-charge face of a projective-gravity effect, with extremal holes — observationally poorly sampled — where the effect is fully exposed. **The proposed mechanism fails on the seed's own terms**: displacement along the meridian is exactly what gravity cannot see (§X.4). **But the intuition lands twice** — §X.0 reconstructs it in plain terms. Exactly — in asymptotically flat Einstein–Maxwell, which is the arena's local comparison limit (§X.1) — in this theory's variables Reissner–Nordström satisfies $N\Omega = 1-(M^2-Q^2)/4r^2$, so *extremality is lapse–fiber balance*, and the relation §III.2 retired is precisely the extremal sector (§X.2). And in another form: Reissner–Nordström's own Einstein–Rosen bridge carries a free antipodal twin map whose quotient is an $\mathbb{RP}^3$ geon, and that twin recedes to infinite distance as $Q\to M$ (§X.3). And the proposal's *two halves* are exact after all — as a split in mass rather than position: $\Omega = U_+U_-$ with $m_\pm = (M\pm Q)/2$, so that **Reissner–Nordström subextremality becomes the quadratic positivity condition $m_+m_-\geq0$**, and a naked singularity sits at the zero of a negative-weight factor (§X.7). Parametrized by the angle $m$ with $Q/M = \cos m$, *the subextremal domain is exactly that angle's real range* (§X.9). Made exact, the formula is a single-monopole Reissner–Nordström bridge in standard Einstein–Maxwell, with Kerr–Newman's extremality *sphere* $Q^2+a^2+\delta^2 = M^2$ as its spinning form — but on a conformal three-sphere of radius $\delta/4$, not on this theory's closed base, where the problem is nonlinear and open (§X.10). Read as a rapidity, the imaginary meridian coordinate supplies the angle, its real range covering exactly the subextremal domain, and $(M,Q)$ is represented on a timelike cone whose light-cone components are the factor weights (§X.11). **The branch is graded at §X.12** into exact facts, parameterizations, parallels and hypotheses, and handing back a three-way fork and one sharp question — *does the global projective quotient enlarge $U(1)$ to $O(2)$?* — which §X.13 answers: the quotient does not itself enlarge $U(1)$; only a descended *isolated* charge would require twisted descent and $O(2)$, and neither way of making charge descend survives. **Within the summed-source architecture, lunar laser ranging bounds duplicated electromagnetic energy at the twin above by about $5\times10^{-11}$ — $\eta\lesssim5\times10^{-11}$** (§X.13). Part X is frozen here; the next branch is the optical question at the head of §XI.2.
